article_content: Prabir Purkayastha, founder and editor-in-chief of the English-language news portal NewsClick, and Amit Chakravarty, the website’s head of human resources, were arrested by Indian authorities under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) on allegations of receiving foreign funds for pro-China propaganda. Their arrests followed raids on NewsClick’s office in New Delhi—which was also sealed by the Delhi Police—and the homes of several journalists and contributors associated with the site. Police seized laptops and mobile phones as part of the investigation. A home ministry official stated that a special investigation team conducted the raids to identify individuals potentially receiving overseas funds aimed at spreading foreign propaganda through a media group. NewsClick officials were not immediately available for comment. According to the company’s website, it covers news from India and abroad with a focus on progressive movements. A case against NewsClick and its journalists was registered on August 17, following a New York Times report alleging that the site had received funds from US millionaire Neville Roy Singham, whom the report claims supported Chinese governmental talking points. Singham and NewsClick have rejected these accusations. Purkayastha previously indicated the allegations were not new and would be addressed in court. Tensions between India and China have been high since 2020, after a deadly border clash resulted in casualties on both sides. Since then, the Indian government has banned several Chinese-owned apps, such as TikTok, and initiated tax probes into some Chinese mobile phone companies. DIGIPUB News India Foundation and the Press Club of India expressed concern over the raids, while a group of journalists planned a protest in New Delhi. Police reported that 37 male suspects were questioned at the NewsClick office and 9 female suspects at their residences, with searches carried out at 30 locations. Among those questioned were journalists Urmilesh, Aunindyo Chakravarty, Abhisar Sharma, Paranjoy Guha Thakurta, and historian Sohail Hashmi. Hashmi described the raid as intimidating and a crackdown on press freedom, after having to hand over his electronic devices to investigators. The Press Club of India also voiced concern. The Prime Minister's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) defended the raids as necessary for investigating foreign funding in media organizations. Information and Broadcasting Minister Anurag Thakur remarked that investigating agencies are free to conduct searches in case of wrongdoing. The INDIA alliance, a coalition of 28 opposition parties, criticized the government for allegedly suppressing the media through investigative agencies over the past nine years. Shoaib Daniyal, political editor at Scroll, argued that not only management but also junior employees and contributors were targeted during the raids, and commented on India’s strict anti-terror laws. India has dropped from 150th to 161st place in the annual World Press Freedom Index by Reporters Without Borders. The Modi government disputes the ranking and maintains that India’s press is vibrant and free. Earlier this year, BBC’s offices in India were raided by tax authorities after releasing a documentary critical of Modi. Several journalists say criticism of the government is often met with harassment, both online and offline. The Network of Women in Media in India also voiced concern about the raids, describing them as targeting dissenting voices. Journalist Abhisar Sharma, who was interrogated for several hours, affirmed his intention to keep challenging those in power.

article_content: Three Australian professional football players were involved in a fight outside a nightclub in West Hollywood, reportedly over pop singer Rihanna’s autograph. The incident left one player with a broken jaw. The AFL players had just completed a two-week high-altitude training camp in Arizona and were in Los Angeles to celebrate. Campbell Brown and Steven May, both of the Gold Coast Suns, were asked to leave Bootsy Bellows nightclub as Rihanna and her entourage were arriving after her concert. According to reports, May attempted to re-enter the club to get Rihanna's autograph, prompting intervention from Josh Gibson of the Hawthorn Football Club. During the altercation, Brown allegedly punched May, breaking his jaw. Some sources suggest the fight may have started because of a dispute over a restaurant bill. May required surgery and is expected to miss five weeks of full training to recover. Australian media report that the incident could lead to the end of Brown’s 205-game AFL career. Footage of the fight was recorded outside Bootsy Bellows and leaked to the media. Brown reportedly hit May twice before other teammates separated them. Both Brown and May were sent back to Australia by their club, pending an investigation. Rihanna was seen in New York for her brother's birthday celebrations and appeared at the American Music Awards earlier in the week. Though the pop star was not directly involved, her presence at the nightclub was a key factor in the incident. The remainder of the team's players returned to Australia the following day. AFL, or Australian Football League, is one of the country's most popular sports, similar to NFL and rugby. Rihanna recently collaborated with Eminem on his song 'The Monster.'

article_content: Despite some reservations, artificial intelligence—especially generative AI capable of producing text and images from prompts—continues to be incorporated into the hardware and software we use daily. Microsoft has been proactive in this space, adding AI chatbot functionalities to its Bing search engine earlier this year. It is now showcasing an early version of its new Copilot AI assistant in Windows 11. According to Microsoft, Copilot is designed to enhance your creativity and productivity, functioning similarly to Bing's chatbot, and can produce anything from travel advice to original poems. To access Copilot in Windows 11, ensure your operating system is fully updated. Go to Windows Update in Settings to check for updates (you may need to enable the 'Get the latest updates as soon as they're available' toggle). By default, a Copilot button will appear on your taskbar, which can be clicked to launch it. If you wish to adjust this, go to Personalization > Taskbar in Settings. You can also open Copilot using the Win+C keyboard shortcut or via the Start menu. If you are new to generative AI, you can try Copilot by asking it to write a short poem, draft an introduction for a cover letter, or compose an email to a colleague. When starting a new chat, you will be able to select between 'More Creative,' 'More Balanced,' and 'More Precise' conversation styles, similar to Bing Chat on the web. This lets you tailor how imaginative Copilot's responses are. Copilot is not limited to creating text. Thanks to its integration with Bing and the web, you can also ask it questions about travel destinations, request cooking or recipe tips, or seek advice on fixing DIY problems at home. Responses are typically accompanied by links to their online sources. You can choose Copilot's conversation style to suit your needs.

article_content: British explorers are preparing to drill through almost two miles of Antarctic ice into Lake Ellsworth to investigate evidence of ancient life and climate, possibly dating back up to a million years. The team used robust tracked vehicles to transport about 70 tonnes of equipment to the remote drilling location, which is considered one of the harshest environments in the world. They plan to return in November to retrieve water and sediment samples from the lake using clean technology adapted from space industry standards. The UK flag now flies at Lake Ellsworth, where all necessary equipment has been assembled ahead of the operation. The team hopes that the samples will reveal new information about Earth’s climate history. Findings from this project could also help scientists assess the stability of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet and predict possible effects on future sea levels. An advance group of four British engineers endured temperatures as low as -35°C, using powerful tractors to haul equipment containers on sledges and skis across deep snow and mountain passes. The 155-mile journey through the Ellsworth Mountains took three days to complete. Scientists have been planning this investigation for more than 15 years. Professor Martin Siegert, the Lake Ellsworth Programme Principal Investigator from the University of Edinburgh, said: 'Completing this stage brings us closer to discovering whether unique, previously unknown forms of microbial life exist in this environment. The samples from Lake Ellsworth could be of great value to the scientific community.' This year, the team will complete and test both the water sampling probe and sediment corer. Sediment samples could provide important insights into the ancient history of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet, including any past collapses that may have influenced sea level rise. In the next phase, researchers will use a high-pressure drill to bore through 1.8 miles of ice, then lower a titanium probe to analyze the lake water, followed by a corer to collect sediment. Drilling will take about three days, and researchers will have roughly 24 hours to collect samples before the borehole refreezes. To avoid contaminating the site, most equipment is being stored one mile away from the drilling point. Lake Ellsworth is approximately 8.6 miles long, 1.2 to 1.8 miles wide, and 150 meters deep—similar in size to Loch Katrine or Lake Windermere. Chris Hill, Programme Manager and member of the advance party, described the success of the logistics as a major achievement and emphasized the pressure of working in the brief Antarctic summer window. The Lake Ellsworth project is being carried out by a consortium funded by the Natural Environment Research Council (NERC), in partnership with the British Antarctic Survey, the National Oceanography Centre, and universities across the UK. There are now over 400 subglacial lakes known beneath Antarctica’s vast ice sheet. A Russian team is also preparing to carry out a similar mission at Lake Vostok in East Antarctica.

A equipe usou veículos robustos sobre esteiras para transportar cerca de 70 toneladas de equipamentos até o remoto local de perfuração, considerado um dos ambientes mais hostis do planeta. Eles planejam retornar em novembro para coletar amostras de água e sedimentos do lago, utilizando tecnologia limpa adaptada de padrões da indústria aeroespacial. A bandeira do Reino Unido agora tremula no Lago Ellsworth, onde todo o equipamento necessário foi reunido para a operação. A equipe espera que as amostras revelem novas informações sobre a história climática da Terra. As descobertas deste projeto também podem ajudar cientistas a avaliar a estabilidade da Plataforma de Gelo da Antártica Ocidental e prever possíveis impactos sobre o nível do mar no futuro. Um grupo avançado com quatro engenheiros britânicos enfrentou temperaturas de até -35°C, usando tratores potentes para rebocar contêineres de equipamentos em trenós e esquis por neve profunda e montanhas íngremes. A jornada de 250 quilômetros pelas Montanhas Ellsworth durou três dias. Cientistas vêm planejando essa investigação há mais de 15 anos. O professor Martin Siegert, pesquisador principal do Programa do Lago Ellsworth da Universidade de Edimburgo, afirmou: “Concluir esta etapa nos deixa mais próximos de descobrir se formas únicas e desconhecidas de vida microbiana existem neste ambiente. As amostras do Lago Ellsworth podem ser de grande valor para a comunidade científica.” Neste ano, a equipe completará e testará tanto a sonda de coleta de água quanto o equipamento para amostragem de sedimentos. Amostras de sedimentos podem trazer importantes insights sobre a história antiga da Plataforma de Gelo da Antártica Ocidental, inclusive sobre possíveis colapsos que afetam o nível do mar. Na próxima fase, pesquisadores usarão uma perfuratriz de alta pressão para atravessar três quilômetros de gelo, depois baixarão uma sonda de titânio para analisar a água, seguida por um equipamento para coletar sedimentos. A perfuração levará cerca de três dias e os pesquisadores terão aproximadamente 24 horas para coletar as amostras antes de o buraco congelar novamente. Para evitar contaminação, grande parte do equipamento foi deixada a um quilômetro do ponto exato de perfuração. O Lago Ellsworth tem cerca de 14 quilômetros de comprimento, entre 2 e 3 quilômetros de largura e 150 metros de profundidade—tamanho semelhante ao Lago Katrine ou ao Lago Windermere. Chris Hill, gerente do programa e membro da equipe de avanço, classificou o sucesso logístico como uma grande conquista e ressaltou a pressão de trabalhar na curta temporada de verão antártica. O projeto do Lago Ellsworth é realizado por um consórcio financiado pelo Natural Environment Research Council (NERC), em parceria com o British Antarctic Survey, o National Oceanography Centre e universidades do Reino Unido. Mais de 400 lagos subglaciais já foram identificados sob a vasta camada de gelo da Antártica. Uma equipe russa também se prepara para uma missão semelhante no Lago Vostok, no leste da Antártica.

article_content:
Scotland's First Minister, Alex Salmond, has cautioned American billionaire Donald Trump against meddling in government affairs ahead of the opening of his controversial golf course. The Trump International Golf Links in Aberdeenshire is set to open on July 10. While Trump envisions the course becoming one of the world's best, plans to build an adjoining hotel have been put on hold due to a dispute over a nearby offshore wind farm project.

Trump alleges that he was misled by Salmond regarding his $1 billion investment, and he has threatened legal action against the Scottish government if the wind farm development continues. However, Salmond, who supports the construction of the golf course, has made it clear that energy policy decisions should be left to Scotland’s democratically elected government.

Speaking at the TED Global conference in Edinburgh, Salmond stated, "Donald Trump is building a fantastic golf course in Scotland that I very much support. Unfortunately, recently, he has tried to tell the Scottish Government how to run our energy policy. My message is yes to great golf courses—Scotland has the greatest golf courses in the world and one more won't do any harm—but let the democratically elected government of Scotland decide its own energy policy."

In April, Trump appeared before the Scottish parliament to express his opposition to the offshore wind farm. Salmond questioned Trump’s strategy of potentially taking legal action, noting that while Scotland is a free society, the likelihood of winning such a case against a government pursuing its elected mandate is slim.

Designed by renowned golf architect Martin Hawtree, the Menie course was constructed on a site of special scientific interest after the Scottish government overruled Aberdeenshire council’s decision to block the project. The government cited economic benefits as outweighing environmental concerns. The course has been discussed as a potential venue for major championships, such as the British Open or the 2022 Ryder Cup.

article_content: US President Joe Biden announced that the 14 members of the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF) have reached agreements on three crucial initiatives: strengthening supply chain resilience, advancing clean energy transitions, and combating corruption. Biden stated that these efforts aim to elevate standards, transparency, inclusivity, and innovation throughout the region. The IPEF comprises Australia, Brunei, Fiji, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, and the United States. Initiated by Biden in May 2022, the framework seeks to enhance regional economic partnerships. India's delegation was led by Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal. During a special IPEF event, Biden emphasized the collaborative push for higher standards in the Indo-Pacific and highlighted ongoing work to ensure workers receive fair opportunities, with a focus on sustainable development. He recognized that while notable progress has been achieved, continued work is needed. The newly signed supply chain agreement aims to detect and prevent disruptions, like those seen during the COVID-19 pandemic. Another agreement will help accelerate the region's clean energy transition, fostering US and private sector investments in innovation and infrastructure. This includes solar energy projects in the Philippines, offshore wind initiatives in Thailand, and US-India collaborations on energy storage. A third agreement targets anti-corruption measures and improvements in tax administration to ensure transparent and secure trade and investment environments. Biden stressed that private sector investment is essential for rapid progress in the region, complementing government funding. Japanese Prime Minister Kishida Fumio welcomed IPEF’s advancement, emphasizing its importance in strengthening the Indo-Pacific’s economic framework and supporting sustainable growth. In related business news, the Indian government is considering transferring unclaimed Sahara-Sebi Refund Account funds to the Consolidated Fund of India while maintaining investor refund opportunities. Apple is aiming for ₹1 lakh crore in iPhone production in India for the fiscal year ending March 2024. Separately, Nawaz Modi, estranged wife of Gautam Singhania, is seeking a substantial share of his net worth as part of a family settlement.

article_content: Forget giving the dog a bone—this pampered pooch would likely prefer filet mignon and lobster if given the chance. Bella Mia, a three-year-old purebred Maltese from Great Neck, New York, is reportedly one of the richest dogs in the world, with a six-figure trust fund. Last year, her owner, Rose Ann Bolasny, granted her a $100,000 annual allowance for weekly grooming, haircuts, and designer shopping sprees. Rose Ann, a 60-year-old accountant with two adult sons, refers to Bella Mia as the 'daughter she never had' and treats her as a child rather than a pet. Bella Mia has more than 1,000 outfits stored in specially designed walk-in closets, accessorized with diamond and pearl jewelry. She has an extensive wardrobe including gowns, coats, pajamas, jeans, skirts, hats, shoes, and even a pair of Uggs. She also has her own bedroom with a double bed and plush toys. The pampered dog often dines at the table, is spoon-fed, and accompanies her family to five-star restaurants while traveling. Rose Ann shares her home with her retired husband Walter, 82, and sons Robert, 38, and Louis, 32. Initially, Rose Ann wasn't sure about having a dog, hoping to travel with her husband after her sons left home. However, she says it was love at first sight when Bella Mia arrived. On her third birthday, Rose Ann and her husband updated their wills to include Bella Mia in their trust fund, ensuring she will inherit a recently purchased house in Florida. Rose Ann said she discussed the decision with her sons, making sure they understood her desire to provide ongoing care for Bella Mia. Despite the opulent lifestyle, Rose Ann highlights Bella Mia's positive work, noting that she visits the Ronald McDonald House each week and different nursing homes as a charity dog. Rose Ann's original approach to pet ownership changed after joining a Maltese dog meet-up in New York, where she discovered the world of pet fashion shows. She began buying outfits and accessories, entering Bella Mia into contests—winning her first at the event. As a puppy, Bella Mia won the prestigious Westminster New York Fashion Show and developed a penchant for luxury. She even attends social events with her canine boyfriend, Bogey. Rose Ann acknowledges that some may view her spending as excessive, but she emphasizes the joy and companionship Bella Mia brings. She concludes, 'We love her with our whole heart and soul. What I love most is that she proves beauty radiates from the inside out.'

article_content: Prime Video has officially renewed 'Gen V,' a spinoff of the popular superhero show 'The Boys,' for a second season. Set during the same time as ‘The Boys’ upcoming fourth season, ‘Gen V’ has quickly received praise from critics and sparked vibrant conversation on social media within its first five episodes. Vernon Sanders, television chief at MGM, told Variety that expanding ‘The Boys’ universe with Sony has been an exciting journey. He noted that ‘Gen V’ has become Prime Video’s leading series in over 130 countries and is the platform’s most popular new original for 2023. Sanders shared his excitement for the show’s ongoing story and commended the cast and crew for their creative efforts. Showrunner Michele Fazekas and executive producer Eric Kripke echoed this enthusiasm, stating that their writers are already preparing for the next season. They promised even more wild storylines, dark humor, and the unique surprises fans expect from the show. Prime Video’s decision to renew ‘Gen V’ highlights its commitment to expanding ‘The Boys’ franchise. Alongside live-action series, the platform also released ‘The Boys Presents: Diabolical,’ an animated anthology set in the same universe. Multiple spinoffs are in production, according to Kripke, so viewers can expect even more from ‘The Boys’ world in the future. The next episode of ‘Gen V’ releases on October 20, and the first season wraps up with its finale on November 3.

article_content: According to a new study, up to three travelers infected with Ebola may board international flights each month from West Africa, raising concerns about the virus spreading to other countries. Researchers used a model incorporating scheduled flights from September to December 2014, historic 2013 itineraries, and current Ebola surveillance data for Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Their findings, published in The Lancet, estimate that approximately three infected individuals per month could depart these countries by air. Dr. Isaac Bogoch, an infectious disease specialist at the University of Toronto and lead author, noted that although the number seems small compared to the populations of these countries—Guinea alone has 11.4 million people and about 1,500 Ebola cases—the risk remains significant for global health. Nonessential travel to and from Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone has dropped markedly in the past six months. Of the roughly 500,000 travelers who left these countries in 2013, over half flew to Ghana, Senegal, the United Kingdom, France, or Gambia. The study found that the likelihood of an Ebola-infected traveler heading to the UK or France is about eight times higher than to the United States. Most outbound travelers, however, still go to other low- or middle-income countries. With the recent imported Ebola case in the US highlighting infection-control challenges, experts like Dr. Jesse Goodman of Georgetown University stress the importance of boosting preparedness in less-resourced nations. The study also evaluates airport screenings, concluding that exit screening at airports in affected countries is more efficient than entry screening elsewhere, but neither method is foolproof due to Ebola’s incubation period, which can last up to 21 days. This means an infected individual may show no symptoms during travel, as was the case with Thomas Eric Duncan, who arrived in the US symptom-free and later became ill. Dr. William Schaffner of Vanderbilt University likened airport screening efforts to squeezing juice with little yield—an imperfect but necessary public health measure. The researchers stress that the most effective way to prevent global spread is by focusing resources on stopping transmission within West Africa; reducing cases there will, in turn, reduce the likelihood of international spread. However, vigilance remains essential worldwide, as imported cases can still occur unexpectedly.

article_content: Carlton Central Infant School in Nottingham has prohibited students from bringing squash (cordial) drinks to school, citing health concerns. Instead, children may only have orange juice, milk, or water while at school. Some parents say their children refuse to drink these alternatives and are going without fluids throughout the school day because they prefer cordial. Nikki Richardson, a mother of four, states that her son Corbyn, age four, returns home thirsty each day because the school does not permit him to drink a no added-sugar, 10-calorie Fruit Shoot drink she provides. She argues that orange juice, which the school allows, contains significantly more sugar and calories than the cordial drinks she gives her child, and describes the policy as illogical. Richardson, supported by other parents, claims the school’s policy is inconsistent, noting that foods such as crisps, chocolate, custard, and sponge cake are still permitted. She has launched a petition requesting the school to reverse its ban on cordial drinks. Another parent, Tiffany Antcliffe, says her five-year-old daughter Amber is also declining to drink at school because she dislikes the available beverages. The school’s administration, led by headteacher Anna Spencer, insists that the policy follows county council guidelines and was introduced to minimize students’ consumption of sugary drinks, which they believe can have negative effects on behaviour. The school requires a doctor's note if a parent wants their child to have cordial for medical reasons. The debate has raised concerns among some parents who feel the restrictions may lead to dehydration, especially during hot weather, as their children will not drink water, milk, or juice. Recent research from Glasgow University suggests that fruit juice, including orange juice, can also be high in sugar and calories, with a 200ml serving of orange juice containing approximately 100 calories and 23 grams of sugar. A new must-have shoe is making waves on the red carpet, and it isn't about red soles. The Lana heels, from the boutique London label Bionda Castana, have recently been seen on celebrities such as Zoe Saldana, Anna Paquin, Emma Roberts, and Eva Mendes. The list continues with Kate Bosworth, who wore them to her Style Thief app launch, Olivia Palermo for her Brides magazine cover, and Cheryl Cole for her June birthday.

Other fans include Bella Thorne, Lizzy Caplan, Gemma Arterton, and Zoey Deutch, solidifying the Lana heels as a go-to choice for Hollywood's style-conscious stars. The pumps, which feature a pointed toe and ankle tie, cost £485 ($800) and come in various colors, making them popular with stylists and celebrities alike.

Bionda Castana was founded by Natalia Barbieri and Jennifer Portman, friends who bonded over their Italian heritage—the name means 'Blonde Brunette' in Italian. The shoes are designed in London and handcrafted in Italy.

Natalia explained to MailOnline that the Lana pumps were inspired by singer Lana Del Rey, whom she calls 'the epitome of cool.' She says the style is successful because it is timeless yet distinct. The Lana's breathable materials and soft mesh toe provide comfort, even after long wear in warm weather. The signature triangle pattern is influenced by modern architecture, refined with a feminine touch.

Beyond the Lana, Bionda Castana enjoys a celebrity following for other designs as well. Rachel Bilson has sported the Rosario, Jennifer Lopez, Amanda Seyfried, Kerry Washington, and Sophia Bush have all worn the Daphne Bis, and Alexa Chung favors the Nicole heels. Lea Michele, Elisabeth Moss, and Rosario Dawson have also been spotted in the label's styles.

Bionda Castana is joined by several up-and-coming labels attracting attention in the footwear scene. London designer Mo Helmi crafts shoes in the same Italian factory used by brands like Dolce & Gabbana, Bottega Veneta, and Jimmy Choo. Paul Andrew, a British-born, U.S.-based designer, is known for his luxurious, 'sexy without severity' footwear, loved by stars like Keira Knightley and Poppy Delevingne. Sophia Webster, with her vibrant, graphic shoes, received J. Crew's endorsement, including a high-profile collaboration, and awards for emerging talent.

article_content: A New Jersey state appeals court has established that someone who knowingly texts a person they know to be driving could be held liable if a crash occurs as a result. This ruling followed a 2009 accident in which 18-year-old Kyle Best, distracted by a text conversation with his girlfriend, Shannon Colonna, drifted across the center line in his pickup truck and collided head-on with motorcyclists David and Linda Kubert. Both Kuberts sustained catastrophic injuries, with both ultimately losing their legs. The Kuberts sued both Best and Colonna, asserting that Colonna’s texts contributed to the accident by distracting Best. While the court determined that a person can potentially be held liable for texting a driver if they know the recipient is driving, it cleared Colonna of responsibility in this instance, citing a lack of evidence that she knew Best was driving when she sent the texts. The case has triggered considerable public debate over who bears responsibility in such situations. Governor Chris Christie and many citizens argue that drivers themselves must bear full responsibility for their attention on the road. Others worry about the practicality and fairness of extending liability to those sending texts. In response to incidents like the Kuberts’, New Jersey has enacted stricter distracted driving laws, including the 'Kulesh, Kubert and Bolish’s Law,' which treats accidents caused by distracted driving as criminal offenses with significant penalties, including fines up to $150,000 and up to 10 years in prison. Legislation has also been proposed to allow police to examine drivers’ phones if there’s reasonable suspicion of phone use during an accident, a move that has prompted privacy concerns from groups like the ACLU of New Jersey.

Ambos sofreram ferimentos graves, e acabaram perdendo as pernas. Os Kubert processaram Best e Colonna, alegando que as mensagens de Colonna contribuíram para o acidente ao distrair Best. Embora o tribunal tenha entendido que uma pessoa pode ser responsabilizada por enviar mensagens a um motorista se souber que ele está dirigindo, Colonna foi inocentada neste caso, pois não havia provas de que ela soubesse que Best estava ao volante ao enviar as mensagens. O caso gerou um intenso debate público sobre de quem é a responsabilidade em situações assim. O governador Chris Christie e muitos cidadãos afirmam que os próprios motoristas devem ser totalmente responsáveis por manter a atenção ao volante. Outros questionam a praticidade e justiça de responsabilizar quem envia mensagens. Em resposta a casos como o dos Kubert, Nova Jersey endureceu as leis contra o uso do celular ao volante, incluindo a 'Lei Kulesh, Kubert e Bolish', que enquadra acidentes causados por distração ao dirigir como crimes, com multas de até US$ 150 mil e até 10 anos de prisão. Uma nova legislação também foi proposta, permitindo à polícia examinar celulares dos motoristas caso haja suspeita razoável de uso durante o acidente — medida que gerou preocupações de privacidade por entidades como a ACLU de Nova Jersey.

German people are often stereotyped as being the first to reserve sun loungers on holiday and as being very direct, sometimes causing misunderstandings with others. The Goethe Institute, Germany's equivalent of the British Council, has highlighted several reasons that may explain these perceptions.

Known for their punctuality and straightforwardness, Germans sometimes come across as blunt, especially to the British, who may interpret this behavior as rude. The Goethe Institute has produced a video to address these misconceptions and to explain how German customs differ from those of other countries.

In the video, a German man stands upright with documents in hand, while a foreigner—possibly British—is shown in a more relaxed posture. Christine Jansen, from the Goethe Institute's Amsterdam branch, told The Local website: 'We created these films to spark discussion about cultural differences when doing business with Germans.'

She added: 'The filmmakers attribute the German preference for focusing on business matters rather than personal topics to historical factors. The long-standing division of Germany into many smaller states meant Germans often felt surrounded by rivals and developed a reserved demeanor.'

Jansen clarified to The Local that the video's mention of being 'surrounded by enemies' refers to historical periods before World War II, but acknowledged that some viewers criticized this aspect of the video.

article_content: Minneapolis and Saint Paul woke up Halloween morning to a thick layer of snow, marking one of the most significant October snowfalls there in years. According to the National Weather Service, more than 2.5 inches piled up overnight. The area last experienced such a major Halloween snow event in 1991, when a blizzard dumped over 8 inches. The record for October snowfall in Minnesota is 9.3 inches, set three years ago, with nearly 9 inches falling in the Twin Cities at that time. While the snow created a striking blend with Halloween decorations, it caused hazardous conditions for drivers: since midnight, the Minnesota State Patrol recorded 191 crashes statewide, with nine resulting in injuries. Meteorologists say skies should clear later in the day, but temperatures are expected to fall to 24 degrees.

De acordo com o Serviço Nacional de Meteorologia, mais de 6 cm de neve se acumularam durante a noite. A última grande nevasca em um Halloween aconteceu em 1991, quando uma tempestade trouxe mais de 20 cm. O recorde de neve em outubro em Minnesota é de 23,6 cm, registrado há três anos, quando quase 23 cm caíram nas Twin Cities. Apesar da paisagem inusitada formada pela mistura de neve e decorações de Halloween, a situação causou problemas para quem dirigia: desde a meia-noite, a Patrulha Estadual de Minnesota registrou 191 acidentes em todo o estado, sendo nove deles com feridos. Meteorologistas preveem que o tempo deve abrir ao longo do dia, mas as temperaturas devem cair para -4°C.

article_content: When President Joe Biden meets with Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Wednesday, every detail will matter—from how they greet each other to where they sit, and even whether water is served in bottles or glasses. Senior U.S. officials describe the process of managing these diplomatic protocols as 'pretty intense.' High-level meetings between U.S. and Chinese leaders involve meticulous planning, factoring in political and cultural sensitivities. In interactions with China, where etiquette and symbolic gestures carry significant weight, seemingly minor details can take on major importance, especially given the often competing interests of Washington and Beijing. "There is probably very detailed planning regarding who enters the room first, whether there will be photos, and other ceremonial elements," said Bonny Lin, a senior fellow at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. Biden and Xi are scheduled to meet next week during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in San Francisco. So far, basic information—even the meeting's exact date and location—remains undisclosed. The White House, citing security reasons, says only that the meeting will take place 'in the Bay Area.' Such secrecy can heighten the pressure on both delegations as they negotiate details like meeting time, length, seating arrangements, security protocols, and interpreter access. Further, questions remain about the substance of the meeting—whether there will be a joint statement and how much of the talks will be made public. Senior U.S. officials plan to allow time for in-depth conversations, divided into several sessions, reminiscent of the nearly three-hour discussion Biden and Xi had at last year’s G-20 summit in Bali. This marks Xi’s first visit to the United States in six years, and his first visit to San Francisco since his time as a provincial Communist Party secretary. Victor Cha, a former White House official, notes that arranging meetings at APEC is somewhat simpler than hosting at a formal location, but organizing summit discussions on the sidelines still presents logistical challenges. 'China, normally, if they come to United States, they want everything. They want all the pomp and circumstance. They want the highest possible respect,' Cha said. 'That is politically not possible. Having APEC in San Francisco helps solve that, as it’s not hosted by the official White House.' Even relatively informal settings can come with high stakes. When President Richard Nixon visited China in 1972, he wore shoes with rubber soles to climb the Great Wall. In 2013, Barack Obama met with Xi at Sunnylands, California, in a relaxed setting with neither leader wearing a tie—a notable detail at the time. Donald Trump and Xi later dined in dark suits at Mar-a-Lago, with Trump famously praising the 'most beautiful piece of chocolate cake.' Bonnie Glaser of the German Marshall Fund suggests the Chinese delegation likely advocated for a venue distinct from the main APEC site and for longer discussions than those at Bali. 'The Chinese want a separate summit,' she said. Venue matters to China—a setting similar to Sunnylands is preferable to places associated with tense meetings, like Anchorage, Alaska. Even weather can become a symbol for Chinese state media. Early forecasts call for rain and mild temperatures in San Francisco. Floral arrangements are not overlooked. In Chinese culture, certain flowers have specific meanings: plum blossoms represent perseverance, lotuses represent peace, and chrysanthemums are associated with death. Xi may expect Biden to personally greet him upon arrival, and his team may also prefer photos of the two leaders together, without staff, to signal a personal connection. 'Chinese officials want to project to their domestic audience that Xi is received with dignity and respect,' said Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution. This could include imagery beyond a standard handshake—perhaps a walk together or a shared meal. Food can also play a key role in such meetings. During Nixon's visit to China in 1971, a military honor guard welcomed him, and elaborate toasts followed a banquet. In 1989, China honored President George H.W. Bush with a Texas-style barbecue, though they blocked his invitation to dissident Fang Lizhi. A formal dinner is ruled out at APEC, but a lunch is possible, though Xi’s typically tight schedule may not allow time for a meal, as noted in a 2017 Chinese documentary on diplomatic principles. Security concerns are ever present. Barack Obama recalled in his memoir that, during his 2009 China visit, his team was advised to leave non-governmental devices behind and to assume that communications and hotels could be monitored. In 1995, then-First Lady Hillary Clinton’s declaration in Beijing that 'human rights are women’s rights, and women’s rights are human rights' drew global attention. Laura Bush, in 2008, made headlines when she visited a refugee camp for people fleeing Myanmar after a stop in China for the Olympics. But interactions between the U.S. and China don’t always center on security or human rights issues. For example, Obama's daughter Sasha spoke some Mandarin during a 2011 White House reception for then-Chinese President Hu Jintao. During a 2014 goodwill trip to China, Michelle Obama and her daughters engaged in cultural exchanges, such as a toboggan ride on the Great Wall and a ping-pong game—though some observers still described the visit as formal in tone.

Autoridades norte-americanas descrevem o processo de gerenciar esses protocolos diplomáticos como 'bastante intenso'. Reuniões de alto nível entre líderes dos EUA e da China envolvem planejamento meticuloso, levando em conta sensibilidades políticas e culturais. Nas interações com a China, onde etiqueta e gestos simbólicos têm grande peso, detalhes aparentemente pequenos podem ganhar enorme relevância, especialmente considerando os interesses muitas vezes conflitantes de Washington e Pequim. "Provavelmente há um planejamento muito detalhado sobre quem entra primeiro na sala, se haverá fotos, e outros elementos cerimoniais", disse Bonny Lin, pesquisadora sênior do Centro de Estudos Estratégicos e Internacionais (CSIS). Biden e Xi estão programados para se encontrar na próxima semana durante a cúpula da Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico (APEC) em São Francisco. Até agora, informações básicas — até mesmo a data e o local exatos — permanecem em sigilo. A Casa Branca, citando motivos de segurança, diz apenas que a reunião acontecerá 'na Bay Area'. Esse sigilo pode aumentar ainda mais a pressão sobre as delegações enquanto negociam detalhes como horário, duração do encontro, disposição de assentos, protocolos de segurança e acesso a intérpretes. Além disso, dúvidas permanecem quanto ao conteúdo da reunião — se haverá uma declaração conjunta e quanta parte da conversa será pública. Autoridades americanas planejam reservar tempo para conversas aprofundadas, divididas em várias sessões, semelhante ao encontro de quase três horas entre Biden e Xi na cúpula do G-20, em Bali, no ano passado. Esta será a primeira visita de Xi aos Estados Unidos em seis anos, além de sua primeira ida a São Francisco desde quando era secretário provincial do Partido Comunista. Victor Cha, ex-funcionário da Casa Branca, ressalta que organizar encontros na APEC é um pouco mais simples do que em um local oficial, mas discussões paralelas ainda apresentam desafios logísticos. 'A China, normalmente, quando vem aos EUA, quer tudo. Toda a pompa e circunstância. Quer o respeito máximo possível', diz Cha. 'Isso não é politicamente viável. Ter a APEC em São Francisco ajuda a resolver esse ponto, pois não é a Casa Branca que hospeda oficialmente.' Mesmo ambientes informais podem ser de grande importância. Quando o presidente Richard Nixon visitou a China em 1972, usou sapatos com solado de borracha para subir a Grande Muralha. Em 2013, Barack Obama encontrou Xi em Sunnylands, Califórnia, em uma reunião informal e sem gravatas — detalhe marcante na época. Donald Trump e Xi jantaram de terno escuro em Mar-a-Lago, com Trump elogiando o 'pedaço de bolo de chocolate mais bonito'. Bonnie Glaser, do German Marshall Fund, sugere que a delegação chinesa provavelmente buscou um local distinto do principal da APEC e conversas mais duradouras do que as ocorridas em Bali. 'Os chineses querem uma cúpula separada', disse ela. O local é importante para a China — preferem um ambiente similar ao de Sunnylands e evitam lugares associados a reuniões tensas, como Anchorage, no Alasca. Até mesmo o tempo pode virar símbolo na mídia estatal chinesa. As previsões apontam chuva e temperaturas amenas em São Francisco. Arranjos florais também têm significado. Na cultura chinesa, certas flores têm significados distintos: ameixeiras representam perseverança, lótus significa paz e crisântemos estão associados à morte. Xi pode esperar ser recebido pessoalmente por Biden na chegada, e sua equipe pode preferir fotos apenas dos líderes juntos, para mostrar conexão pessoal. 'Os oficiais chineses querem projetar ao público doméstico que Xi foi recebido com dignidade e respeito', explica Ryan Hass, do Instituto Brookings. Isso pode incluir imagens além do aperto de mão tradicional — talvez uma caminhada juntos ou uma refeição. Comida também pode ser protagonista nessas reuniões. Na visita de Nixon à China em 1971, uma guarda de honra militar o recebeu e brindes elaborados vieram após um banquete. Em 1989, a China homenageou o presidente George H.W. Bush com um churrasco ao estilo texano, mas bloqueou o convite ao dissidente Fang Lizhi. Um jantar formal está fora de cogitação na APEC, mas um almoço é possível — embora a apertada agenda de Xi possa não permitir, como mostra um documentário chinês de 2017 sobre princípios diplomáticos. Preocupações de segurança são sempre presentes. Barack Obama recorda em seu livro de memórias que, em sua visita à China em 2009, sua equipe foi orientada a deixar dispositivos não governamentais no avião e assumir que comunicações e hotéis poderiam ser monitorados. Em 1995, a então primeira-dama Hillary Clinton chamou atenção mundial ao declarar em Pequim que 'direitos das mulheres são direitos humanos, e direitos humanos são direitos das mulheres'. Laura Bush, em 2008, ganhou destaque ao visitar um campo de refugiados de Mianmar após passar pela China durante as Olimpíadas. Mas nem toda interação entre EUA e China gira em torno de segurança ou temas de direitos humanos. Por exemplo, Sasha, filha de Obama, falou algumas frases em mandarim durante uma recepção na Casa Branca para Hu Jintao, então presidente chinês, em 2011. The video, shared on Instagram by user @nugget, offers a front-row seat to this natural spectacle as brilliant colors dance across the night sky. The phenomenon occurs when energized particles from the sun collide with Earth's upper atmosphere, creating these mesmerizing waves of light around the Arctic. Throughout the footage, the pilot expertly maneuvers the plane, making viewers feel as though they're racing alongside the aurora. This rare glimpse offers a magical view from cruising altitude—moments typically reserved for pilots flying above the clouds. The immersive video quickly drew admiration on Instagram, with users commenting on the planet’s incredible beauty, expressing they could never tire of such a view, and marveling at the phenomenon.

article_content: Drawing inspiration from the fears sparked by the Ebola outbreak, Dallas-area resident James Faulk decorated his townhouse with a striking Halloween display that resembles a quarantine scene. He arranged barrels marked 'biohazard' around his property, bordered his yard with yellow caution tape, and taped the doors and windows with white 'quarantine' labels. Dressed in a face shield and a white protective suit labeled 'CDC Trainee,' Faulk greeted reporters holding a clipboard and a red bag labeled 'biohazard infectious waste.' Faulk’s decorations are a reference to recent events in Dallas, where official biohazard teams were deployed after Thomas Eric Duncan, the first Ebola patient diagnosed in the U.S., was treated in the city. After Duncan’s death on October 8, two nurses who cared for him were also infected, leading to similar cleanup operations at their homes. Residing in the University Park neighborhood, Faulk explained that he started setting up the decorations the previous Sunday, believing the situation had begun to normalize. He added a 'Happy Halloween' banner to inject a festive touch and said his intention was to amuse and startle neighbors. Some locals, like Jill Grover, initially mistook the setup for an actual emergency but soon recognized the Halloween spirit. However, opinions remain divided, as some believe the theme might be too sensitive for those closely affected by the outbreak. Steve Mace, a spokesman for University Park, noted that while there was only a single complaint, police checked and found no violation of laws. Faulk remains enthusiastic and plans to add more spooky elements, like a mock hospital bed, ahead of Halloween.

Após a morte de Duncan, em 8 de outubro, duas enfermeiras que cuidaram dele também foram infectadas, resultando em operações semelhantes de limpeza nas residências delas. Morador de University Park, Faulk contou que começou a montar as decorações no domingo anterior, acreditando que a situação local já estava começando a normalizar. O porta-voz de University Park, Steve Mace, destacou que só houve uma reclamação, e que a polícia verificou e não encontrou nenhuma violação de leis. Faulk segue empolgado e planeja adicionar mais elementos assustadores, como uma cama de hospital cenográfica, nos próximos dias.

article_content: Deepak Shenoy, founder of Capital Mind, argues that LIC (Life Insurance Corporation) remains an undervalued stock in India. He forecasts profits of over Rs 40,000-42,000 crore for the current quarter, making it attractive with a market capitalization near Rs 400,000 crore. At present, LIC’s shares are priced at around ten times earnings, and this ratio may improve as the company’s participating policy share is set to rise from 7.5% this year to 10% next year. Honasa Consumer’s stock rose sharply following its recent quarterly earnings. There are concerns about additional selling pressure due to potential sales from ESOP (employee stock ownership plan) shares, though Honasa has reportedly denied these expectations. The company posted a Rs 29 crore profit for Q2 and reported strong cash flow, surpassing profits during the first half of the year. Nevertheless, liquidity challenges persist as more shares could enter the market, particularly given the lack of lock-in periods for ESOP-related sales. Shenoy suggests adopting a cautious stance until Honasa sustains its profitability over time. BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange) has seen increasing trading volumes, thanks in part to the popularity of zero day to expiry options—a trend gaining traction both globally and in India. BSE initially reduced transaction fees to gain market share, and with demand growing, it has started raising fees again, which should strengthen future earnings. Additionally, with exchange-level management of broker funds, float income for BSE is expected to rise. While BSE shares have already doubled in value, Shenoy believes there is further room for growth but warns of volatility. Shenoy also highlights opportunities in the two-wheeler sector. If rural demand improves post-elections—supported by anticipated cash flow into rural areas—major players like Hero MotoCorp and Eicher could benefit as sales potentially recover to pre-pandemic levels. Early signs show improvement, though full recovery is still pending. In broader market developments, the Nifty index broke past 20,000 on positive investor sentiment as US rate hike concerns eased. Regulatory actions remain in focus: Byju’s is under scrutiny by the Enforcement Directorate for not submitting required documentation and for delays in realizing export proceeds, while the HCL Group is making progress towards establishing a semiconductor assembly and testing (OSAT) unit in Karnataka.

Mike Johnson, recently elected as Speaker of the House, has a documented record of making anti-LGBTQ+ statements. In a 2004 editorial published in The Times, a newspaper in his hometown of Shreveport, Louisiana, Johnson described homosexuality as a 'dark harbinger of chaos and sexual anarchy,' according to CNN. In another editorial in the same publication, also highlighted by CNN, he referred to homosexuality as an 'inherently unnatural' and 'dangerous lifestyle,' calling it a threat to 'the entire democratic system.' Johnson wrote, 'If everyone does what is right in his own eyes, chaos and sexual anarchy will result.'

In a 2005 editorial, Johnson expressed strong opposition to including sexual orientation and gender identity in Shreveport’s employment discrimination laws, arguing it was 'unnecessary.' He wrote, 'Your race, creed, and sex are what you are, while homosexuality and cross-dressing are things you do,' adding, 'This is a free country, but we don't give special protections for every person's bizarre choices.'

Throughout his career as a lawyer, Johnson has opposed LGBTQ+ rights legislation. He served as an attorney for the Alliance Defense Fund, now known as Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF), a Christian law firm advocating for religious freedom, free speech, marriage and family, parental rights, and the sanctity of life, according to its website. The Southern Poverty Law Center classified ADF as an anti-LGBTQ+ hate group in 2016, citing its support for recriminalizing sexual acts between consenting LGBTQ+ adults and state-sanctioned sterilization of trans people, among other reasons.

While at ADF, Johnson wrote an amicus brief opposing the 2003 US Supreme Court decision Lawrence v. Texas, which decriminalized same-sex relationships, as revealed by CNN. In an editorial for The Times, he wrote, 'Make no mistake, the Lawrence decision opens the door to the undermining of many important laws and is ultimately a strategic first shot for the homosexual lobby's ultimate prize — the redefinition of marriage.' Johnson also defended Louisiana’s statewide ban on same-sex marriages in court the following year.

In 2005, Johnson and ADF organized the 'Day of Truth,' a counterprotest to the Day of Silence demonstrations against anti-gay prejudice in schools, according to the Associated Press. In 2015, he founded Freedom Guard, a nonprofit legal ministry aimed at supporting churches and pursuing religious liberty cases nationwide, as reported by The Bridge, a religious community magazine.

Since becoming a congressman for Louisiana in 2016, Johnson has repeatedly voted against bipartisan efforts to codify same-sex marriage, attempted to overturn the Supreme Court’s 2015 decision in Obergefell v. Hodges legalizing such marriages, and introduced the 'Stop the Sexualization of Children Act of 2022.' As Speaker of the House, Johnson now holds significant influence over President Joe Biden’s legislative agenda and the broader direction of the GOP, as noted by the BBC. Johnson’s office did not respond to Insider’s request for comment.

The UK government has acknowledged spending £25 million each year to keep foreign prisoners in custody after they have completed their sentences because they cannot be deported. Recent figures show that nearly 1,000 overseas offenders remain behind bars post-sentence, largely due to legal barriers including human rights laws. Immigration Minister Mark Harper stated that, on average, these individuals spend almost nine months in the UK after serving their time. Ten have been held for over five years.

Justice Secretary Chris Grayling has criticized human rights legislation for restricting the government’s ability to deport foreign criminals. He has suggested that the Conservative party's election manifesto will propose scrapping the Human Rights Act and replacing it with a British Bill of Rights. Officials report that offenders—among them individuals convicted of serious crimes—cannot be easily deported due to protections such as the right to family life under existing laws.

The cost to taxpayers is around £30,000 annually per offender, totalling £25 million each year. This situation has led to criticism from Conservative MPs and accusations of incompetence from Labour, with the number of foreign offenders awaiting deportation rising from 491 to 850 since the Coalition government took office. 

Conservative MP Dominic Raab denounced the situation, arguing that failing to deport dangerous individuals poses unnecessary risks. Labour’s shadow justice secretary, Sadiq Khan, highlighted the issue of overcrowded prisons and blamed the government for inadequate action, stating that 850 foreign offenders are occupying prison space that could be freed through proper deportation procedures.

To address the issue, ministers are introducing legislation to ensure criminals are deported first, with appeals heard in their home countries—an effort to streamline what is seen as an overly complex system. Conservatives are also expected to promise to replace the Human Rights Act in their 2015 manifesto. Under current rules, EU offenders sentenced to two years or more (or one year for drug or sexual offenses) are eligible for deportation.

A Home Office spokesperson emphasized that staying in the UK obliges individuals to respect the law, and the government aims to align removals with the completion of sentences. Detentions may be extended when individuals refuse to cooperate or when obtaining travel documentation presents challenges. The government claims that the new Immigration Act will reduce appeal rights and make it easier to deport those with no right to remain.

article_content: Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart is on the verge of signing a new contract with the Premier League champions. Manager Manuel Pellegrini has indicated that the England number one is ready to commit his future to the club, with an agreement potentially finalized within the next day. The 27-year-old Hart has reportedly been in contract discussions with Manchester City since the summer. His existing deal, believed to be worth £80,000 per week, expires in summer 2016. Hart, a former Shrewsbury trainee, has delivered impressive performances this season, reaffirming his status as first-choice for club and country after losing his place last year. Pellegrini told reporters on Friday ahead of City's home game against Everton: 'I always said it is important for this club to keep Joe with us. He is not only a very good goalkeeper, but also a key figure in the squad. You might have good news within the next day.' While Hart lost his starting spot to Costel Pantilimon in October 2013 after a series of errors, he regained his role in December, though continued to miss domestic cup matches. Since then, Hart's strong form has prompted City’s efforts to renew his contract and secure his long-term future at the Etihad, amid interest from other clubs. Pellegrini added competition for Hart by bringing in Argentinian goalkeeper Willy Caballero from Malaga last summer. Despite the added rivalry, Hart has performed admirably, with Pellegrini praising both goalkeepers: 'Joe is having a very good season. The arrival of Willy Caballero was very important for the club and for everyone – he’s an excellent goalkeeper. Strong competition brings out the best in players, and I’m very happy about that.' Meanwhile, Manchester City will be without their influential captain, Vincent Kompany, for the upcoming Premier League match against Everton. Kompany, who missed the recent trip to Sunderland due to a hamstring injury, faces a race to recover in time for next week’s decisive Champions League clash against Roma. Kompany, aged 28, has struggled with various muscular problems in recent seasons, missing games due to calf, thigh, and groin issues. Pellegrini acknowledged Kompany's aggressive style can make him more susceptible to injuries, but remains optimistic: 'Vincent plays with full intensity every match and trains the same way. We hope, as last season, he’ll manage these injuries. They’re significant, but not long-term problems.'

Amid ongoing instability, 14-year-old Mizune stands out among thousands of Syrian refugees who have fled their homeland since the outbreak of civil war. For Mizune, education is essential to a better future. In the Za'atari refugee camp in Jordan, where her family settled after fleeing Syria, she works hard to highlight the importance of schooling. She spends her days going through the camp, speaking to both children and parents in tents and mosques, enthusiastically sharing why returning to the classroom matters.

Mizune, whose last name is withheld for privacy, is determined her actions will have real impact. “Raising awareness about education is essential,” she says. Some in the camp call her the 'Malala of Za'atari,' referencing Malala Yousafzai, the Pakistani activist celebrated for defending girls’ right to education after surviving an attack. The two became friends—spending significant time together during Malala’s visit to Za'atari in February, united in their passion for educational rights.

Mizune’s advocacy began when UNICEF started building schools in the camp, motivating her to get involved. She believes reaching parents is crucial since their attitudes influence whether children attend school. Despite differing opinions, she and fellow advocates have convinced many families—now about 70% of camp children are enrolled in classes.

According to UNICEF’s Michele Servadei, parents’ reluctance is a major hurdle. Many hope to return to Syria soon and feel schooling is unnecessary in the meantime.

The Syrian conflict, which began with protests against President Bashar al-Assad, has led to widespread violence and the displacement of millions. As of February, the UN estimates 2.6 million Syrian refugees have sought shelter in neighboring countries. Za'atari, now the world’s second-largest refugee camp, houses up to 150,000 people and faces ongoing challenges such as water shortages, overcrowding, and harsh winters.

Despite these difficulties and the continuing uncertainty in Syria, Mizune—who dreams of one day becoming a journalist—remains hopeful. She encourages her peers to value education, believing that their perseverance can help create a brighter future for their country.

Sanjay Nayar, the former CEO and chairman of KKR India and founder of Sorin Investments, is expanding into the climate technology sector. Nayar is joining Peak Ventures, a Mumbai-based venture capital firm specializing in cleantech areas like new energy, food systems, clean water, and broader climate solutions, as a general partner.

Peak Ventures manages an early-stage fund of approximately $150 million, which is expected to accelerate its fundraising following Nayar’s appointment, according to managing partner Samir Shah. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has approved Nayar’s induction as general partner. Shah highlighted that Nayar’s involvement will help the firm scale more rapidly and expand into later-stage climate tech startups. Additionally, Nayar's expertise is seen as crucial for building a large institutional fund, enabling larger investments and enhancing decision-making quality.

Peak Ventures intends to invest in 18-20 early-stage startups, primarily in India, with average investment sizes between $2 million and $5 million. The firm is also open to supporting foreign startups developing scalable technologies suitable for the Indian market, targeting a 75:25 investment split between Indian and global companies. Peak’s partners, Samir Shah and Aakash Shah, have personally invested in climate tech firms like Waaree Energies and VA Tech Wabag. Erik Solheim, former Norwegian environment minister and executive director of the United Nations Environment Programme, has joined Peak Ventures’ advisory board.

The Peak Ventures Sustainability Fund-I will officially launch with six warehoused investments—pre-existing investments being added to the new fund.

While entering climatetech is new territory for Nayar, his Sorin Investments fund has concentrated on technology sectors such as SaaS, edtech, fintech, and logistics. Sorin’s investors include KKR co-founders Henry Kravis and George Roberts, Hero Enterprises chairman Sunil Kant Munjal, and notable Indian family offices. Recent reports confirm that SIDBI and NSIC are expected to invest around Rs 300 crore in Sorin, with the fund expected to close at Rs 1,300 crore.

As a general partner at Peak Ventures, Nayar will have fiduciary responsibility and a more active role than before, representing his family office’s shift toward specialized cleantech investments. Peak Ventures also plans to raise capital from institutions such as development finance entities and sovereign wealth funds.

Indian Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal is on a four-day visit to the United States, aiming to strengthen trade and investment ties. After arriving in San Francisco on November 13, Goyal met with US Trade Representative Katherine Tai to discuss deepening bilateral trade, investment relations, and convergence on key WTO issues before the 13th WTO Ministerial Conference in Abu Dhabi next February.

Goyal also met Dukgeun Ahn, Korea's Minister of Trade, and Gan Kim Yong, Singapore's Minister of Trade and Industry. These discussions took place alongside the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF) and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meetings in San Francisco, where ministers explored regional economic collaboration opportunities.

According to India’s Ministry of Commerce, Goyal urged his Singaporean and South Korean counterparts to expedite the review and conclusion of free trade agreements. He also joined an investors’ round table with venture capitalists and entrepreneurs from sectors such as energy, manufacturing, logistics, and technology.

Recent data indicates Indian exports to the US dropped to $38.28 billion during April-September 2023 from $41.49 billion a year earlier, while imports fell to $21.39 billion from $25.79 billion. Economists polled by The Economic Times forecast India’s GDP will grow by 6.7% in the July-September quarter, driven mainly by the services sector.

India is considering increasing the GST evasion decriminalization threshold to ₹3 crore from ₹2 crore to reduce harassment and improve the business environment. Meanwhile, Indian telecom operators and device makers have expressed reservations about introducing technology to beam TV content directly to mobile devices without cellular data connections, citing the technology’s immaturity.

article_content: In recent months, there has been growing attention on youth crime in Australia, especially in Queensland, where public protests and advocacy groups such as Voice for Victims have pushed for tougher government action. Concerns about a perceived 'youth crime crisis' have driven political debate. But is there truly a crisis? The answer depends on definitions and data. The minimum age of criminal responsibility is 10 in all states and territories, except for the Northern Territory, which recently raised it to 12. Children aged 10 to 13 can only be prosecuted if it's proven they understood what they were doing was seriously wrong. Victorian data show that from 2014 to 2023, youth crime incidents generally trended downward, despite some fluctuation. However, there was a 24% rise in incidents involving offenders under 17 between 2021-22 and 2022-23. In New South Wales, police actions against 10-17-year-olds declined from 2011 to 2022, but between 2021 and 2022, there was a 7% increase in police proceedings and an 11% rise in court cases for more serious youth offenses. The 2021-22 Queensland Crime Report recorded a 13.7% increase in youth offenders compared to the previous year, reaching 52,742—the highest in a decade. Despite recent increases, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports a downward or steady longer-term trend in most states and territories; only the Northern Territory saw a notable recent rise (13%). The ABS measures unique youth offenders, not repeat offenses, but its recidivism data show increases in repeated police actions against youth in several regions. In 2021-22, nearly half of all youth crimes in Queensland were committed by serious repeat offenders. Common offenses included theft, break and enter, and car theft, with youth accounting for more than half of all offenders in these categories. Vehicle thefts by youth nearly doubled from 2012 to 2022. In NSW, theft, break and enter, and stalking or harassment were the most common youth offenses in 2022, with significant increases over 2021. In Victoria, crimes against the person, property offenses, and public order offenses also rose notably in 2022-23. Public perception greatly influences the definition of a crisis. Surveys show many Queenslanders feel youth crime is rising or at a crisis point, with most taking steps to improve home security. Still, most people feel safe at home at night. Queensland has responded to public concern by introducing stricter measures, including detaining youth offenders in police watchhouses and temporarily overriding its Human Rights Act due to capacity issues in youth detention centers. Advocates argue these facilities are unsuitable for children, as they may be housed with adults and often lack adequate facilities. While immediate measures address safety fears, experts stress the importance of tackling underlying issues—like school disengagement, drug use, domestic violence, and poor parenting—to reduce youth crime over the long term.

A idade mínima de responsabilidade criminal é de 10 anos em todos os estados e territórios, exceto no Território do Norte, que recentemente elevou para 12 anos. Crianças de 10 a 13 anos só podem ser processadas se for comprovado que entendiam que o que faziam era gravemente errado. Dados de Victoria mostram que, de 2014 a 2023, os incidentes de crimes juvenis tiveram tendência geral de queda, apesar de algumas variações. No entanto, houve um aumento de 24% nos incidentes envolvendo infratores com menos de 17 anos entre 2021-22 e 2022-23. Em Nova Gales do Sul, as ações policiais contra jovens de 10 a 17 anos caíram de 2011 a 2022, mas entre 2021 e 2022 houve aumento de 7% nos procedimentos policiais e de 11% nas ações judiciais por crimes mais graves. O Relatório de Crimes de Queensland de 2021-22 registrou aumento de 13,7% entre jovens infratores em relação ao ano anterior, chegando a 52.742 — maior número em dez anos. Apesar dos aumentos recentes, o Australian Bureau of Statistics aponta tendência de queda ou estabilidade no longo prazo na maioria dos estados e territórios; apenas o Território do Norte teve aumento significativo recente (13%). O ABS conta infratores jovens únicos, não reincidentes, mas dados mostram crescimento de reincidência juvenil em diversas regiões. Em 2021-22 em Queensland, quase metade dos crimes juvenis foi cometida por reincidentes graves. Os delitos mais frequentes foram furto, arrombamento e roubo de veículos, com jovens respondendo por mais da metade dos envolvidos nessas categorias. O furto de veículos por jovens quase dobrou de 2012 a 2022. Em NSW, furto, arrombamento e perseguição/assédio foram crimes juvenis mais comuns em 2022, com aumentos significativos em relação a 2021. Em Victoria, crimes contra a pessoa, contra o patrimônio e de ordem pública também subiram em 2022-23. A percepção pública influencia fortemente o conceito de crise. Pesquisas mostram que muitos habitantes de Queensland sentem que o crime juvenil está aumentando ou num ponto crítico, e a maioria reforçou a segurança de casa. Ainda assim, a maioria das pessoas relata se sentir segura em casa durante a noite. Queensland respondeu à preocupação pública adotando medidas mais rígidas, como deter jovens infratores em celas da polícia e suspender temporariamente sua Lei de Direitos Humanos devido à superlotação nos centros de detenção juvenil. Defensores dizem que essas instalações são inadequadas para menores, pois podem ser mantidos com adultos e muitas vezes carecem de estrutura apropriada. article_content: BEIJING — China and the United States have pledged to step up their efforts to fight climate change ahead of a major United Nations conference, agreeing to reduce emissions of methane and other greenhouse gases in addition to carbon dioxide. The joint announcement was made just before a summit between Presidents Joe Biden and Xi Jinping, aimed at stabilizing the often tense U.S.-China relationship. Cooperation between the world's two largest emitters of greenhouse gases is seen as critical to the success of the upcoming UN climate talks in Dubai. Earlier this year, it was uncertain whether the two governments would collaborate, due to heightened tensions over issues such as technology, Taiwan, and Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Both countries acknowledged the significant roles they play and, in a joint statement released on Wednesday in Beijing and Tuesday evening in Washington, vowed to work together to address one of humanity’s greatest challenges. They also reaffirmed a G20 pledge, of which both nations are members, to work toward tripling global renewable energy capacity by 2030. Chinese companies are seeking opportunities to export wind and solar equipment, after significant investments in their manufacturing. "If the two countries can cooperate to build support for this target, it could greatly increase its chances of adoption," said Lauri Myllyvirta, lead analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air. The U.S. and China agreed to resume discussions on energy policies and establish a working group to enhance climate action during what they called "the critical decade of the 2020s." Experts say immediate action is needed for any hope of achieving the internationally agreed goal of keeping the average global temperature rise well below 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 Fahrenheit). A climate expert noted that both countries’ commitment to include methane reductions in their next climate action plans is "a major step forward." "Methane was notably absent from China’s previous commitments under the 2015 Paris Agreement," said David Waskow, International Climate Director at the World Resources Institute. He pointed out that China is the world’s largest methane emitter, and that substantial action to reduce these emissions is crucial for slowing near-term global warming. Last week, the Chinese government released an action plan to control methane emissions, including measures to develop a reporting and accounting system. Major sources of emissions include coal mines, oil and gas fields, agriculture, landfills, and sewage treatment plants. Myllyvirta remarked that the plan is general and lacks specific emission targets, so future monitoring will be important. The U.S. and China also announced plans to co-host a meeting on methane and other greenhouse gases with the United Arab Emirates at the U.N. talks in Dubai. Waskow expressed disappointment that the joint statement did not commit to phasing out fossil fuels. This was unsurprising to some — although China has rapidly expanded wind and solar power, it continues to encourage the construction of coal power plants, which it sees as a more reliable power source during peak demand periods. The government announced last week that it will begin making "capacity payments" next year to coal plant operators to keep them ready for use, even as revenues decline due to increased renewable energy output. The U.S.-China statement welcomed climate cooperation between states, provinces, and cities, and said that a high-level event on this theme would be held in the first half of 2024. Last month, California Governor Gavin Newsom visited China to promote joint climate efforts in various regions. ___ Associated Press researcher Yu Bing in Beijing contributed to this report. ___ Follow AP’s climate and environment coverage at https://apnews.com/hub/climate-and-environment
translated_content: PEQUIM — China e Estados Unidos se comprometeram a intensificar seus esforços no combate às mudanças climáticas antes de uma importante conferência das Nações Unidas, concordando em reduzir as emissões de metano e outros gases de efeito estufa além do dióxido de carbono. O anúncio conjunto foi feito pouco antes de uma cúpula entre os presidentes Joe Biden e Xi Jinping, que visa estabilizar o relacionamento frequentemente tenso entre os dois países. A cooperação entre os dois maiores emissores de gases de efeito estufa do mundo é vista como fundamental para o sucesso das próximas negociações climáticas da ONU em Dubai. No início deste ano, havia incerteza sobre a colaboração entre os governos, devido a tensões em questões como tecnologia, Taiwan e a invasão russa da Ucrânia. Ambos reconheceram os papéis significativos que desempenham e, em comunicado conjunto divulgado na quarta-feira em Pequim e na noite de terça em Washington, prometeram trabalhar juntos para enfrentar um dos maiores desafios da humanidade. Eles também reafirmaram um compromisso assumido no G20, do qual ambos fazem parte, de trabalhar para triplicar a capacidade global de energia renovável até 2030. Empresas chinesas buscam exportar equipamentos de energia eólica e solar após investimentos massivos em sua fabricação. "Se os dois países conseguirem cooperar para fortalecer o apoio a essa meta, as chances de adoção aumentam consideravelmente", disse Lauri Myllyvirta, principal analista do Centro de Pesquisa em Energia e Ar Limpo. Os EUA e a China concordaram em retomar discussões sobre políticas energéticas e criar um grupo de trabalho para impulsionar ações climáticas durante o que chamam de "a década crítica de 2020". Especialistas alertam que ações imediatas são necessárias para alcançar a meta internacional de limitar o aumento médio da temperatura global bem abaixo de 2 graus Celsius (3,6 Fahrenheit). Um especialista em clima destacou que o compromisso dos dois países de incluir reduções de metano em seus próximos planos de ação é "um passo importante". "O metano estava ausente dos compromissos anteriores da China sob o Acordo de Paris de 2015", disse David Waskow, diretor internacional de clima do World Resources Institute. Ele ressaltou que a China é a maior emissora mundial de metano e que ações concretas para reduzir esse gás são essenciais para desacelerar o aquecimento global no curto prazo. Semana passada, o governo chinês lançou um plano de ação para controlar as emissões de metano, incluindo medidas para criar um sistema de relatórios e contabilização. As principais fontes de emissões incluem minas de carvão, campos de petróleo e gás, agricultura, aterros sanitários e estações de tratamento de esgoto. Myllyvirta observou que o plano é genérico e carece de metas específicas, portanto, o acompanhamento futuro será fundamental. EUA e China também anunciaram planos de co-organizar uma reunião sobre metano e outros gases do efeito estufa com os Emirados Árabes Unidos durante as negociações da ONU em Dubai. Waskow demonstrou decepção pelo comunicado conjunto não incluir o compromisso de eliminação de combustíveis fósseis. Isso não surpreende alguns — embora a China tenha expandido rapidamente a energia eólica e solar, continua incentivando a construção de usinas a carvão, consideradas fonte confiável para períodos de alta demanda. O governo anunciou na semana passada que começará a fazer "pagamentos por capacidade" no próximo ano a operadores de usinas a carvão para mantê-las disponíveis, mesmo com a redução nas receitas devido ao aumento das renováveis. O comunicado EUA-China destacou a cooperação climática entre estados, províncias e cidades, e afirmou que haverá um evento de alto nível sobre o tema no primeiro semestre de 2024. No mês passado, o governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom, visitou a China para promover esforços conjuntos em várias regiões. ___ A pesquisadora da Associated Press, Yu Bing, em Pequim, contribuiu para este relatório. ___ Acompanhe a cobertura da AP sobre clima e meio ambiente em https://apnews.com/hub/climate-and-environment

article_content: A Stone Age door in remarkable condition has been unearthed in central Zurich, according to a city official on Friday. The artifact—estimated to be over 5,000 years old—was discovered during an archaeological dig ahead of constructing a parking lot for the Zurich Opera. "It is one of the oldest doors ever found in Europe," said Niels Bleicher, chief scientist at the Zurich Monument Preservation Department. Currently, the door remains in situ, but workers plan to lift it out next week. Bleicher explained the door would then be stabilized, preserved, and likely exhibited in a museum. Measuring about 1.5 meters tall, the door is associated with the Horgen archaeological culture and dates back to the late 4th millennium B.C. “It’s crafted from poplar wood, with a sturdy technique and design," Bleicher noted. "The condition is exceptional—even the wooden handles have survived."
