Atualmente, a porta permanece no local, mas trabalhadores planejam retirá-la na próxima semana. Bleicher explicou que a porta será estabilizada, preservada e provavelmente exibida em um museu. Medindo cerca de 1,5 metro de altura, a porta está associada à cultura arqueológica de Horgen e data do final do 4º milênio a.C. "É feita de madeira de álamo, com técnica e design robustos", destacou Bleicher. "A condição é excepcional — até mesmo as maçanetas de madeira foram preservadas."

article_content: Divorce can be a turbulent time, but one luxury resort in upstate New York is offering an alternative: comfort and convenience. Gideon Putnam Resort & Spa in Saratoga Springs, previously known for lavish weddings, is now offering $5,000 weekend divorce packages designed for couples looking to part ways amicably. For the price, soon-to-be ex-spouses can enjoy spa treatments, tennis, hiking, swimming, golf, and ice skating, all while working with attorneys and mediators provided by the hotel. The 'Divorce Hotel' has two main criteria: participants must be U.S. citizens and must agree to use the hotel’s legal and mediation services. Couples stay in separate rooms and share a suite for mediation sessions to finalize the details of their divorce. By the end of the weekend, agreements are signed and sent to a judge for final approval. The process may also be filmed as part of a reality show produced by A. Smith and Co., the production company behind Gordon Ramsay’s 'Kitchen Nightmares'. Jim Halfens, the program’s founder who has run similar projects in the Netherlands, expects to launch the service by the end of September. Rob Sgarlata, a hotel representative, says the goal is to create a supportive environment that minimizes the stress of the situation. 'We welcome all kinds of guests,' he adds. Sgarlata notes that weddings and divorces will be held in different areas of the hotel to avoid overlap and ensure privacy for all guests.

article_content: The FBI announced Tuesday that it will review the April 2009 beating of a man by Denver police officers, following a request from Denver Mayor John Hickenlooper. The incident previously resulted in disciplinary action against two officers, but no criminal charges were filed. Mayor Hickenlooper stated that a federal investigation would help ensure justice is properly served. The FBI said its Denver office will conduct a review to determine if there is a basis for a federal civil rights investigation, but declined to discuss ongoing investigative matters. According to documents released by Denver officials, one officer received a three-day suspension and another was docked a day's pay due to the incident. Hickenlooper acknowledged that the video footage of the incident 'does not look good when viewed in isolation,' but said it only shows part of the story. The officers were disciplined for filing false reports, following a review by the city's manager of safety, Ron Perea. Perea maintained in a letter that the false statements were more a result of misperception than intentional deception. Despite this, Richard Rosenthal, the independent police monitor, called for the officers to be fired, stating they tried to cover up the incident. Michael DeHerrera, the man shown in the video being subdued and struck by police, also demanded the officers' termination and potential prosecution, arguing that anyone else would have faced jail time if they behaved similarly. Surveillance footage from a street camera captured the incident, showing DeHerrera speaking on a mobile phone as officers subdued his friend, who was being arrested after allegedly punching an off-duty officer at a bar. DeHerrera's father, Anthony DeHerrera, a sheriff's deputy in Pueblo County, Colorado, criticized the police response, saying better methods could have been used. He recounted hearing sirens and then a thud while on the phone with his son during the incident. Michael DeHerrera sustained a bloody nose and a cut above his left eye. He admitted to grabbing officers who were struggling with his friend, but denied punching anyone. Witness statements indicated both DeHerrera and his friend shoved a police officer out of camera range. Manager of safety Perea concluded that, while debate exists about the amount of force used, there was insufficient evidence to prove excessive force. Charges against DeHerrera and his friend were dropped, and both received a settlement from the city. Mayor Hickenlooper, now a gubernatorial candidate, said an independent review was appropriate and emphasized Denver's system of checks and balances. He reaffirmed the city's request for a federal review of the incident. CNN's Jim Spellman contributed to this report.

Hickenlooper afirmou que uma investigação federal ajudaria a garantir que a justiça seja feita de forma adequada. O FBI informou que seu escritório em Denver fará uma análise para determinar se há fundamento para uma investigação federal de direitos civis, mas se recusou a comentar casos em andamento. Jade Beall, a photographer based in Tucson, Arizona, faced the removal of one of her breastfeeding photos from Facebook. The image, part of her fifteen-year work documenting women’s bodies, featured seven mothers nursing with nearly all explicit parts blurred. However, after male users reported the image—and one unblurred nipple was noticed—Facebook took the photo down. Beall recalls that most negative messages urging her to delete it came from men who deemed it offensive.

Her journey began after she took self-portraits of herself breastfeeding post-childbirth, an experience that motivated her to celebrate mothers’ diverse and natural bodies. She published ‘A Beautiful Body Project’ last year, compiling authentic portraits and real-life accounts from women combating insecurity and striving for self-acceptance in a critical society.

Beall says she wasn’t shocked by the backlash, noting that social media seems to impose harsher rules on women’s nudity than men’s. She hopes to shift the public dialogue to embrace, not shame, female bodies—especially those changed by motherhood—and challenge the idea that these forms are objectionable or unhealthy.

The book was funded by a successful Kickstarter campaign with support from donors and volunteers. In interviews with outlets such as Cosmopolitan and the Huffington Post, Beall discussed the prevalent issue of women feeling undeserving of being called beautiful—feelings often worsened by society’s critical view toward mothers who don’t rapidly “bounce back” after giving birth. She stresses that this attitude can undermine women’s confidence and make the already tough journey of motherhood even harder.

article_content: For two years, nine-year-old Ben Baddeley, who has cerebral palsy, dreamed of a life-changing operation that would enable him to play football with his younger brother. After enduring extensive preparation for the surgery, Ben’s hopes were dashed when the NHS cancelled the procedure just weeks before it was due. His mother, Amy Baddeley, received a letter from Queen’s Medical Centre in Nottingham explaining that cuts had made the £20,000 surgery 'unfundable' by the NHS.  Amy, of Silverdale, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Staffordshire, described how devastated Ben was by the news. 'He loves football. He just wanted to kick a ball with his brother without being in agony.' Despite teaching himself to walk, Ben's condition causes him significant pain, and his mobility is expected to worsen, potentially leaving him reliant on a wheelchair and unable to play with his five-year-old brother, Josh.  For the past two years, doctors assured the family that Ben was on the waiting list for the operation, urging them to prepare for surgery. When the cancellation letter arrived, Amy said, 'I felt like I had let my little boy down.'  The family expressed frustration that the NHS would reduce funding for operations that could give children like Ben a brighter future, yet continue to fund elective procedures such as gastric bands and breast implants. The Baddeleys, who have helped Ben prepare for the operation since 2012, are now considering legal action against Nottingham University Hospitals Trust for the short-notice cancellation.  Before the operation, Ben underwent a one-hour MRI scan under general anaesthetic and had stopped his regular Botox injections, which help relieve muscle stiffness. Families were informed earlier this year of impending cuts, but the NHS promised to honor procedures with set dates. Although Ben's pre-operation baclofen treatment was booked, his main surgery had not been scheduled, prompting the trust to cancel both procedures and leaving the family to bear the costs.  Amy and her husband Gary, a 37-year-old welder, now need to raise £11,400 to fund Ben's operation privately.  James Hunter, clinical director for the musculoskeletal directorate at Nottingham University Hospitals, stated: 'We have been in contact with parents of children referred to NUH to inform them we will not be proceeding with any further pre-operative tests. It would be unfair on these children and their families for us to continue a process which may not result in surgery.'  The NHS reportedly performs around 5,400 gastric bypasses and 1,300 gastric band procedures each year, and in 2012 it spent £3.5 million on 790 breast implant operations.  To help Ben, visit www.justgiving.com/yimby/benpainfreeforlife.

The UFC women’s bantamweight championship has been vacant since Amanda Nunes announced her retirement after defending the title against Irene Aldana at UFC 289 on June 10, 2023. The 135-pound belt will have a new champion at UFC 297, where Mayra Bueno Silva faces Raquel Pennington on January 20, 2024, in Toronto. The event is expected to be streamed via ESPN+ pay-per-view.

Amanda Nunes, during her illustrious career, secured the bantamweight belt in July 2016 and held it until December 2021, with notable victories over fighters like Miesha Tate, Ronda Rousey, and Holly Holm. Her reign ended at UFC 269 when Julianna Pena submitted her, but Nunes won the title back from Pena in July 2022 and later defended it successfully against Aldana. Nunes was also the women’s featherweight champion from December 2018 until her 2023 retirement, earning that belt with an impressive knockout of Cris Cyborg and successfully defending it twice.

Currently ranked No. 3 in the bantamweight division, 32-year-old Brazilian Mayra Bueno Silva enters UFC 297 with a record of 3-0 (1 no contest). She recently defeated Holm via submission in July, but that win was overturned and declared a no contest due to Bueno Silva testing positive for a prescribed, but undisclosed, ADHD medication. Her suspension ended on November 29.

Raquel Pennington, ranked No. 2, will be making her second attempt at the bantamweight title. The 35-year-old previously faced Nunes for the belt at UFC 224 in May 2018, losing by TKO in the fifth round. Pennington is currently on a five-fight winning streak, with her most recent victory being a split-decision over Ketlen Vieira in January 2023.

AG Fight first reported the news of this matchup, which was confirmed by MMA Fighting. UFC 297 will be the organization’s first return to Toronto since UFC 231 in December 2018. The venue for the event has not yet been announced.

article_content: Satellite imagery has become a vital resource for verifying information in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict, especially as disinformation spreads. Commercial satellite companies find themselves at the center of debate over how they operate and distribute sensitive images in conflict zones. U.S. companies are subject to the Kyl-Bingaman Amendment (KBA), which limits the resolution of satellite images of Israel and its occupied territories to no higher than what is commercially available from non-U.S. sources. For many years, this meant U.S. companies offered less detailed images compared to rivals like Airbus in Europe. In 2020, the U.S. eased these restrictions, dropping the minimum pixel size from 2 meters to 40 centimeters. This adjustment came after recognition that international providers were already supplying much sharper images. Some Israeli officials voiced concerns about the increased detail, preferring less precise imagery. The revision has been advantageous for researchers, offering better visibility into Israel and narrowing the gap between U.S. and foreign imagery. Still, experts note the landscape will keep evolving as technologies improve globally, and the existence of the KBA remains evidence of the U.S. treating Israel differently in policy. During the current conflict, companies like Planet Labs changed how they share images. Instead of publishing every image instantly, Planet now provides select high-resolution images to the media and aid organizations, aiming to prevent their misuse in the conflict. Despite allegations that companies are hiding or altering images, company representatives and independent experts affirm that imagery remains authentic and unmanipulated. Responsible handling of sensitive data is viewed positively, and even if restrictions are applied, alternative sources—including Iranian and Chinese satellites—remain available. As high-quality satellite imagery becomes more accessible, it isn't only governments using it. NGOs, news outlets, and researchers routinely rely on these images to monitor everything from disasters to military actions. The cost to access this data varies depending on the needs and extent of use. Each provider brings different strengths—Planet targets frequent, global imaging; Maxar offers high-powered, less frequent images. The largest customers tend to be governments and defense agencies, some of whom secure exclusive image rights in certain cases. With advanced satellite technology expanding globally, it’s harder for any single entity to restrict access by buying all images. Analysts stress the importance of transparency in how images are sourced and shared, as the risks of censorship or manipulation by some states grow.

article_content: Amazon’s journey toward drone delivery is progressing, with a new milestone: customers in College Station, Texas, can now receive prescription medications from Amazon via drone. Announced Wednesday, this service is available to Amazon Pharmacy customers through Prime Air. The drones deliver medication in under an hour after an order is placed. Amazon says it can fulfill 500 different medications, treating conditions such as flu, pneumonia, and asthma. Packages are prepared by Amazon pharmacists and collected by the drones for delivery. “Our drones fly over traffic, cutting down transit times,” said Calsee Hendrickson, director of product and program management at Prime Air. “That’s the beauty of drone delivery. Medications were the top item customers wanted delivered quickly by drone. Speed and convenience are essential for health-related purchases.” The drones operate between 130 and 400 feet above ground, avoiding obstacles like power lines and people using advanced software. Onboard neural networks help identify objects via a camera feed. On arrival, the drone descends to a delivery marker, releases the package, and returns to the fulfillment center. In 2020, the Federal Aviation Administration granted Amazon permission to use drones for deliveries, following extensive safety documentation and procedures. The rollout hasn’t been without issues, however: a manager claims he was fired after raising safety concerns about the Prime Air program. Amazon has denied these allegations in a statement to Gizmodo, asserting the claims are false and expressing confidence in proving that in court.

article_content: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security has released a video instructing office workers on how to respond during an active shooter situation. The video, titled 'Active Shooter Situation: Options for Consideration,' advises employees to flee the building if it is safe, hide if escape is not possible, and—if no other options are available—attempt to disarm the attacker with whatever objects are at hand, such as scissors. The four-minute video opens with brief references to several of the most deadly public shootings in recent U.S. history, including the Virginia Tech shooting in 2007, the 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood in Texas, and the 2011 attempted assassination of former Congresswoman Gabrielle Giffords. It provides practical advice for workers, such as identifying escape routes in advance, formulating a safety plan, obeying instructions, remaining quiet, putting mobile phones on silent, and staying out of the line of fire. At one point, the video demonstrates a worker grabbing a pair of scissors for self-defense, emphasizing this as a last resort if escape or hiding is not possible. The narrator recommends locking or barricading doors with heavy furniture and calling 911 only when it is safe to do so. When calling, the video suggests providing the operator with information about your location, the number of shooters, details about weapons, and the number of potential victims. It further advises following police instructions when tactical teams arrive, such as keeping hands visible, making no sudden movements, and avoiding loud noises or gestures. This video was released as part of President Barack Obama’s ongoing efforts to reduce gun-related violence in the U.S., particularly after the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting in Connecticut, in which 26 children and teachers died. The video was already in production before Sandy Hook, and Homeland Security has an ongoing program to prepare people for such incidents. Security consultant Andrew Scott told the New York Post that while fighting back with objects like scissors should be seen as a last, worst-case scenario, he agrees with Homeland Security's advice, calling it an 'adequate and positive move.' President Obama has proposed banning military-style assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, along with more stringent background checks for gun purchases. These proposals have sparked significant debate. The video concludes by emphasizing the importance of obeying police instructions, dropping any objects (such as scissors) when officers arrive, and keeping hands visible.

O vídeo de quatro minutos começa com referências a alguns dos tiroteios públicos mais letais da história recente dos EUA, incluindo o massacre de Virginia Tech em 2007, o ataque em Fort Hood no Texas em 2009 e a tentativa de assassinato da ex-congressista Gabrielle Giffords em 2011. Em certo momento, o vídeo mostra um trabalhador pegando uma tesoura para se defender, ressaltando que essa deve ser uma atitude de último recurso. O narrador recomenda trancar ou bloquear portas com móveis pesados e ligar para o 911 apenas quando for seguro. Ao acionar o serviço, deve-se informar a localização, o número de atiradores, detalhes sobre as armas e o número de possíveis vítimas. O vídeo também orienta a seguir todas as instruções dos policiais assim que as equipes táticas chegarem, como manter as mãos visíveis, evitar movimentos bruscos e não fazer barulho ou gestos repentinos. Esse vídeo foi lançado como parte dos esforços do presidente Barack Obama para reduzir a violência armada nos EUA, especialmente após o ataque à escola Sandy Hook, em Connecticut, onde 26 crianças e professores foram mortos. A produção já estava em andamento antes do incidente, e o Departamento de Segurança Interna mantém um programa contínuo de preparação para esse tipo de situação. O consultor de segurança Andrew Scott afirmou ao New York Post que lutar usando objetos como tesoura deve ser medida de último caso, mas considera adequada e positiva a orientação do governo. O presidente Obama propôs banir armas de assalto de estilo militar e carregadores de alta capacidade, além de adotar verificações de antecedentes mais rigorosas para compra de armas. As propostas têm gerado bastante debate. O vídeo termina reforçando a importância de seguir as instruções da polícia, largar qualquer objeto (como tesouras) quando ela chegar e manter as mãos visíveis.

article_content: At least 15 leading government-owned companies in India have been fined by the stock exchanges this week for not complying with the Securities and Exchange Board of India’s (SEBI) listing requirements regarding board composition. Companies such as BPCL, HPCL, Indian Oil, ONGC, GAIL, Indian Railway Finance Corporation, Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers, and Ircon International, among others, received notices from both BSE and NSE. Each company was asked to pay a fine of ₹5,42,800 to both exchanges. According to disclosures, these companies did not have the mandated minimum number of independent directors on their boards. Many of the companies stated in their filings that the power to appoint directors, including independent directors, rests with the government, and they have requested a waiver of the fines. HPCL said it regularly follows up with the government for these appointments. Similarly, BHEL stated that it consistently urges the government to ensure compliance with board composition regulations. Data from Primeinfobase.com shows that out of 77 listed companies with a market cap above Rs1000 crore that have yet to comply with board composition norms, 50 are public sector entities. For instance, out of BHEL’s 11 directors, only three are independent. BPCL and HPCL each have only six independent directors out of 13, according to Primeinfobase.com. Corporate governance experts insist that government-owned companies should adhere to these listing norms. Amit Tandon, founder and managing director of Institutional Investor Advisory Services India, said the government should set an example in establishing standards—especially in board appointments and ensuring board independence. As per SEBI’s Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR), a listed company’s board must include at least one woman director. If the board does not have a regular non-executive chairperson, at least half of its members must be independent directors; if the chairperson is a non-executive director, at least one-third must be independent. Shriram Subramanian, founder and managing director of InGovern Research Services, noted that historically, PSUs have found it difficult to comply with LODR due to insufficient planning for director appointments, particularly when directors retire or resign. He suggested the Prime Minister’s Office direct all ministries to comply with these laws. JN Gupta, founder and managing director of Stakeholders Empowerment Services, explained that while the Department of Public Enterprises sets governance guidelines for public sector companies, they are not always strictly followed. He emphasized that non-compliance affects both a company’s reputation and its valuation.

Empresas como BPCL, HPCL, Indian Oil, ONGC, GAIL, Indian Railway Finance Corporation, Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers e Ircon International, entre outras, receberam notificações tanto da BSE quanto da NSE. Cada empresa foi solicitada a pagar uma multa de ₹5.42.800 para ambas as bolsas. De acordo com as divulgações, essas empresas não possuíam o número mínimo obrigatório de conselheiros independentes em seus conselhos. Muitas dessas empresas afirmaram em seus comunicados que a responsabilidade de nomear conselheiros, inclusive independentes, é do governo, e pediram isenção das multas. A HPCL declarou que faz acompanhamento regular junto ao governo para essas nomeações. Da mesma forma, a BHEL afirmou que sempre solicita ao governo para garantir o cumprimento das normas de composição do conselho. Segundo dados da Primeinfobase.com, das 77 empresas listadas com valor de mercado acima de Rs1000 crore que ainda não cumprem as normas de composição do conselho, 50 são entidades do setor público. Por exemplo, dos 11 conselheiros da BHEL, apenas três são independentes. BPCL e HPCL contam com apenas seis conselheiros independentes entre 13, de acordo com a Primeinfobase.com. Especialistas em governança corporativa defendem que empresas estatais também devem seguir essas normas de listagem. Amit Tandon, fundador e diretor-gerente da Institutional Investor Advisory Services India, disse que o governo deve dar o exemplo ao estabelecer padrões — especialmente na nomeação do conselho e na garantia de independência do mesmo. Segundo as regras de Listagem e Obrigações de Divulgação (LODR) da SEBI, o conselho de uma empresa listada deve incluir pelo menos uma mulher. Se não houver presidente não-executivo regular, pelo menos metade dos membros devem ser conselheiros independentes; se o presidente for não-executivo, pelo menos um terço deve ser independente. Shriram Subramanian, fundador e diretor da InGovern Research Services, observou que, historicamente, empresas públicas têm dificuldade em cumprir o LODR por falta de planejamento para nomeação de conselheiros, principalmente em caso de aposentadorias ou renúncias. Ele sugeriu que o Gabinete do Primeiro-Ministro oriente todos os ministérios a cumprir essas leis. JN Gupta, fundador e diretor-gerente da Stakeholders Empowerment Services, explicou que, embora o Departamento de Empresas Públicas estabeleça diretrizes de governança para empresas estatais, elas nem sempre são rigorosamente seguidas. Ele ressaltou que o não cumprimento afeta tanto a reputação da empresa quanto seu valor de mercado.

article_content: An Arkansas high school has drawn criticism after removing the profile of a gay student, Taylor Ellis, along with six other student profiles, from its yearbook. Ellis, a 17-year-old from Sheridan High School, told CNN affiliate KATV that his story was left out because he is openly gay. Hannah Bruner, an assistant yearbook editor, said Ellis was profiled precisely because being openly gay is unusual in their community and is not often discussed. Sheridan Superintendent Brenda Haynes stated that the decision was made to lead in an appropriate direction for all students and not in response to pressure from any special interest group. The district cited reviewing state law, court cases, and internal policies before deciding not to publish any of the seven profiles. Ellis and others believe the profiles were pulled to avoid singling him out. He expressed confusion at the decision, noting he is already openly gay and has generally felt accepted by fellow students and teachers. Ellis’ mother, Lynn Tiley, said there had been no threats or issues cited by administrators, only vague concerns about his well-being. The story has sparked support from a national civil rights group, the Human Rights Campaign, whose president, Chad Griffin, called the exclusion discriminatory and unreflective of Arkansas values. On Tuesday, the organization held a demonstration at the State Capitol, and by Wednesday, a petition with over 30,000 signatures called for the school to reverse its decision. Despite appeals to state officials, their representatives said the issue remains with the local district. Reflecting on his time at Sheridan High, Ellis said he looks forward to graduation and leaving the school behind.

article_content: Jack Davies, a 21-year-old British backpacker from Llanelli, Wales, moved to Thailand after being inspired by the Leonardo DiCaprio film 'The Beach.' Davies relocated to Ko Phi Phi, a scenic island chain off the coast of Phuket where Danny Boyle's movie was filmed. After spending about three years living, working, and enjoying watersports on the island—following travels that also included time in Australia—he was found dead. Thai authorities are still investigating the cause of his death. Davies was described as adventurous and well-liked, regularly staying in touch with family and friends. His parents, Christine and Jonathan Davies, expressed their heartbreak upon receiving the news. Friends shared tributes online, remembering his joyful spirit and tattoos reflecting his love of travel and music. The UK Foreign Office confirmed his death on August 24, 2014, and is assisting his family.

As autoridades tailandesas ainda investigam a causa da morte. Davies era considerado aventureiro e querido, mantendo contato frequente com família e amigos. Seus pais, Christine e Jonathan Davies, expressaram imensa tristeza ao receberem a notícia. Amigos prestaram homenagens online, lembrando seu espírito alegre e as tatuagens que mostravam sua paixão por viagens e música. article_content: A 4.5-magnitude earthquake shook Southern California on Tuesday evening, the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) reported. Initially listed at a 5.1 magnitude, the event was later updated to 4.5. The earthquake’s epicenter was determined to be roughly 18 miles west-southwest of El Centro, California, just north of Mexicali in Baja California, Mexico. It occurred at a depth of 6.3 miles. According to USGS spokesperson Susan Potter, the tremor is considered an aftershock from a 7.2-magnitude earthquake that struck near Mexicali on April 4, which resulted in at least two fatalities and about 100 injuries. No immediate reports of injuries or property damage have been made regarding Tuesday’s quake. (Reporting by CNN’s Patty Lane.)

O epicentro foi calculado a cerca de 29 quilômetros a oeste-sudoeste de El Centro, na Califórnia, próximo a Mexicali, na Baja Califórnia, México. O tremor ocorreu a uma profundidade de 10 quilômetros. Segundo Susan Potter, porta-voz do USGS, esse abalo é considerado um pós-tremor do terremoto de magnitude 7,2 que atingiu a região de Mexicali em 4 de abril, causando pelo menos duas mortes e cerca de 100 feridos. Até o momento, não há relatos de feridos ou danos em decorrência do tremor desta terça-feira. (Reportagem de Patty Lane, da CNN.)

article_content:
During Rosh Hashanah 2020, while my family and I were with Aunt Esther in Queens, we learned Ruth Bader Ginsburg had died. My teenage daughter Emmanuelle, a vocal feminist, was deeply affected—she couldn't stop crying as we rode home. Even knowing Ginsburg was elderly and ill, her passing felt like a shock.

To comfort her, we discussed how much Ginsburg—who was Jewish, a New Yorker, and a relentless advocate—shaped our lives and beliefs, from LGBTQ rights to gender and racial equality. Her statement that "Women will only have true equality when men share with them the responsibility of bringing up the next generation" became a focal point in our home.

As the child of immigrants raised in New York (I came from Israel in 1995, later joined by my husband; our kids were born in the U.S.), I admired how Ginsburg shattered barriers, pausing often to reflect on her example—balancing career, motherhood, and Jewish values like tikkun olam (healing the world).

In the week after her death, I hoped to create something in her honor, but the emotion felt too raw at first. When TIME magazine’s photography director, Katherine Pomerantz, asked if I’d photograph Ginsburg’s signature collars, it was an opportunity that meant the world. Sharing the assignment with my husband Eran, himself a photographer, turned it into a family project.

I researched the collars extensively—they were symbolic, as Ginsburg and Justice Sandra Day O’Connor introduced them to add a feminine element to the court's otherwise male-oriented robes. Ginsburg embraced her many unique collars as a mark of identity.

When Eran and I arrived at the Supreme Court, tension mixed with excitement. Photographing the collars in such a meaningful place, on the day Justice Amy Coney Barrett was sworn in, felt momentous.

Staff led us through the historic halls and shared tributes to Ginsburg. When we saw her collection of collars, the room fell silent—they seemed to overflow with stories and memories. 

Balancing meticulous photography work and the emotional significance of the moment, I felt proud—of my work, my family, my roots as an immigrant, and the chance to honor Ginsburg’s legacy.

Elinor Carucci is a well-known photographer. This piece was adapted from "The Collars of RBG" by Carucci and Sara Bader (Clarkson Potter, Penguin Random House).

article_content: Bernard Holden, celebrated as one of the founders of the Bluebell Railway, was honored with a remarkable farewell—his coffin was carried by steam train on the very tracks he fought to save. After his death at 104 on October 4, 2012, the train transported his coffin, draped in the Royal Engineers’ flag and topped with his bowler hat and medals, from Sheffield Park to Kingscote along the railway in East Sussex. Friends, family, and uniformed railway staff paid tribute at each station along the way. Holden’s lifelong career in the railway industry saw him rise from a clerk in the 1920s to a manager with Southern and British Railways, and he played a key role during WWII, ensuring safe passage for evacuees. He was instrumental when the Lewes-East Grinstead line closed, leading its preservation and ultimately becoming president of the Bluebell Railway Preservation Society. Born in 1908 at Barcombe station, railway heritage was in his blood. Through his leadership, Bluebell Railway transformed into a major visitor attraction, run mostly by volunteers and recognized for its collection of historic steam locomotives—the largest in the UK next to the National Railway Museum. The railway’s rich history includes its 19th-century origins, battles against closure, and eventual rescue by preservationists. Holden’s vision for reconnecting to the East Grinstead mainline is expected to be realized soon. His funeral took place in Ditchling, and contributions to the ongoing railway expansion are invited by the Bluebell Railway.

Amigos, familiares e funcionários uniformizados da ferrovia prestaram homenagem em cada estação do percurso. A carreira de Holden nas ferrovias começou nos anos 1920, como escriturário, passando a gestor nas Southern e British Railways, e ele foi fundamental durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial, garantindo o transporte seguro de evacuados. Também liderou os esforços para salvar a linha Lewes-East Grinstead do fechamento, tornando-se presidente da Bluebell Railway Preservation Society. Nascido em 1908 na estação de Barcombe, Holden tinha raízes profundas no universo ferroviário. Sob sua liderança, a Bluebell Railway tornou-se uma atração turística importante, operada principalmente por voluntários e reconhecida por seu impressionante acervo de locomotivas a vapor históricas — o maior do Reino Unido depois do Museu Nacional Ferroviário. A história da ferrovia inclui sua fundação no século XIX, batalhas contra o fechamento e a salvação definitiva através dos preservacionistas. O sonho de Holden de reconectar a ferrovia à linha principal de East Grinstead está prestes a ser realizado. O funeral ocorreu em Ditchling, e doações para apoiar a expansão seguem sendo recebidas pela Bluebell Railway.

article_content: Senator Ted Cruz of Texas is strongly opposed to President Obama’s planned executive order on immigration but says he does not back a government shutdown to fight it. In an interview with Fox News, Cruz insisted no Republicans desire another shutdown, putting the blame on the president if any were to happen. Cruz, known for supporting the previous government shutdown over Obamacare, claims Obama’s proposed immigration move oversteps constitutional authority and ignores voter wishes. Through a Politico editorial titled 'Obama Is Not A Monarch,' Cruz criticized the president. Unlike his former combative stance, he now urges Republicans to instead use legislative measures. He proposed blocking all but vital national security appointments, restricting funding for the executive order through appropriations, and prioritizing these steps within Congress. Other Republican leaders, such as Texas Governor Rick Perry and Wisconsin Governor Scott Walker, prefer taking legal action against the president’s immigration policy. Obama’s executive plan, to be revealed in a prime-time speech, is reported to postpone deportation for millions of undocumented parents of U.S. citizens.

Ele sugeriu bloquear todas as indicações presidenciais exceto para cargos essenciais de segurança nacional, restringir o financiamento da ordem executiva por meio de medidas orçamentárias e priorizar essas estratégias no Congresso. article_content: There’s plenty of interesting timing in Samia’s Tiny Desk debut. This was the final Tiny Desk concert produced by Bob Boilen—he returned for one last Monday to accommodate the performance—which meant Samia had to patiently wait while Bob received some reluctant tributes. Additionally, Samia chose to perform five tracks from her acclaimed debut album, 2020’s 'The Baby,' rather than her more recent album, 'Honey.' It’s also notable that Samia is the daughter of actress Kathy Najimy, yet this performance aired a week after the end of the latest 'Hocus Pocus' season. Regardless, Samia’s set offers a remarkable display of her charisma, vocal talent, and detailed lyricism. She has a unique gift for specificity in her songwriting, referencing her favorite bands, recounting conversations with emotional precision, and even reflecting on the songwriting process itself. In 'Is There Something in the Movies?' she sings, 'I only write songs about things that I’m scared of,' followed by, 'So here, now you’re deathless in art.' Taking advantage of the Tiny Desk’s intimate setting, Samia and her band focused on the softer side of their music, including the use of a sample from her grandmother that opens 'Pool.' As a result, listeners are drawn in, hanging on her every word.

article_content: The admission process for nursery, KG, and Class I in Delhi's private schools will commence on Thursday. Registration opens on November 23 and closes on December 15. Most schools will conduct registrations online, with the first list of selected students set to be released on January 12, 2024. Admissions are based on a point system, with common criteria including neighbourhood, siblings, alumni, and occasionally, firstborn children, girl children, or single-parent applicants. The allocation of points for each criterion varies between schools; for instance, Amity International School awards 30 points for proximity, while The Indian School assigns 60. Delhi Public School, Mathura Road, grants 70 points for applicants living within 10 km and 60 points for those within 10-12 km, with distances determined using Google Maps linked to the registration form. Additional point allocations can include staff wards (e.g., Amity International School gives 20 points), and some schools, such as Bal Bharati Public School, Gangaram, reserve 20% of seats for the management quota and 5% for staff children. MM Public School, Pitampura, provides 50 points for neighbourhood, 20 for a girl child, 10 for siblings studying in the school, 10 for a firstborn applicant, and 10 for alumni parents. Twenty-five percent of seats at each private school are reserved for students from economically weaker sections or disadvantaged groups, with these admissions coordinated online by the Directorate of Education. Despite the National Education Policy (NEP) regulations, there have been no changes to the age criteria. The minimum ages remain: 3 years but less than 4 years for nursery, 4 years but less than 5 years for KG, and 5 years but less than 6 years for Class I. The NEP recommends age 6 for Class I and a 5+3+3+4 academic structure: 5 years in foundational stage (up to Class II), preparatory stage until Class IV, 3 years of middle school, and 4 years of secondary (Classes IX-XII). Separately, the income tax department has reportedly uncovered approximately ₹10,000 crore in tax evasion by online retailers selling through social media platforms such as Instagram and Facebook, having sent notices to 45 brands. In response to more than 20,000 GST notices issued since 2022, Indian companies are reassessing business transactions to manage tax liabilities. Additionally, Raymond MD Gautam Singhania's estranged wife, Nawaz Modi, has alleged that Singhania assaulted her and one of their daughters two months ago.

article_content: French Prime Minister Francois Fillon, on Monday, presented specifics of a 26 billion-euro stimulus program aimed at protecting the nation from declining growth and preventing it from slipping into recession like several other European countries. Initially proposed by President Nicolas Sarkozy in December and recently approved by the French parliament, the initiative will support about 1,000 projects. Around 20 billion euros is expected to be distributed over the coming year, equally divided between businesses and public projects, with social housing identified as a primary concern. An additional 4 billion euros will improve France’s transport, energy, and postal infrastructures. Fillon predicts that these measures could increase economic growth by approximately 1.3 percent. While France has managed to avoid the full force of recession that has impacted countries such as Germany and the UK, unemployment figures continue to rise—an increase of 45,000 in December, following a 64,000 jump in November, according to Finance Minister Christine Lagarde. Speaking at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, Lagarde defended the government’s decision for robust public spending, arguing that in times of crisis, stimulating the economy and restoring confidence must take precedence over concerns about future debt.

Inicialmente proposto pelo presidente Nicolas Sarkozy em dezembro e recém-aprovado pelo parlamento francês, o programa beneficiará cerca de 1.000 projetos. Cerca de 20 bilhões de euros serão investidos no próximo ano, divididos igualmente entre empresas e projetos públicos, com a habitação social considerada uma prioridade central. Os outros 4 bilhões de euros serão destinados a melhorias nas infraestruturas de transporte, energia e serviços postais da França. Fillon estima que essas medidas podem aumentar o crescimento econômico em cerca de 1,3%. Britain is at the center of a new spying controversy after reports revealed its intelligence agencies intercepted phone calls and monitored computers of foreign officials during two key meetings in London. Allegations suggest the UK's secret services set up internet cafes at the 2009 G20 summits, making it easy for British agents to access delegates' emails.

Leaked documents from GCHQ, marked ‘top secret’ and reviewed by The Guardian, reportedly boasted about the success of surveillance efforts at the G20, highlighting Turkey and South Africa as targets. According to confidential slides leaked by US whistleblower Edward Snowden, numerous smartphones and BlackBerry devices were tapped to harvest calls, emails, and documents, providing what was described as timely information for UK ministers.

These revelations emerge as Britain prepares to host a G8 summit, bringing fresh scrutiny to the limits of surveillance by GCHQ, Britain’s intelligence agency, and its US counterpart, the NSA. While ministers often justify access to phone and internet records in terms of combating terrorism and serious crime, these actions in 2009 appear to have been aimed at gaining a negotiating advantage.

The surveillance operations during the summits included setting up internet cafes with email interception and key-logging software, as well as bypassing the security of delegates’ BlackBerry devices. Reports indicate that UK officials received live summaries of intercepted communications, and specific targets included the Turkish finance minister and his party.

The leaked documents suggest the operation was approved at a senior level by then-Prime Minister Gordon Brown’s government, and intelligence gathered was shared with British ministers. Reports also highlight the collaboration between GCHQ and NSA analysts, particularly in decoding encrypted calls made by Russian President Dmitry Medvedev.

During the September 2009 G20 finance ministers’ meeting, intercepted call details were displayed live to officials to inform negotiations. The legal basis for such surveillance is the 1994 Intelligence Services Act, which allows for operations in the economic interests of the UK with ministerial approval. This law, controversial since its introduction, raised suspicion among European countries concerned about British businesses gaining an unfair advantage. Although it’s unclear if the ISA was explicitly invoked for the G20 surveillances, the summit was a top strategic priority for then-Prime Minister Gordon Brown.

Alegações sugerem que os serviços secretos do Reino Unido montaram cibercafés durante as cúpulas do G20 em 2009, facilitando o acesso dos agentes britânicos aos e-mails dos delegados.

Documentos vazados do GCHQ, classificados como 'ultrassecretos' e analisados pelo The Guardian, teriam destacado o sucesso dos esforços de vigilância no G20, apontando Turquia e África do Sul como alvos. Essas revelações surgem enquanto o Reino Unido se prepara para sediar uma cúpula do G8, trazendo nova atenção aos limites da vigilância do GCHQ, agência de inteligência britânica, e de sua contraparte norte-americana, a NSA. Embora ministros frequentemente justifiquem o acesso a registros de telefone e internet como medida de combate ao terrorismo e crimes graves, essas ações em 2009 parecem ter sido voltadas para obter vantagem em negociações.

As operações de vigilância durante as cúpulas incluíram a criação de cibercafés com programas de interceptação de e-mails e softwares de captura de teclas, além de burlar a segurança de dispositivos BlackBerry dos delegados. Relatos indicam que autoridades britânicas recebiam resumos em tempo real das comunicações interceptadas, e entre os alvos específicos estavam o ministro das Finanças da Turquia e seu grupo.

article_content: Cash usage continues to fall as banks promote debit cards, automated payments, and new mobile-based services. According to Halifax, only £17.99 of every £100 spent now uses notes and coins, a decrease of £3.03 from last year. Banks prefer electronic payments because they are less expensive to process than cash or cheques. Today, banks are launching Paym, a service letting users make fast electronic payments using mobile phone numbers linked to their current accounts. Supported by all major high street banks, Paym will initially be available to around 30 million people and is expected to reach nine out of ten bank accounts by year-end. However, not all customers welcome the move to digital money—many are concerned about the reliability and security of electronic payments. There have been cases in recent years where customers have been unable to access their bank accounts or use debit cards due to IT system failures. Banks and retailers have also made cheque payments more difficult, with many petrol stations and supermarkets no longer accepting them, and energy providers adding fees for using cheques. This may eventually happen to cash as well. Anthony Warrington, director of personal current accounts at Halifax, states that the shift away from cash is driven by customer demand for convenience. According to Halifax, the breakdown of spending is: debit cards (£28.87 per £100), direct debits (£19.90), cash (£17.99), faster payments (£12.81), cheques (£11.28), standing orders (£7.82), and other bill payments (£1.34). Paym is described as the UK's first industry-wide service to link any bank account with a mobile number for sending payments. Using a recipient’s mobile number, users can send money via their existing mobile banking app—up to £250 per day. Recipients must register their mobile number with their current account. The Payments Council, which oversees Paym, says the service will make it easier for millions to transfer money. Still, Consumer Intelligence found that 47% of the public have no intention of using it, with 71% citing security concerns, 39% worried about stolen phones, and 32% afraid of paying the wrong person. David Black from Consumer Intelligence notes that UK banks must work to reassure and inform customers about the security and advantages of mobile payments. Barclays already offers a mobile payment app called 'Pingit,' and other providers, including Zapp and PayPal, have similar services available or coming soon. At launch, customers of Halifax, Lloyds, Barclays, HSBC, Santander, Bank of Scotland, TSB, Cumberland Building Society, and Danske Bank can use Paym. There is a voluntary industry code to help recover money if sent to the wrong person, but refunds are not guaranteed. Banks are also competing for new customers with enticing account-switching incentives. Halifax’s Reward Account offers £100 to switchers and £5 each month they remain in credit. First Direct gives £100 for switching and an extra £100 if customers choose to leave within a year. The Co-op Bank gives new joiners £100 and donates £25 to charity. Switching to a Post Office current account offers a £100 gift card. Lloyds’ Club Lloyds account pays up to 4% interest on balances ranging from £4,000 to £5,000, requiring a minimum deposit of £1,500 per month. TSB’s Plus Account pays 5% interest up to £2,000 with a £500 monthly deposit requirement. Santander’s 123 account pays interest at 1% for £1,000–£2,000, 2% for £2,000–£3,000, and 3% for £3,000–£20,000. Nationwide FlexDirect offers 5% interest on balances up to £2,500 for the first year, while its FlexAccount includes free travel insurance. Nationwide also has a Refer a Friend scheme, where both the referrer and friend get £50 for successful referrals.

article_content: Russian President Vladimir Putin has arrived in Beijing for China’s third Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) forum, where he will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and leaders from over 130 countries to discuss one of Xi’s key international projects. However, the summit is likely to be overshadowed by the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict and Russia’s continued invasion of Ukraine. This visit to China is one of Putin’s first trips abroad since the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued an arrest warrant against him in March, accusing him of unlawfully deporting children from Ukraine. Since China is not a member of the ICC, it is not required to transfer Putin to The Hague. Earlier this month, Putin visited Kyrgyzstan, which is also not an ICC member. China is the first country outside former Soviet republics that Putin has visited this year. Beijing has rejected Western criticism of its close ties with Moscow despite Russia’s war in Ukraine, stating that their relationship respects international rules and that China can cooperate with any country it chooses. Trade between China and Russia has significantly increased since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, with China importing more Russian oil after many countries imposed sanctions on Moscow. In an interview with Chinese state TV CGTN before his visit, Putin highlighted the emergence of a 'multipolar world' and praised President Xi’s global initiatives. Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov arrived in Beijing ahead of Putin and met with China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Monday. Putin and Xi last met in Russia in March of this year, where Xi remarked at the Kremlin, 'Right now there are changes – the likes of which we haven’t seen for 100 years – and we are the ones driving these changes together.' Putin last visited China for the Beijing Winter Olympics in February 2022, when both countries issued a joint statement reaffirming their 'no-limits' partnership, just days before Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine. This marks the third time Putin has attended the Belt and Road forum, after participating in 2017 and 2019. After a recent meeting with Kim Jong Un in Russia, Putin has accepted an invitation to visit North Korea. Russia’s foreign ministry has confirmed that Lavrov will visit Pyongyang following his stay in Beijing.

No entanto, a cúpula provavelmente será ofuscada pelo conflito contínuo entre Israel e Hamas e pela invasão ainda em curso da Ucrânia pela Rússia. Esta visita à China é uma das primeiras viagens internacionais de Putin desde que o Tribunal Penal Internacional (TPI) emitiu um mandado de prisão contra ele em março, acusando-o de deportar ilegalmente crianças da Ucrânia. Como a China não é membro do TPI, não é obrigada a transferir Putin para Haia. No início deste mês, Putin visitou o Quirguistão, que também não faz parte do TPI. A China é o primeiro país fora das ex-repúblicas soviéticas que Putin visita este ano. Pequim rejeitou as críticas ocidentais à sua estreita relação com Moscou, apesar da guerra da Rússia na Ucrânia, afirmando que a parceria respeita as normas internacionais e que a China pode cooperar com qualquer país que escolher. O comércio entre China e Rússia aumentou significativamente desde a invasão em grande escala da Ucrânia em fevereiro de 2022, com a China importando mais petróleo russo após muitos países imporem sanções a Moscou. Em entrevista à emissora estatal chinesa CGTN antes da visita, Putin destacou o surgimento de um 'mundo multipolar' e elogiou as iniciativas globais do presidente Xi. O Ministro das Relações Exteriores da Rússia, Sergey Lavrov, chegou a Pequim antes de Putin e se reuniu com o ministro das Relações Exteriores chinês, Wang Yi, na segunda-feira. Putin e Xi se encontraram pela última vez na Rússia em março deste ano, quando Xi afirmou no Kremlin: 'Agora estão ocorrendo mudanças – como não víamos há 100 anos – e nós somos os que estão impulsionando essas mudanças juntos.' A última visita de Putin à China foi durante os Jogos Olímpicos de Inverno de Pequim, em fevereiro de 2022, quando ambos os países divulgaram uma declaração conjunta reafirmando a parceria 'sem limites', dias antes do início da invasão russa à Ucrânia. Esta é a terceira vez que Putin participa do fórum da Cinturão e Rota, após comparecer em 2017 e 2019. Após um encontro recente com Kim Jong Un na Rússia, Putin aceitou um convite para visitar a Coreia do Norte. O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia confirmou que Lavrov visitará Pyongyang após sua estadia em Pequim.

article_content: Historic England has reported damage to Hadrian's Wall following the felling of the famous Sycamore Gap tree nearby. The well-known Northumberland landmark was cut down a week ago and now lies on a section of the ancient 73-mile (118km) wall. Built by the Romans between AD 122 and AD 130, Hadrian's Wall holds UNESCO World Heritage Site status. Specialists from Historic England aim to conduct archaeological assessments to determine the full extent of the damage. The Sycamore Gap tree, which grew in a natural dip near Hexham, Northumberland, was cut down during the night of 27 September. According to the National Trust, which manages the area alongside the Northumberland National Park Authority, the tree was planted in the late 1800s. The site, stretching from Tyneside to the Solway Firth, is especially popular among walkers along Hadrian's Wall Path. Experts visiting on Friday confirmed that the wall has suffered some damage, and further appraisals will take place once it is safe to access the site. Historic England has expressed understanding of the public's strong feelings about the tree's loss and its effect on the historic landscape. The organization will continue working with key partners as the situation develops. The Northumberland National Park Authority stated that Sycamore Gap was its most-photographed spot, and the tree's felling triggered widespread anger and disbelief. Hexham MP Guy Opperman described the tree as a 'symbol of the North East' and said local people were shocked and devastated. A man in his 60s and a 16-year-old boy were arrested on suspicion of criminal damage and later released on bail while investigations continue.

article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) — The circumstances surrounding Tony Scott’s fatal fall from a California bridge remain unclear as of Tuesday, with investigators and Scott’s family disputing reports that the renowned British director was suffering from inoperable brain cancer. Scott, famous for directing blockbusters such as 'Top Gun' and 'Beverly Hills Cop II,' apparently took his own life by jumping from the Vincent Thomas Bridge in San Pedro, California around 12:30 p.m. on Sunday, according to Lt. Joe Bale of the coroner’s office. The 68-year-old director left two notes prior to his death: one in his Los Angeles office, apparently intended for his family, and a second in his nearby parked Toyota Prius, which contained contact information for investigators. Authorities have declined to disclose whether the notes revealed anything about Scott’s motivation, though suicide remains the presumed cause of death. Full autopsy results are pending and are expected to be released in the coming weeks, according to the coroner’s office. Speculation around Scott’s health arose after an ABC report suggested he was contemplating suicide following a diagnosis of inoperable brain cancer—a claim his family has denied. 'According to his wife, he did not have brain cancer as reported, and she does not know the source of ABC’s information, which is absolutely false,' said Deputy Chief Coroner Ed Winter. News of Scott’s death sent shockwaves through Hollywood. Many stars who worked with him, including Denzel Washington—who starred in several Scott-directed thrillers such as 2010’s 'Unstoppable'—expressed their sorrow and celebrated his passion for filmmaking. Born in North Shields, England in 1944, Scott began his career in front of the camera as a teenager, appearing in his brother Ridley Scott’s film 'Boy and Bicycle.' In 1995, the siblings co-founded the production company Scott Free Productions. Scott became a household name in 1986 with 'Top Gun,' starring Tom Cruise and Kelly McGillis. He followed with the hit action sequel 'Beverly Hills Cop II' in 1987. Both Cruise and Eddie Murphy released statements expressing their grief and paying tribute to their director. Pepperdine University film professor Craig Detweiler described Scott as 'the supreme stylist' whose films delivered excitement and drama. According to Detweiler, Scott’s death by jumping from a bridge was itself a dramatic, high-adrenaline act that matched the intensity of his films. Actor Michael Rapaport, who appeared in Scott’s 'True Romance,' shared memories of the director’s generosity and warmth, echoed by tributes from colleagues across the industry. Scott’s filmography also includes 'Revenge' (1990) with Kevin Costner, 'Days of Thunder' (1990) with Cruise, and 'Enemy of the State' (1998) featuring Will Smith and Gene Hackman. Scott met his future wife, actress Donna Wilson, on the set of 'Days of Thunder,' and the couple had twin sons. He continued to evolve, working as an executive producer on projects like the miniseries 'Coma' and serving as a producer for the CBS drama 'The Good Wife,' for which he received an Emmy nomination. He and his brother Ridley won an Emmy for the TV movie 'The Gathering Storm' in 2002. Despite his commercial success, Scott’s films were not regularly recognized by the Academy Awards. He was known for his low-key reputation and signature red ball cap. Jeanne Wolf, a longtime entertainment reporter, described Scott as not being showy, but approachable and beloved in Hollywood. Tributes from film industry colleagues, including actor Edgar Ramirez and director Joe Carnahan, emphasized Scott’s warmth, mentorship, and personal kindness. Scott was remembered for sending handwritten notes, often embellished with cartoon self-portraits. Scott’s final directorial project was 2010’s 'Unstoppable,' in which he overcame unique production challenges filming high-speed train sequences. The investigation into Scott’s death continues, with no further information released regarding his motivation. CNN’s Kareen Wynter contributed to this report.

'Segundo sua esposa, ele não tinha câncer cerebral como foi divulgado, e ela não sabe de onde a ABC tirou essa informação, que é absolutamente falsa', disse o vice-chefe legista Ed Winter. Muitas estrelas que trabalharam com ele, incluindo Denzel Washington—protagonista de vários suspenses dirigidos por Scott, como 'Imbatível' (2010)—, expressaram pesar e celebraram sua paixão pelo cinema. Nascido em North Shields, na Inglaterra, em 1944, Scott iniciou a carreira ainda adolescente, aparecendo no filme 'Boy and Bicycle' de seu irmão Ridley Scott. Em 1995, os irmãos fundaram juntos a produtora Scott Free Productions. Scott se tornou conhecido mundialmente em 1986 com 'Top Gun', estrelado por Tom Cruise e Kelly McGillis. Depois veio o sucesso de ação 'Um Tira da Pesada II' em 1987. Cruise e Eddie Murphy divulgaram notas de pesar e homenagem ao diretor. O ator Michael Rapaport, que atuou em 'Amor à Queima-Roupa', de Scott, compartilhou lembranças da generosidade e calor humano do diretor — sentimento reiterado por outros colegas da indústria. A filmografia de Scott inclui ainda 'Vingança' (1990) com Kevin Costner, 'Dias de Trovão' (1990) com Cruise, e 'Inimigo do Estado' (1998) com Will Smith e Gene Hackman. Com o irmão Ridley, ganhou um Emmy pelo telefilme 'The Gathering Storm' em 2002. Apesar do sucesso comercial, os filmes de Scott raramente foram reconhecidos pelo Oscar. Ele era conhecido por seu perfil discreto e pelo icônico boné vermelho. Jeanne Wolf, repórter veterana de entretenimento, descreveu Scott como alguém nada exibido, mas acessível e querido em Hollywood. Homenagens de colegas como o ator Edgar Ramirez e o diretor Joe Carnahan destacaram o calor, a mentoria e a bondade pessoal de Scott; ele era lembrado por enviar bilhetes escritos à mão, muitas vezes com caricaturas suas. O último trabalho de Scott como diretor foi 'Imbatível' (2010), onde superou desafios únicos ao filmar sequências de um trem em alta velocidade. article_content: More than 100 Taliban fighters crossed over from Afghanistan and attacked three Pakistani military posts on Sunday night, resulting in the deaths of at least eight Pakistani soldiers, according to military officials. The clashes took place in Upper Dir, a district in northwest Pakistan, and left at least 15 Taliban fighters dead, Colonel Wasim Ahmed reported to CNN. Pakistani Taliban spokesman Ehsanullah Ehsan stated that the Afghan Taliban led the attacks, with the Pakistani Taliban providing reconnaissance and information in advance. Three additional Pakistani military officials, who requested anonymity due to lack of authorization to speak publicly, confirmed the incident. Sunday's assault is part of a pattern of cross-border attacks originating from areas in eastern Afghanistan, especially since the drawdown of U.S. troops last year. Such attacks have historically strained relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan, with both governments accusing each other of insufficient border security. The United States has typically aligned with Afghanistan in these disputes, often attributing major attacks on Western targets in Afghanistan to militants operating from Pakistan's mostly ungoverned tribal regions. Journalist Aamir Iqbal contributed to this report.

Os confrontos ocorreram em Upper Dir, um distrito no noroeste do Paquistão, e deixaram pelo menos 15 combatentes do Talibã mortos, informou o coronel Wasim Ahmed à CNN. O porta-voz do Talibã paquistanês, Ehsanullah Ehsan, afirmou que o Talibã afegão liderou os ataques, com o Talibã paquistanês fornecendo reconhecimento e informações antecipadamente. Três outros oficiais militares do Paquistão, que pediram anonimato por não terem autorização para falar publicamente, também confirmaram o incidente. O ataque de domingo faz parte de um padrão de ofensivas transfronteiriças provenientes de áreas no leste do Afeganistão, especialmente desde a retirada das tropas dos EUA no ano passado. Esses ataques têm, historicamente, tensionado as relações entre Paquistão e Afeganistão, com ambos os governos se acusando de falhas na segurança da fronteira. Os Estados Unidos costumam apoiar o Afeganistão nessas disputas, frequentemente atribuindo ataques a alvos ocidentais no Afeganistão a militantes operando na região tribal paquistanesa, em grande parte sem controle governamental. O jornalista Aamir Iqbal contribuiu para esta reportagem.

article_content: As the racketeering case against Donald Trump and 18 co-defendants moves forward in Georgia, several of the indicted individuals are struggling to cover their legal expenses. A recent New York Times article highlights Pastor Steven C. Lee, who is raising funds for his defense through online sales of 'MAGA Honey.' Lee was charged with pressuring Ruby Freeman, a Georgia election worker, to falsely confess to election fraud after Donald Trump incorrectly accused her of manipulating ballots. The charges against Lee include violating Georgia’s RICO act, conspiracy to solicit false statements and writings, criminal attempt to influence witnesses, and influencing witnesses. Following the 2020 presidential election, Lee visited Freeman’s home twice, leading her to call the police. According to Reuters, Lee told officers he was a pastor working with others to help Freeman and to seek the truth. He had driven to Georgia from Illinois. The Illinois Family Institute is supporting Lee by promoting the sale of 16-ounce bottles of 'Ultra MAGA, Pure Raw Honey,' which are sold for $20 each and feature a bottle shaped like the classic 'honey bear' but with Donald Trump’s likeness on the spout. Proceeds go towards Lee’s legal defense fund. The Illinois Family Institute describes the honey as healthy and pure, and hopes the distinctive packaging will encourage donations, prayers, and awareness for Lee, who has a history of assisting at various disaster and tragedy sites. article_content: An Italian court recently sentenced 22 Americans, allegedly CIA personnel, to five-year prison terms for their involvement in the 2003 kidnapping of Egyptian cleric Abu Omar in Milan. Robert Seldon Lady, the suspected CIA station chief in Milan, received an eight-year sentence. None of the Americans attended the trial or are currently in custody, which effectively classifies them as fugitives in Italy. This ruling marks the first trial focused on the U.S. practice known as ‘extraordinary rendition’—the covert transfer of suspected terrorists to countries where torture reportedly occurs, a method widely denounced by human rights advocates. Abu Omar was seized on a Milan street in 2003 and transported to Egypt, where he claims to have been tortured. Italian intelligence agencies had been surveilling him over allegations of recruiting militants for Iraq and Afghanistan. Prosecutors asserted that his abduction was a coordinated effort between the CIA and Italian intelligence, though Italian officials denied any involvement. The court's verdict included financial compensation: Abu Omar was awarded 1 million euros (approximately $1.48 million), while his wife received 500,000 euros. Three Americans, including Jeff Castelli (believed to be the CIA station chief in Rome), avoided prosecution due to diplomatic immunity. Italy’s former intelligence chief and a deputy also had their cases dismissed owing to state secrecy, though appeals might follow. Two Italians were convicted for their assisting roles. Sabrina De Sousa, among the defendants, described feeling let down by the U.S. government, as reported by her lawyer Mark Zaid. De Sousa, who maintains she was serving as a diplomat, is suing the State Department in connection to the case. The CIA has refrained from commenting on the allegations. However, U.S. officials previously confirmed their involvement in Abu Omar’s transfer from Italy but withheld names and numbers. The Pentagon, backed by Italy’s Ministry of Justice, contended that the court lacks jurisdiction over Lt. Col. Joseph Romano III, an Air Force officer included in the verdict, invoking the NATO Status of Forces Agreement. Human rights groups, including the ACLU, argued that this outcome highlights the need for the U.S. to pursue accountability for abuses in the extraordinary rendition program, emphasizing that justice was first served abroad. Italian authorities initially indicted 26 Americans and five Italians for the abduction; some Italian intelligence leaders denied involvement and were acquitted. None of the Americans are detained, nor did Italy pursue extradition. There were suggestions that Italian officials were aware of or endorsed the plan, but the government has consistently denied authorizing the abduction.

Lubna Nazir Shaboo, an Indian woman from Kashmir, and her daughter Karima have safely arrived in Egypt after being evacuated from Hamas-controlled Gaza. Their evacuation was facilitated by Indian diplomatic missions in Ramallah, Tel Aviv, and Cairo, according to her husband Nedal Toman, who spoke to PTI from Gaza. The two crossed the Rafah border into Egypt on Monday evening and are now in al-Arish, planning to travel to Cairo the following day.

The Rafah crossing—the sole exit from Gaza—has only opened intermittently in recent weeks, primarily to allow humanitarian aid and the evacuation of some foreign nationals and wounded civilians. Lubna contacted Indian authorities through PTI on October 10, describing the critical conditions in Gaza: persistent bombardments, widespread destruction, and no safe haven. Forced to move to southern Gaza, her family sought evacuation. Lubna expressed her deep gratitude to the Indian missions for their support.

She detailed the frightening noise of continued bombings and the scarcity of safe places in Gaza, highlighting that the region is small and closed off, leaving limited escape options. On October 9, their water supply was cut and electricity was lost, motivating her family and two other families staying with them to flee to southern Gaza.

The crisis in Gaza escalated after October 7, when Hamas militants attacked southern Israel. In response, Israel declared war and launched a counter-offensive aiming to remove Hamas, which has governed Gaza since 2007, and to rescue hostages taken by the group.

In economic news, a survey of 10 economists conducted by The Economic Times forecasts India’s GDP will grow by 6.7% in the July-September quarter, mostly due to a strong services sector. There are also ongoing discussions to increase the GST evasion criminal prosecution threshold to ₹3 crore, to reduce business harassment and improve the business environment. Meanwhile, the telecom sector has expressed concern about adopting direct TV-to-mobile technology prematurely, citing technical challenges.

article_content: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has warned that excluding athletes and teams from competitions for political reasons could jeopardize a country's chances of hosting the Olympic Games. The warning comes amid concerns about the increasing politicization of sports, emphasized by IOC member Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic during an update to global sports leaders regarding future hosts. India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently confirmed that the nation will bid to host the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Poland and Indonesia have also expressed interest in hosting these events. Speaking at the opening ceremony of the IOC session in Mumbai, Modi described hosting the Olympics as ‘an age-old dream’ for India, stating, 'Indians are not just sports lovers, we live it. India will leave no stone unturned in preparing for the successful organization of the 2036 Olympics – this is the dream of 1.4 billion Indians.' He did not specify a host city, but Ahmedabad, home to the world’s largest stadium (named after Modi), is a likely contender. Indonesia and Mexico have officially shown interest in hosting the 2036 Olympics, and last month, Polish President Andrzej Duda told the IOC of Poland’s intention to bid. Poland recently barred Russian athletes from the European Games, while Indonesia lost the right to host the men’s Under-20 World Cup after refusing to host the Israeli team. Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic reiterated at the Mumbai meeting that more restrictions are being placed on athletes’ participation in international competitions due to government actions. She said the IOC panel overseeing potential hosts must consider any breaches of the Olympic Charter at all stages. She emphasized the importance of all interested and preferred hosts committing to the IOC’s code of ethics and conduct. Indonesian football federation president and IOC member Erick Thohir was absent from the meeting. A decision on the 2036 host will not be made before 2026 or 2027 under a new selection process that avoids public campaigns or contested votes, Grabar-Kitarovic added. She reported that the number of interested parties is now in double digits but did not specify if this included both Summer and Winter Games bids. Unlike traditional methods, the IOC now works privately with potential hosts before granting exclusive negotiation rights to a preferred candidate, as it did with Brisbane for the 2032 Olympics. Grabar-Kitarovic said the 2036 selection should occur under new IOC leadership, as President Thomas Bach’s term ends in 2025. There has been discussion among some IOC members about extending Bach’s term, which would require amending Olympic rules, possibly during the 2024 Paris Games. Future Olympic hosts are: Paris in 2024, Los Angeles in 2028, and Brisbane in 2032.

article_content: Apple devices such as Macs and iPhones are often considered safe from most viruses and malware, but researchers at Georgia Tech have revealed a new security risk: they managed to hack an iPhone or iPad in under a minute using a specially designed charger. The group, including Billy Lau, Yeongjin Jang, and Chengyu Song, demonstrated that simply plugging in this 'malicious' charger could compromise an Apple device—without any special tweaks or actions required from users. Their findings are set for presentation at the Black Hat security conference in Las Vegas starting July 27. Apple’s iOS system is recognized for its strong security measures and strict app approval process, but this attack method bypasses those protections. The technique even works on the latest devices and software, without the need for jailbreaking or user participation. To demonstrate, the team built a charger they call 'Mactans,' a reference to the black widow spider (Latrodectus mactans). It's not detailed whether this charger is based on Apple’s standard design or is entirely custom-made. The researchers point out that their results were achieved with limited resources, warning that more skilled or better-funded attackers could pose a greater risk. They also offer practical advice for users and recommend ways Apple might improve security. Apple did not respond to initial requests for comment on this discovery.

article_content: For the first time, the United States government has officially acknowledged the existence of the mysterious Area 51 military base in southern Nevada. However, recently declassified documents reveal that its actual purpose was far less sensational than UFO enthusiasts might hope. The National Security Archive at George Washington University published a report titled 'The Secret History of the U-2,' which details the development and significance of spy planes used during the Cold War. In their research, the Archive obtained declassified documents referencing Area 51, including a map of the base, through a Freedom of Information Act request submitted in 2005. Area 51 has long been associated with secrecy, especially concerning UFOs and extraterrestrial life. Conspiracy theories have flourished, often fueled by the government's past refusal to acknowledge the base's existence or activities. Some conspiracy theorists claim that a crashed alien spacecraft is stored and analyzed at the facility, along with other claims ranging from secret meetings with extraterrestrials to the development of exotic weapons and weather control technology. In reality, the U.S. government sought a secret and reliable location within the country to test the U-2 spy plane. On April 12, 1955, a team led by Richard Bissell, Col. Osmund Ritland, and Kelly Johnson—accompanied by Lockheed’s chief test pilot, Tony LeVier—spotted Groom Lake while flying over Nevada. This site was chosen due to its isolation and suitability for secret testing, and President Eisenhower approved adding the area, designated Area 51, to the Nevada Test Site. Kelly Johnson dubbed the location 'Paradise Ranch' to make it more appealing to workers, a name soon shortened to 'the Ranch.' The first U-2 planes arrived at Area 51 in July 1955, with test flights beginning in early August. Employees were flown in from Burbank, California, at the start of the workweek and returned home on Fridays from October 1955 onward. The CIA handed over the base to the Air Force in 1957, which continued to use it as a training ground for U-2 pilots. According to Jeffrey Richelson, a senior fellow at the National Security Archive, the release of these documents marks the end of official secrecy about Area 51. While no dramatic revelations have surfaced, the hope is that future accounts will provide more thorough explanations of the site's history and other aerial projects.

article_content: Several European footballers have faced disciplinary actions from their clubs following social media posts related to the ongoing Israel-Palestine conflict. Youcef Atal, an Algerian footballer for French club Nice, was suspended after sharing a social media post alleged to contain anti-Jewish sentiments. The suspension came shortly after French prosecutors opened an investigation into Atal for possible 'glorification of terrorism' and incitement to hatred, following complaints from local politicians. In a statement, Nice said the decision was made because of the serious nature of Atal's post, and that disciplinary action was necessary ahead of any sporting or legal proceedings. Atal, who deleted the message and issued a public apology, stated on Instagram that he does not support any message of hate. Atal has played for Nice since 2018, making 117 appearances. Recently, he also posted the Algerian and Palestinian flags together after an international match. The day before Atal’s suspension, German club Mainz 05 suspended Dutch forward Anwar El Ghazi over a social media post about the conflict that the Bundesliga club considered unacceptable. Mainz stated it respects differing perspectives on the Middle East conflict, but that El Ghazi’s position did not align with the club’s values. The content of his post, which has since been deleted, was not specified. Mainz noted that the suspension followed in-depth discussions between the club and El Ghazi, but did not clarify how long it would last. Meanwhile, Bayern Munich is reviewing comments by Moroccan player Noussair Mazraoui, who posted a message wishing for victory for Palestinians. The club plans to meet with Mazraoui after his return from international duty. Additionally, fans have debated whether such disciplinary measures are applied consistently. Some argue that Israeli international Manor Solomon, who posted statements supporting Israel, has not faced similar consequences. Tottenham Hotspur has not commented on Solomon’s social media activity. The situation has prompted calls from some football fans and commentators for clubs to ensure fair and equal application of their social media and conduct policies.
