article_content: Aside from smartwatches, wearable tech just took a leap forward. Dutch designer Borre Akkersdijk has introduced the BB.Suit—a onesie created from cotton interlaced with copper wiring and assembled with a blend of 3D printing technology and circular knitting. This suit integrates Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS chips, all connected via the copper wires, while batteries and processors are stored within internal pockets. Two BB.Suit prototypes were demonstrated by Akkersdijk at the SXSW festival in Texas. These suits function as portable Wi-Fi hotspots, and both their tech modules and color can be customized by swapping out components. The main drawback at the moment is that the embedded chips lack waterproofing, so the suit can't be washed. During the SXSW event, the BB.Suit was used in a project where musicians could upload their music to a website linked to the suit's location—transforming the wearer into a 'walking URL.' Akkersdijk, whose ByBorre label is based in Amsterdam, began work on this concept back in 2009. Despite successful testing, Akkersdijk has no immediate commercial plans for the BB.Suit. He points out that there are technical challenges to solve, such as making the garment lighter, more wearable in warm weather, and more durable by improving waterproofing. At present, Akkersdijk is working with technology companies to refine the BB.Suit and establish a broader smart clothing platform, aiming to resolve the current obstacles before a potential commercial launch.

The first season of 'Our Flag Means Death' charts an unexpected journey. Initially presented as a lighthearted, Monty Python-style comedy riffing on the life of Stede Bonnet—the so-called Gentleman Pirate who left his family for life on the high seas—the show quickly transforms. What begins as amusing banter evolves into a moving queer love story between Stede (Rhys Darby) and the legendary Blackbeard (Taika Waititi, also an executive producer). Ultimately, Stede chooses responsibility, returning home to help his estranged family. With his wife Mary (Claudia O’Doherty), he stages his own death so she can inherit his fortune and live freely, while he plans to reunite with Blackbeard. Mary's words close the season: "To Stede Bonnet: complicated, hard-headed, really quite irritating at times—and now free. May he roam!" 'Free' is the operative word. More than a story about pirates, LGBTQ romance, or maritime history, Max's 'Our Flag Means Death' centers on radical freedom—a concept that might explain its surprising popularity. Season two returns Oct. 5, wrestling with high expectations and exploring the intersection of love and moral responsibility in a pirate setting.

Set in 1717, during the Golden Age of Piracy and the Enlightenment, the show explores freedom against a backdrop of social repression—forced marriages, harsh punishments for homosexuality, and the realities of colonial slavery. Piracy, like the Wild West, attracted those who could not or would not fit into society. Creator David Jenkins openly acknowledges the darker historical truths: the real Blackbeard committed atrocities, and Stede Bonnet owned slaves. Instead, Jenkins chooses to focus on misfits shaped by hard childhoods and restrictive societal roles, rather than portraying them as psychopaths. "I was just uncomfortable in a married state!" Stede exclaims during a feverish episode—a line that echoes historical accounts. True comfort for Stede comes only with Blackbeard, who boards Stede's ship, the Revenge, with intentions to kill and replace him but finds love instead.

The show’s alternative take creates a haven for queerness and gender fluidity. Blackbeard's fan Big Pete (Matthew Maher) and scribe Lucius Spriggs (Nathan Foad) become a couple. Jim Jimenez (nonbinary actor Vico Ortiz) is introduced as a fugitive disguised as a man but later uses they/them pronouns, with no need for explanations. Jim's romance with Oluwande (Samson Kayo) grows, and by season two, Jim has a female admirer. Another beloved character, tavern owner Spanish Jackie (Leslie Jones), juggles 19 husbands. Love is the purest freedom for these characters, but, as in Jackie’s case, not the only one—gender roles are as fluid as gender presentation. Mary's journey after Stede’s absence is equally liberating: she bonds with other widows, experiments with androgynous style, explores a romance with her art teacher (Tim Heidecker), and paints avant-garde art centuries ahead of her time. Staging Stede’s death sets Mary free from marital dependence, with help from a cast of colorful characters and guest stars.

Season two introduces more extraordinary women, including Zheng Yi Sao (Ruibo Qian), a Chinese pirate queen who leads with empathy and develops a connection with Olu. The new season shows that freedom is not always blissful—an episode featuring retired pirate collectors (Minnie Driver, Rachel House) depicts a couple desperately trying to reignite their relationship by poisoning each other, mirroring Ed's spiral after Stede's disappearance. Ed, heartbroken and directionless, spirals into self-destructive behavior, choosing nihilism over connection. As one character notes, Ed must decide: live or die? Jenkins takes risks by pushing his characters into darker territory, challenging Stede and Ed's relationship, and inviting real conflict that goes beyond light comedy. Characters make difficult, sometimes poor choices, which adds depth but occasionally slows the narrative. Despite dips into filler episodes, the show remains entertaining, though it reaches its greatest heights when tackling freedom with courage. In 'Our Flag Means Death,' freedom is everything—but it's rarely smooth sailing.

O que começa com humor se desenvolve em uma emocionante história de amor queer entre Stede (Rhys Darby) e o lendário Barba Negra (Taika Waititi, também produtor executivo). No final, Stede assume a responsabilidade e volta para auxiliar a família. Mary encerra a temporada: "A Stede Bonnet: complicado, teimoso, bastante irritante às vezes — e agora livre. Que ele vague!" ‘Livre’ é a palavra-chave. Mais do que uma trama de piratas, romance LGBTQIA+ ou história marítima, 'Our Flag Means Death', da Max, é sobre liberdade radical — conceito que explica seu sucesso surpreendente. A segunda temporada chega em 5 de outubro, cercada de expectativas e debatendo o amor versus responsabilidade moral no universo da pirataria.

Passada em 1717, na Era de Ouro da Pirataria e do Iluminismo, a série discute liberdade enquanto denuncia a repressão social — casamentos forçados, punições severas à homossexualidade e realidades da escravidão colonial. Como o Velho Oeste, a pirataria atraía quem não se encaixava na sociedade. David Jenkins, criador da série, reconhece as verdades históricas difíceis: o verdadeiro Barba Negra cometeu atrocidades e Stede Bonnet foi dono de escravos. Jenkins prefere focar nos desajustados, marcados por infâncias difíceis e papéis sociais rígidos, ao invés de vê-los como psicopatas. “Eu simplesmente não me sentia confortável no casamento!”, diz Stede em uma cena febril — frase que ecoa relatos históricos. O verdadeiro conforto vem com Barba Negra, que embarca no Revenge de Stede, planejando matá-lo e tomar seu lugar, mas encontra o amor.

A série torna-se refúgio para diversidade queer e de gênero. Big Pete (Matthew Maher), fã de Barba Negra, e o escriba Lucius Spriggs (Nathan Foad) tornam-se um casal. Jim Jimenez (Vico Ortiz, intérprete não-binário) começa como fugitivo disfarçado e depois adota pronomes neutros, sem questionamento. O romance de Jim com Oluwande (Samson Kayo) cresce; na segunda temporada, Jim atrai uma admiradora. Já a dona da taverna, Spanish Jackie (Leslie Jones), tem 19 maridos. Para todos, o amor é a forma mais pura de liberdade, mas Jackie mostra que não é a única — papéis de gênero também flutuam. Após a saída de Stede, Mary se reinventa: faz amizades com viúvas, adota estilo andrógino, vive romance com o professor de arte (Tim Heidecker) e pinta quadros vanguardistas. Fingir a morte de Stede liberta Mary do casamento, com ajuda de figuras marcantes e convidados especiais.

A segunda temporada traz mais mulheres incríveis, como Zheng Yi Sao (Ruibo Qian), rainha pirata chinesa que lidera com empatia e se aproxima de Olu. A série mostra que liberdade não garante felicidade: um episódio com piratas aposentados (Minnie Driver, Rachel House) mostra um casal tentando reacender a relação se envenenando, refletindo a crise de Ed após o sumiço de Stede. Ed, de coração partido, entra em espiral sombria, escolhendo o niilismo à conexão. Como destaca um personagem, ele precisa decidir: viver ou morrer? Jenkins arrisca levando a trama a temas mais obscuros, desafia o romance de Stede e Ed e agrega conflitos profundos. As escolhas difíceis aprofundam a história, ainda que ocasionalmente desacelerem o ritmo. Mesmo com episódios mais lentos, a série segue divertida, mas brilha ao explorar a liberdade com ousadia. 'Our Flag Means Death' celebra a liberdade — mas ela raramente é simples.

article_content: Editor's note: This article is part of a series of reports featured on CNN.com, in conjunction with the upcoming television event, 'God's Warriors,' hosted by CNN chief international correspondent Christiane Amanpour. Madeleine Albright, former U.S. Secretary of State, emphasizes the importance of understanding religion in foreign policy. She explored the connection between politics and religion in her 2006 book, 'The Mighty and the Almighty.' CNN producer Jen Christensen interviewed Albright for 'God's Warriors.' The following is an edited portion of their conversation: CNN: Growing up, I was told not to discuss politics or religion in polite conversation. However, our documentary 'God's Warriors' challenges that idea. The language around these issues can be difficult, and we even needed to create the term 'God's Warriors,' since 'fundamentalism' seemed problematic. Did you encounter this issue when writing your book? Albright: 'Fundamentalism' is a challenging term. Historically, it referred to Christians who interpreted the Bible literally, but now it's used for conservative or reactionary members of all three Abrahamic religions. When writing my book, I found the term carried many negative associations. CNN: In your book, you argue for greater consideration of religion in U.S. foreign policy. Is this a new concept for diplomats traditionally trained in realism? Albright: As a foreign policy practitioner, I used to think we shouldn't bring religion into complex problems. However, my experience changed my mind. To effectively conduct foreign policy today, understanding religion is essential. The U.S. value of separating church and state makes it easy to overlook religion's role, but ignoring it is risky. Religion shapes ideas, policies, and everyday life in many countries, influencing national behavior. CNN: We spoke to Danny Seidemann, a human rights lawyer in Jerusalem. He said a key problem at President Clinton's Camp David talks was that the negotiators didn't fully understand the religious perspectives needed for a successful agreement. Do you agree? Albright: I don't fully agree with that assessment. While preparing for Camp David, we did underestimate the difficulty of negotiating over Jerusalem and its holy sites. The issue is about more than real estate; religious beliefs add complexity. However, President Clinton was well-informed about the region's religious background, and I was honored to work with both Presidents Carter and Clinton, who were both knowledgeable and religious. CNN: The fate of Jerusalem seems especially complex. Albright: Solving the Jerusalem issue would require great wisdom. Since the city is holy to all three Abrahamic religions, religion sometimes divides rather than unites. We discussed the idea of 'divine sovereignty' over Jerusalem. The religious sites there are closely intertwined, making the issue even more complicated. While it's appealing to propose that the city belongs to God and should be internationally administered, the parties involved need to reach agreement. CNN: Is it possible for all three faiths to live together peacefully in Jerusalem? Albright: Ideally, yes, but it's challenging now. While international groups like the Quartet can play a role, ultimately, the decision must come from those in Israel. If achieved, Jerusalem could offer unique opportunities for learning and understanding among the three religions. My first visit to Jerusalem left me with deep reflection—despite ongoing conflict, the city’s religious symbolism is powerful. I believe people should strive for agreement. CNN: Does Jerusalem's situation demonstrate the need for religious understanding in foreign policy? Albright: Absolutely. I'm not a theologian, but as a problem solver, I see the importance of knowing what people believe to resolve serious disputes. There's limited understanding of Islam in the U.S., and many think Islam is monolithic or only exists in the Middle East, when most Muslims live elsewhere. There are many sects within Islam, such as Shia and Sunni, but knowledge goes beyond that. Diplomats should study language, history, culture, and religion before working in another country. CNN: What impact has the religious right had on politics? Albright: Everyone influences politics; that's what democracy is about. The religious right has more impact on domestic policy than foreign policy. CNN: In your book, you mention challenges faced as U.S. representative to the U.N. Albright: Extremists are often uneasy about sovereignty and international organizations, sometimes misinterpreting the U.N. as a world government. Some hold highly extreme views, even seeing the secretary-general as the antichrist. These people fear the U.N. for various reasons, including misconceptions and distrust of foreigners, which has led to a range of critics.

CNN: É possível uma convivência pacífica das três religiões em Jerusalém? Albright: Idealmente, sim, mas atualmente é bem difícil. Entidades como o Quarteto podem ajudar, mas a decisão precisa partir dos próprios envolvidos em Israel. CNN: A situação de Jerusalém mostra a importância da compreensão religiosa na política externa? Albright: Com certeza. Não sou teóloga, mas gosto de solucionar problemas e vejo como conhecer as crenças ajuda a resolver disputas. Nos EUA, há pouco entendimento sobre o islã e muitos acham que é uma religião só do Oriente Médio, quando a maioria dos muçulmanos está em outros países. Existem diversas seitas, como xiitas e sunitas, entre outras. Diplomatas precisam estudar idioma, história, cultura e religião antes de atuar em outro país. CNN: Qual o papel da direita religiosa na política? Albright: Todos influenciam a política, isso é democracia. A direita religiosa influencia mais nos temas internos que externos. CNN: Você falou de desafios como representante dos EUA na ONU. Como foi? Albright: Extremistas ficam inquietos com a soberania e com organizações internacionais, às vezes vendo a ONU como governo mundial. Alguns radicais chegam a enxergar o secretário-geral como anticristo. Essas pessoas desconfiam da ONU por variados motivos, como desinformação e receio de estrangeiros, o que gera muitos críticos.

Two British PhD students, John Hardy and Carl Ellis from Lancaster University, have developed an innovative technology that transforms everyday objects into interactive tablet-like interfaces. Their system, Ubi Displays, employs a projector, a depth camera, and a PC to turn surfaces such as envelopes, fridge doors, or even bedposts into multi-touch displays.

The prototype consists of a box that houses all the required components and must be positioned opposite the target object. The projector casts images—similar to an iPad interface, alarm clocks, or custom widgets—onto physical surfaces. A depth camera and specialized software track users' finger movements, enabling real-time interaction with the projected display.

Hardy and Ellis unveiled their invention at a Google research conference in California. They believe their technology could become 'the next big thing in home technology,' enabling users to work, interact, or access information from almost any surface in their living environment. Demonstrations included turning off an alarm with a touch on a bedpost and getting weather updates on a projected display on the front door.

Having launched their own company, Hardy & Ellis Inventions, the students—both 25—have made a beta version of their toolkit available online to encourage further development. They aim to reduce the size of the device in the future, potentially making it as compact as a smartphone or small enough to fit inside a light bulb.

Hardy pointed out that while traditional screens can be restrictive, their technology is designed to improve integration between the digital and physical worlds by enabling interactive furniture and objects. With Ubi Displays, features like glowing bedposts for notifications could provide more engaging user experiences than conventional app buttons.

Although other interactive projection and touch technologies exist, the inventors assert that their approach substantially advances current capabilities. They envisage a future where engaging and tactile digital interfaces can be created wherever needed.

Eles pretendem, no futuro, reduzir o tamanho do dispositivo, tornando-o tão compacto quanto um smartphone ou pequeno o suficiente para caber dentro de uma lâmpada.

Com o Ubi Displays, recursos como notificações luminosas em cabeceiras podem ser mais envolventes do que botões tradicionais de aplicativos.

Apesar de já existirem outras tecnologias de projeção interativa e toque, os inventores afirmam que a abordagem deles representa um avanço significativo em relação às opções atuais. Eles imaginam um futuro em que interfaces digitais envolventes e táteis possam ser criadas onde for necessário.

article_content: London-based illustrator and designer Aled Lewis spent months hand-stitching a 30-foot tapestry depicting the complete Star Wars saga (Episodes I to VI). Drawing inspiration from the Bayeux Tapestry, Lewis’s creation adopts a similar epic narrative style. It is currently exhibited at Gallery 1988 in Los Angeles with a $20,000 price tag. Lewis started by digitally designing each scene before carefully stitching them onto fabric. The result is a tapestry filled with detailed portrayals of iconic characters like Darth Vader, Yoda, and Luke Skywalker. It also includes playful references for fans—such as quotations in Aurebesh, the fictional script from Star Wars, reminiscent of the Latin captions used in the Bayeux Tapestry. Given the scale and complexity of the project, Lewis eventually needed help from his friends and family. The resulting Coruscant Tapestry pays tribute to Star Wars’ artistic legacy and supports the belief that the franchise has a place in high art. For background, the original Bayeux Tapestry, now more than 900 years old, chronicles the events leading to the Norman Conquest of England in 1066 and is commonly believed to have been commissioned by Queen Matilda, wife of William the Conqueror.

article_content: Natural and human-made disasters have resulted in a staggering $3.8 trillion in crop and livestock losses over the past 30 years, according to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). In its recent report, the FAO states that between 1991 and 2021, disasters caused an average of $123 billion per year in lost food production—roughly five percent of total production, enough to feed up to 500 million people annually. These disasters include floods, droughts, insect infestations, storms, disease outbreaks, and armed conflicts. For the first time, the FAO has attempted to quantify these losses on both a global and personal level, hoping to raise awareness about their scale and significance. FAO statistics reveal that disasters impacting the agriculture sector have increased dramatically, from about 100 per year in the 1970s to 400 per year in the past two decades. 'The international community is recognizing that disasters have quadrupled since the 1970s and are increasingly affecting food production,' said Piero Conforti, deputy head of FAO's statistics department. The report—'The Impact of Disasters on Agriculture and Food Security'—identifies climate change, pandemics, epidemics, and armed conflicts as key systemic risk drivers. The FAO warns that agriculture worldwide faces growing threats from flooding, water shortages, drought, declining yields, loss of biodiversity, and environmental degradation. Annually, disasters cause average losses of 69 million metric tons of grain (equivalent to France's yearly output), 40 million tons of fruits and vegetables, and 16 million tons of meat, dairy, and eggs. Approximately 23 percent of total disaster-related losses occur in agriculture. Poorer countries are hit hardest, with disaster-related losses accounting for up to 10 percent of their agricultural output. Asia suffers most, bearing 45 percent of total agricultural losses and losing about four percent of its own output. Nations in the Horn of Africa, often affected by drought, lose an average of 15 percent of their crop production, while island developing states lose around seven percent. The report highlights that women experience greater impacts from disasters than men due to limited resources and reduced access to information and financing. In places like Pakistan, where women comprise 70 percent of farm laborers, men have found it easier to recover from flood-related job losses. A lack of data prevented the FAO from estimating losses in fishing and forestry sectors. Nonetheless, the report stresses that disaster risks can be reduced through a range of solutions tailored to local contexts. FAO’s Conforti emphasizes the need for diverse strategies—such as crop variety selection, soil management, and enhanced warning systems. For example, during the locust invasions in the Horn of Africa and Yemen in 2020 and 2021, early warnings allowed authorities to treat 2.3 million hectares in time, preventing $1.77 billion in losses to grain and dairy production. Every dollar spent on prevention resulted in $15 of avoided losses, underscoring the effectiveness of timely interventions.

Em seu relatório mais recente, a FAO afirma que, entre 1991 e 2021, os desastres causaram uma média anual de US$ 123 bilhões em perdas na produção de alimentos — cerca de cinco por cento da produção total, o suficiente para alimentar até 500 milhões de pessoas por ano. Esses desastres incluem enchentes, secas, infestações de insetos, tempestades, surtos de doenças e conflitos armados. Pela primeira vez, a FAO tentou quantificar essas perdas em nível global e individual, buscando conscientizar sobre sua escala e importância. Estatísticas da FAO mostram que os desastres que afetam a agricultura aumentaram drasticamente: de cerca de 100 por ano na década de 1970 para 400 por ano nas últimas duas décadas. 'A comunidade internacional reconhece que os desastres quadruplicaram desde os anos 70 e estão afetando cada vez mais a produção de alimentos', disse Piero Conforti, vice-chefe do departamento de estatísticas da FAO. O relatório — 'O Impacto dos Desastres na Agricultura e na Segurança Alimentar' — identifica as mudanças climáticas, pandemias, epidemias e conflitos armados como fatores sistêmicos de risco. A FAO alerta que a agricultura no mundo inteiro enfrenta ameaças crescentes, como enchentes, escassez de água, secas, queda na produtividade, perda de biodiversidade e degradação ambiental. Anualmente, os desastres causam perdas médias de 69 milhões de toneladas de grãos (equivalente à produção anual da França), 40 milhões de toneladas de frutas e vegetais e 16 milhões de toneladas de carne, laticínios e ovos. Aproximadamente 23% das perdas relacionadas a desastres atingem o setor agrícola. Países mais pobres são os mais prejudicados, com perdas por desastres chegando a até 10% de sua produção agrícola. A Ásia é a região mais impactada, concentrando 45% das perdas agrícolas devido a desastres, e perdendo cerca de 4% da sua própria produção. Nações do Chifre da África, frequentemente afetadas pela seca, perdem em média 15% de sua safra, enquanto Estados-ilha em desenvolvimento têm perdas próximas de 7%. O relatório ainda destaca que mulheres sofrem impactos mais severos com desastres do que homens, devido à limitação de recursos e à dificuldade de acesso à informação e financiamento. Em países como o Paquistão, onde mulheres representam 70% do trabalho agrícola, os homens conseguiram se recuperar mais facilmente das perdas de emprego causadas por enchentes. A falta de dados impediu a FAO de estimar as perdas nos setores de pesca e silvicultura. Ainda assim, o relatório reforça que é possível reduzir riscos por meio de soluções adaptadas a cada contexto. Conforti, da FAO, destaca a necessidade de diferentes estratégias — como escolha de variedades de cultivos, manejo do solo e aprimoramento dos sistemas de alerta. Durante as invasões de gafanhotos no Chifre da África e no Iêmen, em 2020 e 2021, alertas antecipados permitiram o tratamento de 2,3 milhões de hectares a tempo, evitando US$ 1,77 bilhão em perdas na produção de grãos e laticínios. Cada dólar investido em prevenção evitou US$ 15 em perdas, comprovando a eficácia dessas intervenções.

article_content: Josephine and Jennifer Onita were returning from a close friend's wedding in Nigeria. Maimuna Anyene was traveling to her brother's wedding. Weddings often inspire transcontinental journeys filled with joy and reunion in one's homeland. Unfortunately, this happiness turned to sorrow for at least two American families this weekend. Anyene, along with her husband and their four children, died when Dana Air Flight 992 crashed Sunday in Lagos, Nigeria's largest city. Aviation authorities have suspended the airline's license. Also on board were the Onita sisters from Missouri City, Texas. Both were accomplished and bright. 'I don't have anyone to talk to anymore,' said their elder sister, Christiana Onita-Olojo. Solomon and Lola Onita immigrated from Nigeria to the Houston area thirty years ago, seeking a better life. Solomon established a financial planning and tax business. Josephine, 23, who also went by Anita, studied accounting at the University of North Texas and managed all five of her father's office locations. Jennifer, 28, graduated in electrical engineering from Texas Tech University, worked at Raytheon and as a NASA contractor, and was studying biomedical engineering. Ayo Akindona, their second cousin, grew up with Jennifer in Missouri City. He fondly recalled spending time at each other's homes and often boasted about knowing a 'rocket scientist.' Josephine had gone shopping with his sister before leaving for Nigeria, and they spent a late night talking at his family home. Josephine had visited Nigeria several times and hoped more family could travel together next time. Akindona received the devastating news from his sister on Sunday evening that Josephine and Jennifer had died in the crash. He still finds it difficult to believe. Houston pastor Banji Adesanmi, who knew the Onita family through the Redeemed Christian Church of God, had originally planned to take the same flight but changed his itinerary. 'I feel bad that I missed it and they did not. They had their whole lives ahead of them,' he wrote in an email from Nigeria. The Onita sisters, along with their brother Solomon Jr., were close siblings. However, Onita-Olojo said the bond between her sisters was beyond words. She spoke with them daily and was anxious for their return to Texas. Her husband had attended the Abuja wedding and returned earlier, while she stayed home with their newborn. Onita-Olojo said it's hard to express the pain of losing two sisters, and her parents, two of their four children. She sees her sisters in her young daughter, who reminds her of both Josephine and Jennifer. 'I have to be strong,' she told a CNN affiliate. In Hartford, Connecticut, friends and neighbors mourned Maimuna Anyene and her family, who were traveling to Lagos for her brother's wedding. Anyene had just returned from maternity leave at United Technologies, where colleagues described her as dedicated and valued. Neighbors were stunned by the loss of the entire family. A neighbor placed flowers at the Anyene home in remembrance. The U.S. State Department stated that seven Americans were among the crash victims, but was still notifying families. The pilot, Peter Waxtan, was an American who had previously worked for Spirit Airlines and Falcon Air Express. Spirit Airlines expressed condolences for Waxtan. Waxtan had started flying for Dana Air in March, according to Oscar Wason, director of operations for the airline. Tributes from friends and colleagues appeared on social media as the community mourned those lost in the tragedy.

In the rain-soaked forests of Dantewada in Chhattisgarh, eastern India, dozens of police officers engaged in a gunbattle with Maoist rebels on Wednesday, according to police reports. Security forces had been tracking the insurgents when a shootout broke out, police spokesman Rajesh Mishra told CNN. While there were no immediate reports of casualties, reinforcements were swiftly dispatched to the scene, Mishra added.

India regards Maoist rebels as its gravest internal security threat. Up to June of this year, officials recorded 1,103 violent attacks across the country attributed to left-wing extremists. More than 200 police officers and 97 rebels were killed in this period, according to federal home minister P. Chidambaram. Police also arrested at least 1,341 suspected Maoists.

"These figures underscore the gravity of the challenge posed by left-wing extremism," Chidambaram said. In April, an ambush in Dantewada left more than 70 officers dead, marking one of the deadliest attacks on security forces by suspected guerrillas.

Officials believe Maoists are aiming to seize political power through what they refer to as a 'protracted people's war.' The rebels, active since the 1960s, claim they are fighting on behalf of the dispossessed. Last year, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh acknowledged that efforts to combat the Maoists had fallen short of targets. Authorities suspect Maoists receive support not only in impoverished and tribal regions but also among young people and the intelligentsia.

"We have not achieved as much success as we would have liked in containing this menace," Singh remarked last September. The rebels reportedly target not only police and alleged informers, as well as those they classify as 'class enemies,' but also infrastructure such as roads, bridges, railways, and power and telecommunications networks.

To address the problem, India is employing a two-pronged strategy that combines development initiatives with police action in Maoist strongholds. However, Chidambaram noted in a July statement that this approach has achieved mixed results. While security forces have foiled many attacks and apprehended key Maoist leaders, the guerrillas have also succeeded in carrying out significant assaults.

article_content: Within horror fandom, discussions can get heated—fans are rarely on the same page, especially about directors like Rob Zombie or companies like A24. Even so, in the early 2000s, enthusiasts found common ground in their widespread aversion to Platinum Dunes and its reboots of legendary horror classics. Founded in 2001 by blockbuster action director Michael Bay, Platinum Dunes aimed to make affordable Hollywood horror films. Although the studio later found success with original projects such as 'The Purge' and 'A Quiet Place,' it first focused on reviving famous 1970s and 1980s horror movies. Their 2003 remake of 'The Texas Chainsaw Massacre' opened the doors for more reimaginings, including 'The Amityville Horror,' 'The Hitcher,' 'Friday the 13th,' and 'A Nightmare on Elm Street.' The company also created a prequel, 'The Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Beginning.' These remakes were greeted by sharp criticism from both reviewers and long-time fans. Critics argued that, despite their high production values and more explicit gore, the new versions lost the rough-edged spirit that made the originals so memorable. Daniel Pearl, the cinematographer for both the original and remake of 'The Texas Chainsaw Massacre,' intentionally gave the new film a distinct, modernized style, moving away from the authentic grittiness of the 1974 classic. While Platinum Dunes' remakes often amped up the violence, their slick and carefully crafted presentation led some to view them as generic and profit-driven rather than inspired. This approach reflected a Hollywood trend in the 2000s: commodifying nostalgia for a wider audience. Directors like Marcus Nispel, David Meyers, and Samuel Bayer—whose backgrounds included commercials and music videos—brought a glossy, advertisement-ready look to these films. Story changes in these remakes, such as softening villains or adding sentimental moments, appeared crafted for broader mainstream acceptance, possibly influenced by test screenings. The article frames the Platinum Dunes remakes as products of their era: visually impressive, more violent, and nostalgic, but ultimately missing the unique essence of the movies they retold. Although initial hatred has faded, these remakes now seem like dated artifacts, outshone by the original films that inspired them. Currently, most of these Platinum Dunes reboots are available on streaming platforms. Still, they remain examples of Hollywood’s penchant for recycling instead of innovating, with little following among horror fans.

Daniel Pearl, diretor de fotografia do 'Massacre da Serra Elétrica' original e do remake, propositalmente trouxe um estilo moderno e diferente do filme de 1974. article_content: A recent wave of deepfake videos has exploited the images of prominent news anchors to promote dubious products and scams. Clips circulating online show CNN’s Wolf Blitzer endorsing a diabetes drug and CBS Mornings’ Gayle King appearing to support weight loss products. These videos, however, are digitally manipulated and have no connection to the actual journalists. Similar fake social media posts have recently targeted Fox News’s Jesse Watters, CBC’s Ian Hanomansing, and BBC presenters Matthew Amroliwala and Sally Bundock. Many journalists have taken to their own accounts to debunk these false endorsements. For example, Gayle King publicly stated on Instagram that she has never used or heard of the product shown in the video. CNN medical correspondent Sanjay Gupta also warned his followers after seeing deepfakes of himself promoting cannabis products, highlighting the potential health risks of these scams. These manipulated videos advertise everything from unproven health treatments to investment schemes that promise guaranteed profits or exclusive access to stocks. Some even feature edited footage of high-profile figures like Elon Musk. Often, the posts link to questionable e-commerce sites or investment opportunities that vanish within days. Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, has officially banned deepfakes since early 2020, except for parody and satire, and other social media platforms have similar rules. Despite these policies, doctored videos continue to spread online. Hany Farid, a digital forensics expert at the University of California-Berkeley, notes that technology now allows voice cloning from just minutes of audio, making it easier to create realistic fakes. While some deepfakes are easily identified by their poor quality, experts warn that improvements in technology pose an increasing threat, especially to television personalities who have ample online footage. Andrea Hickerson, dean of journalism at the University of Mississippi, warns that the misuse of familiar news faces can be dangerous, as audiences trust newscasters like friends and might not expect misinformation to come from such sources. AI-powered misinformation has already contributed to a surge in investment fraud, costing Americans an estimated $3.8 billion in 2022 according to the Federal Trade Commission. Victims have also been targeted in Canada, Australia, and other countries, sometimes with devastating financial losses. Attorney Chase Carlson notes that scammers are combining traditional tactics with online schemes, cryptocurrencies, and AI to make their frauds more sophisticated. Public anxiety about AI-generated misinformation remains high; a September poll by Axios and Morning Consult found that over half of Americans fear these tactics could influence the 2024 US election. AFP has previously debunked deepfake videos falsely portraying President Joe Biden and former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton. Rebekah Tromble, director at The George Washington University’s Institute for Data, Democracy, and Politics, says that such misinformation feeds broader concerns about trust in information and institutions. An October Gallup poll reflected this, with only about one-third of Americans expressing confidence in the news media, matching a historic low. While many of the manipulated videos are low-quality 'cheapfakes,' they still exacerbate what experts call a 'crisis of trust.' Tromble urges caution when sharing suspicious content, emphasizing that skepticism is essential to help curb the spread of disinformation.

article_content: Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is set to investigate the series of muscle injuries threatening his team's resurgence. City faces the prospect of playing through the busy festive period without a senior striker or their captain, following a costly 1-0 victory over bottom-placed Leicester City on Saturday. The club's only available striker, Edin Dzeko, suffered a calf injury during the warm-up. Later in the match, captain Vincent Kompany was forced off with a recurring hamstring issue. Both players are unlikely to return before the New Year, joining forwards Sergio Aguero and Stevan Jovetic on the injury list. Their absence leaves significant gaps at both ends of the pitch, prompting Pellegrini to seek potential causes for the spate of muscle problems, though the manager refuses to make excuses. 'Maybe we must find a reason why,' Pellegrini commented after the win – their seventh straight victory. 'It is very unlucky to have the three strikers out with injuries but we must try to solve the problem by playing differently or maintaining clean sheets. It is difficult because we have many games in late December, but I never complain about unavailable players.' Kompany had just returned from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and had previously missed a match at QPR in November with a calf problem. Dzeko had recently recovered from a four-game spell out with a calf strain. Jovetic has battled ongoing hamstring issues, which flared up in City's midweek Champions League win over Roma. Top scorer Aguero, meanwhile, is sidelined for up to eight weeks with knee ligament damage. Full-back Aleksandar Kolarov missed all of November with a calf injury. Due to a shortage of strikers, teenager Jose Angel Pozo was included in the squad at the last minute for the match against Leicester, and the lack of options could force City to consider signings in the January transfer window. Pellegrini acknowledged this possibility, saying: 'In January we will see; it is an option. Our squad must always be strong.' Manchester City will soon face the additional loss of Yaya Toure, who will depart for the African Nations Cup next month. This increases the likelihood Pellegrini will seek to extend Frank Lampard's loan from New York City, which is set to expire at the end of the month. Lampard, who scored the decisive goal against Leicester – his sixth for City – remains an important figure, and Pellegrini wants him to stay. The manager emphasized Lampard's value extends beyond covering for injured strikers. 'He is a very important player,' Pellegrini stated. City, though labored, secured the crucial three points to prevent Chelsea from increasing their lead at the top of the table. Leicester started brightly and finished strongly, but City's defense held firm and secured a third clean sheet in a week. Right-back Bacary Sagna praised the team's defensive effort: 'As a defender, it is always nice to keep a clean sheet but all the team defended well. Leicester is very athletic and tried to test us, but we stayed compact and got the three points. We must keep working.' Leicester manager Nigel Pearson expressed frustration at his team's inability to capitalize on chances or keep clean sheets. The newly promoted Foxes sit bottom of the table without a win in 11 games. Pearson stated: 'It is frustrating that we're not converting key opportunities or keeping clean sheets. We are currently adrift at the bottom and must correct that. From a tactical viewpoint, we didn't let City dominate, but ultimately, the key is being effective at both ends, and we haven't managed that.'

O único atacante disponível do clube, Edin Dzeko, sofreu uma lesão na panturrilha durante o aquecimento. Mais tarde, o capitão Vincent Kompany teve que deixar o campo devido a uma recorrência de lesão na coxa. Ambos provavelmente não retornarão antes do Ano Novo, juntando-se aos atacantes Sergio Aguero e Stevan Jovetic na lista de lesionados. Essas ausências criam grandes lacunas nas duas extremidades do campo, levando Pellegrini a buscar possíveis causas para tantas lesões musculares, embora o treinador se recuse a dar desculpas. 'Talvez devamos encontrar um motivo', comentou Pellegrini após a vitória – a sétima consecutiva da equipe. 'É muito azar ficar sem os três atacantes por lesão, mas temos que resolver o problema jogando de forma diferente ou mantendo o gol limpo. É difícil porque temos muitos jogos no fim de dezembro, mas nunca reclamo dos jogadores indisponíveis.' Kompany tinha acabado de retornar após três partidas fora por lesão na coxa e já havia perdido um jogo em novembro contra o QPR por problema na panturrilha. Dzeko também tinha acabado de concluir um período afastado de quatro jogos por estiramento na panturrilha. Jovetic lida com lesões recorrentes na coxa, agravadas na vitória do City sobre a Roma na Liga dos Campeões. O artilheiro Aguero está fora por até oito semanas, com lesão nos ligamentos do joelho. O lateral Aleksandar Kolarov igualmente perdeu todo o mês de novembro devido a lesão na panturrilha. Por conta da falta de atacantes, o jovem José Angel Pozo foi incluído de última hora no elenco contra o Leicester, e a falta de opções pode forçar o City a buscar reforços na janela de transferências de janeiro. Pellegrini admitiu essa possibilidade: 'Em janeiro veremos; é uma opção. Nosso elenco precisa ser sempre forte.' Em breve, o City também perderá Yaya Touré, que disputará a Copa Africana de Nações no próximo mês. Isso aumenta as chances de Pellegrini tentar estender o empréstimo de Frank Lampard, que termina no fim do mês. Lampard, autor do gol da vitória contra o Leicester – seu sexto pelo City – continua sendo peça fundamental, e Pellegrini quer mantê-lo. O técnico destaca que o valor de Lampard vai além de apenas suprir os desfalques por lesão. 'Ele é um jogador muito importante', afirmou Pellegrini. Apesar das dificuldades, o City conquistou três pontos fundamentais e impediu o Chelsea de ampliar a vantagem na liderança do campeonato. O Leicester começou bem e terminou pressionando, mas a defesa do City segurou firme e garantiu o terceiro jogo seguido sem sofrer gols. O lateral-direito Bacary Sagna elogiou a atuação defensiva da equipe: 'Como defensor, sempre gosto de deixar o gol limpo, mas todo o time defendeu bem. O Leicester é muito forte fisicamente e tentou nos dificultar, mas nos mantivemos compactos e garantimos os três pontos. Precisamos seguir trabalhando.' O técnico do Leicester, Nigel Pearson, demonstrou frustração com a falta de aproveitamento ofensivo e defensivo da equipe. Os recém-promovidos Foxes estão na lanterna e não vencem há 11 jogos. Pearson declarou: 'É frustrante não estarmos convertendo as chances nem mantendo o gol limpo. Estamos isolados na parte de baixo da tabela e precisamos mudar isso. Taticamente, não deixamos o City dominar, mas o principal é ser efetivo nas duas áreas – e isso tem faltado.'

article_content: Afghanistan's World Cup ambitions face a significant test as they take on Australia today in Mumbai. Every Afghanistan player carries a story of resilience and hardship. This World Cup has given them a chance to shine, move past their struggles, and bring hope to millions back home. With four wins from seven matches, Afghanistan remain in contention for a semifinal place. To reach the semifinals, Afghanistan must win their final two group games, against Australia and South Africa—an immense challenge given the strong form of both opponents. Australia, their rivals at the Wankhede Stadium, are five-time champions and have won five straight matches after losing their first two in this edition. For Australia, a win guarantees a place in the semifinals. Afghanistan has always boasted quality bowlers, particularly in spin, but this tournament has also seen key contributions from batters Rahmanullah Gurbaz (236 runs), Ibrahim Zadran (320 runs), Rahmat Shah (264 runs), Hashmatullah Shahidi (282 runs), and Azmatullah Omarzai (234 runs). Many of their wins have come while chasing targets, underlining their batting progress. Their bowlers, especially spinners like Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, and Mohammad Nabi, have kept opposing batting line-ups under constant pressure. Australia has been preparing extensively to counter Afghanistan’s spin threat. Steve Smith emphasized the importance of handling spin during the middle overs, saying it will be crucial to building a strong foundation for their innings. Australia's squad receives a boost as both Glenn Maxwell and Mitchell Marsh return; both trained with the team ahead of the clash. Australia is showing consistent improvement as the knockout stages approach.

article_content: LONDON (AP) — King Charles III immersed himself in London’s vibrant Korean community on Wednesday ahead of the upcoming state visit by South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol. During the visit, President Yoon and his wife, Kim Keon Hee, will be welcomed with Britain’s traditional royal ceremonies and will commemorate the sacrifices of British soldiers during the Korean War. Charles and Queen Camilla will formally welcome the president and first lady on November 21 during a ceremony at Horse Guards Parade in London, where President Yoon will inspect a guard of honor, according to Buckingham Palace. Later, the president and first lady will participate in a wreath-laying ceremony at the Korean War Memorial to mark the 70th anniversary of the end of the war. They will also visit Westminster Abbey, where the president will lay a wreath at the grave of the Unknown Warrior. During the state visit, President Yoon will address members of both Houses of Parliament before attending a state banquet at Buckingham Palace. Yoon will also participate in a business forum on November 22, followed by talks with Prime Minister Rishi Sunak at No. 10 Downing Street. Prior to the visit, King Charles visited New Malden in southwest London, which has one of Europe’s largest Korean communities. Charles was welcomed by schoolchildren waving British and South Korean flags and enjoyed a performance by a Korean choir. He spoke with locals about K-pop music and received kimchi, a traditional Korean fermented vegetable dish, as a gift ahead of his 75th birthday on November 14. Charles joked with residents, asking, “Will it blow my head off?” about the kimchi. Local resident Sunny Lee told reporters that the King commented on the traditional performance and expressed regret about not seeing a live K-pop show. The president and first lady will arrive in the United Kingdom on November 20 and depart on November 23.

article_content: Former Major League Baseball outfielder Andruw Jones was arrested and later released on battery charges after a domestic dispute with his wife in suburban Atlanta early Christmas morning, according to authorities. Jones was booked into the Gwinnett County Detention Center, located northeast of Atlanta, at 3:48 a.m. He was released on bond at 11 a.m., with his bond set at $2,400, jail records show. Jones played for the Atlanta Braves from 1996 to 2007, earning recognition for his defensive prowess with ten consecutive Gold Glove Awards. At age 19, he became the youngest player to homer in his first two World Series at-bats in 1996. After his tenure with the Braves, Jones played as a reserve outfielder for the New York Yankees over the last two years. This month, the 35-year-old agreed to a one-year, $3.5 million contract with the Rakuten Eagles in Japan's Pacific League.

article_content: Jennifer Kelly, 29, has been elected as councillor for South Kintyre ward following a by-election. She succeeds her father, Donald Kelly, who stepped down from Argyll and Bute Council after 22 years of service. Jennifer expressed gratitude at the opportunity to continue her father’s legacy, telling BBC Scotland News: "It's still a bit surreal. I've always been interested in local politics, especially since my dad served so long as a councillor—it was something we often discussed at home. Walking down the main street with him, people would regularly approach to ask for help or to thank him, which was sometimes overwhelming. During my campaign, several individuals said they valued my dad's contributions to the area and believed I would do the same, which earned me their support." She described her father’s advice during the campaign as "invaluable," adding that being able to ask for his guidance informally is a huge asset as she steps into local government. Donald Kelly represented South Kintyre since 2001, first as a Conservative, then as an independent councillor. Jennifer intends to serve as an independent as well. She recalled early involvement with local causes, influenced by her father’s activism: "I was only five when my dad campaigned to stop the closure of Drumlemble Primary School. I even appeared in a magazine holding a handmade sign for the cause." As a high school student, she brought a petition supported by her father to school to gather more signatures. Now elected, Jennifer plans to champion the issues her father cared about while launching her own initiatives. She is both the youngest and only female councillor for the ward, which she sees as an opportunity to engage with younger voters. "Being a younger woman, I hope to connect with the younger electorate. Some people may feel more comfortable bringing certain matters to me. I even had voters say it was their first time voting, but they decided to support me." Jennifer looks forward to making a personal impact as councillor. Political families are common in Scotland, as with former SNP president Winnie Ewing and her MSP children, Fergus and Annabelle. Across the UK, the Johnson and Miliband siblings are further examples. Family ties are also present in local councils; the Kellys are not alone at Argyll and Bute Council, where a mother and son were elected to different wards in 2022.
translated_content: Jennifer Kelly, de 29 anos, foi eleita vereadora para o distrito de South Kintyre em uma eleição suplementar. Ela sucede seu pai, Donald Kelly, que se aposentou do Conselho de Argyll and Bute após 22 anos de serviço. Jennifer expressou sua gratidão pela oportunidade de continuar o legado do pai, dizendo à BBC Scotland News: "Ainda parece um pouco surreal. Sempre me interessei por política local, especialmente porque meu pai atuou como vereador por tanto tempo—era algo muito presente nas conversas em casa. Ao andar com ele na rua principal, as pessoas frequentemente o abordavam para pedir ajuda ou agradecer, o que por vezes era emocionante. Durante minha campanha, várias pessoas disseram que valorizavam as contribuições do meu pai para a região e acreditavam que eu faria o mesmo, então decidiram me apoiar." Ela descreveu os conselhos do pai durante a campanha como "inestimáveis", acrescentando que poder contar com a orientação dele informalmente é uma grande vantagem ao iniciar na política local. Donald Kelly representou South Kintyre desde 2001, inicialmente como conservador e depois como vereador independente. Jennifer pretende seguir como independente. Ela se lembra do envolvimento precoce em causas locais, inspirado pelo ativismo do pai: "Eu tinha só cinco anos quando meu pai participou de uma campanha contra o fechamento da escola primária Drumlemble. Cheguei a aparecer em uma revista segurando um cartaz feito à mão para essa causa." Já no ensino médio, levou uma petição apoiada pelo pai à escola para coletar assinaturas. Agora eleita, Jennifer pretende defender as pautas pelas quais o pai lutava e também lançar suas próprias iniciativas. Ela é a vereadora mais jovem e a única mulher representando o distrito, o que considera uma oportunidade para envolver eleitores mais jovens. "Por ser uma mulher mais jovem, espero dialogar mais com o público jovem. Algumas pessoas podem sentir-se mais à vontade em conversar comigo sobre certos temas. Ouvi relatos de pessoas dizendo que era a primeira vez que votavam e quiseram me apoiar." Jennifer está empolgada para deixar sua marca pessoal como vereadora. Famílias políticas são comuns na Escócia, como o exemplo da ex-presidente do SNP, Winnie Ewing, e seus filhos, Fergus e Annabelle, ambos MSPs. No Reino Unido, os irmãos Johnson e Miliband são exemplos semelhantes. Laços familiares também são frequentes nos conselhos locais; os Kellys não são os únicos no Conselho de Argyll and Bute, que elegeu uma mãe e um filho para diferentes distritos em 2022.

IBM has announced a $500 million investment fund aimed at startups working on generative AI solutions for businesses, signaling the company’s growing involvement in the rapidly expanding field of AI investments. Generative AI—which enables the creation of original text, images, or audio—has made striking progress thanks to firms like OpenAI and Anthropic. With the launch of the IBM Enterprise AI Venture Fund, IBM intends to support and accelerate the adoption of AI-driven tools in enterprise settings.

Rob Thomas, IBM’s senior vice president of software and chief commercial officer, told Axios that this initiative represents a new direction for IBM, emphasizing innovative growth. The fund will invest in startups at any point in their growth, without setting targets for the number of deals or a specific timeline. IBM is particularly interested in companies addressing industry-specific needs—such as healthcare or business processes—as long as their offerings are not in direct competition with IBM’s products.

Thomas also pointed out that many business clients have dabbled in AI but have yet to see meaningful returns. He expects that more startups will shift focus to serving enterprise customers to develop reliable business models. Additionally, Thomas noted the potential for non-U.S. companies to lead in generative AI innovation, though IBM’s investment scope will remain global.

In committing $500 million, IBM joins industry leaders like Microsoft and Meta, highlighting fierce competition and the accelerating race to lead the next wave of AI-powered business transformation.

article_content: A University of Bristol study has found that feeding dogs raw (uncooked) meat increases the risk that they will excrete E. coli resistant to ciprofloxacin, a widely used antibiotic in humans and animals. The study surveyed 600 healthy pet dogs. E. coli is the leading cause of urinary tract and bloodstream infections in the UK, and can also cause food poisoning. Infections from resistant E. coli strains can be life-threatening. Ciprofloxacin, part of the fluoroquinolone class of antibiotics, is classified by the World Health Organization as critically important for treating various infections. Researchers identified ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli in the intestines of 600 healthy dogs using survey data provided by owners regarding diet, environment, walking habits, and antibiotic use. The study’s statistical analysis showed that feeding dogs uncooked meat was the only significant risk factor for excreting resistant E. coli. This finding supports previous research linking raw meat diets and antibiotic-resistant bacteria in dogs. Reduced use of ciprofloxacin and other fluoroquinolones in the UK, both in human and veterinary medicine, has led to lower resistance rates. Nevertheless, usage and resistance remain high globally. Dr. Jordan Sealey, who led the research, emphasized that while the study did not set out to focus on raw food, it found a strong association between raw feeding and excretion of ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli. Professor Matthew Avison added that raw meat, whether intended for humans after cooking or as raw dog food, can contain antibiotic-resistant E. coli. Cooking kills these bacteria, and thorough hygiene while handling raw meat reduces risk. Raw feeding increases potential exposure to resistant bacteria for both dogs and their owners, since dogs fed raw meat are more likely to shed these organisms. Dr. Sealey noted that switching to cooked diets or sourcing higher-quality raw meat that can be safely cooked may help reduce risk. Much of the raw pet food on the market cannot be safely cooked and may be harmful to dogs if cooked. Choosing meat from farms with minimal antibiotic use, especially in the UK or similar countries, may also lower the risk of dogs consuming resistant bacteria. Professor Avison suggested that the raw pet food industry should source meat from farms with responsible antibiotic practices and routinely test meat for resistant bacteria before sale. He advocated for stricter bacterial limits on meat intended for raw consumption compared to meat to be cooked. E. coli is commonly found in the intestines of humans and animals and can be transmitted through poor hygiene or contaminated food, including raw meat. Dogs may shed resistant bacteria into the home, which can then be passed to humans. Resistant E. coli can inhabit human intestines for years before causing illness. In the UK, E. coli causes hundreds of thousands of urinary tract infections and thousands of bloodstream infections each year, often leading to severe illness or sepsis. Ciprofloxacin-resistant strains are more challenging to treat and increase the risk of hospitalization and death.

article_content: Twenty-five Japanese nationals suspected of operating cyber scam activities were deported from Cambodia to Japan on Wednesday, according to General Khieu Sopheak of Cambodia's Interior Ministry. These individuals had been arrested in Phnom Penh in September after Cambodian police acted on information from Japanese authorities, and a chartered flight arranged by the Japanese government returned them home. General Khieu Sopheak thanked Japan for its cooperation in tackling cybercrime. Online scams are a significant and growing concern in Asia. The United Nations human rights office reported in August that criminal networks have coerced hundreds of thousands of people across Southeast Asia, including Cambodia and Myanmar, into illegal online activities like fraudulent investments, romance scams, and unlawful gambling. The report suggests more than 100,000 people may be affected in Cambodia, and about 120,000 in Myanmar. In a similar case this April, Cambodian officials deported 19 Japanese suspects from Sihanoukville, a city known for cybercrime operations. Reports last year highlighted many people being lured into jobs in Cambodia, only to be trapped and forced to conduct online scams. These activities are frequently coordinated by organized international crime groups, taking advantage of weak law enforcement and targeting well-educated young job seekers with deceptive offers of high earnings, later isolating and threatening them to ensure their participation.

Eles foram presos em Phnom Penh em setembro após a polícia do Camboja agir com base em informações das autoridades japonesas. O governo japonês providenciou um voo fretado para levá-los de volta. O general Khieu Sopheak agradeceu ao Japão pela cooperação no combate ao cibercrime. Golpes online são uma preocupação cada vez maior na Ásia. O escritório de direitos humanos da ONU informou em agosto que redes criminosas vêm forçando centenas de milhares de pessoas no Sudeste Asiático, incluindo Camboja e Mianmar, a participarem de esquemas ilegais pela internet, como fraudes de investimentos, golpes românticos e jogos de azar proibidos. Segundo o relatório, mais de 100 mil pessoas podem estar sendo afetadas no Camboja e cerca de 120 mil em Mianmar. Em caso parecido, em abril, autoridades cambojanas deportaram 19 japoneses suspeitos da cidade de Sihanoukville, famosa por operações fraudulentas online. Desde o ano passado, têm surgido relatos de pessoas de vários países atraídas para empregos no Camboja, mas que acabam enganadas e forçadas a participar desses golpes. Com frequência, essas quadrilhas internacionais de crime organizado se aproveitam da fiscalização frágil, recrutando jovens qualificados com promessas de altos lucros e, depois, mantendo-os isolados e sob ameaças para que executem os golpes.

article_content: Pedro Pascal, widely recognized for his roles in 'Game of Thrones' and 'The Mandalorian,' is reportedly in negotiations to portray Reed Richards (also known as Mister Fantastic) in Marvel Studios' upcoming 'Fantastic Four' film, according to entertainment outlet Deadline. Pascal gained fame for his portrayal of Prince Oberyn Martell in 'Game of Thrones' and later starred as the titular character in Disney+'s 'The Mandalorian.' Marvel Studios has tapped Matt Shakman—director of 'WandaVision'—to helm the new 'Fantastic Four' movie. Shakman joined the project after Jon Watts, director of the 'Spider-Man' trilogy, stepped down. The film is scheduled to be released in US theatres on May 2, 2025. Marvel Studios acquired the movie rights to the Fantastic Four from 20th Century Fox, after three previous film adaptations. The Fantastic Four first appeared in Marvel Comics in 1961, created by Jack Kirby and Stan Lee. The team includes Reed Richards (Mister Fantastic), Sue Storm-Richards (the Invisible Woman), her brother Johnny Storm (the Human Torch), and their friend Ben Grimm (the Thing).

article_content: To manage risk and reduce volatility, investors often diversify by investing in multiple asset classes. While this provides stability, relying on fund managers’ decisions in multi-asset funds can introduce unexpected changes to portfolio risk, pushing investments away from their intended targets. A central issue is that fund managers sometimes shift allocations—such as raising domestic equity exposure from 45% in 2013 to 65% by 2023 in certain funds. These changes, based on manager judgement or models, may disrupt both new and experienced investors’ planned risk levels. Additionally, many multi-asset strategies still have minimal exposure to international markets. Embracing global diversification could boost portfolio resilience and improve long-term investment outcomes. Rule-based asset allocation is a modern approach that addresses uncertainty by using preset guidelines for how assets are mixed and rebalanced. This method removes manager bias and provides consistency, transparency, and predictable risk profiles through scheduled reviews and adjustments. Investors can pursue rule-based allocation in two ways. The DIY method lets individuals set and manage their own asset mix, possibly with advisor help. However, this approach requires strong discipline, constant monitoring, and awareness of tax implications from frequent changes. Alternatively, rule-based multi-asset mutual funds are becoming popular. These funds maintain exposures within set limits using pre-established rules, helping investors avoid the emotional pitfalls of hands-on management. Still, investors should confirm that chosen funds consistently match their risk preferences, as discretion sometimes leads to shifting allocations. Ultimately, whether through DIY methods or professionally managed mutual funds, rule-based asset allocation offers investors a structured, transparent route to diversified portfolios aligned with their chosen risk. The evolving financial landscape in India, including regulatory moves like SEBI’s new real estate ownership framework, continues to expand opportunities for stable, long-term investing.
translated_content: Para gerenciar riscos e reduzir a volatilidade, investidores costumam diversificar seus aportes em diferentes classes de ativos. Embora isso traga estabilidade, depender apenas das decisões dos gestores de fundos multiativos pode levar a mudanças inesperadas no risco da carteira, afastando os investimentos dos objetivos originais. Um problema recorrente é que gestores mudam as alocações — como aumentar a exposição em ações locais de 45% em 2013 para 65% em 2023 em alguns fundos. Essas alterações, baseadas em julgamento próprio ou modelos específicos, podem prejudicar o equilíbrio de risco tanto para investidores iniciantes quanto para experientes. Além disso, muitas estratégias multiativas ainda possuem pouca exposição internacional. Ampliar a diversificação para mercados globais pode tornar a carteira mais resistente e otimizar os resultados no longo prazo. A alocação de ativos baseada em regras traz mais previsibilidade, pois segue orientações pré-estabelecidas para composição e rebalanceamento da carteira. Esse método elimina os vieses do gestor, garantindo consistência, transparência e perfil de risco definido, com revisões periódicas. O investidor pode optar por duas maneiras de seguir regras de alocação. No modelo DIY (faça você mesmo), o próprio investidor define e acompanha a divisão dos ativos, talvez com apoio de um consultor. Porém, isso exige disciplina, monitoramento constante e atenção aos impactos fiscais de mudanças frequentes. Outra opção, cada vez mais acessível, são os fundos multiativos baseados em regras claras. Esses fundos mantêm a exposição dentro de limites estabelecidos, evitando erros comuns em carteiras autogeridas. Mesmo assim, é importante verificar se o fundo realmente preserva o perfil de risco desejado, já que algumas gestões ainda fazem ajustes discricionários. Em resumo, seja de forma autônoma ou com ajuda de profissionais, a alocação baseada em regras proporciona uma maneira estruturada e transparente de manter uma carteira diversificada e alinhada ao perfil de risco escolhido. O cenário financeiro, inclusive no Brasil, segue evoluindo, com iniciativas regulatórias como o novo marco da SEBI para propriedade fracionada de imóveis, abrindo caminho para investidores em busca de estabilidade e crescimento sustentável a longo prazo.

article_content: The United Nations says it needs firm security guarantees before it can begin stockpiling large amounts of aid at Gaza’s Rafah border crossing. While Israeli airstrikes in Gaza persist for a second week, vital relief remains stalled, and fears of a worsening humanitarian crisis mount. Negotiations for a temporary ceasefire—meant to facilitate aid via Rafah—fell through on Monday, as Egypt reported its talks with Israel produced no results, and Israel retains control over the border. Nonetheless, international assistance is building up across the border. In recent days, at least eight aid planes from Turkey, the UAE, Jordan, and Tunisia have reached Egypt’s El Arish airport, with the Egyptian Red Crescent noting a convoy of more than 100 trucks. UN agencies are also staging food and medical essentials at Rafah, the only Gaza border not fully under Israeli authority. The World Health Organization (WHO) delivered 78 cubic meters of medical supplies through El Arish on Sunday, enough for 300,000 people. World Food Programme (WFP) planes landed Sunday and Monday, containing 20 tonnes of high-energy biscuits and two mobile storage units. UNICEF has additional supplies, like bottled water, purification tabs, blankets, hygiene kits, and medical goods, en route. But getting these essentials into Gaza remains uncertain. 'Supplies are piling up at the border as residents, only kilometers away, are running out of food,' WFP’s Abeer Etefa told Al Jazeera, warning that local stocks are nearly gone and urgent relief is crucial to prevent further catastrophe. After Hamas fighters attacked southern Israel on October 7—killing at least 1,400 people, mostly civilians, per Israeli sources—the Israeli government imposed a total blockade on Gaza, stopping electricity, water, and fuel. Subsequent Israeli airstrikes have reportedly killed over 2,800 and wounded nearly 11,000 in Gaza, according to Palestinian officials. The UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA) says it cannot deliver aid via Israel: 'We are not allowed to do that,' an agency spokesperson stated. UN humanitarian coordinator Lynn Hastings explained that Israeli officials are linking humanitarian shipments to the release of hostages held by Hamas. She said, 'Their current course could destroy Gaza.' Egypt is also not allowing Gaza residents with dual nationality to cross into Egypt, stating this would only happen if Israel permits aid into the enclave. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said it needs security assurances before moving large aid shipments, citing contradictory reports about border openings. OCHA spokesperson Jans Laerke noted, 'We need clarity because flying aid is expensive, and resources are limited—we can't just leave aid sitting unused.' With over two million people in Gaza under siege, supplies like drinkable water, medicines, and fuel are running scarce. WHO recently warned Gaza could run completely out of water, electricity, and fuel within a day. Hospitals are reportedly at risk of collapsing due to these shortages. Despite this, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office has stated that there is no current ceasefire and no exchange of humanitarian aid for the evacuation of foreigners. UN humanitarian chief Martin Griffiths plans to travel to the Middle East soon for talks, hoping for a breakthrough.
translated_content: As Nações Unidas afirmam que precisam de garantias de segurança concretas antes de começar a estocar grandes quantidades de ajuda na passagem de Rafah, na fronteira de Gaza. Enquanto os ataques aéreos de Israel continuam por uma segunda semana, o fornecimento vital permanece parado e aumentam os receios de agravamento da crise humanitária. As negociações para um cessar-fogo temporário — que permitiria a entrada de ajuda por Rafah — fracassaram na segunda-feira, já que o Egito relatou conversas frustradas com Israel, que mantém o controle da fronteira. Ainda assim, a assistência internacional se acumula do outro lado. Nos últimos dias, pelo menos oito aviões com ajuda da Turquia, Emirados Árabes, Jordânia e Tunísia pousaram no aeroporto egípcio de El Arish; o Crescente Vermelho Egípcio informou uma caravana de mais de 100 caminhões. Agências da ONU também posicionam alimentos e suprimentos médicos em Rafah, a única fronteira de Gaza sem controle total de Israel. A Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) enviou 78 metros cúbicos de suprimentos médicos por El Arish no domingo — suficientes para 300 mil pessoas. O Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA) pousou domingo e segunda-feira, levando 20 toneladas de biscoitos energéticos e duas unidades móveis de armazenamento. A Unicef prepara o envio de água, purificadores, cobertores, kits de higiene e suprimentos médicos adicionais. A liberação destes itens essenciais ainda é incerta. “Os suprimentos estão se acumulando na fronteira enquanto quem mora próximo passa fome”, relatou Abeer Etefa, do PMA, à Al Jazeera. O estoque local quase zerou e a chegada imediata de ajuda é vital para evitar tragédia maior. Após o ataque do Hamas ao sul de Israel em 7 de outubro — que matou ao menos 1.400 pessoas, a maioria civis, segundo autoridades israelenses — Israel impôs bloqueio total à Faixa de Gaza, cortando eletricidade, água e combustível. Os bombardeios já teriam causado mais de 2.800 mortes e 11 mil feridos em Gaza, segundo fontes palestinas. A agência da ONU para refugiados palestinos (UNRWA) diz não estar autorizada a entregar ajuda por Israel: “Não temos permissão para isso”, informou o porta-voz. Lynn Hastings, da ONU, explicou que o envio de mantimentos está sendo atrelado por autoridades de Israel à libertação de reféns pelo Hamas. Ela alertou: “Esse caminho pode destruir Gaza”. O Egito também impede a entrada de gazenses com dupla nacionalidade em seu território, afirmando que isso só será liberado se Israel permitir a passagem da ajuda. O Escritório das Nações Unidas para a Coordenação de Assuntos Humanitários (OCHA) diz necessitar de segurança antes de enviar grandes carregamentos, citando relatos contraditórios sobre a abertura da fronteira. Segundo o porta-voz Jans Laerke: “Voar ajuda custa caro, e com recursos limitados precisamos ter certeza de que ela será utilizada”. Mais de dois milhões de pessoas em Gaza enfrentam escassez de água potável, remédios e combustível sob o cerco. A OMS alertou que a região pode ficar sem esses insumos em 24 horas. Hospitais estão à beira do colapso. Mesmo assim, o governo de Benjamin Netanyahu afirmou que não existe acordo de cessar-fogo ou troca de ajuda pela saída de estrangeiros. O chefe humanitário da ONU, Martin Griffiths, irá ao Oriente Médio negociar e espera por avanços positivos.

article_content: Britain continues to allow the export of millions of pounds worth of military equipment to Russia despite concerns that Moscow is supporting separatist rebels in Ukraine, Members of Parliament have warned. The Commons Committees on Arms Export Controls (CAEC) revealed that 251 export licences for controlled goods to Russia, valued at at least £132 million, remain active. These licences cover items such as sniper rifles, night sights, small arms ammunition, gun mountings, body armour, military communications equipment, and equipment employing cryptography. Despite a promise in March by then-foreign secretary William Hague to halt military sales to Russia that could be used against Ukraine, only 31 licences have been revoked, according to the committees. Currently, Britain is still selling more than £100 million worth of military equipment to Russia, including sniper rifles, ammunition, and body armour, despite calls for sanctions. This information emerged after Prime Minister David Cameron yesterday strongly criticized other European countries, such as France, for continuing defence sales to Russia, even as Moscow is believed to support the separatists. CAEC chairman Sir John Stanley stated that the low number of revoked licences highlights the weakness of Hague’s original pledge, which only applied to equipment potentially used against Ukraine and not to Russia’s broader defence needs. He noted that while Britain had been proactive among European countries in restricting defence sales to Russia, further steps were needed. 'Russia is an authoritarian regime. We should have taken a more cautious approach towards Russia for some time,' Sir John said. Sir John has now written to the new Foreign Secretary, Philip Hammond, asking if he will suspend or revoke the remaining licences. The CAEC also strongly criticized the previous awarding of export licences for chemicals that could be used in the production of chemical weapons to Syria. The previous Labour government issued five licences for the export of sodium fluoride, which the committee described as 'highly questionable,' while the current government issued two additional licences for sodium and potassium fluoride after the Syrian civil war began, a decision labelled as irresponsible. The committee deemed the government’s claim that there was no basis to refuse these licences as 'grossly inaccurate.' The CAEC, composed of the Commons Foreign Affairs, Defence, International Development, and Business, Innovation and Skills committees, also expressed concern that the government had relaxed its policy on exporting equipment to countries where there is concern about its use for internal repression. There are fears that Russia is arming pro-Kremlin rebels in eastern Ukraine—widely believed to be responsible for the downing of Malaysian Airways flight MH17 last week. The committee noted that a previous guideline stating that licences should not be issued if there was 'concern' about use for internal repression has been removed from the latest government policy, leaving only a requirement for a 'clear risk' of repression. In evidence to the CAEC, Business Secretary Vince Cable insisted the policy had not changed; however, the committee stated that Labour’s former foreign minister Peter Hain, who set the earlier guidelines in 2000, directly contradicted this. 'We consider there has been a significant change of policy. We don’t accept that there has been no change of policy,' said Sir John. A UK Government spokesperson said: 'This Government has not approved any licences for the export of rifles or ammunition to the Russian military. Export licences for rifles and ammunition cover hunting and sporting rifles supplied to private individuals and to authorised dealers for resale. We do not believe that there is a credible risk that these weapons will be diverted for use by the Russian military.'

O Comitê de Controle de Exportações de Armas (CAEC) revelou que 251 licenças de exportação de produtos controlados para a Rússia, avaliadas em pelo menos £132 milhões, permanecem ativas. Essas licenças abrangem itens como rifles de precisão, miras noturnas, munição de armas pequenas, suportes para armas, coletes à prova de balas, equipamentos de comunicação militar e equipamentos com criptografia. Apesar da promessa feita em março pelo então secretário de Relações Exteriores William Hague de interromper as vendas militares para a Rússia que pudessem ser usadas contra a Ucrânia, apenas 31 licenças foram revogadas, segundo o comitê. Atualmente, o Reino Unido ainda vende mais de £100 milhões em equipamentos militares para a Rússia, incluindo rifles de precisão, munição e coletes à prova de balas, apesar dos pedidos de sanções. Essa informação veio à tona após o primeiro-ministro David Cameron ter criticado fortemente outros países europeus, como a França, por continuarem as vendas de defesa à Rússia mesmo com Moscou supostamente apoiando os separatistas. O presidente do CAEC, Sir John Stanley, afirmou que o baixo número de licenças revogadas evidencia a fragilidade da promessa original de Hague, que se aplicava apenas a equipamentos potencialmente usados contra a Ucrânia, não abrangendo necessidades mais amplas de defesa da Rússia. Sir John enviou uma carta ao novo secretário de Relações Exteriores, Philip Hammond, perguntando se ele vai suspender ou revogar as licenças restantes. A alegação do governo de que não havia base para recusar tais licenças foi taxada de 'grosseiramente imprecisa'. O CAEC, composto por comitês parlamentares relevantes, também expressou preocupação com o relaxamento da política de exportação para países suspeitos de uso repressivo interno. Temores persistem de que a Rússia esteja armando rebeldes pró-Kremlin no leste da Ucrânia, amplamente responsabilizados pela queda do voo MH17 da Malaysian Airways na semana passada.
