Dicas importantes para criar lealdade incluem: - Criar uma identidade de marca distinta, com mensagens consistentes e visuais atraentes, além de contar uma história que envolva o público. - Oferecer valor compartilhando conhecimento, educando e entretendo os clientes. - Postar conteúdos úteis e compartilháveis nas redes sociais, como dicas de uso do produto. - Oferecer brindes, como amostras ou testes gratuitos. - Promover engajamento organizando concursos, sorteios e compartilhando histórias de clientes. - Contribuir com a comunidade, especialmente se seu negócio for local. A experiência do cliente (CX) é fundamental: 78% dos clientes têm mais chance de comprar novamente ou indicar empresas que personalizam a comunicação e as ofertas. Para melhorar a personalização: - Realize campanhas baseadas em identidade, adaptadas a personas do cliente. - Envie e-mails personalizados de pessoas reais do time. - Responda individualmente a feedbacks e avaliações. - Use notificações push e recomendações de acordo com o comportamento do cliente. Conhecer seu público é essencial para marketing segmentado e personalização. Sem isso, campanhas são menos eficazes e a rotatividade pode aumentar em até 16%. Analise e ajuste regularmente seu público-alvo para se alinhar às suas necessidades. Foque em solucionar problemas dos seus clientes. Por exemplo, o app Hilton Honors permite ao hóspede fazer check-in, ver o quarto virtualmente, destrancar portas, pedir transporte e acumular pontos — tudo pelo celular, dando mais controle ao cliente. À medida que a base de clientes cresce, também cresce o volume de dados. Soluções digitais como help desks e CRMs centralizam informações dos clientes, facilitando uma visão completa e atendimento eficiente. Clientes satisfeitos têm mais chances de voltar e fazer novas compras. Métricas como NPS, satisfação, esforço do cliente, CLV e pesquisas auxiliam a medir esse sentimento. Monitorando feedbacks, é possível melhorar serviços e resolver problemas antes que prejudiquem a relação. A tecnologia fornece insights valiosos sobre preferências e hábitos de comunicação dos clientes, ajudando na criação de estratégias eficazes. Em resumo, priorizar o relacionamento com o cliente reduz custos de aquisição, aumenta a retenção e diminui a rotatividade. Com marketing segmentado, comunicação eficaz, experiências personalizadas e soluções baseadas em dados, as empresas constroem conexões duradouras com seus clientes. article_content: Earlier this month, two men fishing about 12 miles (19 kilometers) off the coast near Dundee Beach in Australia's Northern Territory were stung by the elusive Irukandji jellyfish, considered one of the most venomous sea creatures on Earth. These jellyfish, nearly invisible and around the size of a dime (about 2 centimeters across), can trigger severe symptoms called Irukandji syndrome. Victims may experience headaches, intense pain, muscle cramps, nausea, and, in rare cases, dangerous heart complications. On October 10, after being stung, both men were promptly airlifted from their boat and taken to a hospital for emergency care. The exact species responsible is unknown, though most incidents are attributed to Carukia barnesi, as noted by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI). Irukandji venom works similarly to tetrodotoxin—a deadly compound in pufferfish and blue-ringed octopuses—by disrupting nerve-to-muscle communication. Irukandji syndrome symptoms can start within five minutes of a sting, according to the Queensland Ambulance Service. Because there is no antivenom for Irukandji venom, treatment focuses on symptom relief. Experts recommend applying vinegar to the sting site immediately to help prevent further venom release from the jellyfish barbs. Most people recover completely, though some may have lingering pain for months. Fortunately, both fishermen were released from the hospital after 48 hours and are expected to make a full recovery. Each year, Australia sees between 50 and 100 cases of Irukandji syndrome, LiveScience reports.

Essas águas-vivas, quase invisíveis e com cerca de 2 centímetros de diâmetro (do tamanho de uma moeda pequena), podem desencadear sintomas graves conhecidos como síndrome de Irukandji. As vítimas podem sentir dores de cabeça, dor intensa, câimbras musculares, náusea e, em casos raros, complicações cardíacas perigosas. Em 10 de outubro, após serem picados, ambos os homens foram rapidamente resgatados de helicóptero e levados ao hospital para atendimento de emergência. A espécie exata responsável é desconhecida, embora a maioria dos casos seja atribuída à Carukia barnesi, segundo o Centro Nacional de Informação em Biotecnologia (NCBI). O veneno da Irukandji age de maneira semelhante à tetrodotoxina — uma substância extremamente tóxica presente em baiacus e polvos-de-anéis-azuis —, interrompendo a comunicação dos nervos com os músculos. Os sintomas da síndrome de Irukandji podem aparecer em até cinco minutos após a picada, de acordo com o Serviço de Ambulância de Queensland. Como não existe antiveneno para o veneno da Irukandji, o tratamento é focado no alívio dos sintomas. Especialistas recomendam aplicar vinagre imediatamente no local da picada, pois isso pode evitar que mais veneno seja liberado pelos ferrões da água-viva. A maioria das pessoas se recupera completamente, embora algumas possam sentir dores persistentes por meses. Felizmente, ambos os pescadores receberam alta após 48 horas de internação e devem se recuperar totalmente. A Austrália registra entre 50 e 100 casos da síndrome de Irukandji por ano, segundo o LiveScience.

article_content: A U.S. Navy plane overshot a runway and ended up in Kaneohe Bay, Hawaii, on Monday. When the Honolulu Emergency Medical Services Department arrived at the scene, military officials reported that all nine people on board made it safely to shore with no injuries, according to department spokesperson Shayne Enright. Coast Guard spokesperson Petty Officer Ryan Fisher said the Coast Guard responded, but rescue operations were quickly called off after learning that all parties were safe. The P-8A aircraft overshot the runway at a Marine base on Kaneohe Bay, said U.S. Marine Corps spokesperson Gunnery Sgt. Orlando Perez. He did not have further details. A witness photo showed the plane floating just offshore, evoking memories of the 2009 'Miracle on the Hudson' when pilot Chesley 'Sully' Sullenberger landed a commercial plane in the Hudson River and all 155 people survived. The P-8A and the Airbus A320 Sullenberger piloted are similar in size. Diane Dircks, 61, visiting from Illinois, and her family had just returned to the dock after rainy weather cut their boat trip short when they noticed the plane in the water. 'We went running over to the end of the dock, and I took some pictures,' Dircks said. They then heard sirens from all directions. Her daughter, an avid birdwatcher, used binoculars to observe the plane and the rescue boats arriving. 'It was unbelievable,' Dircks said. It was cloudy and rainy in the afternoon at the time of the crash, with visibility about 1 mile (1.6 kilometers), according to Thomas Vaughan, a National Weather Service meteorologist in Honolulu. The P-8A is often used for submarine hunting, reconnaissance, and intelligence gathering. It is made by Boeing and shares many parts with the 737 commercial jet. This plane belongs to the Skinny Dragons of Patrol Squadron Four, based at Whidbey Island, Washington. Patrol squadrons now deploy to Hawaii on a rotational basis. Water landings—also called ditching—are rare in commercial aviation and difficult due to factors like wave action and flooding, experts previously told Business Insider. Many overshot landings have historically occurred on land. For example, in October 2022, a Korean Air plane overshot a runway after two landing attempts, damaging its exterior, and in 2020, an Iranian plane missed a landing strip and slid onto a busy highway. There were no fatalities in either incident. Landings are the most dangerous part of a flight, responsible for 49% of fatal plane accidents, according to Business Insider. This is partly due to the limited time pilots have to react near the ground. Experts note that stopping a plane is generally more challenging than keeping it in flight. Marine Corps Base Hawaii is about 10 miles (16 kilometers) from Honolulu on Oahu. It is home to about 9,300 military personnel and 5,100 family members and is one of several important military installations on Oahu. The base sits on Kaneohe Bay, which also contains coral reefs, a hammerhead shark breeding ground, and a University of Hawaii marine biology research institute.

article_content: A debate lasting more than five years over the proposed Keystone XL oil pipeline from Canada could stretch even longer following a recent call for a health study. On Wednesday, Democratic Senators Barbara Boxer of California and Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island urged Secretary of State John Kerry to investigate reports of higher cancer rates and other illnesses in regions affected by "tar sands" oil from northern Alberta. Their letter sought to delay the project, which is supported by Republicans, some Democrats, the oil industry, and labor unions. According to a Pew Research Center poll from September, 65% of respondents favored building the pipeline. Why is this project still being debated? The controversy has turned the pipeline into a political challenge for President Barack Obama and the Democratic Party as they try to retain control of the Senate in the upcoming November congressional elections. The proposed pipeline, by Canadian company TransCanada, would transport oil from northern Alberta to the Gulf Coast, crossing six U.S. states. The $5.3 billion project requires federal approval because it crosses the U.S.-Canada border, placing the decision with the State Department, overseen by John Kerry. A recent U.S. State Department report indicated that the pipeline would have little effect on climate change overall. However, environmental groups continue to oppose the project, arguing that extracting and refining tar sands oil produces 17% more carbon pollution than conventional oil, contributing to climate change. Opponents fear the project would increase U.S. dependence on this "dirtier" oil, when the country should be reducing fossil fuel use to address climate concerns. Tom Steyer, of NextGen Climate Action, wrote in a CNN opinion piece that the Keystone XL pipeline represents a gateway to the unchecked development of one of the world's dirtiest fossil fuels. Supporters counter that extensive studies since 2008 show the pipeline would not significantly increase greenhouse gas emissions and point out benefits such as more than 3,000 temporary U.S. jobs, and a projected total of fewer than 50 permanent jobs upon completion. Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell, a Republican from Kentucky, called the pipeline ‘the single largest shovel-ready project in America’ and said it would bring thousands of private-sector jobs without costing taxpayers. The oil for the pipeline comes from western Canada's tar sands, especially the areas around the Athabasca River, where oil-rich bitumen saturates the sand. The process for separating bitumen from sand was developed in the 1920s; now, major international companies have invested billions to build extraction and refining complexes near Fort McMurray, Alberta. The Keystone XL pipeline would begin in Hardisty, Alberta, and run 1,179 miles through several U.S. states, ultimately reaching the Gulf Coast, with a capacity of 830,000 barrels of oil per day. Interest in the project grew after the September 11, 2001 attacks, as the U.S. sought to reduce dependence on Middle East oil. Increased oil prices made Canadian tar sands projects more feasible. Republicans and labor unions support the pipeline for economic reasons, while four Democratic senators facing difficult re-election campaigns also back the project. Environmental groups and donors such as Tom Steyer oppose the project due to climate concerns. Steyer has pledged up to $100 million to promote climate change mitigation efforts. Senators Boxer and Whitehouse have additionally called for a comprehensive health review as part of the State Department's assessment, pointing to documented increases in carcinogens and mercury in communities near tar sands sites, higher rates of rare cancers, and the difficulty of cleaning up oil spills. President Obama has prioritized climate change in his administration, implementing stricter fuel efficiency and pollution standards. The Keystone XL question has become a defining issue in the U.S. climate debate. In a climate change speech last year, Obama stated that the pipeline must be essentially carbon-neutral to gain approval. The recent State Department report found minimal additional carbon emissions would result from the pipeline. Ultimately, Obama will make the final decision, though election-year dynamics may influence timing. Legal and regulatory processes, including a recent Nebraska court ruling against the pipeline’s route, are likely to delay any final approval. After the State Department’s January 31 environmental report, there is a 90-day period for public comment. Secretary Kerry will then assess if the project is in the national interest. Meanwhile, TransCanada has rerouted the pipeline after earlier delays linked to environmental concerns in Nebraska. The process may extend beyond the November elections, as similar postponements occurred before the 2012 presidential vote.

Processos legais e regulatórios, incluindo uma recente decisão da Justiça de Nebraska contra a rota do oleoduto, devem atrasar uma aprovação definitiva. Após o relatório ambiental do Departamento de Estado em 31 de janeiro, abre-se um prazo de 90 dias para comentários públicos. O secretário Kerry avaliará se o projeto é de interesse nacional. Enquanto isso, a TransCanada já mudou a rota do oleoduto após atrasos anteriores relacionados a preocupações ambientais em Nebraska. article_content: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has issued a warning to healthcare providers to be vigilant for cases of lead exposure in children who may have consumed cinnamon-flavored applesauce products. In an official health advisory published on Monday, the CDC notified doctors that as of November 7, there have been 22 reported cases of children with elevated blood lead levels after eating cinnamon applesauce pouches. The CDC urges providers to report any such cases to local health authorities. The agency is working with the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and state and local partners to investigate the cause. Additionally, two more companies have recalled cinnamon applesauce pouches due to potential lead contamination. State laboratories have found 'extremely high' levels of lead in certain batches of cinnamon applesauce pouches, which have since been recalled by WanaBana, Schnucks, and Weis. Cases of high blood lead levels have been reported in 14 states: Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Missouri, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and Washington. These pouches were sold through retailers such as Amazon, Dollar Tree, and Sam’s Club. The FDA issued a warning last month after an investigation in North Carolina identified four children with elevated lead levels, all linked to WanaBana apple cinnamon fruit puree pouches. The FDA has advised families not to consume these products and to either dispose of the pouches or return them to the store for a refund. Caregivers are encouraged to have blood tests done for any children who may have eaten these products to check for lead exposure. Lead is toxic, and no amount is considered safe for humans. Although symptoms may not appear right away, lead poisoning can result in developmental delays and various health problems in children. Initial symptoms may include headaches, stomachaches, muscle aches, vomiting, anemia, irritability, fatigue, and weight loss. The companies involved are cooperating with the FDA to determine the source of contamination. They are actively working with the agency on this matter.

article_content: The sun is shining, barbecues are out, beaches are packed, and the commute to work is a bit quieter than usual. That can mean only one thing: football's summer transfer window has arrived. Most managers dislike it, fans crave constant updates, and sports journalists are absorbed by it. With another month of speculation, rumors, and intrigue before it ends, CNN examines what it all means. Every summer brings a transfer saga. In recent years, an Arsenal player has often been at the center, as rival clubs try to lure him from Arsene Wenger. Typically, after a summer of rumors, the player remains for one more shot with Arsenal’s manager, but eventually, as with Patrick Vieira (Juventus), Thierry Henry (Barcelona), and Robin Van Persie (Manchester United), the desire for a new challenge prevails. This summer, in a change of roles, Arsenal is the club seeking stars from elsewhere. Gonzalo Higuain chose Napoli over Arsenal, while Arsenal’s attention has shifted to Luis Suarez. Only time will reveal if Arsenal’s bid will convince the Uruguayan to join. Another significant saga involves Tottenham Hotspur, who are fighting to keep Gareth Bale, while Real Madrid looks to sign him. The possibility of Cristiano Ronaldo and Bale playing together has excited Madrid fans. Recent developments suggest Tottenham are prepared to let Bale leave, with the large transfer fee expected to soften the loss. Historically, interest from Chelsea or Manchester City would conclude any transfer discussions. This time, however, Edinson Cavani moved to Paris Saint Germain instead of England. The financial superiority of the Premier League seems to be diminishing as clubs in leagues like France’s Ligue 1 grow stronger, with teams like Monaco and PSG outspending big-name English clubs, including securing Falcao over Chelsea. Across Europe, financial austerity continues, with unemployment high and fans protesting ticket prices. Nevertheless, football transfer spending is growing, shown by reports of Real Madrid considering record-breaking fees. FIFA data indicates transfers in early 2013 increased significantly, and multimillion-dollar deals remain frequent. On social media, especially Twitter, rumors spread quickly. Individuals claiming to be 'in the know,' some later exposed as imposters, regularly influence public discussion. These fakes sometimes exploit young players, especially in Africa, where new initiatives aim to protect talent. Even experienced players, like Francisco Sandanza, have been deceived by false agents. Ultimately, the transfer window brings emotional upheaval to players, managers, and fans. Public displays of stress and disappointment are routine. As the window closes, footballers’ futures become clearer—until the cycle resumes when it reopens in January.

article_content: In September 2023, Earth's global temperature averaged 1.75°C above pre-industrial levels, a temporary breach of the 1.5°C threshold set as a target by international leaders. Continued warming at this level makes coral reef survival difficult and jeopardizes the livelihoods of communities relying on reefs for food, coastal defense, and tourism. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) reports that up to two-thirds of the planet's coral reefs could decline over the next few decades, even under optimistic climate scenarios. While full restoration of reefs lost to climate change is not feasible, researchers are investigating whether artificial reefs, typically built with concrete or similar materials, can recreate some critical features and benefits of natural reefs. Artificial reefs have shown a remarkable capacity to attract diverse marine life—sometimes rivaling the biodiversity found on natural reefs. They provide solid surfaces for corals and sponges to grow, and offer hiding and living spaces for fish, crabs, and octopuses. Until recently, it was unclear whether these artificial habitats create additional ecological communities or simply attract organisms from nearby reefs. This distinction matters for ensuring the resilience of marine life as natural reefs disappear. A recent study published in the journal Marine Biology is the first to test if artificial reefs in tropical regions can perform the same roles as natural reefs. The results are encouraging: although artificial reefs are not yet identical to their natural counterparts, they are starting to duplicate key ecological processes and show potential for further improvement as they mature. Natural coral reefs excel at supporting life even in nutrient-poor tropical waters—a puzzle known as Darwin’s Paradox. This is possible because coral reefs rapidly recycle nutrients within their densely populated communities, keeping overall nutrient levels low and preventing algae takeover. To compare reef types, researchers measured nutrient cycling and storage on both artificial and natural reefs off north Bali, Indonesia. The North Bali Reef Conservation initiative, co-founded by one of the researchers, has worked with local fishers and international volunteers to deploy more than 15,000 artificial reef modules, covering about two football fields in size. Artificial reefs there show promising signs. High phosphate readings just beneath the sand indicate numerous fish, while nutrient levels in water samples above the sediment stayed low, as seen on healthy natural reefs—evidence that nutrient cycling is happening efficiently. However, sediments around the artificial reefs store less carbon compared to natural reefs, likely due to fewer invertebrate species present. As more invertebrates settle in over time, the artificial reefs are expected to function increasingly like natural reefs. This research offers hope that artificial reefs can, over time, replicate more processes seen in natural reefs, and support coastal communities impacted by reef loss. However, the researchers emphasize that only by drastically reducing greenhouse gas emissions can coral ecosystems truly be safeguarded for the future. For reefs already lost to pollution, destructive fishing, or development, artificial structures may help reclaim some of their lost value. Scientists suggest it could take about five years for artificial reef communities to start functioning like natural reefs, reinforcing the need to start restoration efforts promptly.

Se esse aquecimento persistir, a sobrevivência dos recifes de coral ficará comprometida, assim como o sustento das comunidades que dependem deles para alimentação, proteção costeira e turismo. O Painel Intergovernamental sobre Mudanças Climáticas (IPCC) relata que até dois terços dos recifes de coral do planeta podem desaparecer nas próximas décadas, mesmo nos cenários climáticos mais otimistas. Embora a restauração completa dos recifes perdidos para as mudanças climáticas não seja viável, pesquisadores estão investigando se recifes artificiais, geralmente construídos com concreto ou materiais semelhantes, podem replicar algumas características e benefícios essenciais dos recifes naturais. Os recifes artificiais têm demonstrado uma capacidade notável de atrair uma grande diversidade de vida marinha—às vezes comparável à biodiversidade dos recifes naturais. Essas estruturas oferecem superfícies sólidas para o crescimento de corais e esponjas, além de esconderijos e espaços para peixes, caranguejos e polvos. Até recentemente, não se sabia se esses habitats artificiais criam novas comunidades ecológicas ou apenas atraem organismos dos recifes naturais próximos. Essa diferença é importante para garantir a resiliência da vida marinha à medida que os recifes naturais desaparecem. Um estudo recente, publicado na revista Marine Biology, foi o primeiro a testar se recifes artificiais em regiões tropicais podem desempenhar as mesmas funções que recifes naturais. Os resultados são animadores: embora os recifes artificiais ainda não sejam idênticos aos naturais, começam a duplicar processos ecológicos essenciais e mostram potencial de melhora à medida que amadurecem. Os recifes naturais de coral são excelentes em sustentar a vida mesmo em águas tropicais pobres em nutrientes—um quebra-cabeça conhecido como Paradoxo de Darwin. Isso é possível porque os recifes reciclavam rapidamente os nutrientes entre as comunidades densamente povoadas, mantendo os níveis baixos e impedindo o crescimento excessivo de algas. Para comparar os tipos de recifes, pesquisadores mediram a ciclagem e o armazenamento de nutrientes em recifes artificiais e naturais, no norte de Bali, Indonésia. A iniciativa North Bali Reef Conservation, co-fundada por um dos pesquisadores, trabalhou com pescadores locais e voluntários internacionais para instalar mais de 15.000 módulos de recifes artificiais, cobrindo cerca de dois campos de futebol. Esses recifes artificiais apresentam sinais promissores. Altas leituras de fosfato logo abaixo da areia indicam a presença de muitos peixes, enquanto os níveis de nutrientes nas amostras de água acima dos sedimentos permaneceram baixos, como acontece em recifes naturais saudáveis—evidenciando reciclagem eficiente de nutrientes. Contudo, os sedimentos ao redor dos recifes artificiais armazenam menos carbono que os dos recifes naturais, provavelmente devido à menor quantidade de invertebrados. Com a colonização desses organismos ao longo do tempo, é esperado que os recifes artificiais passem a funcionar cada vez mais como recifes naturais. Essa pesquisa traz esperança de que os recifes artificiais podem, ao longo do tempo, replicar mais processos vistos nos recifes naturais e apoiar comunidades costeiras impactadas pela perda dos recifes. No entanto, os pesquisadores enfatizam que somente com uma drástica redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa será possível proteger verdadeiramente os ecossistemas de corais no futuro. Para recifes já perdidos por poluição, pesca predatória ou desenvolvimento, as estruturas artificiais podem ajudar a recuperar parte de seu valor ecossistêmico. Os cientistas sugerem que pode levar cerca de cinco anos para as comunidades de recifes artificiais começarem a funcionar como recifes naturais, reforçando a necessidade de iniciar os esforços de restauração o quanto antes.

article_content: Tottenham Hotspur and Arsenal will meet in the north London derby on Saturday lunchtime, with a place in the top four of the Premier League at stake. The hosts are two points behind the fifth-placed Gunners and could move ahead of them into a Champions League spot with a win. Arsenal are in impressive form, currently on a five-match winning run with four clean sheets. Below is a closer look at the strengths of each side, along with a combined best eleven from both squads. Goalkeeper – Hugo Lloris. With Arsene Wenger not favoring Wojciech Szczesny, David Ospina is Lloris' main competition, but the choice is clear. Lloris is reliable with both his hands and feet, often leaving his area to intercept danger. He is considered one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League. Right Back – Mathieu Debuchy. Both teams lack depth at right back. Kyle Walker has not developed as hoped, and Calum Chambers has struggled for form at Arsenal. Debuchy is the preferred choice, though injuries have affected his season. Nevertheless, on his day, he is strong in both defense and attack. Centre Backs – Jan Vertonghen & Laurent Koscielny. Vertonghen is a consistent performer for Spurs, and Koscielny is selected ahead of Per Mertesacker, whose form has dipped. This pairing offers balance and reliability. Left Back – Kieran Gibbs. Both Gibbs and Danny Rose are quick and attacking-minded, but Gibbs is chosen. Without injuries, he could be England’s first-choice left back, especially with Luke Shaw’s struggles at Manchester United. Right Midfield – Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain. Andros Townsend has yet to build on previous progress, while Oxlade-Chamberlain has become a vital player for Arsenal and England with his direct style. Central Midfield – Aaron Ramsey. Many candidates were considered, including Ryan Mason and Francis Coquelin, but Ramsey’s quality and composure earn him the spot. With six goals, he contributes in key moments and is a central figure for his team. Attacking Midfield – Christian Eriksen. Santi Cazorla and Mesut Ozil have shown moments of brilliance, but Eriksen’s consistency and 11 goals this season make him the standout. Left Midfield – Theo Walcott. Nacer Chadli is improving, but Walcott’s pace and finishing since his return from injury make him the top threat from wide areas. Second Striker – Alexis Sanchez. Versatile and relentless, Sanchez has impressed in his debut season with 18 goals, showcasing high work rate and skill. Striker – Harry Kane. Kane has outperformed fellow strikers at Spurs and rivals such as Giroud and Welbeck, scoring 20 goals so far. He is having a breakthrough season. Sports analysts from BSports predict that Arsenal are the most likely team to win the north London derby.

article_content: Thom Evans, the 28-year-old former Scottish rugby player, has taken on a new role as the face of the Aston Martin Collection by BespokeHQ. The Aston Martin Collection offers bespoke two- and three-piece suits, jackets, overcoats, shirts, and ties, all starting at £1,000. article_content: A significant drop in mega-cap tech stocks pulled the broader US stock market down on Wednesday. Alphabet's shares fell 10% after its third-quarter earnings showed a notable slowdown in cloud revenue growth. This weakness in the cloud sector also pushed Amazon's shares down by over 5%. Microsoft, however, was the exception among major tech firms, rising about 3% following strong earnings. The sell-off was compounded by higher bond yields, as the 10-year US Treasury yield climbed about 12 basis points to 4.95%. This sharp increase followed a five-year Treasury note auction that drew weak demand. Investors remain nervous ahead of next week's announcement on potential increases in Treasury auction sizes, worrying about an oversupply. In Washington, the US House of Representatives elected Mike Johnson as House Speaker after weeks of Republican disagreements since Kevin McCarthy's removal. Now, attention turns to whether Johnson can steer the House to pass a bill to prevent a government shutdown before the mid-November deadline. 'Markets, especially Treasury markets, needed to see government operations resume. Now, all eyes are on November 17 to keep the government open,' said Jamie Cox, managing partner at Harris Financial Group. At 4:00 p.m. Wednesday, US stock indexes closed as follows. Elsewhere, developments occurred in commodities, bonds, and cryptocurrency markets.

article_content: Cryptocurrency markets have seen dramatic price increases this week, with Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Solana at the forefront. The surge in prices is largely attributed to renewed optimism from institutional investors, particularly following BlackRock’s announcement of a new application for an Ethereum spot ETF, shortly after their previous Bitcoin ETF proposal. This development sparked a significant short squeeze in the Ethereum market, leading to record funding rates and considerable volatility among traders who bet against the asset. Markus Thielen, representing Matrixport, characterized the current climate as challenging for skeptics of Ethereum, highlighting that market-neutral hedge funds stand to benefit. The anticipation is that crypto hedge funds are likely to see increased investments amid these market shifts. After setbacks following the NFT market downturn and a cooling of web3 enthusiasm, Ethereum rebounded above $2,000, pushing up other major cryptocurrencies such as XRP and Solana as well. Further confidence in the crypto sector was bolstered by reports that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has initiated talks with Grayscale to possibly convert its Bitcoin trust into a spot ETF. According to eToro analyst Simon Peters, Bitcoin has broken through the previously stubborn $30,000–$31,000 resistance range, with eyes set on reaching $45,000, a level not seen since March 2022. In summary, the influx of institutional interest and favorable market news are strengthening sentiment and driving renewed excitement in the cryptocurrency space.

article_content: Atletico Madrid is struggling to overcome financial challenges in their attempt to re-sign Fernando Torres from Chelsea. Recently, Atletico’s chief executive Miguel Angel Gil visited London and tabled a £12.5 million bid for the 30-year-old forward, who previously starred for Liverpool. The negotiations are hitting a roadblock, as Torres is reluctant to accept a reduced salary of less than his current £8 million per year, and Chelsea is holding out for a fee closer to £20 million, having purchased him for £50 million three years ago. There is hope for a homecoming, as Torres could rejoin his childhood club, Atletico Madrid, but serious financial issues remain. Torres’s impact at Chelsea has not met expectations set during his successful stint at Liverpool, yet Chelsea is aiming to recover as much as possible on their investment. Additionally, Atletico’s coach Diego Simeone has expressed interest in welcoming Torres back to Vicente Calderon, though such a move would push the club’s finances to the limit. Alternative signings like Alvaro Negredo are hampered by his injury and a £26 million fee, making a transfer unlikely. Despite successful recent exchanges such as Diego Costa and Filipe Luis between Chelsea and Atletico, talks involving Romelu Lukaku have not advanced, as Simeone has his sights set on other players.

article_content: Swinhay House, situated near Wotton-under-Edge in the south Cotswolds, England, features an eye-catching glass roof and a prominent viewing tower. Known for its modern, eco-friendly approach, this mansion gained fame as ‘Appledore’—the residence of Sherlock Holmes’ adversary Charles Augustus Magnussen—in the BBC’s acclaimed detective series. In reality, Swinhay House is the innovative creation of Sir David McMurtry, renowned engineer and founder of Renishaw, who spent over £30 million developing the property. Spanning eleven floors, the mansion contains eight bedrooms arranged across several wings, and includes upscale amenities such as a two-lane bowling alley, squash court, a 25-meter swimming pool, an underground eight-bay garage, enclosed winter garden, and a panoramic viewing room. Despite its grandeur, Sir David chooses not to live in Swinhay House, as his wife Terry considers it too extravagant and prefers a smaller nearby residence. The home is a benchmark for sustainability, utilizing advanced energy-saving systems like geothermal heating, comprehensive insulation, and specialized triple-glazed windows imported from Scandinavia to optimize natural light and temperature control. Architect David Austin, recognized for his environmentally conscious methods, was responsible for the residence’s design, while Andy Rathbone designed the extensive 60 acres of landscaped gardens, which include a unique curving lake and decorative bird sculptures. The estate covers a total of more than 230 acres, incorporating woods, meadows, and orchards. Eye-catching architectural highlights include a bow-shaped gallery capped with a glass turret, a fully enclosed winter garden, and several self-contained apartments distributed over the eleven levels. Designed in collaboration with the architectural firm Roberts Limbrick, much of the home is partially built below ground, insulated by waterproof concrete for energy efficiency. The landscape is not only visually striking but also serves as part of the home’s heat-exchange system, using the artificial lake to help regulate temperature. Swinhay House is both a showcase of award-winning sustainable architecture and a sought-after location for television productions and fashion photography.

article_content: Park Geun-hye, known as the 'Queen of Elections,' reinforced her reputation after leading the ruling Saenuri Party to victory in South Korea's legislative vote. After securing a majority in the National Assembly, Park reiterated the party’s commitment to honoring their promises and moving away from past political errors. She stressed the importance of starting anew and not falling back on outdated practices. Saenuri clinched 152 out of 299 seats, while the Democratic United Party (DUP), the main opposition, won 127. This victory is expected to boost Park’s campaign in the December presidential election. DUP Secretary-General Park Sun-sook admitted the party's defeat, apologizing for missing the opportunity to turn public disappointment with the ruling government into electoral gains, despite earlier predictions of a DUP win. She promised the party would reflect deeply and work to regain the public’s trust. Voter turnout hit 54.3%, an increase of over eight percentage points from the previous election. The run-up to voting was marred by corruption scandals that undermined confidence in well-known parties. In response, the ruling party rebranded itself as Saenuri, leaving behind the Grand National Party name. Meanwhile, the DUP faced its own controversy after revelations that candidate Kim Yong-min made sexist remarks in a 2004 radio broadcast; the party apologized but kept Kim in his position.

O Saenuri conquistou 152 das 299 cadeiras, enquanto o principal partido de oposição, o Partido Democrático Unido (DUP), obteve 127. Essa vitória deve fortalecer a candidatura de Park nas eleições presidenciais de dezembro. O período pré-eleitoral foi marcado por escândalos de corrupção que fragilizaram a confiança nos partidos tradicionais. Como resposta, o partido governista adotou o nome Saenuri, deixando de lado a antiga denominação de Partido Grande Nacional. O DUP também encarou polêmica quando veio à tona que Kim Yong-min, um de seus candidatos, fez comentários sexistas em um programa de rádio em 2004; o partido pediu desculpas, mas não afastou Kim do cargo.

article_content: Polling for the 119-seat Telangana Assembly will take place on November 30. After failing to form a seat-sharing alliance with Congress, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] in Telangana on Sunday announced its first list of 14 candidates for the upcoming Legislative Assembly elections. CPI(M) state secretary Tammineni Veerabhadram will contest from Palair constituency in Khammam district, while former MLA Julakanti Ranga Reddy will seek re-election from Miryalguda. Veerabhadram stated that the party had earlier decided to contest 17 seats and is still considering additional candidates for a few more constituencies. In business news, India has cleared its first-ever 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) in the defense sector, allowing Swedish company Saab to set up a facility to manufacture rockets. The State Bank of India (SBI), the country’s largest lender, reported an 8% increase in its second-quarter net profit, driven by strong loan demand and reduced provisions. SBI anticipates continued robust loan growth supported by the expanding economy. Edtech company Byju’s released a delayed, partial audit for the fiscal year ending March 2022, reporting core business revenue of ₹3,569 crore—a 2.3 times increase in standalone business. The core business EBITDA loss narrowed to ₹2,253 crore in FY22, compared to ₹2,406 crore the previous year.

Veerabhadram afirmou que o partido havia decidido anteriormente disputar 17 cadeiras e ainda está avaliando a indicação de candidatos para mais alguns distritos. No setor de negócios, a Índia aprovou o primeiro investimento estrangeiro direto (IED) de 100% no setor de defesa, permitindo que a empresa sueca Saab instale uma fábrica para produzir foguetes. O State Bank of India (SBI), maior banco do país, registrou um aumento de 8% no lucro líquido do segundo trimestre, impulsionado pela forte demanda por empréstimos e pela redução de provisões. O SBI prevê continuidade no crescimento robusto dos empréstimos, apoiado pela expansão econômica geral. A edtech Byju’s divulgou uma auditoria parcial e atrasada referente ao exercício encerrado em março de 2022, mostrando receita de R$ 3.569 crore em seu negócio principal — um aumento de 2,3 vezes. article_content: Police divers have launched a search of two ponds in the woods at Burghfield, Berkshire, following a new tip about the 2002 disappearance of Catherine Nee. Catherine, known as Kathy, was 32 when she was last seen living in Ilfracombe, Devon, after becoming estranged from her family. Although her absence was at first considered voluntary, her family’s continued efforts led to a missing persons investigation starting in 2012. In 2013, a 48-year-old man from Thames Valley was arrested on suspicion of murder, but he was released without charge. Catherine, originally from Reading, Berkshire, has six grandchildren she has never met. Her mother, Nellie, now 71, continues to hope for her daughter’s return and says the family is eager to reconnect. Detective Inspector Kevin Mahon explained that police are searching the Burghfield ponds for clues linked to Catherine’s disappearance. The origin of the tip-off has not been disclosed, though it is confirmed it did not come from someone currently in prison. Authorities are urging anyone who knew Catherine or who might have information to come forward.

article_content: Rafael Nadal made tennis history by winning his fourth consecutive French Open title, dominant against world number one Roger Federer in the final. Nadal claimed victory with a straight-sets win—6-1, 6-3, 6-0—handing Federer his third straight defeat to Nadal at Roland Garros. This achievement places Nadal alongside Bjorn Borg as the only men to win the French Open four times in a row. Nadal didn't lose a set throughout the tournament and remains undefeated at the event, with 28 consecutive wins. Federer, hoping to secure the only Grand Slam that had eluded him, was hampered by unforced errors and unable to overcome Nadal's strong performance. Nadal quickly gained an advantage and maintained control for the entirety of the match, while Federer showed frustration over his play. Nadal was handed the trophy by six-time French Open winner Bjorn Borg. Despite the defeat, Federer congratulated Nadal and is now setting his sights on Wimbledon for a fresh opportunity.

Nadal não perdeu nenhum set durante toda a competição e mantém sua invencibilidade no evento, com 28 vitórias seguidas. article_content: Relations between the UK Labour Party and the US White House have become strained after US President Barack Obama voiced support for Prime Minister David Cameron and Conservative economic policies. Labour’s deputy leader, Harriet Harman, reacted publicly, suggesting President Obama does not fully understand the economic challenges faced by most British citizens. The tension emerged after Obama praised the UK’s economic progress during Cameron’s Washington visit, referring to the British leader as a ‘great friend’. With the UK’s general election approaching, this endorsement frustrated Labour officials, who have traditionally maintained strong links with America’s Democrats. Harman disagreed with Obama’s view that Britain’s economic growth signals things are going well, stressing that many families still struggle due to stagnant pay and rising living expenses, even if the broader statistics look positive. She voiced these concerns during an appearance on LBC Radio. Labour was particularly caught off guard by Obama’s public backing, especially since they had hired David Axelrod, a senior Obama campaign advisor. Some Labour members are questioning the benefit of this move. Labour leader Ed Miliband had hoped that his previous White House visit and meeting with President Obama would prevent a public endorsement of Cameron ahead of the election. Instead, Obama’s warm remarks about Cameron have increased frustration among Labour’s leadership.

article_content: French riot police clashed with train workers during a week-long strike, resulting in some of the worst disruption to the country's rail network in years. Angry train staff hurled bottles and blocked traffic over a bill to reform the state-run railway system. The unrest shows no signs of stopping as the reform bill heads to the lower house of Parliament for debate today. During the demonstrations, a man was seen photographing while walking through smoke from a flare. Police fired tear gas at train workers protesting the proposed reforms to the Paris rail system. The protests turned violent as train workers and police confronted each other over the changes to the state-run railway laws. The bill seeks to unite the SNCF, the state-owned train operator, with the RFF railway network. This move would pave the way to open railways to competition. Workers worry the reforms could result in job losses and reduced security. The government argues the reform is vital to create a stronger railway structure, as France and other European countries gear up for railway liberalization. Several hundred workers protested near the National Assembly on Paris' Left Bank on Tuesday, waving red union flags and demanding the bill be delayed or amended. Protesters blocked cars, attempted to breach police barricades near parliament, and set off flares while throwing bottles. Officers responded with tear gas and batons, detaining several protesters. Eventually, the protesters retreated and continued demonstrating peacefully. Commuters arriving at Paris train stations, such as Gare de l'Est and Gare de Lyon, faced substantial delays. Many trains were canceled, causing congestion and frustration among travelers. Some Paris commuters had to rely on the few trains available or alternate modes of transport. Later on Tuesday, French television footage showed protesters marching onto train tracks at Paris' Montparnasse station, a major hub for travel to western and southwestern France. The strike began last Wednesday and, though involving only a minority of workers, has caused widespread disruption on national and commuter train services. About one-third of trains were canceled nationwide on Tuesday. While international lines such as the Eurostar between Paris and London were unaffected, the strike created difficulties for international travelers using commuter rail to reach Charles de Gaulle Airport. Prime Minister Manuel Valls broke with tradition by commenting publicly, stating Monday that the strike was 'not useful and not responsible.' Lawmakers began debating the bill Tuesday afternoon.
translated_content: A tropa de choque francesa entrou em confronto com trabalhadores ferroviários durante uma greve que já dura uma semana, causando algumas das maiores interrupções na rede ferroviária do país em anos. Funcionários revoltados lançaram garrafas e bloquearam o trânsito em protesto contra um projeto de lei para reformar o sistema ferroviário estatal. A agitação não dá sinais de parar, já que o projeto segue para debate na câmara baixa do Parlamento hoje. Durante as manifestações, um homem foi visto tirando fotos enquanto caminhava pela fumaça de um sinalizador. A polícia usou gás lacrimogêneo contra ferroviários que protestavam contra as reformas propostas para o sistema ferroviário de Paris. Os protestos ficaram violentos quando trabalhadores e policiais se enfrentaram devido às mudanças nas leis do setor. O projeto de lei busca unir a SNCF, operadora estatal de trens, com a rede ferroviária RFF. Esse passo abriria caminho para a concorrência no setor ferroviário. Trabalhadores temem que as reformas possam resultar em perda de empregos e menos segurança. O governo afirma que a reforma é essencial para criar uma estrutura mais forte, enquanto França e outros países europeus se preparam para a liberalização do setor. Centenas de trabalhadores protestaram perto da Assembleia Nacional, na margem esquerda de Paris, na terça-feira, agitando bandeiras sindicais vermelhas e exigindo a suspensão ou alteração do projeto. Manifestantes bloquearam carros, tentaram passar pelas barreiras policiais próximas ao parlamento e acenderam sinalizadores, além de lançar garrafas. Os policiais reagiram com gás lacrimogêneo e cassetetes, detendo alguns manifestantes. Por fim, os manifestantes recuaram e continuaram o protesto de forma pacífica. Passageiros que chegavam às estações de trem de Paris, como Gare de l'Est e Gare de Lyon, enfrentaram longos atrasos. Muitos trens foram cancelados, gerando congestionamentos e frustração entre os viajantes. Alguns parisienses tiveram que contar com os poucos trens disponíveis ou procurar formas alternativas de transporte. Mais tarde, na terça-feira, imagens da TV francesa mostraram manifestantes caminhando pelos trilhos na estação Montparnasse, importante ponto de ligação com cidades do oeste e sudoeste da França. A greve começou na quarta-feira passada e, embora envolva apenas uma minoria de trabalhadores, causou ampla interrupção nos serviços regionais e nacionais. Cerca de um terço dos trens foi cancelado em todo o país na terça-feira. Embora linhas internacionais como a Eurostar entre Paris e Londres não tenham sido afetadas, a greve dificultou a vida de quem tentava chegar ao aeroporto Charles de Gaulle usando os trens locais. O primeiro-ministro Manuel Valls quebrou a tradição ao se pronunciar publicamente, afirmando na segunda-feira que a greve era 'inútil e irresponsável'. Os parlamentares começaram a debater o projeto na tarde de terça-feira.

article_content:
For most children, a bump or scrape is a normal part of everyday life. But for two-year-old Hugo Tornqvist, even the slightest touch can trigger a life-threatening chain of events. Hugo was born with Junctional Herlitz Epidermolysis Bullosa (JEB), a rare genetic disorder that makes his skin extremely fragile, causing it to blister and peel with minimal friction. Doctors initially predicted Hugo would not live past eight months, but he has defied the odds.

Living just outside Karlskrona, Sweden, with his mother Hanna and her partner Magnus, Hugo endures daily challenges. The only visible sign of his condition is his sensitive skin, which develops sores and blisters easily. Internally, his entire body is affected, and he faces serious complications such as respiratory problems that can cause his airways to suddenly close. Last summer, Hugo was hospitalized with severe breathing difficulties, and on another occasion, his eyes were swollen shut for three weeks.

At one point, blisters covered 70% of his body, but today this has reduced to around 15%. Despite a compromised immune system and the need for tube feeding due to throat scarring, Hugo has developed at a normal pace. The family’s home is specially adapted, with soft padding throughout, especially in his bedroom, to minimize injury. Hugo is not permitted to interact with other children, and his siblings can only visit every other weekend to reduce his risk of infection.

His mother shares that each day with Hugo is a blessing, but the family can only plan a couple of days ahead due to the uncertainty of his condition. Despite everything, she describes Hugo as a resilient and cheerful child. JEB is so rare that doctors have few answers about Hugo's outlook. The family encountered challenges with their insurance provider early on, but now they receive full support for Hugo’s care.

Most children with Herlitz JEB do not survive infancy, with around 40% dying during the first year and nearly all by age five. Complications include chronic wounds, respiratory failure, infection (sepsis), finger and toe fusion, joint deformities, and hair loss. The condition can also lead to malnutrition because of internal blistering and scarring.

Despite the hardships, Hugo’s mother remains hopeful, saying that they fight every day for Hugo and for other families facing this rare disease.
translated_content:
Para a maioria das crianças, um esbarrão ou arranhão faz parte do dia a dia. Mas, para o pequeno Hugo Tornqvist, de dois anos, até o menor toque pode desencadear uma sequência de eventos que ameaça sua vida. Hugo nasceu com Epidermólise Bolhosa Juncional Herlitz (JEB), uma doença genética rara que torna sua pele extremamente frágil, fazendo com que ela forme bolhas e descasque ao menor atrito. Os médicos inicialmente previram que Hugo não viveria além dos oito meses, mas ele superou todas as expectativas.

Vivendo nos arredores de Karlskrona, na Suécia, com sua mãe Hanna e o parceiro dela, Magnus, Hugo enfrenta desafios diários. O único sinal visível da condição é a pele sensível, que desenvolve feridas e bolhas facilmente. Internamente, todo o seu corpo é afetado, e ele sofre complicações graves, como problemas respiratórios que podem fazer suas vias aéreas fecharem de repente. No último verão, Hugo foi hospitalizado por dificuldades respiratórias graves e, em outra ocasião, seus olhos ficaram completamente inchados por três semanas.

Em determinado momento, bolhas cobriam 70% de seu corpo, mas hoje esse número caiu para cerca de 15%. Apesar da imunidade baixa e da necessidade de alimentação por sonda devido a cicatrizes na garganta, Hugo se desenvolveu normalmente. A casa da família é especialmente adaptada, com almofadados em todos os cômodos, principalmente em seu quarto, para minimizar ferimentos. Hugo não pode ter contato com outras crianças e seus irmãos só podem visitá-lo a cada duas semanas para reduzir o risco de infecções.

Sua mãe conta que cada dia ao lado de Hugo é uma bênção, mas a família só consegue planejar dois dias por vez devido à incerteza da condição. Apesar de tudo, ela descreve Hugo como uma criança forte e alegre. A JEB é tão rara que os médicos têm poucas respostas sobre o futuro de Hugo. A família enfrentou dificuldades com a seguradora no início, mas agora já recebe apoio total para os cuidados de Hugo.

A maioria das crianças com JEB Herlitz não sobrevive à infância, sendo que cerca de 40% falecem no primeiro ano e quase todas antes dos cinco anos. Complicações incluem feridas crônicas, insuficiência respiratória, infecção (sepse), fusão dos dedos, deformidades nas articulações e queda de cabelo. A doença também pode causar desnutrição devido às bolhas e cicatrizes internas.

Apesar dos desafios, a mãe de Hugo mantém a esperança e afirma que lutam todos os dias por ele e por outras famílias que enfrentam essa doença rara.

article_content: Ahead of a town hall meeting on Tuesday night, Ferguson's mayor said that the aftermath of Michael Brown's shooting death brought attention to the city's racial divide. "I think what it showed was ... even though I always knew that African-Americans had experiences that were definitely frustrating, many of those issues never surfaced. What opened my eyes was how significant that frustration can be for many people," Mayor James Knowles said. Police Chief Thomas Jackson agreed with the mayor. "The issues that have come up since the shooting have made us realize that there is still a lot of work to be done," Jackson stated. Jackson emphasized that community outreach is a crucial step the police department and the local government need to take to make Ferguson more unified. Protests began last month after Ferguson Officer Darren Wilson fatally shot unarmed 18-year-old Michael Brown. Some nights, the protests turned into looting, vandalism, and violence before they eventually calmed. Jackson has tried to improve relations by attending daily protests in city streets. On one occasion, after apologizing on Thursday, Jackson met with demonstrators, but not everyone welcomed his presence. "If you are not resigning tonight, go home," a protester shouted using a bullhorn. Shortly after Jackson agreed to walk and talk with the protestors, a scuffle broke out behind him, prompting officers to make arrests. Jackson was quickly escorted inside a building, though there was no indication he was threatened. For several hours, police officers stood in front of the police department, with protesters nearby—some mingling, others chanting. Despite tensions, Jackson said he will continue attending the protests. "I don't think it's ever a mistake for me to engage with people who want to talk to me and my police department. I think it's important to keep communication open. If some want to turn it into a hostile situation, that's their decision, not mine. I wish things had turned out differently," he said. The chief blamed outsiders for causing problems. Jackson stated last week that he would not resign, and Mayor Knowles, who was re-elected in April, said now isn't the time for that change. "We're moving forward as a community. If we change leadership now, I'm not sure that will help," he said. The upcoming town hall meeting, which is closed to the media, comes two nights after the latest violent protests. Police say eight people were arrested for failing to disperse and resisting arrest outside the police department on Sunday night when protests turned violent. Lt. Ron Miesner of the Missouri State Highway Patrol said that only one was from Ferguson, while the rest were from elsewhere in the St. Louis area: three from St. Louis, one from Richmond Heights, one from Florissant, one from Bridgeton, and one person was homeless. Last week, the burning of a memorial near the site where Brown was killed reignited protests. Sunday's demonstrations occurred in front of the police station, about 2 miles from the usual protest location. Previous protests at the police station had been mostly peaceful, but on Sunday, according to CNN affiliate KTVI, some in a crowd of about 150 threw rocks and bottles at officers around 10 p.m. No injuries were reported. The eight people arrested were taken to a nearby jail, booked, and released, KTVI reported.

"Acho que o que ficou claro foi... mesmo eu sempre soubendo que os afro-americanos tinham experiências definitivamente frustrantes, muitos desses problemas nunca vieram à tona. O que me abriu os olhos foi perceber o quanto essa frustração pode ser significativa para muitas pessoas", disse o prefeito James Knowles. O chefe de polícia Thomas Jackson concordou com o prefeito. "As questões que surgiram desde o tiroteio nos fizeram perceber que ainda há muito trabalho a ser feito", afirmou Jackson. Jackson destacou que o alcance comunitário é um passo crucial que o departamento de polícia e o governo local precisam dar para tornar Ferguson mais unido. Os protestos começaram no mês passado após o policial de Ferguson Darren Wilson matar o jovem desarmado Michael Brown, de 18 anos. Em algumas noites, os protestos se transformaram em saques, vandalismo e violência até finalmente se acalmarem. Jackson tentou melhorar as relações indo aos protestos diários nas ruas da cidade. Em uma dessas ocasiões, após pedir desculpas na quinta-feira, Jackson se encontrou com manifestantes, mas nem todos receberam bem sua presença. "Se você não vai renunciar hoje à noite, vá para casa", gritou um manifestante com um megafone. Logo após Jackson concordar em caminhar e conversar com os manifestantes, uma confusão aconteceu atrás dele, levando policiais a fazerem prisões. Jackson foi rapidamente escoltado para dentro de um prédio, embora não houvesse indício de que estivesse ameaçado. Por várias horas, policiais ficaram em frente ao departamento de polícia, com manifestantes próximos—alguns circulando, outros entoando cantos. Apesar das tensões, Jackson disse que continuará indo aos protestos. "Não acho que esteja errado engajar com pessoas que querem conversar comigo e com meu departamento de polícia. Acho importante manter a comunicação aberta. Se alguns querem transformar a situação em algo hostil, é decisão deles, não minha. Gostaria que as coisas tivessem sido diferentes", disse ele. O chefe culpou pessoas de fora por causarem problemas. Jackson afirmou, na semana passada, que não iria renunciar, e o prefeito Knowles, que foi reeleito em abril, disse que agora não é hora para essa mudança. "Estamos avançando como comunidade. Se mudarmos a liderança agora, não sei se isso ajudaria", declarou. A próxima reunião pública, fechada à imprensa, acontece dois dias após os protestos violentos mais recentes. Segundo a polícia, oito pessoas foram presas por se recusarem a dispersar e resistirem à prisão do lado de fora do departamento de polícia no domingo à noite, quando os protestos se tornaram violentos. O tenente Ron Miesner, da Patrulha Rodoviária do Estado do Missouri, informou que apenas um era de Ferguson; os demais eram de outras áreas de St. Louis: três de St. Louis, um de Richmond Heights, um de Florissant, um de Bridgeton e uma pessoa em situação de rua. Na semana passada, o incêndio de um memorial próximo ao local onde Brown foi morto reacendeu os protestos. As manifestações de domingo aconteceram em frente à delegacia, a cerca de 3 km do local usual dos protestos. Protestos anteriores na delegacia foram em sua maioria pacíficos, mas no domingo, segundo a afiliada da CNN KTVI, algumas pessoas entre cerca de 150 presentes jogaram pedras e garrafas nos policiais por volta das 22h. Não houve relatos de feridos. As oito pessoas detidas foram levadas para uma cadeia próxima, fichadas e liberadas, informou a KTVI.

article_content: Gabriela Ionescu, a 32-year-old woman from Carei in north-western Romania, has rebuilt her life after enduring years of domestic abuse. She married young to escape her home, but her first husband was violent and ultimately knocked out most of her teeth. Following the breakdown of this marriage at age 27, Gabriela remarried quickly. Her second husband, however, was emotionally abusive—belittling her appearance and treating her as domestic help. Gabriela struggled with her self-image and avoided social situations, feeling unattractive and lacking self-worth. Unable to afford dental reconstruction, she believed people judged her by her looks. Everything changed when she saw an advertisement for a Romanian reality TV show offering free plastic and dental surgery in exchange for the right to document the process. Gabriela applied and was selected, receiving a new set of teeth that transformed her appearance. Seeing this positive change gave her the confidence she needed to leave her second husband and start a new life. Gabriela now reports feeling excellent and happy, surrounded by supportive friends and feeling empowered by her transformation.

Após o fim desse casamento, aos 27 anos, Gabriela rapidamente se casou novamente. No entanto, o segundo marido era emocionalmente abusivo — menosprezava sua aparência e a tratava como empregada doméstica. Gabriela enfrentava dificuldades com sua autoestima e evitava situações sociais, sentindo-se pouco atraente e sem valor próprio. Sem condições de pagar pela reconstrução dentária, acreditava que as pessoas a julgavam pela aparência. Tudo mudou quando ela viu um anúncio de um reality show romeno oferecendo cirurgia plástica e dentária gratuita em troca do direito de documentar o processo. Gabriela se inscreveu e foi selecionada, recebendo um novo conjunto de dentes que transformou sua aparência. Gabriela agora relata que se sente ótima e feliz, cercada de amigos apoiadores e fortalecida por sua transformação.

article_content: Saudi Arabia is on course to host the 2034 FIFA World Cup after being the sole nation to submit a hosting interest, according to FIFA. The decision is set to be made official at the end of next year, contingent upon Saudi Arabia satisfying all required technical standards. The kingdom has been investing significantly in sports such as football, Formula One, and golf, and is now positioned to step in after the unprecedented 2030 World Cup, which will be jointly organized by Spain, Portugal, and Morocco, with select matches taking place in South America. This announcement comes a year following Qatar’s historic role as the first Middle Eastern World Cup host in 2022. During that tournament, Saudi Arabia’s team achieved a surprising victory over eventual champions Argentina in the group stage. At this stage, only preliminary expressions of interest have been recorded for 2034. FIFA will evaluate the full bids for both 2030 and 2034 before holding votes at separate congresses at the end of 2024. Although Saudi Arabia faces no bidding competition, leading to a likely selection, there remain concerns related to the environmental impact of the expanded 2030 tournament and whether Saudi Arabia's approach aligns with FIFA’s human rights standards for 2034.

A decisão deve ser oficializada no fim do próximo ano, caso a Arábia Saudita cumpra todos os requisitos técnicos. O reino vem investindo muito em esportes como futebol, Fórmula 1 e golfe e agora está prestes a assumir após a inédita Copa do Mundo de 2030, que será organizada conjuntamente por Espanha, Portugal e Marrocos, com algumas partidas na América do Sul. Esse anúncio surge um ano após o papel histórico do Catar como primeiro anfitrião do Oriente Médio em 2022. Naquele torneio, a seleção saudita surpreendeu ao vencer a futura campeã Argentina na fase de grupos. No momento, apenas manifestações preliminares de interesse foram registradas para 2034. A FIFA avaliará as propostas completas para 2030 e 2034 antes de realizar as votações em congressos separados no final de 2024. Apesar de não haver concorrentes para 2034, o que praticamente garante a escolha da Arábia Saudita, seguem em debate preocupações sobre o impacto ambiental do torneio ampliado de 2030 e a compatibilidade da postura do país com os padrões de direitos humanos da FIFA para 2034.

article_content: A retired New York City detective has applied forensic science to help resolve one of the art world's long-standing mysteries involving the authenticity of a disputed Jackson Pollock painting. For 57 years, Ruth Kligman, Pollock's mistress, claimed that he created the painting 'Red, Black & Silver' as a love token just a month before he died in a car accident. Recently, forensic expert Nicholas Petraco has supported her story with the discovery of a polar bear fur, a hair matching Pollock, and sand unique to Pollock’s neighborhood embedded in the painting. Abstract artist Jackson Pollock was photographed with Ruth Kligman before his death in 1956. Kligman consistently said that 'Red, Black & Silver' was painted for her. 'Red, Black & Silver,' which appeared on the cover of Kligman’s memoir, is believed to be Pollock’s last work, according to her. Kligman, who began her relationship with Pollock at age 26, recalled watching him create the 2ft x 2ft abstract artwork after she asked him to demonstrate his painting technique. After Kligman's death in 2010, her estate trustees asked retired detective Petraco to use forensic analysis to investigate the painting. He found polar bear fur from a rug in Pollock's East Hampton home, a hair matching Pollock, and local sand within the artwork. Jonathan Cramer, a co-trustee of the estate, told the New York Post, 'There’s a polar bear hair in the painting... It’s like CSI. Science can now be used to authenticate the art, tracing the painting back to where it was made.' This is a pioneering use of crime scene investigation techniques to authenticate art by examining what is within the painting itself. If the trustees validate Petraco’s findings, Kligman’s estate could benefit greatly; a Pollock of similar size sold for $58.3 million at Sotheby’s in May last year. Art investigators typically use fingerprints, brushstroke and signature analysis, and carbon dating to determine authenticity. Such clues can lead to significant gains for collectors. In another case, a $5 thrift store painting was offered $5 million after forensic analysis linked a fingerprint on the canvas to Pollock. While it wasn’t officially certified, it became highly valuable to collectors. For 'Red, Black & Silver,' Petraco identified Pollock's hair, East Hampton sand, and fur from a polar bear skin rug that Pollock owned. Kligman, described as strikingly beautiful, tried for decades to have the painting recognized as Pollock's final work. According to her, Pollock presented it to her as, 'Here’s your painting, your very own Pollock.' Kligman met Pollock at Cedar Tavern in Greenwich Village while working at a gallery; Pollock was 44 and reportedly drinking heavily. In her 1974 memoir, 'Love Affair: A Memoir of Jackson Pollock,' Kligman describes watching Pollock create 'Red, Black & Silver' on his East Hampton lawn one July afternoon and calls it 'the final painting of your life, your legacy to me.' A month after that day, Kligman survived the car crash that killed Pollock and another woman. With Pollock's widow, Lee Krasner, on the authentication board, Kligman’s attempts to have the painting certified were unsuccessful. Kligman, an artist and muse to many, died in 2010. Her estate included 'Red, Black & Silver,' over 700 artworks, and letters from artists and friends such as Willem de Kooning, Franz Kline, and Andy Warhol. As she had no heirs, the painting’s future is uncertain.
translated_content: Um detetive aposentado de Nova York aplicou ciência forense para ajudar a resolver um dos antigos mistérios do mundo da arte envolvendo a autenticidade de uma pintura disputada de Jackson Pollock. Durante 57 anos, Ruth Kligman, amante de Pollock, afirmou que ele criou a obra 'Red, Black & Silver' como prova de amor, apenas um mês antes de morrer em um acidente de carro. Recentemente, o especialista forense Nicholas Petraco apoiou sua história com a descoberta de pelo de urso polar, um fio de cabelo compatível com o de Pollock e areia específica do bairro do artista, encontrados na pintura. O artista abstrato Jackson Pollock foi fotografado com Ruth Kligman antes de sua morte em 1956. Kligman sempre disse que 'Red, Black & Silver' foi pintada para ela. 'Red, Black & Silver', que aparece na capa das memórias de Kligman, é considerada por ela como a última obra de Pollock. Kligman, que começou seu relacionamento com Pollock aos 26 anos, lembra-se de vê-lo criar a obra abstrata de 60cm x 60cm após pedir que ele mostrasse como pintava. Após a morte de Kligman, em 2010, os curadores de seu espólio pediram ao detetive Petraco para realizar uma análise forense da pintura. Ele encontrou pelo de urso polar vindo de um tapete da casa de Pollock em East Hampton, um cabelo compatível e areia local misturados à obra. Jonathan Cramer, coadministrador do espólio, disse ao New York Post: 'Há um pelo de urso polar na pintura... É tipo CSI. Agora a ciência pode autenticar a arte, rastreando a obra até o local de origem.' É um uso inovador de técnicas de investigação criminal para autenticar obras de arte por meio dos materiais contidos na própria pintura. Se os curadores aceitarem as descobertas de Petraco, o espólio de Kligman pode ser muito beneficiado; uma obra de tamanho semelhante de Pollock foi vendida por US$ 58,3 milhões na Sotheby's em maio do ano passado. Investigadores de arte normalmente usam impressões digitais, análise de pinceladas, assinaturas e datação por carbono para determinar a autenticidade. Esses pequenos indícios podem render grandes ganhos a colecionadores. Em outro caso, uma pintura comprada num brechó por US$ 5 foi avaliada em US$ 5 milhões após análise forense encontrar uma digital na tela ligada a Pollock. Embora não tenha sido oficialmente certificada, tornou-se muito valiosa para colecionadores. Em 'Red, Black & Silver', Petraco identificou cabelo de Pollock, areia de East Hampton e pelo de um tapete de urso polar pertencente ao artista. Kligman, considerada muito bonita, tentou durante décadas que a obra fosse reconhecida como o último trabalho de Pollock. Segundo ela, Pollock teria dito: 'Aqui está sua pintura, seu próprio Pollock.' Kligman conheceu Pollock no Cedar Tavern, em Greenwich Village, enquanto trabalhava em uma galeria; Pollock tinha 44 anos e era conhecido por beber bastante. Em suas memórias de 1974, 'Love Affair: A Memoir of Jackson Pollock', Kligman conta que viu Pollock criar 'Red, Black & Silver' no gramado de sua casa em East Hampton numa tarde de julho, dizendo que era 'a última pintura de sua vida, seu legado para mim.' Um mês depois, Kligman sobreviveu ao acidente que matou Pollock e outra mulher. Com a viúva de Pollock, Lee Krasner, no conselho de autenticação, as tentativas de Kligman de certificar a pintura não tiveram sucesso. Kligman, artista e musa de muitos, morreu em 2010. Seu espólio incluiu 'Red, Black & Silver', mais de 700 obras de arte e cartas de artistas e amigos como Willem de Kooning, Franz Kline e Andy Warhol. Sem herdeiros, o futuro da pintura é incerto.

article_content: A new analysis by Save the Children reveals a worrying trend: by the end of 2023, an estimated 17 million children will be born into hunger, a figure representing a 22% jump from ten years ago. This means that every minute, 33 infants will enter the world already facing severe food insecurity. The child rights organization’s data—drawn from UN and FAO statistics—shows almost one-fifth more newborns suffering from hunger in 2023 compared to 2013, when the number was 14.4 million. Economic turmoil, ongoing conflicts, and frequent climate disasters are cited as main contributors to this growing crisis. The situation is especially dire in Africa and Asia, which together account for 95% of undernourished newborns worldwide. The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) stands out as the country where hunger among infants is most acute; 1.5 million babies are projected to be born malnourished in the DRC in 2023, marking a record high for the nation. Overall, 6.6 million Congolese children under age five are expected to suffer from undernutrition this year. Personal accounts from those affected underscore the grim reality. Sifa, a 33-year-old mother living in a displacement camp in North Kivu, DRC, describes her constant struggle to provide enough food for her five children, fearing the loss of another child to hunger after losing three to disease and violence. She often sacrifices her own meals for her children and sends her daughter out in search of food despite the dangers. In Afghanistan, among Asian countries facing severe undernutrition, the situation is no less dire. Around 440,000 babies are forecasted to be born into hunger. Zolaikha, 23, speaks of her 10-month-old daughter Marium, who became severely ill due to malnutrition and unsafe water. The family's limited income means nutritious food is out of reach, leaving her children vulnerable to sickness and pain. Vishna Shah-Little, a regional director with Save the Children, warns that millions of children risk having their childhoods stolen by hunger—threatening their health, dreams, and futures. She urges urgent action to safeguard these children before it's too late. At a recent food security summit in the UK, Save the Children emphasized that resolving child hunger requires ending conflicts, addressing the climate crisis, reducing global inequality, and investing in stronger health and social protection systems. The group calls for enhanced collaboration, investment, and grassroots leadership to prepare for and prevent crises. Save the Children additionally urges world leaders to expand affordable, community-based interventions to treat and prevent malnutrition, promote breastfeeding, and strengthen local healthcare. Without decisive, large-scale action, these warnings may keep repeating themselves in the years ahead.

article_content: The Osun State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has accused Governor Ademola Adeleke of taking credit for projects in the state that were actually funded by a private individual. On Tuesday, Governor Adeleke and his Edo State counterpart, Godwin Obaseki, inaugurated projects in Ilesa that were donated by Chief Olakanmi Sarumi. During the event, Governor Adeleke encouraged Osun indigenes worldwide to participate in the state's tax credit scheme for infrastructure development, describing it as a win-win for residents. However, APC Osun chairman, Tajudeen Lawal, asserted that the tax credit initiative mentioned in relation to the Ilesa projects originated from former governor Adegboyega Oyetola. Lawal stated, 'The government lacks ingenuity and creativity. The recent events in Ilesa, where credit was taken for projects funded by Mr. Sarumi, show a decline in governance standards.' He further argued that it was misleading for Governor Adeleke’s spokesperson to suggest the projects inaugurated by Governor Obaseki were the product of Adeleke’s tax credit policy. Lawal emphasized that the tax credit scheme was begun under Oyetola's administration, noting the projects were at an advanced stage before Adeleke took office in November 2022. While recognizing the need for government continuity, Lawal criticized attempts to claim credit for work initiated under the previous administration or by private individuals. In response, Osun Governor’s spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, clarified that Governor Adeleke was invited to commission the road financed by Sarumi and did not claim the state government built it. Rasheed added that the current administration has completed over 55 kilometers of roads, with another 45 kilometers ongoing, and does not claim credit for projects it did not undertake. He defended the governor’s encouragement of private contributions to community development and dismissed APC’s criticism as political distractions. Rasheed concluded that Governor Adeleke remains focused on enhancing infrastructure and rebuilding the state despite opposition criticism.

article_content: Erin Mendenhall has been re-elected as Salt Lake City’s mayor, prevailing over former mayor Rocky Anderson in a ranked-choice election. The latest ballot count released Wednesday shows Mendenhall with 58% of the vote, compared to Anderson's 34%, as reported by the Salt Lake Tribune. Anderson conceded the race in a phone call to Mendenhall and wished her well in her continued leadership. Despite the mayoral role being nonpartisan, Salt Lake City leans Democratic, distinguishing it from the predominantly Republican state of Utah. At her election night event, Mendenhall pledged to tackle her second term with revitalized energy, viewing her win as a mandate for progress and unity rather than fear-based division. A debate held in late October brought attention to significant local issues, including water conservation, climate change, crime, and homelessness. Anderson, who previously served as mayor between 2000 and 2008, criticized Mendenhall for her approach to housing affordability, advocating for city-led mixed-income housing rather than reliance on private developers. This was Salt Lake City’s first major election using the ranked-choice voting system, implemented in 2021. The process enables voters to rank up to three candidates by preference, redistributing votes from eliminated candidates until a majority winner emerges.

Embora o cargo de prefeito seja oficialmente apartidário, Salt Lake City tem tendência democrata, ao contrário do estado de Utah, que é majoritariamente republicano. Durante a comemoração na noite da eleição, Mendenhall prometeu iniciar o novo mandato com energia renovada, interpretando o resultado como um apoio ao progresso e à união, rejeitando a divisão motivada pelo medo. Um debate realizado no final de outubro abordou temas importantes para a cidade, como conservação da água, mudanças climáticas, criminalidade e pessoas em situação de rua. Esse método permite que os eleitores classifiquem até três candidatos, redistribuindo os votos dos eliminados até que um dos candidatos atinja a maioria simples.
