Há uma década, as relações entre França e Estados Unidos eram tensas. A oposição francesa à invasão do Iraque pelos EUA em 2003 resultou em gestos como a troca do nome 'batatas fritas' para 'freedom fries' pelos americanos, além de um aumento do sentimento anti-França. Hoje, no entanto, ao buscar apoio para possível ação militar na Síria, o secretário de Estado John Kerry chama a França de 'nosso aliado mais antigo', e o presidente francês François Hollande reforça a amizade entre os dois países.

Enquanto isso, o Reino Unido — aliado tradicional dos EUA — enfrentou um raro revés depois que o Parlamento votou contra o envolvimento na Síria, deixando o premiê David Cameron em uma posição desconfortável. Isso colocou a França como principal aliada de Washington, enquanto o Reino Unido assume um papel secundário nas discussões sobre possível intervenção militar.

O relacionamento entre França e EUA já alternou entre parceria próxima e divergências. A França apoiou a Revolução Americana, mas criticou intervenções militares lideradas pelos EUA em tempos recentes. Em 2003, o presidente Jacques Chirac se opôs à invasão do Iraque sem aval da ONU, alertando para riscos ao multilateralismo internacional. A postura de Chirac foi criticada por autoridades dos EUA, como o então secretário de Defesa Donald Rumsfeld, que chamou a França de 'velha Europa.'

A resistência francesa à estratégia militar americana é antiga. Por exemplo, durante os ataques aéreos dos EUA à Líbia em 1986, após atentado a soldados americanos em Berlim, a França negou uso de seu espaço aéreo. Recentemente, Hollande informou a Obama que retiraria as tropas francesas do Afeganistão, mas a França apoiou a campanha da OTAN na Líbia sob Nicolas Sarkozy e enviou forças ao Mali em 2013 para combater militantes islamistas, a convite do governo malinês.

Apesar da cooperação atual, grande parte da população francesa se opõe à intervenção na Síria. Pesquisas mostram que quase dois terços dos franceses rejeitam a ação militar, e 58% não confiam na liderança de Hollande nesse contexto.

Mesmo com o novo destaque da França junto a Washington, é cedo para descartar o forte 'relacionamento especial' entre EUA e Reino Unido. Apesar do revés no Parlamento britânico, ambos governos reafirmam a parceria, destacando sua resiliência. EUA e Reino Unido já estiveram juntos em conflitos como a Guerra das Malvinas e a Segunda Guerra Mundial, e tendem a se alinhar novamente futuramente.

Enquanto isso, Obama busca fortalecer alianças com França, Turquia e parceiros árabes regionais, enquanto o Reino Unido se reorganiza diplomaticamente.

A leaked image allegedly shows Samsung's upcoming Galaxy handset, according to a Dutch website. The device appears to have a 5.5-inch display and is rumored to feature either a 16 or 20-megapixel camera. The official unveiling is expected at Mobile World Congress, held in Barcelona from March 2-5. The image depicts a phone with a very thin bezel and rounded edges resembling the iPhone 6. Previous reports from BGR suggest the model, possibly codenamed SM-G925F (likely the Galaxy S6), will include a 5.5-inch Quad HD (2560 x 1440) display, an octa-core processor, Mali-T768 GPU, and a 16-megapixel rear camera. However, the French site nowherele.fr claims the leaked image actually shows another Samsung model, not the Galaxy S6.

Earlier this month, Samsung announced plans to reduce the number of smartphones it produces each year by 25–33% due to heightened competition and a drop in profits. Instead of saturating the market, Samsung aims to focus on making fewer, higher-quality devices while ramping up production of these core models for cost efficiency.

Despite declining profits, Samsung maintained its lead in global smartphone shipments for the last quarter—though it was the only top-five manufacturer to record a sales decline. According to IDC, Samsung's shipments fell 8% to 78.1 million units, dropping its market share from 33% to 24% year-over-year. Meanwhile, Apple, Xiaomi, Lenovo, and LG each reported shipment growth exceeding 15%.

Samsung's earlier partnership with Android helped it become a global leader, but now other Android manufacturers are matching its performance and design. Despite reporting its lowest quarterly earnings in three years (July–September profits at £2.5 billion or $3.8 billion, down from £6 billion or $9.5 billion in 2013), Samsung shares rose 4% in Seoul following better-than-expected results and optimism for a strong fourth quarter.

At a presentation in New York, Samsung's head of investor relations, Robert Yi, confirmed the company would reduce its smartphone lineup in 2015. Samsung also plans to revamp its lower-tier range, improve price competitiveness, and use higher-quality components to differentiate its products. Vice President Kim Hyun-joon highlighted the rapid growth of the mid-to-low end market as an opportunity. Analyst Lee Seung-woo from IBK Securities suggested Samsung should focus on distinctive design policies. The company accelerated the launch of Galaxy Note 4 in China to get ahead of Apple's iPhone 6 and 6 Plus launch.

While the launch of the Galaxy S5 received positive reviews, it wasn't enough to prevent falling sales. In emerging markets such as India and China, local competitors have overtaken Samsung's smartphone sales. Samsung acknowledged it had responded too slowly to shifting market trends and is now committed to increasing the competitiveness of its lineup.

article_content: Billionaire investor Marc Andreessen, cofounder of Andreessen Horowitz, has caused a stir with a detailed manifesto defending fast-paced growth in artificial intelligence and technology. His 5,000-word essay claims that innovation has always moved humanity forward, citing examples like Andy Warhol, Milton Friedman, and the myth of Prometheus. Andreessen sees advances like the electric light and AI as key to improving quality of life. He strongly opposes slowing or regulating AI progress, arguing that restrictions could cost lives by preventing potential breakthroughs. Andreessen goes so far as to describe opponents of unhindered tech development as barriers, warning that halting progress can be morally wrong. Central to his argument is the idea of 'effective accelerationism' (e/acc), which encourages tech growth at maximum speed and minimal oversight. This philosophy, also favored by other Silicon Valley leaders such as Garry Tan, promotes 'techno-optimism' and resists bureaucratic obstacles. Critics point out that Andreessen's view dismisses real worries about ethics, job displacement, environmental issues, and threats to democratic processes. The manifesto attacks what Andreessen sees as excessive regulation and negative attitudes surrounding technology. AI and work expert Carl-Benedikt Frey of Oxford recognizes that too much regulation could block potentially life-saving innovations like new drugs or safer autonomous vehicles. Yet, he also notes that unchecked technological growth can bring its own social risks. Throughout history, technological changes have benefited some while challenging others, as seen in movements like the Luddites during the Industrial Revolution. Despite the controversies, Andreessen continues to push for bold, rapid innovation in emerging tech.

During the initial days of the COVID-19 pandemic, Indigenous Nations across the country—including my own—felt a disproportionate impact on our communities. The loss of elders, who are the keepers of our teachings and knowledge passed down through oral tradition, was especially devastating. Every word they share is invaluable, and losing them put our cultures and languages at risk.

To respond to this crisis, the Oceti Sakowin (composed of the Lakota and Dakota peoples) recognized all language speakers as 'essential workers,' giving them priority access to vaccinations. As a Dakota and Yaqui student at Harvard Medical School, I saw the wisdom in this innovative public health policy by our Nations.

Elsewhere, leaders like Emily Lerosion of the Samburu tribe in northern Kenya helped share COVID-19 information in their Indigenous languages. With our languages and knowledge at stake, my Tribe—the Crow Creek Sioux Tribe—encouraged me and others to return to Oceti Sakowin lands, spending time with our elders and learning our language to pass on to future generations.

Supporting this mission, Peter Langkeek, Chairman of the Crow Creek Sioux Tribe, wrote an official letter to Harvard Medical School. He formally notified them that I would be taking a year-long spiritual and religious leave (February 2022–February 2023) to focus on our language and participate in sacred ceremonies, emphasizing that the Dakota, Nakota, and Lakota languages are crucial for our people's health. He highlighted that, globally, an Indigenous language disappears every two weeks, and that the Oceti Sakowin lost many elders and language keepers during the pandemic. Language is fundamental to our physical, mental, and spiritual well-being. The possibility of a Dakota medical doctor improving healthcare through our language is significant. Our languages are also recognized and protected under the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples endorsed by the United States.

Harvard Medical School ultimately acknowledged the importance of my language learning as both my right and my Tribal government's right to support the intergenerational health of its citizens—a move that felt momentous for academia in supporting Indigenous peoples’ rights.

This personal story illustrates how Indigenous languages empower wellbeing, and how public institutions can play a role in their protection and revitalization. Indigenous Peoples make up around 5% of the global population but represent more than 4,000 spoken languages. Each is intimately tied to Indigenous homelands and contains generations of traditional science and knowledge beneficial to ecological health. Language loss not only harms environmental stewardship but also increases risks for poor health outcomes among Indigenous Peoples, including higher rates of suicide, mental illness, and substance use.

Despite the importance, many Indigenous communities lacked access to COVID-19 information in their languages, partly due to underrepresentation in health professions and barriers in public health communication from major institutions like the CDC and WHO. Often, Indigenous language speakers were left behind in the global public health response.

I recall, during my clinical training in Boston, treating a young Indigenous patient from Guatemala who struggled to communicate in Spanish—his primary language was an Indigenous dialect unavailable on our hospital's translation list. This experience underscored broader consequences of language barriers in healthcare, especially for Indigenous immigrants.

To address these gaps, we need more Indigenous health professionals globally, and the healthcare field must fully value Indigenous, intergenerational knowledge—including linguistic expertise. My journey to learn my language is ongoing, and I remain committed to supporting this vital part of our heritage. I dream of a future where my great-grandchildren can see a Dakota doctor, converse in our language, receive culturally sensitive care, and have access to both modern and traditional healing.

By sharing these experiences as an Indigenous medical student, I hope to help Western medicine better support Indigenous Peoples and advance the vision of linguistic and cultural revitalization for all.

Durante os primeiros dias da pandemia de COVID-19, as Nações Indígenas por todo o país — inclusive a minha — sentiram o impacto desproporcional em nossas comunidades. A perda dos anciãos, guardiões dos nossos ensinamentos e conhecimento transmitidos oralmente, foi especialmente devastadora. Cada palavra que compartilham é inestimável, e perdê-los colocou nossas culturas e línguas em risco.

Para responder a essa crise, a Oceti Sakowin (composta pelos povos Lakota e Dakota) reconheceu todos os falantes de línguas como "trabalhadores essenciais", dando-lhes prioridade na vacinação. Como estudante Dakota e Yaqui na Harvard Medical School, reconheci a sabedoria dessa política inovadora de saúde pública de nossas Nações.

Em outros lugares, líderes como Emily Lerosion, da tribo Samburu, no norte do Quênia, ajudaram a compartilhar informações sobre a COVID-19 em suas línguas indígenas. Com nossos idiomas e conhecimentos ameaçados, minha tribo — a Crow Creek Sioux Tribe — incentivou a mim e a outros a retornar às terras do Oceti Sakowin, passar tempo com os anciãos e aprender nosso idioma para transmitir às próximas gerações.

Apoiando essa missão, Peter Langkeek, presidente da Crow Creek Sioux Tribe, enviou uma carta oficial à Harvard Medical School. Ele notificou formalmente que eu tiraria um ano de licença espiritual e religiosa (de fevereiro de 2022 a fevereiro de 2023) para me dedicar ao nosso idioma e participar de cerimônias sagradas, enfatizando que as línguas Dakota, Nakota e Lakota são essenciais para a saúde do nosso povo. Ele destacou que, mundialmente, uma língua indígena desaparece a cada duas semanas e que a Oceti Sakowin perdeu muitos anciãos e guardiões do idioma durante a pandemia. O idioma é fundamental para nosso bem-estar físico, mental e espiritual. A possibilidade de um médico Dakota melhorar a saúde utilizando nosso idioma é enorme. Nossas línguas também são reconhecidas e protegidas pela Declaração da ONU sobre os Direitos dos Povos Indígenas, endossada pelos Estados Unidos.

A Harvard Medical School acabou reconhecendo a importância do meu aprendizado linguístico como meu direito e também como um direito do meu governo tribal de apoiar a saúde intergeracional de seus cidadãos — uma decisão marcante para promover os direitos dos povos indígenas na academia.

Esta história pessoal mostra como as línguas indígenas fortalecem o bem-estar e como as instituições públicas podem ajudar a protegê-las e revitalizá-las. Os povos indígenas correspondem a cerca de 5% da população mundial e têm mais de 4.000 línguas faladas. Cada idioma está profundamente conectado às terras ancestrais e contém gerações de conhecimentos tradicionais que beneficiam a saúde ambiental. A perda linguística não só prejudica a proteção ambiental, como também aumenta os riscos à saúde entre os povos indígenas, incluindo taxas maiores de suicídio, doenças mentais e abuso de substâncias.

Apesar disso, muitas comunidades indígenas não tiveram acesso a informações sobre a COVID-19 em seus idiomas, devido à baixa representação nas profissões da saúde e obstáculos na comunicação por parte de órgãos como CDC e OMS. Frequentemente, falantes de línguas indígenas foram deixados de lado na resposta global de saúde pública.

Lembro, durante meu estágio clínico em Boston, de atender um jovem indígena da Guatemala que lutava para se comunicar em espanhol — sua língua principal era um dialeto indígena, não disponível na lista de tradução do hospital. Essa experiência evidenciou as consequências mais amplas das barreiras linguísticas na saúde, especialmente para imigrantes indígenas.

Para superar essas falhas, precisamos de mais profissionais da saúde indígenas no mundo todo, e o setor deve valorizar plenamente o conhecimento indígena intergeracional — inclusive o linguístico. Minha trajetória de aprendizado segue, e continuo comprometido com essa parte vital da nossa herança. Sonho com um futuro em que meus bisnetos possam ser atendidos por um médico Dakota, conversar em nossa língua, receber cuidados culturalmente sensíveis e ter acesso tanto à cura moderna quanto à tradicional.

Ao compartilhar minhas experiências como estudante indígena de medicina, espero que a medicina ocidental apoie melhor os povos indígenas e avance rumo à realização dessa visão de revitalização linguística e cultural para todos.

article_content: Natalie Raanan, a US teenager who was abducted by Hamas during a family visit to Israel, is now home in Chicago, according to Yinam Cohen, Israel's Consul General to the Midwest. The pair were freed on October 20, with Hamas stating the release was for humanitarian reasons. Judith’s return to the US has not yet been scheduled. The family was in Israel to celebrate Natalie's graduation from high school and Tamar Ranaan’s 85th birthday. Both Natalie and Judith were brought to a military base in the center of Israel after their release. Judith, suffering from health problems, was treated by the Red Cross. President Joe Biden said the US government has been working nonstop to secure the release of American hostages. Of the 239 people kidnapped by Hamas on October 7, only four have been released so far, with Natalie and Judith being the only Americans. Meanwhile, Shani Louk, an Israeli-German woman previously believed to be a hostage, has been confirmed dead. Violence has significantly escalated since the attacks, with Gaza’s Hamas-run health ministry reporting over 8,000 deaths due to Israeli airstrikes.

article_content: HYDERABAD: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi on Monday stated that Telangana cannot afford the Congress or BJP coming to power, alleging that both parties are conspiring to support the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) in spreading its influence in the state. Speaking in Nampally, Owaisi claimed that the Congress and BJP want to help the RSS achieve power in Telangana. He emphasized that it is important to prevent either party from gaining control. Owaisi's remarks followed the BJP's promise to implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in Telangana and to officially observe September 17 as 'Hyderabad Liberation Day' in its election manifesto. He also accused the Congress of working with the BJP in several constituencies. 'To stop the BJP, it must be defeated in Goshamahal, Nirmal, Mudhole, Nizamabad Urban, Huzurabad, Korutla, Adilabad, Karimnagar, Musheerabad, Khairatabad, and Amberpet,' Owaisi said. 'The Congress is cooperating with the BJP in these areas and if the minority vote is split, the RSS will benefit. My mission is to stop the spread of the RSS. Please value your vote and use it wisely,' he urged voters. Owaisi strongly criticized both the Congress and BJP, saying both rely on the politics of hate. He alleged that Congress MPs in Telangana are influenced by the RSS and claimed the BJP government has weakened the economy, harmed small businesses, and failed to create jobs. He declared that he would not allow the RSS to gain ground in Telangana. He also criticized Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi for their comments on AIMIM's election strategy. 'On one hand, Rahul accuses us of taking money and contesting. On the other, Priyanka says we are not contesting enough. They should know that I am not foolish and should plan better if they want to challenge me and KCR (K. Chandrashekar Rao),' said Owaisi. Earlier on Monday, Owaisi campaigned door-to-door in Nampally ahead of the Telangana Assembly elections. The elections are expected to be a three-way contest between the BJP, Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), and Congress. Voting is scheduled for November 30, with results to be announced on December 3, along with those from four other states.

article_content: Shoppers at the Asda supermarket in Cambridge were taken aback to find that signs for produce were written in Welsh, despite the city being nearly 200 miles from Wales. The bilingual signs, which provided the names of fruits and vegetables in both Welsh and English, left many customers puzzled about their presence. According to a spokesperson for the Beehive Centre store, the Welsh signs were accidentally installed due to a printing error, leaving the staff to temporarily use them until the correct signage arrived. Staff and customers joked about the blunder, even referencing the Welsh word 'wps,' meaning 'oops.' Local resident Catherine Wade, 38, expressed her bewilderment, noting that she doubted there were many Welsh speakers in Cambridge, making the signs feel out of place. National statistics indicate that only about 19 percent of Wales’s population speaks Welsh fluently, reinforcing its status as a minority language. Despite the confusion, the store ensured English translations were available so shoppers could still navigate the aisles. In the meantime, employees encouraged customers to have a bit of fun learning some Welsh words as they waited for the correct signs.

Segundo um porta-voz da loja do Beehive Centre, as placas em galês foram instaladas por engano devido a um erro na impressão, obrigando a equipe a usá-las temporariamente até que as corretas chegassem. Funcionários e clientes levaram o equívoco com bom humor, inclusive mencionando a palavra galesa 'wps', que significa 'ops'. A moradora local Catherine Wade, de 38 anos, demonstrou espanto e comentou que duvidava que houvesse muitos falantes de galês em Cambridge, tornando as placas ainda mais estranhas. Dados nacionais mostram que apenas cerca de 19% da população do País de Gales fala galês fluentemente, reforçando seu status de idioma minoritário. Apesar da confusão, a loja garantiu que as traduções em inglês estivessem disponíveis para que os clientes pudessem se orientar. Enquanto isso, os funcionários incentivaram os consumidores a se divertirem aprendendo algumas palavras em galês enquanto aguardavam pelas placas corretas.

article_content: The home security camera landscape is crowded, but most devices are static or limited to basic adjustments. Enabot stands out by engineering wheeled smart cameras that roam freely, unlike standard fixed cameras. Previous Enabot models such as the EBO Air and EBO SE served as mobile companions, marketed mainly as fun playmates for children and pets. These earlier versions were affordably priced and featured entertaining elements but offered basic security functionality. Now, Enabot's EBO X marks a shift toward advanced home monitoring. This larger robot, equipped with wheels, acts as a smart guardian, navigating your home via V-SLAM technology for autonomous mapping and patrol. EBO X is loaded with premium features: Harman Kardon speakers for audio, an 8-megapixel 4K UHD camera with night vision and a stabilized gimbal, and full Alexa integration. The companion app enables remote operation, push notifications, and real-time alerts for events like falls and when a child cries, using intelligent detection systems. User privacy is prioritized, with options to retract the camera inside the robot’s body, mute the microphone, and store recordings on a local microSD card. Control of the EBO X can be shared among household members through its mobile app. With Alexa built in, users can issue voice commands to the EBO X or control other Alexa-compatible devices, even without the traditional 'Alexa' wake word. Two-way voice communication makes it easy to check in on loved ones or pets remotely. Autonomous charging lets the robot find its dock when power is low, and users can define restricted zones that the robot will avoid. Occasionally, the V-SLAM navigation can falter on uneven flooring. The app boasts an intuitive design with a gamified interface, offering access to customizable robot settings and seamless firmware updates over the air. RGB lighting customization adds a personal touch. Although some playful aspects from previous models—such as the animated voice and laser pointer features—are absent, the EBO X compensates with powerful upgrades that suit those focused on security and family care. Despite a price tag exceeding $1,000, the EBO X offers a feature set more versatile and cost-effective than rivals like Amazon Astro. By combining mobility, robust surveillance, smart home integration, and interactivity, it represents a compelling smart home hub for users seeking convenience and peace of mind.

Agora, o EBO X marca uma evolução no monitoramento doméstico. Maior e com rodas, atua como guardião inteligente, patrulhando a casa de forma autônoma com ajuda da tecnologia V-SLAM. Embora alguns atrativos dos modelos antigos — como voz animada ou ponteira laser — não estejam presentes, o EBO X aposta em avanços funcionais focados em segurança e bem-estar. article_content:
Brazilian designer Alexandre Herchcovitch has introduced what he claims are the world's first jeans designed to combat cellulite. Dubbed 'beauty denim,' these jeans are made using Emana yarn, a synthetic fiber developed in Brazil and also used in sportswear and lingerie. According to Herchcovitch, the jeans harness the wearer's body heat to produce infrared rays, which reflect back onto the skin. This process is said to stimulate microcirculation and cellular metabolism, aiming to prevent the buildup of cellulite.

Herchcovitch presented the anti-cellulite jeans during a fashion show in Rio de Janeiro, stating that five years of research demonstrated the product's effectiveness. Despite these claims, medical experts remain skeptical, pointing out that there is no miracle cure for cellulite, which is often attributed to poor diet, poor circulation, and a slow metabolism. In the UK, approximately 90% of women over the age of 30 are affected by cellulite, prompting a range of treatments from creams to surgery.

The Emana yarn used in the jeans is said to absorb electromagnetic waves naturally emitted by the human body, known as Far Infrared Rays, to stimulate skin tissue. Leggings made from Emana yarn are already available in the UK from online retailers and at Harrods. Herchcovitch has not yet announced when his designer jeans will be available for purchase or at what price.

This is not the first time a fashion label has marketed clothing claiming to fight cellulite. In 2004, Miss Sixty introduced jeans, trousers, and skirts treated with an anti-cellulite serum called Skintex, which contained retinol—a vitamin A derivative used in skincare to boost collagen. The brand claimed the serum would be absorbed into the skin through friction while wearing the clothing, but medical experts dismissed this as a marketing ploy. The line was discontinued after a year.

article_content: On Monday, five prominent stocks drew investor attention as both their prices and open interest rose—a classic signal of fresh long positions being established. Experts advise that, to improve trading decisions, investors should check whether these stocks are trading near their 52-week highs, or if they are crossing key moving averages such as the 20, 50, or 100-day. Unusual surges in far out-of-the-money call option activity may also point to possible informed trades. Separately, Nawaz Modi, estranged from Gautam Singhania, is seeking three-quarters of his estimated $1.4 billion fortune for herself and their two daughters in ongoing settlement discussions. article_content: Soon after Mitt Romney declared his intention to run for Orrin Hatch's Senate seat in Utah in 2018, he received a call from then-President Donald Trump. Trump, whose win in Utah in 2016 was less commanding than for past GOP candidates, seemed eager to develop a connection with Romney, knowing he'd likely be heading to Washington. According to 'Romney: A Reckoning' by McKay Coppins, Trump boasted to Romney about his popularity in Utah, crediting his move to scale back federal national monuments. In 2017, Trump had reduced the Bears Ears National Monument by about 1.1 million acres (85% less) and the Grand Staircase-Escalante by 800,000 acres (about 45% less). These decisions were celebrated by Utah's Republican leaders, who have long bristled at federal land control, but Native American tribes in the area were overwhelmingly against the cuts. During the conversation, Trump mistakenly claimed he had restored 'two million square miles' to Utah, confusing square miles and acres. Romney and his aide found the error amusing, since Utah is approximately 85,000 square miles. Romney didn't correct Trump, instead keeping the joke to himself that such a number would cover half the country. Trump went on to say, as a 'real estate guy,' he fully understood measurements, insisting it was 'square miles.' After joining the Senate in 2019, Romney's relationship with Trump deteriorated, with Romney eventually voting to convict Trump in both of his impeachment trials—once for alleged abuse of power over Ukraine, and later for incitement related to the Capitol riot on January 6, 2021. President Joe Biden, in October 2021, restored nearly two million acres to both Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante national monuments. Trump's representatives were contacted for comment.

Em outubro de 2021, o presidente Joe Biden devolveu quase dois milhões de acres aos monumentos Bears Ears e Grand Staircase-Escalante. Representantes de Trump foram procurados para comentar.

article_content: George Norcross, a prominent South Jersey businessman and Democrat, stated on Monday that he may take legal action against the Philadelphia Eagles following his removal from Sunday’s game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field, after he displayed both an American and an Israeli flag from his private box. Norcross claims he was forcibly removed and assaulted by security personnel—not police—when he refused to take down the flags. In a public statement, Norcross expressed confusion over why displaying American and Israeli flags was considered 'obscene or indecent' by the Eagles or the NFL. He cited the organization’s previous support for other international causes, such as Ukraine, and underscored his motivation to support Israel, which had recently suffered an attack by Hamas. Donald Norcross, George's brother and a Democratic representative from Camden, commented on social media, highlighting the apparent contradiction between the game’s tribute to veterans and the controversy over the flag display. The incident reportedly occurred about 11 minutes into the second quarter of the Eagles-Cowboys matchup, a game the Eagles ultimately won 28-23 with a last-second defensive effort. The Eagles and the NFL have not yet issued a public statement regarding the incident.

article_content: Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted on Thursday of defrauding customers of his now-defunct cryptocurrency exchange, FTX. Here are some key moments from the trial:  "BUILDING THE PLANE AS THEY WERE FLYING" During opening statements, Bankman-Fried's attorney Mark Cohen described FTX as a young company facing negative publicity and a downturn in the cryptocurrency market. "Sam and his colleagues were building the plane as they were flying it," Cohen said.  CAROLINE ELLISON LIVED IN 'DREAD' Caroline Ellison, the former chief executive of Bankman-Fried's crypto hedge fund Alameda Research and his on-and-off girlfriend, testified that she knew Alameda had borrowed billions of dollars from FTX. This left the exchange in a risky position if many customers tried to withdraw their money. She said she lived in "dread" and that FTX's collapse last November was a "relief." "I felt a sense of relief that I didn't have to lie anymore," Ellison said through tears.  'WE LIED' TO THE PUBLIC Gary Wang, Bankman-Fried's college roommate and ex-colleague, testified that Bankman-Fried instructed him to give Alameda special trading privileges on FTX. "We gave special privileges to Alameda Research on FTX, which allowed it to withdraw unlimited amounts of funds from the platform, and we lied about this to the public," Wang said.  'A LOT OF PEOPLE GOT HURT' On his first day on the stand, Bankman-Fried said, "We thought that we might be able to build the best product on the market. It turned out basically the opposite of that. A lot of people got hurt."  $8 BILLION DEBT 'SURPRISED' BANKMAN-FRIED Bankman-Fried testified he was "very surprised" when he discovered in October 2022 that Alameda had borrowed $8 billion from FTX customer deposits, and that the loan was not recorded on Alameda's main account. He believed the hedge fund had enough assets to repay the debt. "If it were far larger, I would have been calling a crisis," he said while testifying.  BANKMAN-FRIED'S FATE RESTS WITH FORMER FRIENDS During closing arguments, Prosecutor Nicolas Roos urged jurors to rely on the testimonies of Ellison, Wang, and Nishad Singh, FTX's former director of engineering—all of whom were once in Bankman-Fried's inner circle before becoming cooperating witnesses. "If you believe even one of those witnesses is telling the truth about this, the defendant is guilty," Roos said.

"Sam e seus colegas estavam construindo o avião enquanto voavam", disse Cohen.  CAROLINE ELLISON VIVIA EM 'MEDO' Caroline Ellison, ex-CEO do fundo de hedge cripto de Bankman-Fried, Alameda Research, e sua namorada intermitente, testemunhou que sabia que a Alameda havia pegado bilhões de dólares emprestados da FTX. 'MUITA GENTE FOI PREJUDICADA' No seu primeiro dia no banco das testemunhas, Bankman-Fried disse: "Achamos que poderíamos construir o melhor produto do mercado. Aconteceu basicamente o oposto disso. Muita gente foi prejudicada."  DÍVIDA DE US$ 8 BILHÕES 'SURPREENDEU' BANKMAN-FRIED Bankman-Fried testemunhou que ficou "muito surpreso" ao descobrir, em outubro de 2022, que a Alameda havia emprestado US$ 8 bilhões dos depósitos de clientes da FTX, e que o empréstimo não estava registrado na conta principal da Alameda. "Se você acreditar que ao menos uma dessas testemunhas está dizendo a verdade, o réu é culpado", disse Roos.

article_content: Two former Navy SEALs, Glen Doherty and Tyrone Woods, were among four Americans killed last week in an attack on the U.S. Consulate in Benghazi, Libya. According to sources familiar with the incident, they died after rushing to aid their colleagues. Doherty and Woods were in Benghazi as security contractors. On September 11, 2012, they were at a secure annex elsewhere in the city when they learned the main consulate building was under attack. The diplomats there, protected by a small armed force of only nine, were overwhelmed by the worsening situation. Doherty and Woods, along with other security personnel, left the safety of the annex and entered the chaos. They gathered the consulate staff under attack and safely led them to another secure building. Their responsibilities also included recovering the body of computer specialist Sean Smith, who died from smoke inhalation due to a fire set by the attackers. According to sources, diesel fuel was used to start the blaze, and thick black smoke worsened the confusion. U.S. Ambassador Chris Stevens went missing during the attack and was not among those evacuated. He was later confirmed dead. The State Department has not released details on how Stevens died, but media reports say he was taken by locals to Benghazi Medical Center. After returning to the annex, the ordeal continued for Doherty, Woods, and the security team. A more intense assault began on the annex. Military officials told CNN that attackers used rocket-propelled grenades and possibly mortars. 'It was during that second attack that two additional U.S. personnel were killed and two others were wounded,' a senior administration official said. The two victims were later identified as Doherty and Woods. The men's remains were honored during a transfer ceremony attended by Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and President Barack Obama. Doherty, who grew up in Massachusetts and loved the outdoors, served two tours in Iraq beginning with the 2003 invasion before leaving the military in 2005. He became a private security contractor with experience in Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Yemen. A diplomatic source told CNN that Doherty's mission in Libya was to search for shoulder-fired anti-aircraft missiles after the fall of former Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi. Woods, a registered nurse and certified paramedic, completed multiple tours of duty in Iraq and Afghanistan. After retiring from the Navy, he worked in diplomatic security positions in regions from Central America to the Middle East. President Obama said, 'Four Americans, four patriots—they loved their country and chose to serve it well. They had a mission, and they believed in it, knowing the dangers and accepting them. They didn't just embrace the American ideal—they lived it: the courage, the hope, and, yes, the idealism.' CNN's Arwa Damon contributed to this report from Benghazi, Libya.

article_content: By Isaac Kohen, founder of Teramind, a provider of behavior analytics, business intelligence, and data loss prevention (DLP) solutions for enterprises.  Data is the backbone of the digital economy, powering everything from personalized experiences to advanced artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Often referred to as the world’s most valuable resource, data drives growth, innovation, and development.  A 2023 Ernst & Young analysis states, “Data is a company’s most valuable asset. It offers untapped potential for growth, sparks new opportunities, and is the foundation upon which we can build a better working world.”  While data collection and analysis were once hidden behind free services and tailored experiences, today’s consumers recognize the value of their data and increasingly scrutinize companies' data practices. Many feel their data is less secure, their privacy less protected, and their preferences overlooked. This has led to growing mistrust between companies and customers regarding data collection.  A history of data breaches and privacy violations has further eroded confidence, with companies often showing they cannot—or will not—adequately protect customer information.  If data is one of our most valuable assets, business leaders must reset their approach to collecting, analyzing, storing, and using customer data. Based on my experience, here are three steps to help restore customer confidence in your organization's data use practices:  1. Be transparent about data collection policies. Rather than hiding data practices behind dense privacy notices, organizations should clearly communicate the reasons, methods, and uses of customer data in plain language. As Adobe explains, 'Data transparency is the practice of using data intentionally and honestly, according to both the law and business ethics.' This is especially important as the adoption of AI systems accelerates across industries. Cisco’s 2023 Data Privacy Benchmark Study found 92% of organizations believe they must do more to reassure customers about data usage.  To ensure transparency, consider: - Informing clients about your data handling practices. - Providing a detailed inventory of collected data. - Creating clear privacy guidelines. - Empowering clients with control over their information.  Transparent data collection isn’t just beneficial—it’s often legally required as privacy regulations demand more responsible data stewardship.  2. Minimize data access within the organization. Excessive internal access to customer data can lead to violations and misuse. For example, in 2021 Facebook limited access after discovering thousands of employees could access private user data, ultimately reducing access to fewer than 5,000 employees—and fewer than 100 for highly sensitive information.  Limiting access should be a cornerstone of restoring customer trust. Business can use automated software solutions to: - Prevent accidental data mishaps with customized monitoring of communications. - Protect data with secure protocols for file activity and transfers. - Record actions by all individuals accessing servers, including third parties. - Apply time-based policies to safeguard data outside business hours. - Restrict access according to user roles.  By minimizing access, companies demonstrate commitment to data security, strengthening stakeholder trust.  3. Proactively invest in cybersecurity. Confidence in data practices will remain low if breaches persist. Many organizations only improve cybersecurity after suffering incidents. IBM’s 2023 Cost of a Data Breach report states 51% of organizations plan to increase security investments after a breach, including better incident response plans, employee training, and threat detection tools.  Instead of waiting, proactively invest in cybersecurity by allocating resources to: - Employee training and awareness. - Advanced security technologies. - Hiring and retaining skilled personnel. - Robust incident response and recovery strategies.  Such investments prepare companies for emerging threats and foster lasting customer trust in a cost-effective manner.  Safeguarding Data, Safeguarding Trust  In the digital era, data is central to business growth, but the gap in trust between consumers and companies around data practices is significant. Against a backdrop of breaches and privacy concerns, organizations must rethink their data strategies.  Emphasizing transparency, limiting data access, and proactively strengthening cybersecurity are critical steps toward protecting valuable data and rebuilding consumer trust. The future of the digital economy depends on mutual trust and respect, and actively nurturing this relationship is the path to sustained success.
translated_content: Por Isaac Kohen, fundador da Teramind, fornecedora de soluções de análise comportamental, inteligência de negócios e prevenção de perda de dados (DLP) para empresas.  Os dados são a espinha dorsal da economia digital, impulsionando desde experiências personalizadas até sistemas avançados de inteligência artificial (IA). Muitas vezes chamados de recurso mais valioso do mundo, os dados promovem crescimento, inovação e desenvolvimento.  Uma análise da Ernst & Young de 2023 afirma: "Os dados são o ativo mais valioso de uma empresa. Eles oferecem potencial inexplorado para crescimento, impulsionam novas oportunidades e são a base sobre a qual podemos construir um mundo melhor para se trabalhar."  Antes, a coleta e análise de dados ficavam ocultas por trás de serviços gratuitos e experiências personalizadas, mas hoje os consumidores reconhecem o valor de seus dados e analisam cada vez mais as práticas das empresas. Muitos sentem que seus dados estão menos seguros, sua privacidade menos protegida e suas preferências pouco consideradas. Isso gerou uma crescente desconfiança entre empresas e clientes quanto à coleta de dados.  O histórico de vazamentos de dados e violações de privacidade prejudicou ainda mais a confiança, com empresas frequentemente mostrando que não conseguem ou não querem proteger adequadamente as informações dos clientes.  Se os dados são um dos ativos mais preciosos, líderes empresariais precisam redefinir sua abordagem em relação à coleta, análise, armazenamento e uso dessas informações. Com base na minha experiência, compartilho três passos para ajudar a restaurar a confiança dos clientes nas práticas da sua organização:  1. Seja transparente sobre as políticas de coleta de dados. Em vez de ocultar práticas por trás de notificações densas de privacidade, as empresas devem comunicar claramente, em linguagem simples, os motivos, métodos e finalidades da coleta de dados dos clientes. Como a Adobe destaca, 'Transparência de dados é o uso intencional e honesto das informações, de acordo com a legislação e ética empresarial.' Isso se torna ainda mais importante com o avanço da IA nas empresas. O Estudo de Benchmark de Privacidade de Dados 2023 da Cisco mostra que 92% das organizações acreditam que precisam fazer mais para tranquilizar clientes sobre suas práticas de dados.  Para garantir a transparência, considere: - Informar os clientes sobre como os dados são tratados; - Fornecer um inventário detalhado das informações coletadas; - Criar diretrizes de privacidade claras; - Oferecer controle efetivo aos clientes sobre seus dados.  A transparência não é apenas positiva—muitas vezes, é exigida por leis de proteção de dados que demandam mais responsabilidade das empresas.  2. Minimize o acesso a dados dentro da organização. O acesso interno excessivo a dados de clientes pode gerar violações e abusos. Em 2021, por exemplo, o Facebook reduziu o acesso ao descobrir que milhares de funcionários podiam acessar informações privadas, restringindo a menos de 5.000 pessoas e a menos de 100 nos dados mais sensíveis.  Limitar o acesso interno deve ser prioridade para restaurar a confiança. Adote soluções automatizadas para: - Prevenir incidentes acidentais, monitorando comunicação e acessos; - Proteger dados com protocolos seguros para transferências e manipulação; - Registrar as ações de todos que acessam servidores, inclusive terceiros; - Aplicar políticas baseadas em horários para proteger dados fora do expediente; - Restringir o acesso conforme funções e níveis de permissão.  Com acesso restrito e monitorado, a empresa demonstra compromisso com a segurança e fortalece a confiança dos parceiros.  3. Invista proativamente em cibersegurança. A confiança nas práticas de dados permanece baixa enquanto os vazamentos persistirem. Muitas empresas só reforçam a segurança após incidentes. O Relatório de Custos de Vazamentos de Dados 2023 da IBM aponta que 51% pretendem aumentar investimentos depois de ataques, como treinamento, tecnologias e resposta a incidentes.  Faça diferente: invista preventivamente em: - Treinamento e conscientização dos funcionários; - Tecnologias avançadas de segurança; - Atração e retenção de profissionais capacitados; - Estratégias fortes de resposta e recuperação.  Esses investimentos preparam as empresas para ameaças emergentes e estimulam a confiança do cliente, de forma eficaz e econômica.  Protegendo Dados, Protegendo Confiança  Na era digital, dados são centrais para o crescimento dos negócios, mas a confiança entre consumidores e empresas nunca esteve tão abalada. Com o aumento de vazamentos e preocupação com a privacidade, é fundamental repensar as estratégias.  Transparência, limitação de acesso e cibersegurança reforçada são essenciais para proteger dados e recuperar a confiança dos consumidores. O futuro da economia digital depende dessa relação de respeito mútuo, e investir nesse relacionamento é o caminho para o sucesso sustentável.

article_content: Almost seven decades after the Holocaust, the place of Jews in German society remains a sensitive subject. With Germany’s Jewish population under 200,000 in a nation of 82 million, most postwar Germans lack personal connections or familiarity with Jewish people. To address this gap, the Jewish Museum in Berlin launched an exhibit, 'The Whole Truth,' where a Jewish volunteer sits in a glass enclosure for two hours daily until August, welcoming questions from visitors about Jewish life. The installation's base asks: 'Are there still Jews in Germany?' The display has sparked strong reactions. Some visitors gather around volunteers like Israeli Ido Porat, the first to participate, eager to ask direct questions. Museum official Tina Luedecke explains that many visitors seek to better understand Jewish culture, given their limited exposure. 'This offers people a rare chance to learn firsthand,' she says. However, not everyone agrees with the approach. Prominent figures like Berlin’s Stephan Kramer criticize the concept, seeing it as dehumanizing. 'They asked me to join, but I declined,' he told the Associated Press, making a pointed comparison to uncomfortable historical imagery. Other Jewish community members echo concerns, referencing historical precedents and questioning whether this tactic truly improves relations. Israeli Eran Levy, who lives in Berlin, expressed discomfort: 'It feels degrading and unhelpful.' Similarly, volunteer Leeor Englander notes that being publicly identified as Jewish in Germany can already feel like being on display. 'Once people know, you're expected to answer every question about our religion and history.' Curator Miriam Goldmann, herself Jewish, stands by the exhibit’s bold approach. She believes provoking strong reactions is necessary to confront taboos and move conversations forward, even if some find it uncomfortable. Inside the exhibition, stereotypes are addressed head-on: displays ask, 'How can you recognize a Jew?' alongside traditional headwear and further questions about Jewish identity and traits. Despite controversy, visitor engagement is high. People query volunteers on topics ranging from Sabbath customs to Judaism’s stance on various social issues. Some participants, like Porat and Dekel Peretz, observe that German perceptions of Jews often revolve solely around the Holocaust, ignoring the richness and diversity of Jewish life. Porat, while admitting the exhibit can feel objectifying, says that encountering curiosity is a common experience for Jews in Germany. Not everyone favors the method. Rabbi Yehuda Teichtal from the Chabad community suggests more personal connections can be forged at community centers, where those interested can learn about Judaism without the spectacle of a glass box.

Para abordar essa lacuna, o Museu Judaico de Berlim lançou a exposição 'A Verdade Completa', onde um voluntário judeu se senta em uma caixa de vidro por duas horas diárias até agosto, pronto para responder perguntas dos visitantes sobre a vida judaica. Alguns visitantes se reúnem em volta de voluntários como o israelense Ido Porat, o primeiro a participar, ansiosos por fazer perguntas diretas. No entanto, nem todos concordam com a abordagem. Figuras proeminentes como Stephan Kramer, de Berlim, criticam o conceito, considerando-o desumanizante. O israelense Eran Levy, que mora em Berlim, comentou: 'É degradante e não ajuda.' De modo similar, o voluntário Leeor Englander ressalta que ser identificado publicamente como judeu na Alemanha já pode ser uma experiência de exposição. 'Quando sabem quem você é, esperam que responda a todas as questões sobre nossa religião e história.' A curadora Miriam Goldmann, também judia, defende a abordagem ousada da exposição. article_content: Burger King is accelerating the rollout of digital order kiosks, which executives say benefit both staff and customers and often result in larger orders. 'We're starting to make some progress figuring out kiosks,' said Josh Kobza, CEO of Restaurant Brands International—the parent company of Burger King—during a Friday investor call. Digital kiosks are large touchscreen devices that allow diners to order and pay directly in the restaurant instead of at the counter. Kobza noted that piloting kiosks in more company-owned locations has delivered 'tremendous results,' with the 'vast majority' of orders in these stores now made using the kiosks. Internationally, Burger King has already expanded kiosk usage—more than half of its overseas outlets now feature the technology, according to Kobza. He added that as consumer acceptance has grown, he believes the US is ready for more kiosks, predicting a faster global rollout. Kobza said kiosks reduce 'stressful interaction' at the counter for both customers and staff, typically lead to larger orders, and allow employees to focus more on preparing meals. Patrick Doyle, RBI’s executive chairman, called kiosks 'a win on every single front.' Digital kiosks enable labor cost savings, improve order accuracy, and allow restaurants to adjust menus and prices in real-time. They also suggest add-ons based on customer choices, making it easier to personalize orders, and can promote high-demand items according to the time of day or weather conditions. During the last quarter, 14% of Burger King’s orders were placed digitally—up more than 40% year-on-year—with company-operated locations using kiosks reaching a 28% digital order rate. Kobza expressed a long-term vision for fully digital ordering, saying, 'We should have all of the order-taking done through digital ordering channels over time...that’s sort of our North Star.' In the quarter ending September 30, Burger King reported systemwide sales growth of 10.3% to $7.06 billion compared to the same period in 2022. Comparable sales rose 6.6% in the US and 7.6% in international markets, despite a slight decrease in the number of US locations due to some closures. Burger King is currently executing a $400 million rebranding initiative, 'Reclaim the Flame,' which invests in advertising, digital upgrades, kitchen tech, and restaurant remodels.

No exterior, o Burger King já expandiu o uso desses quiosques — mais da metade dos restaurantes internacionais contam com a tecnologia, segundo Kobza. article_content: The Kano State Police Command confirmed on Wednesday the arrest of seven individuals for protesting the Court of Appeal’s judgment that upheld the removal of Governor Abba-Kabir Yusuf of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP). State Police Commissioner Hussaini Gumel announced that the seven protesters were detained near Kano Line as they moved toward State House Road. "We have successfully stopped the protesters and arrested seven of them. Armed officers have been deployed in the area, and an intensive investigation is underway. We will provide updates in due course," Gumel stated. He advised residents to go about their lawful activities, assuring that police and other security agencies have implemented adequate security measures to prevent further unrest. "I urge residents to promptly report anyone or any group engaging in protest activities, within or outside the city, to the nearest security outfit for immediate action," Gumel added. According to The PUNCH, some youths, believed to be supporters of the NNPP, protested in Kano on Wednesday following the appeal court's ruling against the governor.

O Comissário de Polícia do Estado, Hussaini Gumel, anunciou que os sete manifestantes foram detidos próximo ao Kano Line enquanto se dirigiam para a State House Road. "Conseguimos impedir os manifestantes e prender sete deles. Policiais armados foram destacados para a área, e uma investigação intensiva está em andamento. Forneceremos atualizações em breve", afirmou Gumel. Ele aconselhou os moradores a seguirem com suas atividades normalmente, garantindo que a polícia e outras agências de segurança implementaram medidas adequadas para evitar novos distúrbios. "Peço aos moradores que denunciem imediatamente qualquer pessoa ou grupo que esteja realizando protestos, dentro ou fora da cidade, à unidade de segurança mais próxima para ação imediata", acrescentou Gumel. Many photographers would flee if a cheetah charged toward them at full speed, but 51-year-old Adalberto Mangini held his ground to capture breathtaking slow-motion photos. The cheetah sprinted through an enclosed runway at speeds reaching 70 mph, chasing after a fake chicken. This formidable predator is part of a breeding and rehabilitation program and will eventually be released into the wild. The technique used—training the cheetah to chase a faux chicken on a high-speed zip line—is part of its preparation, managed by staff at the Mukuni Big 5 Safari in Livingstone, Zambia.

Mangini, a photographer and sales manager from Milan, Italy, explained: “My body was completely covered with red dust afterwards.” He spent days meticulously studying the cheetah’s running pattern to determine the optimal spot to photograph the graceful animal. Despite his careful planning, he admits that he had an escape route ready in case the cheetah did not stop running. “I was always ready to move quickly,” Mangini said.

Laura Bongiorni, who traveled with Mangini, noted that young cheetahs arrive at the rehabilitation center mainly from South Africa. She highlighted that populations of cheetahs and lions in Zambia have faced drastic declines. The center launched its specialized breeding program to raise captive cheetahs for eventual release into Zambia’s national parks and conservancies—places where cheetahs once lived freely but are now nearly extinct.

Mangini demonstrated how closely he could approach the rehabilitated cheetahs, emphasizing that even typically wild and dangerous animals can become approachable with respect and the right methods. "Do not show any fear, as they can sense it; respect them, touch them appropriately, talk to them—they will soon recognize your voice," he advised. He also noted that cheetahs become easier to approach the longer you spend time with them, and each animal has its own unique personality. Cheetahs are the most vulnerable of the big cats and have become endangered due to habitat loss and declining prey numbers.

O guepardo disparou por uma pista cercada, atingindo velocidades de até 112 km/h, enquanto perseguia um frango falso. Esse imponente predador faz parte de um programa de reprodução e reabilitação, e deve ser devolvido à natureza. A técnica usada — treinar o guepardo para perseguir um frango de mentira preso em um cabo super-rápido — faz parte desse processo, coordenado pela equipe do Mukuni Big 5 Safari, em Livingstone, Zâmbia.

Mangini, fotógrafo e gerente de vendas de Milão, Itália, explicou: “Fiquei completamente coberto de poeira vermelha depois.” Ele passou dias estudando de forma detalhada o padrão de corrida do guepardo para escolher o melhor local para fotografar o animal gracioso. Apesar do planejamento cuidadoso, ele admite que tinha uma rota de fuga pronta caso o guepardo não parasse de correr. “Eu sempre estava pronto para me mover rapidamente”, disse Mangini.

Laura Bongiorni, que acompanhou Mangini, comentou que os jovens guepardos chegam ao centro, principalmente, vindos da África do Sul. Ela destacou que as populações de guepardos e leões na Zâmbia sofreram quedas graves. O centro criou um programa especial de reprodução para criar guepardos em cativeiro, com o objetivo de soltá-los nos parques nacionais e áreas de conservação da Zâmbia—locais onde antes viviam livremente, mas agora estão quase extintos.

Mangini demonstrou como conseguiu se aproximar dos guepardos reabilitados, reforçando que mesmo animais normalmente selvagens e perigosos podem ser abordados com respeito e os métodos adequados. “Não mostre medo, pois eles sentem; respeite, toque no lugar certo, converse com eles—logo reconhecerão sua voz”, aconselhou. Ele também mencionou que fica mais fácil se aproximar dos guepardos quanto mais tempo se passa com eles, e cada animal tem uma personalidade única. Os guepardos são os mais vulneráveis entre os grandes felinos e estão ameaçados pela perda de habitat e diminuição do número de presas.

article_content: Paytm, owned by One97 Communications, has entered into a three-year collaboration with Amadeus, a global leader in travel technology. This partnership will see Paytm integrating Amadeus’s travel platform in order to streamline the entire process of booking trips, from searching to making payments. The alliance is designed to blend Paytm's large customer base with Amadeus's technology, enhancing convenience and efficiency for users. By adopting Amadeus's automation and New Distribution Capability (NDC), Paytm will expand its travel offerings in its app, including global flight options, hotel bookings, and low-cost carriers. The platform will leverage artificial intelligence to provide users with dynamic pricing and personalized travel suggestions. The cooperation also aims to introduce a unified Passenger Name Record (PNR) system with Indian airlines. Further, customers will benefit from multiple secure payment methods—such as UPI, Paytm wallet, and Paytm Postpaid—within the app. This partnership is set to reinforce Paytm’s standing as a top provider of travel services in India.

Flying at 35,000 feet, browsing the web can often feel slow. However, Gogo – the primary provider of in-flight wireless service in the U.S. – says that's about to change. The company plans to roll out new technology that will speed up in-flight internet connections by the end of next year.

Called Gogo GTO (Ground to Orbit), the system will boost in-flight wireless speeds from approximately 10Mbps to 60Mbps—six times faster than current rates. This improvement will make browsing in the air feel much closer to what passengers expect on the ground.

The increased speed will result from upgrades to Gogo’s satellite and ground-based towers, plus a new antenna for aircraft that is twice as efficient and half the size of the current version.

Virgin America will be the first airline to offer Gogo’s GTO service, but Gogo is also in talks with other partners, including American Airlines, Delta, and United. Meanwhile, JetBlue plans to use ViaSat, a competing provider, to introduce its own Wi-Fi service.

Gogo also offers an on-board video streaming service. Although pricing for the new GTO service has not yet been disclosed, Gogo currently charges $15 for three hours of internet use on some flights.

Chamada de Gogo GTO (Ground to Orbit), a novidade vai aumentar a velocidade do Wi-Fi nos aviões de cerca de 10Mbps para 60Mbps – seis vezes mais rápido que atualmente. Assim, a experiência de navegar no ar vai ficar bem mais parecida com a que os passageiros têm em terra.

O aumento de velocidade vem com melhorias nos satélites, torres em terra da Gogo e uma nova antena – duas vezes mais eficiente e com metade do tamanho da anterior.

A Virgin America será a primeira companhia aérea a oferecer o GTO, mas a Gogo já negocia com outros parceiros, como American Airlines, Delta e United. Enquanto isso, a JetBlue quer lançar seu próprio Wi-Fi usando a ViaSat, uma concorrente.

A Gogo também oferece streaming de vídeo a bordo. Os preços do novo GTO ainda não foram divulgados, mas atualmente a Gogo cobra US$ 15 por três horas de internet em alguns voos.

article_content: When Opal launched its first webcam, the C1, during the height of the pandemic, there was immediate demand—tens of thousands signed up after just one announcement tweet. The company only had four people at the time, including CEO Veeraj Chugh, who worked hard to fulfill orders as quickly as possible. Now, Opal has expanded its hardware team and supply chain. Developing the new Tadpole webcam went much more smoothly, as the company could now work closely with suppliers to create custom parts and visit manufacturing sites in China—something that wasn't possible during earlier lockdowns. Rather than being just an updated C1, the Tadpole takes a different route. It’s designed to clip onto a laptop, is extremely compact at 1.25 inches squared and about as thick as a pack of gum. According to Opal, it weighs roughly the same as an AA battery—and it feels that way when you hold it. Available in black and white, the Tadpole comes with a clip on the back and a built-in USB-C cable, making it straightforward to set up. It uses a 48-megapixel Sony IMX582 sensor and an f/1.8 lens, capturing video up to 4K—so it’s a major step up from most laptop webcams and even rivals high-end cameras like the Insta360 Link. Opal designed the Tadpole because users wanted a way to have high-quality video on the go. Many had asked for a travel case for the C1, but the Tadpole answers this by being purpose-built for portable use—in places like airports, coworking spaces, and conference rooms—while still looking great on screen. Its VisiMic microphone is designed to focus on your voice and cut background noise from outside the camera’s view. In practice, it works decently, but isn’t a dramatic upgrade over other noise-cancelling microphones. Muting is as easy as tapping a pad on the USB plug, though since it's a hardware function, you might occasionally forget it's on. In my experience, the Tadpole's video quality stands out, especially in tough lighting, and it’s much better than my MacBook Air’s built-in webcam. It’s hassle-free compared to the C1, which often had software and setup issues—the Tadpole just works, with extra software optional instead of necessary. article_content: On October 7, during a spacewalk outside the International Space Station (ISS), observers noticed an unidentified object in NASA's live-streamed footage, sparking speculation that it might be an alien spacecraft. Experts, however, clarified that the object was most likely a camera artefact, such as a lens flare or a speck of dust. Despite this straightforward explanation, conspiracy theories and speculation from some ufologists circulated online, claiming the sighting as evidence of extraterrestrial life. The alleged 'UFO,' visible briefly in a NASA video and marked by a red ring, appeared for only a few seconds before the camera angle changed. Professor Andrew Balogh of Imperial College London's Department of Physics noted that such sightings are usually explained by camera effects or, less often, unidentified debris. He pointed out that the object's absence from other footage and its stationary position further support the lens artefact theory. Suggestions that the object was a SpaceX Dragon or Soyuz spacecraft were dismissed, as both were docked at the ISS at the time. The theory that it could have been detached debris was also considered unlikely since the object was not present in other images. NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman and ESA's Alexander Gerst were performing the spacewalk to move a faulty cooling pump and install a backup power cable. This was the first spacewalk for both astronauts and the ISS’s 182nd overall. The ISS, launched in 1998, can accommodate up to six crew members and has been continuously occupied for over 13 years. It orbits 264 miles (425 km) above Earth, completing a circuit every 92.91 minutes at a speed of approximately 17,100 miles (27,600 km) per hour. Space science writer Amy Teitel supported the view that the 'UFO' was likely a reflection or trick of light inside the camera, citing the lack of movement. While some online commentators and publications speculated further, the majority of scientific experts agree that the object is almost certainly a lens artefact, especially given the lighting conditions with the ISS in full sunlight. Nigel Watson, author of the UFO Investigations Manual, acknowledged the object's fleeting appearance, noting that while some interpret such events as evidence of UFO activity, these incidents are more plausibly explained by lens flare or light reflection. In conclusion, the scientific consensus maintains that the object seen during the ISS spacewalk was not an alien spacecraft, but rather a visual artefact common in space photography.

article_content: The idea of balancing current carbon emissions through 'offsetting' with reduction projects elsewhere is now central to the climate responses of many governments and businesses. However, this concept deserves critical examination. Offsetting assumes that releasing carbon stored for millions of years in fossil fuels can be compensated by new actions within today’s carbon cycle. Since the Kyoto Protocol, offsetting has become a globally favored approach. 'Net zero' emissions is also key to New Zealand's climate policy and its Emissions Trading Scheme, but how these might change with a new government is uncertain due to varying coalition positions. At first glance, net zero seems reasonable—planting trees can restore lost forests and provide environmental benefits by sequestering atmospheric carbon. Still, this does not mean Earth can absorb all fossil carbon emissions from human activity. The assumption that present-day harm can be 'offset' by future actions elsewhere, an idea seen in other environmental fields, is misleading. To put this in perspective, global carbon emissions from burning fossil fuels are about 10 billion tons per year. Continuing at this rate, emissions from now to 2050 would reach 280 billion tons—seven times the biological sequestration potential estimated at 38 billion tons for 2015–2050. Before significant fossil fuel use, the carbon cycle was in a dynamic balance—carbon inputs and outputs were equal. The industrial release of coal, oil, and gas has added 'new' carbon, disrupting this balance. Long-term carbon storage in plants, soils, and oceans can only mitigate carbon within the existing carbon cycle, not the additional fossil carbon released by burning fossil fuels. While the carbon in a tree and that from fossil fuels may be chemically identical, trees only offset lost biological carbon (such as replacing felled trees), not extra fossil fuel emissions. Depending on tree planting to balance fossil carbon locks future generations into maintaining forests permanently, which is risky because of threats like wildfires, storms, and droughts exacerbated by climate change. Land dedicated to new forests is unavailable for other uses such as food production, and currently, trees are being removed worldwide at double the rate they are replanted. Critics argue the popular 'net zero' idea can act as a delaying tactic or self-deception, effectively excusing ongoing fossil fuel use. In New Zealand, for instance, subtracting carbon sequestered by forests planted since 1990 from total emissions can make emissions appear 27% lower than they are. Labeling what’s left as 'net emissions' can be misleading, especially when new trees only replace previous ones, not offset fossil emissions. There have been instances of fraudulent and 'phantom' carbon credits, and research shows many traded offsets do not correspond to real emissions reductions. Despite critiques—including from the New Zealand Climate Change Commission, which points out that adding fossil carbon to the atmosphere is essentially permanent—reliance on offsets remains widespread. Beyond natural methods, technological carbon capture and storage (CCS) is being promoted but is expensive, energy-hungry, largely unsuccessful, and its permanence is uncertain, according to the IPCC. The energy return from fossil fuels is declining, and carbon capture could make this worse; the IPCC estimates that 13–44% of energy from fossil fuels could be consumed just by the capture process. Suggesting that net zero is achievable without deep economic and societal changes only delays essential action. Even replanting entire nations with trees might only absorb about ten years' worth of current emissions at best. Reversing deforestation and restoring forests are necessary to address past land-use emissions, but tree planting alone is not sufficient to offset ongoing fossil fuel pollution. The only real solution is to both restore forests and eliminate fossil fuel emissions. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons license.
translated_content: A ideia de equilibrar as emissões atuais de carbono por meio de 'compensação' com projetos de redução em outros lugares agora é central nas estratégias climáticas de muitos governos e empresas. No entanto, esse conceito merece uma análise crítica. A compensação parte do princípio de que liberar carbono armazenado por milhões de anos em combustíveis fósseis pode ser compensado por novas ações dentro do ciclo atual do carbono. Desde o Protocolo de Kyoto, essa prática se tornou preferida no mundo todo. 'Emissões líquidas zero' também é um pilar da política climática da Nova Zelândia e do seu Esquema de Comércio de Emissões, mas qualquer mudança com um novo governo é incerta por causa das diferentes posições das coalizões. Num primeiro momento, reduzir emissões a zero parece razoável—plantar árvores pode restaurar florestas perdidas e ajudar o meio ambiente sequestrando carbono do ar. Mas isso não quer dizer que o planeta consiga absorver todo o carbono fóssil emitido pelas pessoas. A ideia de que danos atuais possam ser 'compensados' por ações futuras em outros lugares—algo visto em outros campos ambientais—é enganosa. Para ter uma noção, as emissões globais de carbono de combustíveis fósseis estão em cerca de 10 bilhões de toneladas por ano. Se continuar nesse ritmo, de hoje até 2050, seriam 280 bilhões de toneladas—sete vezes mais que o potencial máximo de sequestro biológico, estimado em 38 bilhões de toneladas de 2015 a 2050. Antes do uso massivo de combustíveis fósseis, o ciclo do carbono estava em equilíbrio dinâmico—entradas e saídas se equilibravam. A industrialização com carvão, petróleo e gás desestabilizou esse equilíbrio ao liberar carbono acumulado por milhões de anos. O armazenamento de carbono nas plantas, solos e oceanos só compensa carbono já presente no ciclo, e não o excesso resultante da queima de fósseis. Apesar de o carbono de uma árvore e o do combustível fóssil serem quimicamente iguais, árvores só compensam carbono biológico perdido (como de árvores cortadas), não as emissões adicionais de fósseis. Confiar no plantio de árvores para compensar carbono fóssil faz com que futuras gerações precisem manter florestas permanentemente, enfrentando riscos como incêndios, tempestades e secas, que se intensificam com as mudanças climáticas. Dedicar terras a novas florestas reduz espaço para agricultura e outros usos. E, no momento, a derrubada de árvores no mundo ocorre ao dobro do ritmo do replantio. Críticos defendem que a ideia de 'emissões líquidas zero' pode ser uma forma de adiar decisões ou se enganar, permitindo a continuidade do uso de combustíveis fósseis. Na Nova Zelândia, por exemplo, subtrair o carbono capturado por florestas plantadas após 1990 nas contas pode dar a falsa impressão de 27% de redução nas emissões. Chamar o resto de 'emissões líquidas' pode ser ilusório, já que muitas árvores novas só substituem antigas ao invés de compensar emissões fósseis. Já ocorreram fraudes e créditos de carbono 'fantasma', e estudos mostram que muitos créditos negociados não correspondem a reduções reais. Apesar das críticas—including da Comissão de Mudança Climática da Nova Zelândia, que destaca que carbono fóssil lançado na atmosfera é praticamente permanente—há uma dependência generalizada das compensações. Além dos métodos naturais, técnicas de captura e armazenamento de carbono (CCS) vêm sendo promissoras, mas são caras, exigem muita energia, tiveram pouco sucesso até agora e não são necessariamente permanentes, segundo o IPCC. A energia líquida dos fósseis está diminuindo, e processos de captura podem piorar ainda mais esse cenário; o IPCC calcula que de 13% a 44% da energia extraída dos fósseis pode ser usada só na captura. Achar que é possível zerar as emissões sem mudanças econômicas e sociais profundas só posterga decisões inevitáveis. Mesmo replantando países inteiros com árvores, no máximo daria para absorver cerca de dez anos das atuais emissões globais. Reverter o desmatamento e restaurar florestas são fundamentais para lidar com emissões passadas por uso de solo, mas plantar árvores sozinho não compensa a poluição resultante do uso de combustíveis fósseis. A única solução real é restaurar florestas e, ao mesmo tempo, acabar com as emissões de carbono fóssil. Este artigo foi republicado de The Conversation sob licença Creative Commons.

Wildlife teams in boats worked Wednesday to guide nearly 50 pilot whales out of shallow, dangerous waters at Florida's Everglades National Park, hoping to prevent more deaths after 10 whales had already died. Blair Mase, coordinator for NOAA’s marine mammal stranding network, reported that six whales were found dead and four had to be euthanized due to poor condition. Some whales were stranded on the remote shoreline near Highland Beach, on the park’s western edge, about 20 miles from their usual deep-water habitat. 

Reaching the area takes more than an hour by boat, and the lack of cellphone service complicates rescue operations. ‘We want to keep expectations low because the challenges are very, very difficult,’ Mase explained. Park spokeswoman Linda Friar said rescuers attempted to herd the whales, which were in about three feet of water and roughly 75 feet from shore, back to sea, though the animals were uncooperative. 

Workers tried earlier in the day to nudge the whales into deeper water without success. Short-finned pilot whales typically inhabit deep ocean waters, and the shallow terrain poses additional risks. Even if attempts to lead the 41 remaining whales out to sea succeeded, they would face a maze of sandbars and shallow patches. The whales’ strong social bonds further complicate matters, as members of the group tend to follow each other, even into danger.

Officials learned of the stranding Tuesday around 4 p.m. but couldn’t reach the site before nightfall. When teams arrived Wednesday morning, 45 whales were still alive. The rescue strategy relies on keeping the animals safe during low tide, then using high tide to guide them back to deeper waters. So far, six whales have been rescued.

The precise reason for the stranding is unclear, but experts speculate the whales entered the complex system of sand flats and shoals on the Gulf side of the park and became cut off from their natural habitat and food source. Mase noted that more whales could face euthanasia if their condition worsens. Scientists are conducting necropsies to look for disease or clues to why the whales became stranded.

Rescue officials remain concerned about the future of the 41 remaining whales, acknowledging the odds are against a successful operation given the geography and the whales’ social behavior. ‘Ultimately, the outlook does not look good,’ Mase said.

Strandings like this are uncommon, though not unheard of: in 2012, 22 pilot whales stranded at Avalon State Park in Fort Pierce, Florida, and only five survived.

Equipes de resgate usaram barcos na quarta-feira para tentar guiar quase 50 baleias-piloto para fora das águas rasas e perigosas do Parque Nacional Everglades, na Flórida, tentando evitar mais mortes após 10 animais já terem morrido. Blair Mase, coordenadora da rede de encalhe de mamíferos marinhos da NOAA, informou que seis baleias foram encontradas mortas e quatro precisaram ser sacrificadas devido ao estado debilitado. Algumas baleias ficaram encalhadas em uma região remota próxima a Highland Beach, na parte oeste do parque, cerca de 32 quilômetros de onde vivem normalmente, em águas profundas.

O acesso à área leva mais de uma hora de barco e a falta de sinal de celular dificulta ainda mais o resgate. "Queremos manter as expectativas baixas porque os desafios são muito, muito difíceis", explicou Mase. A porta-voz do parque, Linda Friar, disse que as equipes tentaram cercar as baleias, que estavam em cerca de um metro de profundidade e a aproximadamente 23 metros da margem, para levá-las de volta ao mar, mas os animais não colaboraram.

Baleias-piloto de nadadeira curta vivem normalmente em águas oceânicas profundas, e o terreno raso representa riscos extras. Os laços sociais fortes entre as baleias complicam ainda mais, pois tendem a seguir umas às outras, mesmo em perigo.

Autoridades tomaram conhecimento do encalhe na terça-feira por volta das 16h, mas não conseguiram chegar antes do anoitecer. Quando as equipes chegaram na manhã de quarta-feira, encontraram 45 baleias ainda vivas. O motivo exato do encalhe é desconhecido, mas especialistas acreditam que as baleias entraram em um sistema de bancos de areia e áreas rasas do lado do Golfo e acabaram presas, isoladas do habitat e fonte de alimento. Mase comentou que outras baleias podem precisar ser sacrificadas se piorarem. Cientistas estão realizando necropsias para buscar doenças ou pistas sobre a razão do encalhe.

Equipes de resgate demonstram preocupação quanto ao futuro das 41 baleias remanescentes, reconhecendo que as chances de sucesso são pequenas devido à geografia e ao comportamento social. “No fim das contas, as perspectivas não são boas”, disse Mase.

Encasques como esse são incomuns, mas já aconteceram antes: em 2012, 22 baleias-piloto encalharam em Avalon State Park, em Fort Pierce, Flórida, e só cinco sobreviveram.
