article_content: A 2001 diary belonging to Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was discovered, offering insights into his affairs during the year his wife, Mary, gave birth to their fourth child. In a section labeled 'cash accounts,' Kennedy listed first names of women he was involved with, giving each a score out of ten. The list includes 37 women, with 16 names marked with a ten, believed to indicate intercourse. Alongside notes on his political activism and family life, the diary contains admissions of guilt and remorse over repeated infidelity. Kennedy frequently writes about struggling with his 'lust demons,' and marks days he resisted temptation as ‘victory.’ For example, on November 5, 2001, he wrote, ‘I’m like Adam and live in Eden, and I can have everything but the fruit. But the fruit is all I want.’ At one point, his wife, Mary Richardson Kennedy, found the red journal, and it reportedly contributed to her distress during their pending divorce. She died by suicide in May 2012. The diary later came into the possession of the New York Post. When questioned by a reporter, Kennedy denied keeping a diary during that year. In his early entries, Kennedy shares the news of his wife's pregnancy with their fourth child. He later writes about personal challenges, often using 'mugged' to describe being seduced. On February 6, he wrote about narrowly avoiding an encounter after praying for strength. On May 21, after dining with Leonardo DiCaprio, he noted being 'mugged' and gave a ten next to a woman's name, adding, ‘I’ve got to do better.’ In July 2001, Kennedy spent 30 days in jail in Puerto Rico after being arrested for trespassing at a U.S. Navy training facility in Vieques. He wrote positively about the experience, feeling that incarceration freed him from temptation, stating, ‘I’m so content here. There’s no women. I’m happy! Everybody here seems happy. It’s not misogyny. It’s the opposite! I love them too much.’ On July 8, days before his son Aiden was born, Kennedy wrote affectionately about his wife and expressed gratitude for his family and life. Kennedy also reflected on personal weaknesses and the challenge of living up to his father's legacy, writing, ‘After daddy died I struggled to be a grown-up... Every time I was afflicted with sexual thoughts, I felt a failure. I hated myself. I began to lie - to make up a character who was the hero and leader that I wished I was.’ Near the end of his jail time, Kennedy mentioned a 'three-point plan' to address his struggles with infidelity, but did not detail it. By mid-August, women's names reappear in his journal. Although Kennedy recognized many positive aspects of his life—such as family, wealth, health, and work—he acknowledged always wanting more. November 2001 saw a particularly high number of affairs, with at least one name recorded on 22 dates, including a string of 13 consecutive days, and three encounters in a single evening at a charity event.

É o oposto! Eu as amo demais.’ Em 8 de julho, poucos dias antes do nascimento do filho Aiden, Kennedy fez um registro carinhoso sobre a esposa e demonstrou gratidão pela família e pela vida. Kennedy também refletiu sobre suas fraquezas e o desafio de viver à altura do legado do pai, escrevendo: ‘Depois que papai morreu, lutei para ser adulto... Cada vez que tinha pensamentos sexuais, eu me sentia um fracasso. Me odiava. Passei a inventar um personagem, o herói e líder que eu queria ser.’ Perto do fim do tempo na prisão, Kennedy mencionou um ‘plano de três pontos’ para lidar com seus problemas de infidelidade, mas não detalhou o que seria. Em meados de agosto, nomes de mulheres voltam a aparecer em seu diário. Apesar de reconhecer muitas coisas boas em sua vida—família, riqueza, saúde e trabalho—Kennedy admitiu estar sempre buscando mais. Novembro de 2001 foi especialmente ativo, com ao menos um nome anotado em 22 datas, inclusive em 13 dias consecutivos, além de três encontros em uma única noite de evento beneficente.

article_content: Well-known figures like David Cameron, Donald Duck, and Marilyn Monroe have each had their own bedtime attire choices—ranging from pajamas to nothing at all. So, what truly is the best option for sleepwear? Research from the U.S. National Sleep Foundation shows that about one in three adults sleep naked, and experts say this could have significant benefits. Specialists emphasize that keeping cool at night is essential for quality sleep. Dr. Chris Idzikowski from the Edinburgh Sleep Centre explains that your body temperature needs to drop slightly to trigger sleep, and wearing fewer clothes makes this easier. Overheating can disrupt your ability to fall asleep or stay asleep. Professor Russell Foster, an Oxford expert in sleep science, adds that lighter or no nightwear helps the body regulate temperature, supporting deeper, more restorative sleep. This type of sleep aids memory and bodily repairs. Having warm hands and feet can help your core temperature decrease at bedtime. If your extremities are cold, your body tends to hold onto heat, making it harder to nod off. Conditions like Raynaud’s syndrome or hormonal changes in older adults and women can increase sensitivity to cold. A 2008 study in the Netherlands found that gently raising skin temperature—by even a small amount—helped participants, particularly older people, sleep more deeply and wake less often. Tools like hot water bottles are recommended over socks to warm feet, as they allow you to release heat. Sharing a bed can also help regulate temperature. Research into brown fat, a type of tissue that burns calories for warmth, indicates that sleeping in cooler rooms may stimulate its activity. A U.S. study in the journal Diabetes observed that people sleeping in cooler environments had more active brown fat and better insulin sensitivity, though comfort remains important. The habit of sleeping naked could also boost relationship happiness. A UK survey found higher satisfaction among those who skipped nightwear. Physical contact at night increases the release of oxytocin, a hormone linked to lower blood pressure and anxiety, according to Dr. Kerstin Uvnas-Moberg. Women may be able to lower their risk of infections like thrush by avoiding tight nightwear. Consultant gynecologist Austin Ugwumadu advises sleeping in loose garments or nothing at all to enable better airflow and comfort.

Russell Foster, professor da Universidade de Oxford e especialista em ciência do sono, acrescenta que usar roupas leves ou dormir sem roupas ajuda a regular a temperatura corporal, promovendo um sono mais profundo e restaurador, fundamental para a memória e a recuperação do corpo. article_content: In Kharkiv, in north-eastern Ukraine, authorities have announced plans to build the country’s first underground school. Mayor Ihor Terekhov explained that this project is intended to give thousands of children a safe way to attend school in person while missile attacks in the area continue. Since Russia’s large-scale invasion began in 2022, more than 360 schools have been destroyed and over 3,000 damaged throughout Ukraine. According to UNICEF, only about one in three Ukrainian students can currently take lessons in person due to ongoing attacks by missiles, drones, and artillery. Many children are now learning in improvised shelters such as metro stations, despite a lack of proper facilities. Meanwhile, the EU’s Fundamental Rights Agency reports that roughly 1.3 million Ukrainian children have fled to EU countries, where schools continue to face challenges integrating them. Mayor Terekhov made the announcement on social media, emphasizing that the new underground school will comply with advanced safety standards. He reaffirmed that educational funding will not be reduced, even with budget limitations. Specific details about when the school will open or its intended student capacity have not yet been shared. For now, over 1,000 students in Kharkiv are already attending classes at five metro stations that have been converted for school use. These children are transported by bus, attend school in two shifts (morning and afternoon), and are protected by police and emergency workers. Ukraine’s Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko commented on the unusual but necessary reality of holding classes underground. Due to Kharkiv’s location only 30 kilometers from the Russian border, the city was heavily bombarded and faced street combat during the first weeks of the conflict. Ukrainian forces pushed Russian troops out of the city during a swift counteroffensive last autumn.

article_content: Senior civil servants at the Department for Education (DfE) were asked to wear party hats during a directors meeting leading up to Christmas, while discussing ways to save money amid government-wide cuts. The meeting included the director of strategy and director of finance and was described internally by Simon Judge, the DfE’s director of finance, in a blog post on the government intranet. Participants had to keep their hats on until they shared their proposed cost-saving measures. The exercise was not photographed and was intended, according to Mr Judge, to encourage directors to identify ways to increase efficiency and reduce bureaucracy in their areas. Union representatives criticized the activity as 'highly insensitive,' especially as many staff members faced the prospect of job losses. The PCS Union sent a letter to the DfE, describing the meeting as inappropriate. However, the DfE responded by saying the activity addressed non-sensitive topics and did not include staff reduction discussions. They also referred to the union's characterization as 'inaccurate' and 'unhelpful.' Simon Judge wrote about the game in his weekly blog, accessible only to civil servants and officials, explaining that each participant stated which practices they would stop as part of the DfE's efficiency review, after which they could remove their party hats. The DfE clarified that the meeting focused on service improvements, streamlining systems, and reducing bureaucracy, which included proposals for saving money. Union representatives maintained their criticism, labeling the activity as 'outrageous' given the broader context of staff reductions. Currently, around 480 DfE staff work at Mowden Hall in Darlington, where employees could be transferred as part of potential nationwide civil service cutbacks of around 1,000 jobs. Kathy Prendiville, PCS education group secretary, expressed strong disapproval of the activity in a letter to Chris Wormald, the DfE’s permanent secretary, calling it a serious lapse in judgment, particularly during a time of staff anxiety about possible layoffs. Recently, hundreds of Mowden Hall workers protested to keep their jobs, and more than 1,100 people signed a petition to support them. Darlington MP Jenny Chapman stated her disappointment with DfE staff conduct, saying public sector workers should act with greater sensitivity. A DfE spokesperson said staff did not act insensitively and reiterated that the meeting was a routine directors’ gathering focused on strategic planning to improve systems – not on job cuts. The spokesperson added that management understood staff concerns about potential layoffs and remained committed to clear communication and support for affected employees, emphasizing the need for these changes to improve education and children's services in the country.

O sindicato PCS enviou uma carta ao DfE, descrevendo a reunião como inadequada. No entanto, o DfE respondeu dizendo que a atividade abordava temas não sensíveis e não incluía discussões sobre cortes de pessoal. Também classificaram a descrição do sindicato como 'imprecisa' e 'inútil'. Simon Judge comentou sobre a dinâmica em seu blog semanal, acessível apenas a servidores e funcionários, explicando que cada participante dizia quais práticas seriam encerradas como parte da revisão de eficiência do DfE, após o que poderia retirar o chapéu. Atualmente, cerca de 480 funcionários do DfE trabalham no Mowden Hall, em Darlington, onde podem ser transferidos como parte de cortes em toda a função pública de cerca de 1.000 empregos. Kathy Prendiville, secretária do grupo educacional do sindicato PCS, expressou forte desaprovação da atividade em carta a Chris Wormald, secretário permanente do DfE, classificando-a como um grave erro de julgamento, especialmente em um momento de ansiedade dos funcionários sobre possíveis demissões. A deputada Jenny Chapman, de Darlington, afirmou estar desapontada com a conduta dos funcionários do DfE, dizendo que trabalhadores do setor público devem agir com mais sensibilidade. Um porta-voz do DfE afirmou que os funcionários não agiram de forma insensível e reiterou que a reunião foi um encontro rotineiro de diretores, focado em planejamento estratégico para melhorar sistemas – e não em cortes de empregos. O porta-voz acrescentou que a gestão entende as preocupações dos funcionários sobre possíveis demissões e permanece comprometida com uma comunicação transparente e apoio aos afetados, destacando a necessidade dessas mudanças para melhorar a educação e os serviços para crianças no país.

article_content: Three people—a 27-year-old man from Denholme, a 32-year-old man from Thornton, and a 19-year-old woman from Denholme—died after a car crashed into a hairdresser's shop late last night in Bradford, West Yorkshire. The black Mitsubishi Evo left the road on Thornton Road, near its junction with Kipping Lane, just after 11pm before colliding with a stone building. Nearby residents rushed to help, but all three occupants died at the scene. The car was left badly damaged, and the shop, which was closed at the time, sustained significant damage and was boarded up the next day. Police are appealing for witnesses or anyone who saw the car prior to the crash to contact West Yorkshire Police's Major Collision Enquiry Team via 101. No other vehicles were involved in the collision. Local resident Andy Rushworth described arriving at the scene and attempting to help the victims but said there was nothing that could be done.

O Mitsubishi Evo preto saiu da pista na Thornton Road, perto do cruzamento com a Kipping Lane, pouco depois das 23h, antes de bater em um edifício de pedra. Moradores da região correram para ajudar, mas todos os três ocupantes morreram no local. O carro ficou completamente destruído, e o salão, que estava fechado no momento, sofreu danos significativos e foi fechado com tábuas no dia seguinte. A polícia está pedindo a testemunhas, ou a qualquer pessoa que tenha visto o carro antes do acidente, que entre em contato com a Equipe de Investigação de Colisões Graves da Polícia de West Yorkshire pelo telefone 101. Nenhum outro veículo esteve envolvido na colisão. O morador Andy Rushworth contou que chegou ao local e tentou ajudar as vítimas, mas disse que nada pôde ser feito.

article_content:
Hugh Rodley, a 65-year-old who claimed a noble title, faces a significant prison term after orchestrating a £6 million investment scam targeting mainly pensioners. Together with Julian Silver, Adam Corbett, and Sonny Willis, Rodley convinced roughly 600 elderly people to invest their savings in companies promising large returns, but these investments were fraudulent.

The group assembled detailed target lists—called 'sucker lists'—and persistently pressured their chosen victims into investing in companies like World Aqua Tech PLC and ART IT PLC. These firms conducted little or no actual business, and no investor saw any returns.

Money obtained through the scam was spent on luxury vehicles and renting an expensive home, as evidence presented in court confirmed. Despite being told their money would go into secure and exotic ventures, investors ultimately received nothing; one 87-year-old lost over £800,000.

This fraud ran from 2004 to 2007 and followed Rodley's previous conviction in 2010 for trying to steal £229 million from Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation—a plot foiled by a failed technical component. At Southwark Crown Court, Rodley and his partners were found guilty of conspiracy to defraud. Phillip Dennett was cleared of the fraud but convicted for laundering funds.

Prosecutor Simon Farrell called the operation a textbook 'boiler room fraud,' using relentless phone calls and sales pressure. Despite many victims being successful professionals, they were overcome by these aggressive tactics. Authorities found a 'floor book' listing over 1,000 potential targets, roughly 600 of whom were deceived. While £6 million was marked as investments, only about £2.7 million could be directly traced.

Rodley denied any wrongdoing, stating he acted in good faith and that his associates were genuine businessmen. A jury disagreed, returning a guilty verdict. Bernard Davies, accused of involvement, had died in 2009. The case outlined fraud across several companies from 2005 to 2007, with networks targeting people who previously invested small sums.

article_content: Border Patrol agents assigned to the El Centro Sector in California discovered drugs hidden inside the tires of a pickup truck at the California/Mexico border on Sunday, according to KESQ.com. Using a backscatter X-ray system similar to those at airport checkpoints, agents noticed abnormalities with the vehicle's tires. Inside, they found black tar heroin and methamphetamine, with a combined street value exceeding $650,000. The heroin alone was valued at $575,600, while the meth was estimated at $76,700. The truck's driver, a 43-year-old Mexican citizen, was arrested. Both the driver and the seized drugs are now in the custody of the Drug Enforcement Agency. Nearly 70 pounds of heroin and meth were discovered and displayed by Border Patrol agents at the Calexico station.

article_content: Phil Knight, known today as the co-founder of Nike, didn’t begin his journey as a star athlete. Growing up in Portland, Oregon, and competing at the University of Oregon, Knight’s running career was unremarkable, but his fascination with sneakers sparked a lifelong ambition: to create shoes for athletes. Early setbacks didn’t deter him. Instead, each loss fueled his drive and passion for improving footwear. After earning a scholarship to pursue an MBA at Stanford in 1962, Knight's career path shifted dramatically. During a pivotal entrepreneurship course—taught by his former track coach, Bill Bowerman—Knight was inspired by Bowerman’s experimental approach to creating better running shoes. This mentorship would prove crucial, both in sparking Knight’s innovative thinking and eventually forming a business partnership. Knight got his start in the shoe business by establishing Blue Ribbon Sports, distributing Japanese Tiger running shoes. Balancing work and study, he sold shoes from the trunk of his car while completing his MBA. After years of learning about the industry, Knight and Bowerman founded Nike in 1971, investing just $1,500 and aiming to design lighter, faster, performance-driven shoes for athletes. The now-iconic Nike 'Swoosh' logo was created by Carolyn Davidson, then a graphic design student at Portland State University. She was asked to design the logo, which Knight adopted in 1971, compensating her with a modest fee as a token of appreciation. Today, the 'Swoosh' is recognized around the world. Nike’s early years were challenging—building a brand from the ground up, managing supply chain issues, and facing intense competition. Breakthrough came during the 1972 Olympics, when Nike-sponsored athletes excelled, boosting the company’s sales to $3 million. Despite these successes, Knight and Bowerman wrestled with creative differences. Ultimately, relentless innovation and a focus on athlete needs propelled Nike to global prominence. Within two decades, Nike became the world’s top-selling athletic footwear brand. Estimates suggest that a third of adults worldwide own a pair of Nikes. The company has since expanded into apparel, equipment, and digital offerings, and sponsors many of the biggest names in sports, including Michael Jordan, Cristiano Ronaldo, Serena Williams, and the U.S. Olympic team. Nike’s rise is credited largely to Knight’s vision and leadership—he retired as chairman in 2016. Widely celebrated as one of the most influential entrepreneurs, Knight has received numerous awards and is known for his philanthropy, including billions donated to various organizations, especially the University of Oregon. Knight’s story highlights how determination and belief in one’s vision can transform failures into iconic global achievements. His journey from an average athlete to a pioneering business leader is a testament to perseverance. As he once said, 'The only time you must not fail is the last time you try.'

Peacock will be removing a number of movies at the end of November as part of its typical content rotation. Some titles, such as E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, have come and gone from the platform so many times that it’s hard to keep track. However, many of these films are likely to return in the future. Since you have a subscription for November, you might want to make the most of it while these titles are still available.

To help you plan your movie night, we’ve highlighted three films leaving Peacock this month that you shouldn’t miss: one acclaimed young adult adaptation and two movies produced by Judd Apatow.

With The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes now in theaters, it’s a great time to revisit the original films. The Hunger Games and its three sequels will only be available on Peacock through the end of November, so catch them while you can. Our top pick is the first film in the series, starring Jennifer Lawrence as Katniss Everdeen, a young woman who volunteers for a deadly competition to protect her younger sister. Alongside her is Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson), who claims to love Katniss despite barely knowing her. Facing off against 22 other tributes, Katniss and Peeta are told by the Gamesmaker, Seneca Crane (Wes Bentley), that there’s hope they can win together, even though there can only be one official victor.

Another must-watch is Step Brothers, a comedy featuring Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly as Brennan Huff and Dale Doback—two men in their 40s who still haven’t grown up. When their single parents (played by Mary Steenburgen and Richard Jenkins) get married, Brennan and Dale become reluctant stepbrothers and eventually realize they have plenty in common. Their immaturity puts a strain on their parents, who hope they’ll finally embrace adulthood.

Lastly, Amy Schumer’s Trainwreck delves into the messy life of Amy Townsend, a woman grappling with a drinking problem and fear of commitment. Amy’s relationship with her boyfriend Steven (John Cena) doesn’t fill the void in her life, but a new connection with Dr. Aaron Conners (Bill Hader) offers a potential path to change. The story also follows her tense bond with her sister Kim (Brie Larson) and her responsibilities caring for her ailing father (Colin Quinn), as Amy tries to cope with the chaos around her.

Watch The Hunger Games, Step Brothers, and Trainwreck on Peacock before they’re gone.

article_content: Julie Clark, cofounder of CAST Preschool and Childcare Center in Woodbury, Connecticut, said her goal was to form a community, not just a school. Some of her students' parents had attended the center as children themselves. After more than 30 years, Clark sold her childcare center this past summer. Clark, 68, said she will continue working as a consultant until the end of December. "I've become very involved in advocacy for early childhood, and I would like to stay involved with that, but I will not be going to work anywhere," Clark told Insider. She discussed selling her center and the challenges facing childcare, including low staff pay, labor shortages, and the high cost of care for families. "I have been writing letters to governors for 25 years about how early childhood is underfunded," Clark said. "Parents pay way too much for childcare." Clark believes more government support is needed. "The government needs to find a way to help fund early childhood, not only for teachers and businesses, but for the economy," she said. The American Rescue Plan helped centers pay employees, but much of that funding ended in September, and many centers risk closing or making cuts. Department of Labor data shows childcare costs thousands of dollars a year everywhere in the U.S. Clark said her center's tuition increased in recent years; annual costs for children under 3 attending CAST Preschool three days a week, 9 a.m. to 12 p.m., rose from $4,680 (2019-2020) to $5,263 (2023-2024). Allison Robinson, founder of The Mom Project, said parents often weigh childcare costs against the opportunity cost of staying home, describing it as an "investment" in their careers. She also highlighted the problem of "childcare deserts," where families can't access quality care. Some CAST Preschool teachers worked there for at least 15 years. Clark, who was a single mother, started hiring young mothers and offered free childcare for their children. Though her center was usually fully staffed, she knew others had to close classrooms due to staff shortages. Clark noted that many centers are being sold to corporations or other entities with more financial resources. With the funding 'cliff' ending support, Julie Kashen of The Century Foundation said centers may have to increase rates or close classrooms. "The more centers close classrooms or go out of business, the harder it is for parents to find care," Clark said, noting that infant and toddler care is especially difficult to secure due to legal ratios and high overhead. "We now have two nurseries, each limited to seven babies, because of the one-to-four teacher ratio. But seven babies for two people is still a lot. Overhead and labor costs are high, yet employees are not paid what they deserve," Clark said. Despite high prices, many providers struggle to make enough to sustain their businesses. Clark said she invested in her teachers, but still couldn't pay them what they're worth. Many earned between $15 and $20 an hour, per documents reviewed by Insider. "Early-childhood educators do not make what they're worth at all. It's more than a job. It has to be a passion—you don't do it for the money," she said, adding, "It should be a labor of love that pays well." The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the median wage for childcare workers in 2022 was $13.71/hour, much lower than the median for all occupations ($22.26/hour). Clark sold to a business she hopes can better support staff. Another key reason for selling was her cancer diagnosis in 2019 and the desire to spend more time with her husband. "With a cancer diagnosis, you don't know how much time you have left, and I wanted to make the most of it with my husband. The pandemic also made things difficult," Clark said. article_content: Barbara Metcalfe recounts her personal struggle with menopause, describing it as a 'waking nightmare.' Despite cold outdoor temperatures, she experiences intense night sweats, requiring frequent changes of sheets. Her partner, Peter, is supportive, though both have endured disrupted sleep. Metcalfe entered surgical menopause at age 50 after a hysterectomy due to abnormal pre-cancerous cells in her womb. She experiences severe symptoms, including hot flushes, insomnia, mood swings, memory issues, and physical discomfort, affecting her daily life. Feeling inadequately prepared or informed by medical professionals post-surgery, she turned to the internet for information. Both hormone replacement therapy and natural remedies provided little relief or caused unwanted side effects. Metcalfe emphasizes that menopause is rarely discussed openly, leaving many women feeling isolated. Workplace misunderstandings and lack of support compounded her difficulties, with exhaustion and cognitive symptoms making daily tasks harder. Although some, like broadcaster Jenni Murray, highlight positive aspects of menopause, Metcalfe finds her own experience debilitating. She has found some symptom relief through anti-depressants tested in clinical trials, but recognizes there is no cure. Metcalfe calls for greater awareness and better support for menopausal women in both healthcare and work environments.

Most children would rather play outside than watch television, but many are confined to their back gardens by cautious parents, according to new research. Safety concerns about traffic and stranger danger prevent children from venturing unaccompanied into the street, parks, woods, or other open spaces. As a result, areas that once encouraged adventure have become off-limits for many youngsters, even though they often prefer exploring outside to staying indoors with screens.

A study by Eureka! The National Children’s Museum in Halifax, West Yorkshire, highlighted this trend. The report, co-authored by museum staff, found that 81% of children surveyed preferred outdoor play over watching TV. However, 59% reported they were never allowed to leave the house or garden unsupervised.

The museum surveyed 1,367 adults and 1,456 children aged 5 to 11 about their play habits and attitudes. While 95% of adults agreed that risk is beneficial for play, one quarter believed play could be improved by making the world safer. Nearly half of parents (49.7%) admitted they do not permit their children to play outside their home or garden alone, and only 0.5% let their children explore as far as they want. Just 37% allow children to go to the end of the street without supervision.

When asked to choose their top three favorite places to play, children picked parks (54%), gardens (45%), and home (42%). In comparison, parents recalled their favorite childhood play spaces as the street (46.7%), fields or woods (44.5%), and the garden (39.8%).

Sixty-seven percent of children preferred free, unstructured play over organized games and activities. According to parents, children spend about 25 hours a week playing, with technology accounting for just 17% of this time.

The report “Play For Today” noted: “Contrary to media perceptions, children aren’t constantly glued to screens and actually prefer outdoor play. Parents recognize that play is essential for childhood development and value it as highly as formal education. However, time limitations and anxiety about unsupervised outdoor activity mean that families often default to keeping children indoors.”

The report warned that free, independent play in various outdoor environments is out of reach for many children unless accompanied by an adult. This raises concerns about children’s increasing indoor lifestyles and the early academic pressures they now face.

The survey also found that 33% of adults lack enough time to play with their children. In July, former children’s minister Tim Loughton highlighted that children could spend almost a year watching TV or using computers by age seven. In a report for the charity 4Children, Loughton cited research suggesting that children are at risk of developing a lifelong dependency on screens and called for reduced emphasis on health and safety restrictions that limit rough-and-tumble play. NHS statistics indicate that hospital admissions of children after falling from trees have halved in the past decade.

article_content: In challenging times, a nation instinctively looks to its leader for comfort and direction. This was evident after the tragic school shooting in Connecticut, just as it has been throughout American history. Among presidents, Abraham Lincoln stands out as someone who truly embraced the role of both decision-maker and morale-booster, relentlessly pursuing justice even in the darkest hours. Steven Spielberg’s film 'Lincoln', currently receiving multiple award nominations, invites audiences to see a more human, intricate side of this iconic figure, far beyond the polished stories presented in classrooms. Instead of a flawless hero, viewers encounter a president wrestling with extraordinary moral and political dilemmas. The movie zeroes in on the final months of the Civil War, specifically Lincoln’s tense campaign to persuade Congress to pass the 13th Amendment, permanently ending slavery in the United States. In a powerful scene, Daniel Day-Lewis, portraying Lincoln, questions whether the suffering caused by the ongoing war should end immediately. The film argues that Lincoln may have chosen to let the conflict continue, using the war’s horrors as leverage to gain political support for the amendment. Though this point remains debated among historians, the film maker’s perspective is well-supported within the story. Lincoln’s pursuit of his goal was not always pure or noble in every detail. The film reveals how he and his allies, including his Secretary of State William Seward, rallied both Republicans and Democrats in Congress, sometimes resorting to questionable methods. Political operatives, under Seward’s caution to avoid illegal acts and mentioning the president, offered patronage jobs and other incentives in exchange for votes. Even Lincoln’s cooperation with radical Republicans, led by Thaddeus Stevens, came with moral compromises. Based on Doris Kearns Goodwin’s research, the story also highlights Lincoln’s ability to unite former political opponents in his cabinet, showing true leadership in assembling a team that worked towards a common goal. This approach later inspired visible examples in modern politics, such as when President Obama included Hillary Clinton in his Cabinet after running against her. 'Lincoln' doesn’t romanticize politics. It presents the rough reality, where idealism often collides with the need for strategic maneuvering. The film reminds us how dramatically America’s notions of equality have evolved, and how yesterday’s ‘radicals’—chiefly found among Republicans of the era—fought for what is now broadly accepted. While the story offers plenty for idealists and realists alike, it ultimately suggests that even great progress can involve hard decisions and ethical uncertainty. Lincoln’s unwavering vision kept him focused on the greater good, even as he faced criticism for his tactics. Spielberg’s film encourages viewers to reflect on how solutions to today’s challenges—whether they relate to civil rights, political divisions, or systemic change—require both determination and the courage to make difficult choices. Lincoln’s legacy is a powerful reminder that morally ambiguous paths can still lead to lasting justice.

article_content: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius has acknowledged that the EU will not meet its goal of delivering one million artillery shells to Ukraine by March 2024. Speaking before EU defense ministers in Brussels, Pistorius admitted the promise, announced in March as a historic deal to send one million 155-mm shells within a year, will fall short. Ukrainian forces continue to face shortages in crucial ammunition as they confront Russian advances. President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that these shortages contributed to delays in starting Ukraine’s widely anticipated summer counteroffensive. Ukrainian officials have observed that Russian troops fire between 25,000 and 30,000 shells per day—up to four times more than Ukrainian forces. A coalition of 25 EU countries and Norway pledged to accelerate their supply of ammunition to Ukraine via the European Defence Agency, pooling resources through existing stockpiles and joint procurement. This effort was a significant shift from the EU's usual practice of individual national defense policies. Still, Pistorius clarified that he had never personally promised the delivery of one million shells and acknowledged earlier doubts about the feasibility of the target, saying, 'Those concerns have unfortunately proven correct.' Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba commented that although EU political support for Ukraine remains strong, bureaucracy and underdeveloped defense production continue to hinder efforts. Kuleba mentioned persistent problems with ammunition production capacities, logistical issues, and challenges in securing external manufacturing contracts. According to EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell, Europe’s defense industry needs to reprioritize and redirect more of its output to Ukraine rather than exporting nearly 40% of products to other countries. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg noted that the UK, US, and other Western allies are expanding their production as well, with improvements also seen in Germany and other EU states. The Pentagon reported in September that monthly shell production has reached 28,000 units, with the aim of boosting this number to 57,000 by spring, supporting both Ukraine’s military and replenishing US resources. President Zelensky recently warned of intensified Russian attacks near the eastern cities of Donetsk, Kupyansk, and Avdiivka. Vitaliy Barabash, head of Avdiivka’s military administration, described the destruction of the town—where over 1,500 civilians still remain—and emphasized its strategic value due to its location on elevated ground overlooking Donetsk. In addition, three people died and 15 were wounded in Russian shelling of the Kherson region on Tuesday. Minister Kuleba stressed that Ukraine now stands as Europe’s frontline, insisting on the urgent need for the EU and candidate countries to enhance the quality and capacity of their defense industries.

article_content: Aston Villa ended their winless run with a slim 1-0 victory over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park, courtesy of Christian Benteke’s goal in the first half. Benteke, back on the pitch after serving a suspension and recovering from an injury, pounced on a defensive blunder from Palace’s Scott Dann at the 32-minute mark, neatly finishing past Julian Speroni. This was Benteke’s first goal since March and eased the pressure mounting on Villa manager Paul Lambert, who has been under scrutiny from supporters. Villa looked unsettled early, needing a crucial goal-line clearance by Ciaran Clark after goalkeeper Brad Guzan mishandled Yannick Bolasie’s attempt. Palace pressed for an early advantage and appealed for a penalty when Tom Cleverley challenged Wilfried Zaha, but the official allowed play to continue. Joe Cole’s return was brief, as he limped off with a hamstring injury after nine minutes. The decisive play saw Dann failing to clear a pass, allowing Benteke to intercept and score. Although Palace created several chances—most notably a diving header from Marouane Chamakh and a last-minute scramble in the Villa area—Guzan’s key saves ensured Villa maintained their lead. Post-match, Lambert commended Benteke’s influence and expressed hope that the striker could avoid injuries and suspensions going forward. Meanwhile, Palace boss Neil Warnock expressed frustration at not being awarded a penalty and recognized Benteke’s impact. The game drew a crowd of 23,935, with Michael Oliver officiating.

article_content: Scotland coach Steve Clarke praised his team's progress after they secured a spot at next year's European Championship with two games to spare. Spain's 1-0 victory over Norway on Sunday guaranteed Scotland a top-two finish in Group A, earning them automatic qualification for Euro 2024 in Germany. This achievement marks only the second time that Scotland has qualified for consecutive European Championship finals, the first being for the 1992 and 1996 tournaments. "I would like to congratulate the players for their efforts in qualifying for back-to-back tournaments," Clarke said. "I'm not sure they will fully appreciate the importance of their achievement yet, but to qualify for successive Euros after more than 20 years is phenomenal and a testament to their hard work. I said after Euro 2020 that we wanted to become regular qualifiers, and reaching successive Euro finals shows the progress we've made." Clarke mentioned the team would celebrate qualification before shifting focus to preparing for Tuesday's friendly against France. "Then we turn our attention to Georgia and Norway next month and aim to finish with as many points as possible," he added. Captain Andy Robertson, who left the squad during the international break due to a shoulder injury picked up in the 2-0 defeat to Spain, described qualification as 'mission accomplished'. "Euro 2020 was a great experience, and our goal next summer is to build on that experience and improve on our last tournament performance," the defender said.

Esse feito marca apenas a segunda vez que a Escócia se classifica para finais consecutivas do Campeonato Europeu, a primeira tendo ocorrido nos torneios de 1992 e 1996. "Gostaria de parabenizar os jogadores pelo esforço em garantir vaga em dois torneios seguidos", disse Clarke. "Não tenho certeza se eles vão realmente perceber a importância do que conquistaram, mas se classificar para duas Euros seguidas após mais de 20 anos é fenomenal e prova do trabalho árduo deles. Disse depois da Euro 2020 que queríamos nos tornar presenças constantes em grandes competições, e chegar a duas finais de Euro seguidas mostra o progresso que tivemos." Clarke comentou que a equipe iria comemorar a classificação antes de focar na preparação para o amistoso contra a França, nesta terça. "Depois, vamos focar em Geórgia e Noruega no mês que vem, buscando terminar com o maior número de pontos possível", acrescentou. article_content: Recent heavy rains in southern Brazil have caused the famous Iguazu Falls, located on the border between Argentina and Brazil, to swell to nearly their highest water volumes in a decade. Authorities report that flooding has submerged one of the park's main tourist walkways. Storms in the Brazilian state of Paraná led to a surge of water flow through the massive falls, reaching 24.2 million liters per second on Monday. This marks the second-highest flow ever recorded at Iguazu, more than 16 times the falls' normal rate of 1.5 million liters per second. "It is the highest volume of water in recent years," said Urbia, the company managing the national park that surrounds the falls, an important biodiversity hotspot. The greatest recorded water volume occurred in 2014, when the falls reached an astonishing 46.3 million liters per second. Raging, muddy floodwaters nearly engulfed the park’s top attraction, the tourist walkway leading to the Devil’s Throat, renowned for its breathtaking panoramic views. Park officials kept the walkway closed on Tuesday for safety, even as water levels began to recede to 18.1 million liters per second. Iguazu Falls ranks among the largest waterfall systems in the world, featuring 275 individual waterfalls formed by the Iguazu River.

article_content: Kibbutz Be'eri, just three miles from Gaza, was once considered far from the frontlines of conflict. Today, its deserted streets bear scars of violence. In the home where seven members of Gilad Korngold’s family were kidnapped by Hamas, little remains of family life: bullet holes mark the walls, rooms are charred and collapsed by fire, and metal doors are riddled with gunfire. “Look at this!” Gilad says, holding back tears as he walks inside. “This is how much they hate us.” The safe-room door withstood bullets, but steel shutters were forced open. Among the kidnapped are his son Tal, daughter-in-law Adi, eight-year-old grandson Naveh, and three-year-old granddaughter Yahel. It is the first time Gilad has seen the house, which belongs to Adi’s parents, since the attack. He reflects, “It’ll take generations to rebuild the kibbutz, if they rebuild at all. I think many people won’t return.” What was destroyed here isn’t just physical homes, but also Israel’s assurance to its citizens of safety—even so close to Gaza. “It was an illusion,” Gilad says. “For 25 years, we thought we were safe and strong here. But now, I hope someone realizes a new strategy is needed.” Inside the empty home, the challenge facing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is clear: restoring public trust in Israel’s ability to protect its people, while also facing rising pressure to secure the release of more than 200 hostages held in Gaza—including Gilad’s family. Secret negotiations are reportedly ongoing. Hamas has suggested it might free the hostages in exchange for all Palestinian prisoners held in Israel. Many families, including Gilad’s, believe Israel should do whatever it takes. However, Israel’s government remembers that the Hamas leader in Gaza, Yahya Sinwar—now blamed for this attack—was himself freed in a prisoner swap 12 years ago. Netanyahu faces a difficult choice: risk national security to secure the hostages’ release, or maintain his current stance. He has defended his government’s intense bombardment of Gaza in conversations with the hostages’ families, asserting that destroying Hamas and rescuing hostages remain joint priorities. “The key is the level of pressure,” he told them. “The greater the pressure, the greater the chances.” Still, many families remain unconvinced. Gilad recalls staying awake all night during the escalation of Israeli air strikes, desperately waiting for news. Support for hostage families has grown following widespread media coverage, with more people joining their rallies. A recent poll by a major Israeli newspaper showed public support for a ground invasion had dropped from over two-thirds to less than a third in a week—including as four hostages were released by Hamas. Yet, early indicators show Israelis are deeply divided over releasing Palestinian prisoners in exchange for the hostages. While the government’s objectives have fostered national unity, debate continues around the methods used. In Tel Aviv, a new clock marks every hour since the hostages were taken, surrounded by posters and ongoing vigils. The hostages’ families—and the nation—await news as Israel faces irrevocable change. Back in Be’eri, the sounds of continuing strikes reach empty streets every few minutes. Amid the ashes, Gilad finds his grandson’s football, preserved under a layer of soot—a reminder of life before the attack.

Negociações secretas estariam em andamento. O Hamas sugeriu que pode libertar os reféns em troca de todos os prisioneiros palestinos em Israel. Muitas famílias, incluindo a de Gilad, acreditam que Israel deve fazer o que for necessário. Por outro lado, o governo israelense lembra que o líder do Hamas em Gaza, Yahya Sinwar — agora responsabilizado por este ataque — foi libertado em uma troca de prisioneiros há 12 anos. Ele tem defendido os bombardeios intensos em Gaza nas conversas com famílias de reféns, ressaltando que destruir o Hamas e resgatar os reféns são prioridades conjuntas. “A chave é o grau de pressão”, disse a eles. “Quanto maior a pressão, maiores as chances.” Ainda assim, muitas famílias não se sentem convencidas. Gilad recorda ter passado a noite acordado durante a intensificação dos ataques israelenses, esperando notícias desesperadamente. Uma pesquisa recente de um jornal israelense mostrou que o apoio público à invasão terrestre caiu de mais de dois terços para menos de um terço em uma semana — período em que quatro reféns foram libertados pelo Hamas. Embora os objetivos do governo tenham promovido união nacional, persiste o debate sobre os métodos. Em Tel Aviv, um novo relógio marca cada hora desde que os reféns foram levados, cercado por cartazes e vigílias constantes. As famílias dos reféns — e o país — aguardam novidades enquanto Israel passa por mudanças irreversíveis. De volta a Be'eri, sons de ataques continuam ecoando pelas ruas vazias a cada poucos minutos. Entre as cinzas, Gilad encontra a bola de futebol do neto, preservada sob a fuligem — uma lembrança da vida antes do ataque.

Britney Spears debuted a new brunette look at Elton John's Oscars viewing party on Sunday night but experienced an awkward moment when she misidentified the designer of her dress. When asked by WWD about her plunging black sequin gown, the 31-year-old singer claimed it was by Versace. In reality, it was designed by Michael Cinco Couture—a fact that was later clarified by her publicist.

Although it's expected that a celebrity’s stylist handles wardrobe details, it's still surprising Britney was unaware of which label lent her a gown likely worth thousands. In contrast, Beyoncé is known for returning borrowed dresses dry-cleaned with handwritten thank-you notes, according to designer Rubin Singer. On the other end of the spectrum, Lindsay Lohan reportedly altered a borrowed Theia Couture gown with scissors after it tore, as Us Weekly reported.

Britney, newly single after her split from fiancé Jason Trawick, looked stunning at the event, which was also attended by Emma Roberts, Nicki Minaj, and Anna Paquin. Lately, she is rumored to be dating a man named David, who works in field research at a law firm.

article_content: Oscar-winning filmmaker Malik Bendjelloul died by suicide last month at the age of 36. He tragically ended his life at Stockholm's Solna Centrum station during rush hour, about a year after winning an Academy Award for his documentary 'Searching for Sugar Man.' Friends and family were initially puzzled by his death but later reported observing significant changes in his behavior as Bendjelloul dealt with sudden fame and searched for a new creative project. His brother, Johar Bendjelloul, confirmed that Malik had suffered a brief period of depression. 'Depression is something you can die from,' he said. Close friends described Bendjelloul as a generally happy person, making his death even more shocking. Karin af Klintberg, a friend, stated, 'He was the least likely person to take his own life.' In the last year, Bendjelloul became more isolated and lonely. The success of 'Searching for Sugar Man'—the story of musician Sixto Rodriguez, who was rediscovered after years of living in poverty—left him uncertain about his next steps. He spent several months in New York working on a project about a South African conservationist but developed insomnia and reported feeling lonely. After returning to Sweden in early May, he briefly considered a new project offered by Klintberg but withdrew a day later, saying he wanted a smaller challenge. Friends believe his struggle to find a new direction contributed to his mental health decline. Mentor Per Sinding Larsen said, 'When there wasn’t anything to work on, the darkness came up.' Bendjelloul was known for his precise routines, such as running laps in his apartment at the start and end of each workday and writing from 8 am to noon every day. He maintained strict habits outside of work as well, including eating the same breakfast daily for months and ending a past relationship at an exact milestone. Klintberg reflected that these routines may have been a way for Bendjelloul to avoid disappointment. She described his experience with depression as unexpected and overwhelming. 'Searching for Sugar Man' won multiple awards, including the Oscar, BAFTA, and honors from numerous film guilds. Bendjelloul grew up in Sweden, studied journalism and media production, and previously worked for Swedish broadcaster SVT before traveling and discovering the idea for his documentary. For confidential help, call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-8255 or visit http://www.suicidepreventionlifeline.org/

article_content: Vaishnavi Group, a real estate developer, has entered into an agreement with Manipal Hospitals, a leading multi-speciality hospital chain, to develop a built-to-suit hospital in South Bengaluru. This initiative strengthens the partnership between the two companies. The proposed hospital, named Vaishnavi Sushrutha after the renowned Indian surgeon Sushrutha, will occupy a super built-up area of 3.3 lakh square feet. Designed as a tertiary care facility, it will provide 250 beds and offer a comprehensive range of curative and preventive healthcare services. Construction of the hospital began in March 2022 on Kanakapura Main Road and is expected to be completed by December 2024. Upon completion, it will be one of the most advanced hospitals in the city. Darshan Govindaraju, Director at Vaishnavi Group, stated that the evolving needs of the medical and wellness industry, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic, have heightened public health awareness and increased demand for specialized healthcare. He emphasized that extending the partnership with Manipal Hospitals reflects Vaishnavi’s reputation as a preferred partner for specialized projects. A spokesperson for Manipal Hospitals expressed enthusiasm for the collaboration and highlighted the organization's commitment to expanding high-quality healthcare across Bengaluru. According to a report by international property consultant CBRE, India will require 1.3 billion square feet of additional healthcare space and 2.9 million more hospital beds by 2030 to reach the global average of 3.2 beds per 1,000 people. Growing medical tourism and the demand for private healthcare in both rural and urban areas are expected to further drive sector growth.

Essa iniciativa fortalece a parceria entre as duas empresas. O hospital proposto, chamado Vaishnavi Sushrutha em homenagem ao renomado cirurgião indiano Sushrutha, terá uma área construída de 33 mil metros quadrados. Projetado como uma unidade de atendimento terciário, contará com 250 leitos e oferecerá uma ampla gama de serviços de saúde curativos e preventivos. Ele destacou que a ampliação da parceria com o Manipal Hospitals reforça a reputação da Vaishnavi como parceira preferencial para projetos especializados. Um porta-voz do Manipal Hospitals demonstrou entusiasmo com a colaboração e destacou o compromisso em ampliar o acesso a cuidados de saúde de qualidade em Bengaluru. Segundo relatório da consultoria internacional CBRE, a Índia precisará de 1,3 bilhão de metros quadrados adicionais em espaços de saúde e de mais 2,9 milhões de leitos hospitalares até 2030 para atingir a média global de 3,2 leitos por mil habitantes. article_content: A couple lost their bid for compensation from a travel agent after claiming their holiday in Turkey was disrupted by the call to prayer from a nearby mosque. The German man and woman, who were not named, requested a refund of half of the £1,900 spent on their all-inclusive stay, stating they were disturbed by the sound of the Adhan five times daily. They said their trip to Doganbey, a town on Turkey’s Aegean coast, was ruined by loudspeaker announcements from a nearby mosque starting at 6am. In their complaint against a travel agent in Hannover, they said they could not relax at the five-star Angora Beach Resort Hotel. The couple also sought compensation for a missing armrest on their flight and a rough landing on their return journey. Hannover district court dismissed the complaint last week, finding the unnamed travel agent was not at fault. The court stated the couple should have expected the sounds of the call to prayer due to the hotel’s central location, likening it to the ringing of church bells in Germany. ‘The complainants should have taken this authentic sound into account while booking the resort,’ the court said, as quoted by The Local. ‘The call to prayer is customary in Turkey and comparable with church bells in a Christian country. This does not constitute a deficiency of service.’ The court also ruled that the bumpy landing was due to weather, which was outside the tourism company’s control. ‘Since landings depend on weather conditions, passengers might have to experience occasional rough touch downs,’ the court added.

Disseram que a viagem para Doganbey, uma cidade na costa do Egeu, foi prejudicada pelos anúncios em alto-falante de uma mesquita próxima a partir das 6h. Na reclamação contra uma agência de viagens em Hannover, alegaram que não conseguiram relaxar no hotel cinco estrelas Angora Beach Resort. O casal também solicitou compensação por um apoio de braço faltando no voo e por uma aterrissagem difícil na viagem de volta. O tribunal distrital de Hannover rejeitou a queixa na semana passada, considerando que a agência de viagens não era responsável. O tribunal afirmou que o casal deveria esperar ouvir o chamado à oração devido à localização central do hotel, comparando-o ao toque dos sinos das igrejas na Alemanha. "Os reclamantes deveriam ter considerado esse som autêntico ao reservar o resort", disse o tribunal, conforme citado pelo The Local. "O chamado à oração é tradicional na Turquia e comparável ao toque de sinos em um país cristão. Isso não é uma falha nos serviços oferecidos." O tribunal também decidiu que a aterrissagem difícil foi causada pelo clima, algo fora do controle da empresa turística. "Como as aterrissagens dependem das condições meteorológicas, os passageiros podem enfrentar pousos bruscos ocasionalmente", acrescentou o tribunal.

article_content: The Woodland Hills Youth Development Center in Nashville is once again under scrutiny following a series of concerning events involving violence and escape attempts. This week alone, two significant disturbances have shed light on ongoing security issues and staff shortages. On Wednesday night, about 28 teens broke out from a common area into the yard, some wielding sticks and discharging a fire extinguisher. Officials reported two staff members suffered minor injuries. Just two days earlier, 32 youths escaped through a weak point in the perimeter fence; by Thursday, six of them were still missing. Footage and photos showed teens roaming the facility’s grounds with improvised weapons, using fire extinguishers, and even climbing onto the roof to throw rocks. Law enforcement and SWAT teams formed a perimeter to prevent further escapes and eventually brought the situation under control. Ten identified ringleaders were transferred to another detention center. Some participants in Wednesday’s incident were also involved in the earlier mass escape. These episodes add to the troubled history of Woodland Hills, which houses juveniles aged 14 to 19, most convicted of three or more felonies. The center has faced a spike in assaults, and federal assessments have flagged significant concerns over staff-related abuse. Records show police have responded to numerous violent incidents at the facility, including attacks on staff. Although Woodland Hills is more like a secure high school than a traditional prison, with no guard towers or barbed wire, security challenges remain. Monday’s breakout was enabled by insufficient overnight staffing and a compromised section of the fence. While some escapees were caught by police or returned by their families, their relatives voiced anxious hopes for the teens’ safety upon return. Residents are held in individual locked rooms but have access to common areas, wear standard uniforms, and participate in education and job training. Despite rehabilitation being the focus, recent events have led officials, such as Commissioner Jim Henry, to initiate security and policy reviews at all state juvenile facilities. These incidents highlight ongoing difficulties balancing safety with rehabilitation, and question the effectiveness of the current system in safeguarding both youths and staff.

SHIZUOKA CITY: In a distillery still fueled by cedar wood from nearby forests, the Shizuoka Distillery, a leader among Japan's new wave of independent whisky makers, crafts its spirits to meet surging global demand. This year marks the 100th anniversary of whisky production in Japan, following the founding of Suntory's first distillery in Yamazaki in 1923. At this milestone, Japan boasts more than 100 licensed distilleries—twice as many as 10 years ago—with each aiming to make its mark in this rapidly expanding market.

Shizuoka Distillery claims that its cedar fire is the world's only wood-fueled blaze beneath a whisky still, distinguishing itself among new makers. While these businesses are small compared to beverage giants like Suntory, their ambitions match those of more established names.

Taiko Nakamura, age 54, was inspired to found Shizuoka Distillery in 2016 after a trip to Scotland. "I saw this distillery, and I was amazed that such a small place in the mountains could sell whisky around the world," he said. "That made me want to make my own whisky and have people globally enjoy it."

The craft whisky surge in Japan follows earlier cycles of boom and bust. Once considered an imitation of Scotch, Japanese single malts and blends began winning international awards around 2008. This recognition sent global demand soaring, eventually outpacing supply by about 2015 and causing prices to rise dramatically. For instance, a set of 54 bottles from Ichiro's Malt, a leader in Japanese craft whisky, sold for $1.5 million at a Hong Kong auction in 2020. Recently, Sotheby's auctioned what it called the most valuable collection of Japanese whisky ever, featuring a 52-year-old bottle that sold for 300,000 pounds ($373,830).

Major producers Suntory and Nikka (a division of Asahi Group) have spent the last decade increasing capacity and stock, as Japanese whisky must be aged at least three years under 2021 regulations. Suntory, the nation's best-known whisky producer, recently invested 10 billion yen ($67 million) to upgrade its distilleries, including its Yamazaki site. Chief blender Shinji Fukuyo welcomes new Japanese distillers, saying Suntory is happy to advise startups if it helps raise the overall quality of Japanese whisky.

Foreign investment is also entering Japan’s whisky industry. In 2021, global beverage company Diageo bought an undisclosed stake in Komasa Kanosuke Distillery, founded in 2017 by a traditional shochu maker. The IJW Whiskey Company of Kentucky has launched a Japanese subsidiary, Cedarfield, building what may become Japan's largest distillery in Hokkaido, according to a Nikkei report in March. Cedarfield declined to comment on its plans.

However, the influx of new players and increased supply has raised concerns in the industry about lower-quality spirits potentially harming Japan's reputation. "That's a real fear," said Casey Wahl, an American who started Kamui Whisky on the remote island of Rishiri, near Japan's northern edge.

Nakamura of Shizuoka Distillery says that small producers can only stay true to the process and wait for the results. "I believe we need to put all our effort into making Japanese whisky that lives up to the standards set by our predecessors," he said.

CIDADE DE SHIZUOKA: Em uma destilaria ainda abastecida por madeira de cedro das florestas próximas, a Shizuoka Distillery, referência entre a nova onda de produtores independentes de uísque do Japão, produz destilados para atender à crescente demanda global. Este ano marca os 100 anos da produção de uísque no Japão, desde a fundação da primeira destilaria da Suntory em Yamazaki em 1923. Neste marco, o país já conta com mais de 100 destilarias licenciadas — o dobro de dez anos atrás — e todas buscam se destacar em um mercado que não para de crescer.

A Shizuoka Distillery afirma que seu fogo à base de cedro é o único do mundo usado sob um alambique de uísque, o que a diferencia dos novos produtores. Apesar de serem pequenos em relação a gigantes como a Suntory, estes negócios têm ambições tão grandes quanto os nomes mais tradicionais.

Taiko Nakamura, 54 anos, decidiu fundar a Shizuoka Distillery em 2016 após uma viagem à Escócia. "Vi uma destilaria e fiquei impressionado que um lugar tão pequeno nas montanhas vendesse uísque para o mundo todo", conta ele. "Quis então fazer meu próprio uísque para que pessoas de todos os cantos possam experimentar."

O avanço dos uísques artesanais no Japão vem após ciclos de crescimento e queda no setor. Antes visto como mera imitação do Scotch, o uísque japonês começou a ganhar prêmios internacionais a partir de 2008. Isso fez a demanda global explodir, superando a oferta por volta de 2015 e impulsionando os preços. Um conjunto de 54 garrafas da Ichiro's Malt, pioneira no uísque artesanal japonês, foi vendido por US$ 1,5 milhão em leilão em Hong Kong, em 2020. Recentemente, a Sotheby's vendeu o que chamou de coleção mais valiosa de uísques japoneses em leilão, com uma garrafa de 52 anos por 300 mil libras (US$ 373.830).

Grandes produtoras como Suntory e Nikka (do grupo Asahi) ampliaram a produção e o estoque na última década, já que o uísque japonês precisa ser envelhecido por no mínimo três anos segundo normas de 2021. A Suntory, maior nome do segmento, investiu recentemente 10 bilhões de ienes (US$ 67 milhões) na modernização de suas destilarias, incluindo a de Yamazaki. O mestre blender Shinji Fukuyo afirma apoiar os novos produtores japoneses, e diz que a Suntory está disposta a aconselhar startups que ajudem a elevar o padrão do uísque nacional.

O setor também atrai investidores estrangeiros. Em 2021, a multinacional Diageo comprou participação (valor não divulgado) na Komasa Kanosuke Distillery, fundada em 2017 por um tradicional fabricante de shochu. A americana IJW Whiskey Company criou a subsidiária Cedarfield, que está construindo o que pode ser a maior destilaria do Japão em Hokkaido, segundo o jornal Nikkei. A Cedarfield não comentou os planos.

No entanto, o crescimento rápido e a entrada de tantos novos concorrentes preocupam o setor pela possível queda de qualidade e danos à reputação japonesa. "Esse é um medo real", disse Casey Wahl, americano fundador da Kamui Whisky na remota ilha de Rishiri, no extremo norte do Japão.

Nakamura, da Shizuoka, acredita que pequenos produtores só podem respeitar o processo e aguardar resultados. "Acho que precisamos dedicar todo nosso esforço para produzir uísques à altura dos padrões dos nossos antecessores", conclui.

article_content: Asian stocks mostly climbed Tuesday as investors waited for significant events such as a US-China summit and the release of key economic data from the US, Japan, and China. Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose by 0.5% to close at 32,757.44, while Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 increased by 0.6% to 6,992.10. South Korea’s Kospi jumped 1.1% to 2,429.21. In contrast, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index slipped 0.4% to 17,359.13, and the Shanghai Composite edged up only slightly, finishing at 3,047.13. According to Stephen Innes from SPI Asset Management, Asian markets were buoyed ahead of US inflation data, with investors hoping for signs that interest rates may have reached a peak. The anticipation of discussions between US President Joe Biden and China’s President Xi Jinping at a Pacific Rim summit also contributed to a more upbeat mood. The meeting will mark their first in-person talks in a year and takes place amid the world’s two leading economies navigating delicate relations. China is scheduled to publish its monthly economic indicators on Wednesday, while Japan is set to report its latest GDP data. These updates are expected to give investors deeper insights into regional economic health. On Wall Street, trading started the week on a mixed note: the S&P 500 dipped by 0.1% to 4,411.55, the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.2% to 13,767.74, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.2% to close at 34,337.87. The current corporate earnings season is winding down, with most companies having exceeded analyst forecasts. This week, retail giants like Target, TJX, and Walmart are expected to release their latest results, focusing attention not just on recent performance but predictions for the months ahead. The US economy remains resilient even after the Federal Reserve recently raised interest rates to their highest since 2001. However, uncertainty remains about whether growth can continue as the effects of higher borrowing costs filter through. That’s why investors are watching the October inflation report closely. Economists expect inflation to continue cooling, with prices likely up 3.3% over the year, compared to 3.7% in September. Should this trend persist, it could prompt the Fed to pause further rate increases and possibly consider cutting rates sooner than anticipated. Elsewhere, the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note remains at 4.63%, unchanged from late Friday but down from recent highs over the past month on speculation the Fed may halt its rate hikes. Nonetheless, yields remain well above historical averages, putting pressure on high-growth sectors like tech. Apple shares fell 0.9%, and Microsoft was down 0.8%, weighing on the overall S&P 500. Moody’s, the credit rating agency, warned it might eventually downgrade the US’s top-tier 'AAA' debt rating, citing rising interest costs and persistent political divisions in Congress. The threat of a government shutdown and ongoing concerns over the national deficit have also contributed to increased Treasury yields. On the commodities front, oil prices inched up, with US crude trading at $78.42 a barrel after a 16-cent increase, and Brent crude rising 17 cents to $82.69. In currency markets, the US dollar was steady at 151.72 yen, and the euro slightly dipped to $1.0699.

Esses resultados devem ajudar investidores a entender melhor o cenário econômico regional. Em Wall Street, o início da semana foi de resultados mistos: o S&P 500 caiu 0,1% para 4.411,55, o Nasdaq recuou 0,2% para 13.767,74, enquanto o Dow Jones subiu 0,2%, fechando em 34.337,87. A temporada de balanços das empresas está chegando ao fim, com a maioria superando as previsões. Esta semana, varejistas como Target, TJX e Walmart soltam balanços, e as atenções se voltam para tendências futuras além do desempenho recente. A economia dos EUA se mantém forte mesmo com o Federal Reserve elevando a taxa de juros para o maior patamar desde 2001. O rendimento do título do Tesouro americano de 10 anos está em 4,63%, estável em relação à sexta-feira, mas menor do que há um mês, refletindo a possibilidade de o Fed encerrar o ciclo de alta. Ainda assim, o rendimento segue elevado frente à média de anos anteriores, pressionando ações de tecnologia. As ações da Apple caíram 0,9%; Microsoft perdeu 0,8%, pesando sobre o S&P 500. Essas tensões e preocupações quanto ao déficit público têm ampliado os rendimentos dos Treasuries. No mercado de commodities, o petróleo registrou leve alta: nos EUA, o barril fechou em US$ 78,42 (+US$ 0,16), enquanto o Brent avançou US$ 0,17, cotado a US$ 82,69. article_content: Three initial public offerings (IPOs)—Gandhar Oil, Flair Writing, and Fedbank Financial—opened for subscription on Wednesday and will close on November 24. Analysts have shared their recommendations for investors regarding these offerings.  Gandhar Oil: Gandhar Oil's IPO includes a fresh equity issue of ₹302 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of ₹199 crore. Promoter-shareholders, including Kailash Parekh and Gulab Parekh, as well as other investors like Green Desert Real Estate and Fleet Line Shipping, will be selling shares through the OFS. Analysts suggest subscribing to the IPO, highlighting the company’s robust financial performance and expanding international prospects. Prathamesh Masdekar, a research analyst at StoxBox, stated that the issue is fairly valued at a P/E of 7.1x at the upper price band based on FY23 earnings and is suitable for medium- to long-term investors. Gandhar Oil raised ₹150 crore from 16 anchor investors at ₹169 per share, with 50% of the shares reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 35% for retail investors, and 15% for non-institutional investors. Gandhar Oil is a leading manufacturer of white oils, increasingly focusing on the consumer and healthcare sectors. Its product portfolio includes more than 350 products under the 'Divyol' brand, mainly spanning personal care, healthcare, lubricants, and industrial oils.  Flair Writing: Flair Writing’s IPO comprises a fresh issue of ₹292 crore and an OFS of ₹301 crore. The OFS involves share sales by Khubilal Jugraj Rathod (₹76 crore), Vimalchand Jugraj Rathod (up to ₹57 crore), as well as Nirmala Khubilal Rathod and Manjula Vimalchand Rathod. The issue price is set at ₹304 at the upper end. Analysts recommend subscribing to the IPO, noting its reasonable valuation and strong brand reputation. According to Anand Rathi, Flair Writing is among the top three players in India’s writing instruments market, with steady revenue growth, a diversified product range, and a notable international presence. The company’s flagship 'Flair' brand has been established for over 45 years, and it holds about 9% of the market share in India’s overall writing and creative instruments sector as of March 2023. The offer’s allocation is split 50% to QIBs, 35% to retail investors, and 15% to non-institutional investors.  Fedbank Financial: The Fedbank Financial IPO was also launched on Wednesday, featuring a fresh equity issue of ₹600 crore and an OFS of 3.51 crore shares. The OFS consists of parent company Federal Bank selling 54.7 lakh shares and True North Fund VI LLP offloading 2.96 crore shares. The price band is set at ₹133–140 per share, with the company targeting a total raise of ₹1,092 crore at the upper end. Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to strengthen the company’s Tier-I capital, supporting future growth and business expansion. Remaining funds will go towards covering offer expenses. The IPO is valued at a P/BV of 2.5x at the upper price band. Anand Rathi recommends a ‘subscribe – long term’ rating, while SBI Securities highlights the company’s strong growth among gold loan NBFCs, its healthy asset quality, and low-cost borrowing capabilities, distinguishing it from its peers. As per market sources, the grey market premium (GMP) for the IPO stands at around 3.5%.  Other Market/Business Updates: - India's income tax department has identified nearly ₹10,000 crore in tax evasion among businesses selling via social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook over a three-year period, sending notices to 45 brands so far. - In response to more than 20,000 GST notices since 2022, Indian companies are now prioritizing tax compliance checks before engaging in mergers, acquisitions, and other transactions. - Nawaz Modi, estranged wife of Raymond Managing Director Gautam Singhania, has alleged that Singhania assaulted her and one of their daughters two months ago. article_content: Winding streets branching from Sukhumvit Road—between the Phrom Phong, Thong Lor, and Ekkamai BTS stops—showcase some of Bangkok’s most exciting urban experiences. Food stalls dish out steaming broths and deftly handle woks, filling the air with lively chatter and the aroma of classic dishes like tom yam. A constant influx of chic restaurants and bars offers premier options for dining and drinking in the city. Unlike Bangkok’s temple-dotted areas, this vibrant district is a hub of modern life. Well-to-do Thais still favor the area, evidenced by grand residences and slow-moving streams of luxury cars on Soi Thong Lor (Sukhumvit 55) and Soi Ekkamai (Sukhumvit 63) each evening. Despite the luxury, enduring late-night diners and traditional specialty shops balance trendy juice bars, contemporary malls, and high-end restaurants. Daytime brings plenty to explore—quirky cafes, spas, and eclectic shops, from vinyl havens to fashion boutiques—but the neighborhood is especially energetic after dark.

Uma variedade constante de restaurantes e bares elegantes oferece ótimas opções para comer e beber na cidade. Ao contrário das áreas cheias de templos, este bairro dinâmico é um polo da vida moderna. O local segue sendo favorito entre os tailandeses mais abastados, como mostram as mansões luxuosas e a procissão de carros de alto padrão que circula lentamente pela Soi Thong Lor (Sukhumvit 55) e Soi Ekkamai (Sukhumvit 63) todas as noites. Apesar do luxo, restaurantes tradicionais de madrugada e lojas especializadas antigas equilibram os bares de suco, shoppings modernos e restaurantes sofisticados. Durante o dia, há muito o que fazer—cafés descolados, spas e lojas diversas, de discos de vinil a boutiques de moda—mas é à noite que o bairro realmente ferve.

article_content: Eight people, including a child, lost their lives when lightning struck a Seventh Day Adventist church in Lilongwe, the capital of Malawi, during Saturday afternoon prayers. The tragedy occurred around 4:30 pm during the region's rainy season, as a sudden lightning bolt hit the busy church. Officials from Malawi’s Ministry of Health stated that all eight victims were declared dead after being brought to Kamuzu Central Hospital. Forty additional worshippers received medical treatment, and one remains in intensive care. Charles Mwansambo, chief of health services at the ministry, called the incident an unforeseeable natural disaster. A witness told the Nyasa Times that the strike triggered panic, with a loud crash causing a stampede as people tried to escape. December marks the beginning of Malawi’s rainy season, a time when storms and high humidity are common. Local news sources report that, in addition to this event, three more people have died from lightning strikes in the past month.

A tragédia ocorreu por volta das 16h30, durante a estação chuvosa da região, quando um raio atingiu a igreja lotada. Autoridades do Ministério da Saúde do Malawi disseram que todas as oito vítimas foram declaradas mortas ao chegarem ao Hospital Central Kamuzu. Outros quarenta fiéis receberam atendimento médico, sendo que uma pessoa permanece em estado grave. Charles Mwansambo, chefe dos serviços de saúde do ministério, classificou o incidente como um desastre natural imprevisível. Uma testemunha contou ao Nyasa Times que a descarga provocou pânico, com um forte estrondo causando uma correria enquanto as pessoas tentavam fugir. Dezembro marca o início da estação das chuvas no Malawi, período em que são comuns tempestades e alta umidade. Fontes da mídia local relatam que, além deste evento, outras três pessoas morreram atingidas por raios no último mês.

South Korea’s football coach, Juergen Klinsmann, has urged midfielder Lee Kang-in to stay humble as the Paris Saint-Germain playmaker’s reputation grows. Lee received a warm reception after scoring twice in South Korea’s 4-0 friendly win over Tunisia in Seoul on Friday, capping a month where the 22-year-old also helped his country keep the Asian Games gold medal in China.

"It's a pleasure to work with him because he’s always positive, always smiling, but also hungry for success," Klinsmann said. "He needs to stay hungry. It’s not easy for Kang-in, as he’s treated like a pop star here—which isn’t always good, since a pop star doesn’t score goals. He must remain humble, focused, work hard, and continue to fight."

Seen as one of South Korea’s most promising footballers since moving to Spain to join Valencia’s academy as a child, Lee played 62 games for the La Liga team before transferring to Real Mallorca in 2021. Last year, he featured in four World Cup matches—three as a substitute—for South Korea, and this summer he signed with Paris Saint-Germain for 22 million euros.

Lee played a key role in earning South Korea the Asian Games gold medal, and this victory brought him exemption from the country’s compulsory military service, which is important for his future in European football.

"Every time he comes back to Korea, countless people will be cheering for him," Klinsmann added. "When a club like Paris Saint-Germain signs a Korean player, it means he’s truly special. Kang-in is highly talented. Now he’ll have the chance to learn from top players in Paris, understand what the Champions League requires, and experience the pressure of fighting for major titles."
