Lee foi calorosamente ovacionado após marcar dois gols na vitória por 4 a 0 sobre a Tunísia, em amistoso em Seul, na sexta-feira, encerrando um mês em que o jogador de 22 anos também ajudou o país a manter a medalha de ouro nos Jogos Asiáticos na China.

"É um prazer trabalhar com ele porque ele está sempre positivo, sempre sorrindo, mas também com sede de sucesso", disse Klinsmann. "Ele precisa manter essa fome. Não é fácil para Kang-in, pois aqui ele é tratado como uma estrela pop — o que nem sempre é positivo, já que uma estrela pop não marca gols. Ele deve permanecer humilde, focado, trabalhar duro e continuar lutando."

Reconhecido como um dos talentos mais promissores do futebol sul-coreano desde pequeno, depois de se mudar para a Espanha para integrar a base do Valencia, Lee disputou 62 jogos pelo clube espanhol antes de se transferir para o Real Mallorca em 2021. No ano passado, atuou em quatro partidas da Copa do Mundo — três delas saindo do banco — e, neste verão, assinou com o Paris Saint-Germain por 22 milhões de euros.

Lee teve papel fundamental na conquista da medalha de ouro nos Jogos Asiáticos, vitória que lhe garantiu isenção do serviço militar obrigatório, algo importante para sua carreira na Europa.

"Sempre que ele voltar à Coreia, haverá milhares de pessoas torcendo por ele", acrescentou Klinsmann. "Quando um clube como o Paris Saint-Germain contrata um sul-coreano, é porque é um jogador realmente especial. Kang-in tem muito talento. Agora ele poderá aprender com jogadores de alto nível em Paris, entender o que a Liga dos Campeões exige e sentir a pressão de disputar grandes títulos."

article_content: A WestJet passenger says her suitcase ended up in Jamaica after the airline mishandled it during a domestic flight in Canada. An Apple AirTag helped her locate the bag, according to a report by CityNews. Lorraine Pedersen told Business Insider that she traveled on a WestJet flight from Toronto to Winnipeg on October 23. However, when she arrived in Winnipeg—less than 100 miles north of the Minnesota–North Dakota state border—her suitcase was missing. "I was on a business trip and all my clothes were gone," Pedersen said. She had placed an AirTag in her bag, which notified her it was in Kingston, Jamaica. When she contacted WestJet about her bag, they told her it could not be in Jamaica since there were no flights from Toronto to Kingston that day. Business Insider viewed a screenshot confirming the AirTag had located the bag. "They kept saying it wasn't their fault, and that they hadn't sent it there since they didn't have a flight to Jamaica that day," Pedersen told Business Insider. "I just wanted my suitcase back because my AirTag showed its exact location, but again WestJet did not believe me," she added. Pedersen later contacted Norman Manley International Airport in Kingston and confirmed her suitcase had arrived on a Swoop flight. Swoop is a subsidiary of WestJet. The suitcase remained in Jamaica for two weeks as WestJet declined to transport it back to Toronto, where Pedersen lives. "They told me to buy enough clothes for every day, but they wouldn't cover the cost of those clothes," she continued. WestJet did not respond to Business Insider's request for comment. When Pedersen's suitcase was returned to Toronto, she said it appeared to have been broken into and that several belongings were missing. She estimated that the total value of stolen items and replacement clothes was around 4,000 Canadian dollars (almost $3,000). Business Insider could not independently verify this amount. "I was very hurt to learn that my bag had been rummaged through and things were stolen while it was in Jamaica," Pedersen told Business Insider. WestJet confirmed to CityNews that the airline mishandled Pedersen's suitcase. "Unfortunately, the bag was loaded in error, and situations like this are extremely rare," WestJet stated, adding that Pedersen was compensated with "the maximum liability." The amount of compensation was not disclosed. According to the Canadian Transportation Agency, passengers can claim up to 2,350 Canadian dollars (roughly $1,712) from airlines for lost or damaged items. Pedersen told CityNews that WestJet asked her to file a home insurance claim for missing items, but she does not plan to do so as it could increase her insurance premium. "My biggest complaint against WestJet is that they did not take responsibility," Pedersen told Business Insider. More passengers have started using AirTags on their luggage after multiple incidents of mishandled bags by airlines. In August, a passenger in the US used an AirTag to track down a lost bag. In September, a man traveling from Oklahoma to Ireland found his missing golf gear with the help of an AirTag.

article_content: Yoruba nation agitator, Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, has regained his freedom from Beninese authorities. Adeyemo announced on Sunday that he is now legally permitted to leave Cotonou, the capital of Benin Republic, and return to Nigeria or travel to other countries. "I am now free to return to Nigeria and visit any country in the world. I have met all the legal conditions attached to my bail from a few years ago and will be returning to Nigeria, my country of origin, soon. There are no longer any legal barriers preventing me from returning home," Adeyemo told the Nigerian Tribune. He regained his freedom after about two years of trial by the Beninese government. Adeyemo had gained national prominence in March 2021 when he declared the sovereignty of the Yoruba Nation. He launched a campaign to drive out suspected criminal herdsmen and kidnappers from southwestern states and urged Yorubas living in other regions to return home. After a raid on his residence in Ibadan by the Department of State Services (DSS) in July 2021—in which at least one person died and some of his property was vandalized—Adeyemo left Nigeria. The DSS stated that they recovered several firearms, ammunition, charms, and other items during the operation. In August 2022, a judgment related to the raid was set aside by the Court of Appeal. Adeyemo was later arrested at Cardinal Bernardin International Airport in Cotonou, Benin Republic, while attempting to travel to Germany. Efforts by the former Nigerian administration, led by President Muhammadu Buhari, to extradite Adeyemo back to Nigeria were unsuccessful. Adeyemo's release has triggered various reactions, with some groups calling for the release of other activists and continued debates over security and governance in Nigeria.

Brainstorming sessions are often considered effective for generating new ideas. However, recent research suggests that more focused methods, such as creative design reasoning, produce higher-quality suggestions. The study, titled 'Brainstorming versus creative design reasoning,' will be presented at the Design Computing and Cognition conference in London and challenges the widely held belief that 'quantity breeds quality.'

The research team, including Dr. Akin Kazakci from the Ecole Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Paris, studied 30 professional designers with an average of 12 years' experience in R&D and innovation. These participants were divided into ten groups of three and tasked with creating a 'breakthrough museum concept' that offers an immersive experience inspired by Antarctica. The designs needed to be mobile and eco-friendly. Each group had 90 minutes to develop and summarize their concept on an A3 sheet before presenting it.

The researchers compared individual idea generation to group brainstorming sessions and found that individuals generated up to 44% more ideas and a broader variety of concepts. In groups, participants were more likely to fixate on similar ideas.

A panel of 14 professionals, including museum experts and project managers unaware of the research purpose, evaluated the final concepts for novelty, feasibility, and value. The results showed that teams with fewer ideas produced designs rated more highly by the panel. The best team produced 60 ideas compared to an average of 82 across all teams. The study concluded by rejecting the 'quantity breeds quality' hypothesis.

O estudo, intitulado 'Brainstorming versus raciocínio criativo em design', será apresentado na conferência Design Computing and Cognition em Londres e questiona a crença amplamente difundida de que 'quantidade gera qualidade'.

A equipe de pesquisa, incluindo o Dr. Akin Kazakci da Ecole Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Paris, estudou 30 designers profissionais com média de 12 anos de experiência em P&D e inovação. Os projetos precisavam ser móveis e ecológicos. Cada grupo teve 90 minutos para desenvolver e resumir seu conceito em uma folha A3 antes de apresentá-lo.

Os pesquisadores compararam a geração de ideias individualmente com sessões de brainstorming em grupo e descobriram que os indivíduos geraram até 44% mais ideias e uma variedade maior de conceitos. Em grupos, os participantes tendiam a se fixar em ideias semelhantes.

Um painel de 14 profissionais, incluindo especialistas em museus e gestores de projetos, alheios ao propósito da pesquisa, avaliou os conceitos finais quanto a novidade, viabilidade e valor. O estudo concluiu rejeitando a hipótese de que 'quantidade gera qualidade'.

article_content: Chelsea Women’s manager Emma Hayes will leave the English champions at the end of the season, the club confirmed Saturday, amid reports that she is set to be named the next United States coach. Hayes is among the most successful managers in women’s football, having guided Chelsea to six WSL titles. The 47-year-old has also claimed five FA Cups, two League Cups, the Spring Series trophy, and the Community Shield with Chelsea. Hayes, who led Chelsea to two domestic doubles and one treble, is now widely expected to step into international management with the United States. Several US media outlets reported Saturday that Hayes is in advanced talks with the United States Soccer Federation, with her appointment expected soon. The US Women’s National Team is currently led by interim coach Twila Kilgore, who replaced Vlatko Andonovski after the USA's World Cup exit in the round of 16. Chelsea paid tribute to Hayes as they announced her upcoming departure. "Chelsea FC can today confirm that highly decorated Chelsea Women’s manager Emma Hayes OBE will depart the club at the end of the season to pursue a new opportunity outside of the WSL and club football," the club said in a statement. Hayes joined Chelsea in 2012—six years before the WSL became fully professional—and transformed the club into a powerhouse in women’s football. She has been named WSL Manager of the Season six times and was awarded The Best FIFA Women’s Coach in 2021. Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly and co-controlling owner Behdad Eghbali said, “Emma’s contribution to Chelsea cannot be understated. She has been a pioneer in women’s football and is hugely respected within the game. We look forward to continuing to work together over the coming months.” Hayes has often been mentioned as a potential candidate to manage men’s teams, but she insists that top roles in women’s football should be viewed as significant in their own right. Chelsea co-sporting directors Laurence Stewart and Paul Winstanley added, “Emma has been one of the biggest drivers of change in women’s football. Her achievements at Chelsea are unrivaled and will live in the club’s history forever. Given everything she has contributed to Chelsea in over a decade, and the legacy she leaves behind, we would never stand in her way when she felt it was the right time to pursue a new challenge.”

article_content: Japan's government plans to allocate approximately 2 trillion yen ($13 billion) to bolster its chip industry, marking the country's latest effort to reclaim its position in the vital semiconductor sector. While Japan is a leading supplier of chipmaking equipment and materials, it lost its manufacturing advantage over the past decades. To reverse this, the government is now providing substantial subsidies to chipmakers for capacity expansion. A portion of these funds—set aside in a supplementary budget for the current fiscal year—will support Taiwanese chip giant TSMC and the Japanese venture Rapidus, which aims to produce advanced semiconductors in Hokkaido. This investment in the chip sector is part of a broader 13.1 trillion yen spending package approved by Prime Minister Fumio Kishida's government for 2023/24. The spending will be financed largely through the issuance of nearly 9 trillion yen ($59.8 billion) in government bonds, which has sparked some concern about Japan's growing national debt.

Embora o Japão seja um importante fornecedor de equipamentos e materiais para fabricação de chips, perdeu sua vantagem na manufatura nas últimas décadas. Para reverter isso, o governo está agora oferecendo subsídios significativos para que fabricantes de chips ampliem sua capacidade. Parte desses recursos—reservados em um orçamento suplementar para o atual ano fiscal—será destinada a apoiar a gigante taiwanesa TSMC e a empresa japonesa Rapidus, que pretende produzir semicondutores avançados em Hokkaido. article_content: Trevor Jones may not be a household name, but his music is widely recognized. The South African composer is renowned for scoring films such as 'The Last of the Mohicans' and 'In the Name of the Father.' Over his three-decade career, Jones has composed more than 100 original scores for Hollywood blockbusters and popular television shows. Despite his success and acclaim, Jones’s journey was far from ordinary. As a mixed-race child growing up in Apartheid-era South Africa, he spent his early years in Cape Town's District 6, a neighborhood known for its diversity and turbulence. 'It was a very violent area,' Jones recalls. 'There were so many nationalities, people from so many parts of the world.' Challenging times and a rich mix of cultures and influences shaped the young Jones. He has carried these musical inspirations throughout his career. 'My tastes cover every style, from medieval to classical, avant-garde, folk and ethnic, jazz, rock, and pop,' Jones says. Jones listed a selection of musicians and artists who have influenced him on his path to becoming a leading film composer. Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika: Composed over 100 years ago by a schoolteacher in Johannesburg, this song forms part of the South African national anthem, along with Die Stem van Suid-Afrika. The hymn became a symbol of African liberation and was once adopted as the national song of Zambia, Tanzania, Namibia, and Zimbabwe, though Namibia and Zimbabwe have since chosen different anthems. 'I can't help but feel goosebumps whenever I sing Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika,' Jones shares. 'As a South African, this music holds deep meaning for me.' Sir Edward Elgar: Spanning the Victorian, Edwardian, and Georgian eras, Sir Edward Elgar was an influential English composer who helped revitalize British classical music. He was also an early adopter of the gramophone. 'I listen to Elgar's works regularly for inspiration and to marvel at his compositional mastery,' says Jones. 'Pieces like Elegy, Sospiri, and Introduction and Allegro from the album 'A Portrait of Elgar' are especially inspiring.' Hugh Masekela: 'The man and his music are an inspiration to us all,' Jones says of South African jazz multi-instrumentalist Hugh Masekela. Skilled with the trumpet, cornet, flugelhorn, and trombone, Masekela has sold millions of albums. He collaborated with groups like The Byrds and Paul Simon, and his 1987 hit 'Bring Him Back Home' became an anthem for the movement to free Nelson Mandela. Jones praises Masekela's albums like 'Hope,' 'Home is Where the Music Is,' and 'African Breeze' as proof of his stature as one of Africa’s greatest musicians. Ariel Ramirez: The Argentine composer, music director, and pianist is regarded as a leading figure in Argentine folk music. Jones singles out Ramirez's 'Misa Criolla' and 'Navidad Nuestra,' both featured on the 2000 album with Spanish tenor José Carreras and the Grupo Huracana ensemble, as particularly meaningful. Bernard Herrmann: Jones greatly admires Bernard Herrmann, the composer behind many of the 20th century’s iconic film scores. Herrmann worked closely with directors such as Alfred Hitchcock, Orson Welles, and Martin Scorsese. He composed the scores for classics like 'Citizen Kane,' 'Psycho,' and 'Taxi Driver.' 'Herrmann’s music deeply enriches each film,' Jones says. 'The craftsmanship and depth of his scores elevate every story he worked on.'

article_content: Douglas Carswell, formerly a Conservative MP, defended his decision to join UKIP, stating: 'I stab people in the front, not the back.' Carswell returned to his Clacton constituency alongside UKIP leader Nigel Farage amid speculation that more Conservative MPs might consider defection. UKIP donor Stuart Wheeler confirmed he had dined with around eight Conservative backbench MPs in an effort to encourage them to switch parties. He indicated there were more MPs he could have approached. Carswell was seen walking through Clacton-on-Sea with Farage, greeting constituents, and was met with both support and criticism from the public. At a press conference, Carswell said he was taking a risk by resigning and triggering a by-election but denied accusations of disloyalty to Prime Minister David Cameron, whom he described as 'a nice guy' but not serious about change in Europe. Carswell insisted he had always been frank and direct with colleagues: 'I've been straight with people.' Some passers-by voiced disapproval, calling Carswell a 'traitor,' while others showed support and praised him. Wheeler, a former Conservative who joined UKIP, stated he understood the sense of divided loyalty among MPs he met, as he had experienced the same transition. Prime Minister Cameron was caught off guard by Carswell’s move, which was quickly publicized by Farage. Cameron called the defection 'deeply regrettable' and 'counterproductive.' Farage claimed to have been in talks with several Conservative MPs and predicted more could defect if Carswell won the upcoming by-election, expected in October. There was initial resistance from existing UKIP Clacton candidate Roger Lord to make way for Carswell, though UKIP said Lord was selected for the general election, not the by-election. Official figures showed an increase in net immigration, undermining Cameron’s pledge to reduce it below 100,000 per year. Senior Conservative figures urged for clearer leadership on Europe and immigration, and acknowledged Carswell's move as a wake-up call. Carswell criticized the Conservative leadership for not delivering on promises regarding EU reform, political modernization, and border control. Cameron continued to argue that only a Conservative majority would guarantee an in/out referendum on Britain’s EU membership. Bookmakers quickly considered Carswell the favorite to win the by-election, which was scheduled to occur soon to prevent UKIP from gathering more momentum. His sudden departure surprised Eurosceptic colleagues, particularly after he had recently urged loyalty to the party. Former Defence Secretary Liam Fox commented that only a Conservative government would ensure a referendum on the EU and control on immigration.

Mia Love, a 36-year-old first-generation Haitian-American, aims to become the first black Republican woman elected to Congress. She currently serves as mayor of Saratoga Springs, a predominantly white town in Utah, and is a member of the Mormon faith. Love, the daughter of immigrants, received significant attention after her speech at the GOP convention in Tampa, which was met with enthusiastic applause.

In her speech, Love described her family's journey to the United States, making references to civil rights leaders Rosa Parks and Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. 'Our story has been told over 200 years,' she said. 'With small steps and giant leaps—from a woman on a bus to a man with a dream.'

Love is running against six-term Democratic incumbent Rep. Jim Matheson, and her campaign emphasizes conservative values such as small government and fiscal responsibility.

She criticized President Obama, accusing him of dividing Americans by income, gender, and social status. 'My parents immigrated to the U.S. with $10 in their pockets, believing in the America they had heard about,' Love said. 'When times were tough, they didn't look to Washington—they looked within. The America I knew was based on self-reliance and the possibility of achieving the American dream.'

Love argued that President Obama's policies have not been successful, asserting, 'We are not better off than we were four years ago, and no rhetoric, bumper sticker, or Hollywood campaign ad can change that. Mr. President, I am here to tell you we are not buying what you are selling in 2012.'

Born in Brooklyn, New York, and raised in Connecticut, Love moved to Utah in 1997, where she later married and converted to Mormonism. Her parents came to the United States 39 years ago, with her father working several jobs to support the family. In an interview with Fox News, Love recalled her father telling her, 'Your mother and I have done everything we could to get you here. We've worked hard. We've never taken a handout. You're not going to be a burden to society. You will give back.'

article_content: A leading U.S. evangelical, James Dobson, has accused Senator Barack Obama of misrepresenting the Bible and offering what he calls a "fruitcake interpretation" of the U.S. Constitution. On his radio program Tuesday, Dobson, founder of Focus on the Family, challenged comments Obama made during a June 2006 speech to the liberal Christian group, Call to Renewal. In that speech, Obama highlighted the challenges of governing solely by biblical principles, referencing passages that sanction slavery or ban eating shellfish. "Which passages of scripture should guide our public policy?" Obama asked, noting conflicting messages within the Bible. He also described Jesus’ Sermon on the Mount as so radical that its application would challenge modern institutions like the Defense Department. Dobson argued that Obama was misrepresenting biblical teachings by focusing on now-outdated Old Testament laws. He stated, "I think he's deliberately distorting the traditional understanding of the Bible to fit his own worldview." Obama responded that his speech emphasized the importance of faith in public life and encouraged translating religious concerns into universal language to promote debate, not division. Obama's religious affairs director, Joshua DuBois, pointed to the 2006 speech as evidence of Obama’s commitment to outreach and unity across religious lines. He also mentioned efforts to connect with Focus on the Family in advance of the Democratic convention. Dobson further objected to Obama’s suggestion that people of faith should appeal to broader values when participating in democracy, arguing that this undermines religious conviction. The article also notes that Obama’s mention of both Dobson and Rev. Al Sharpton in his speech drew criticism from Focus on the Family leadership. The debate comes as Obama’s campaign seeks to connect with evangelical voters, many of whom have reservations about supporting Republican nominee John McCain. Dobson has said he will not vote for McCain. Focus on the Family leaders remain skeptical that Obama’s approach will resonate with evangelicals, pledging to advocate for their beliefs.

Police spokeswoman Barbara Morgan stated that the boxing champion was taken into custody just before midnight on a misdemeanor battery charge. article_content: People worldwide eat over 100 billion bananas each year, with almost half being the Cavendish variety. Now, this fruit is threatened by a fungal disease called Panama Disease (TR4). Scientists are attempting various solutions: genetically modifying Cavendish bananas to resist TR4, grafting techniques, and using natural selection to breed disease-resistant strains without genetic engineering. Some experts warn that growing largely one type of banana creates a risky monoculture, and suggest that increasing genetic diversity among bananas is a more robust long-term fix. Switching to a variety of bananas, however, would increase costs and require major changes in how bananas are transported and ripened, since Cavendish became popular due to its affordability, productivity, and long shelf life. A similar scenario happened with the Gros Michel banana, which was destroyed by an earlier version of Panama Disease. While scientists are making progress in protecting Cavendish bananas, there’s uncertainty over whether current solutions will be enough. History suggests the dominant banana variety could change again if a lasting fix isn’t found.

Cientistas estão tentando várias soluções: modificar geneticamente bananas Cavendish para resistirem ao TR4, aplicar técnicas de enxertia e usar seleção natural para desenvolver variedades resistentes sem modificação genética. Alguns especialistas alertam que plantar quase só um tipo de banana cria um monocultivo arriscado e que aumentar a diversidade genética das bananas é uma solução mais segura no longo prazo. Entretanto, adotar diferentes variedades aumentaria os custos e exigiria grandes mudanças no transporte e amadurecimento, já que a Cavendish ganhou espaço por ser barata, produtiva e durar mais tempo. Apesar dos avanços científicos para proteger a Cavendish, resta dúvida se as soluções atuais vão bastar. Se a história se repetir, a banana favorita do mundo pode mudar de novo em breve.

article_content: Over 7,000 athletes representing 500 schools will compete for more than 1,000 medals and 32 team titles at the inaugural MTN CHAMPS athletics championship in Nigeria. The competition is organized by Making of Champions, in partnership with the Athletics Federation of Nigeria (AFN) and the Nigeria School Sports Federation (NSSF), and is sponsored by MTN. MTN CHAMPS is designed for three age categories: cadets (U-14), youth (U-17), and juniors (U-20). Events will be held in four cities: Benin City, Ibadan, Uyo, and Abuja. The championship will take place as follows: Benin City (October 12-14), Uyo (October 26-28), Ibadan (November 9-11), and Abuja (November 29-December 1), with a grand final in Abuja on December 2. At a press conference in Lagos, MTN Chief Marketing Officer Adia Showo announced that the top 10 performers will earn placement in the MoC Academy, where they will receive structured training focused on discipline, time management, and essential life skills. Showo emphasized MTN's commitment to empowering Nigerian youth, aiming to provide the necessary technology and platforms for young athletes to thrive. AFN president Tonobok Okowa praised the championship, noting that it fills a significant gap in youth competitions and helps retain young athletes who might otherwise drop out between the ages of 15 and 18 due to lack of opportunities. MoC founder Bambo Akani highlighted the event’s importance as a milestone for athletics in Nigeria, expressing confidence that MTN CHAMPS will discover and develop sporting talents nationwide.

Despite being rushed to the hospital, he was declared dead on arrival. Yadav, who had recently obtained a Master's in Computer Applications and was working from home, was due to be married soon. Mohith Reddy, chairman of the Tirupati Urban Development Authority, visited Yadav’s family to express condolences. Separately, a 23-year-old man in West Bengal reportedly died by suicide after India’s loss in the final, with police investigating and having registered a case of unnatural death. India’s cricket team had won 10 straight matches before the final. The defeat was an emotional blow to players and fans, with visible distress among team members like Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. In other news, investigators discovered about ₹10,000 crore in tax evasion by social media sellers, prompting action against multiple brands. Indian companies are also being more cautious with business deals amid increased scrutiny over tax compliance. Meanwhile, Nawaz Modi has accused her estranged husband, Gautam Singhania of Raymond, of physical assault.

article_content:
Texas health officials have reported that products from Peanut Corporation of America's Plainview facility may be contaminated with salmonella, based on results from private lab tests. Following these findings, the Texas Department of State Health Services requested the plant's closure. Doug McBride, a department spokesperson, said samples collected last week tested positive in an external lab, and state tests were expected soon.

The company voluntarily closed the Plainview plant on Monday night, after lab results indicated possible salmonella presence in some products. Separately, the FDA has shut down and is investigating a Blakely, Georgia peanut plant, which is linked to a salmonella outbreak associated with eight deaths and about 600 illnesses in 43 states. Both the FDA and Texas authorities are continuing to review the Plainview facility's procedures and food safety records. No illnesses have been directly attributed to Plainview products, and health officials are developing criteria for the plant to meet before it can reopen.

Officials stated that peanut meal and granulated peanuts remained at the Plainview facility, and dry roasted peanuts that were shipped had been recalled before reaching consumers. It is still unclear if the salmonella detected is the same strain as in the national outbreak.

According to the company's website, the Plainview closure was voluntary and in cooperation with authorities. The original peanut butter recall, once thought to affect mainly institutions, has expanded to over 1,000 products, some of which have been found in retail outlets, including discount stores. Brands such as Casey’s, Parnell’s Pride, Reggie, and Robinson Crusoe are among those affected.

Despite FDA reassurances that major peanut butter brands are not implicated in the outbreak, sales have dropped by at least 20%. Other companies such as ConAgra Foods and J.M. Smucker are running ads and offering discounts to encourage ongoing purchases. The FBI also raided the Blakely, Georgia plant during the investigation.

article_content: For the first time, a self-driving vehicle has managed to outperform a human on the racetrack. Stanford University researchers, together with Audi and Volkswagen, engineered 'Shelley,' an autonomous Audi TTS capable of exceeding 120 mph. At Thunderhill Raceway Park in Northern California, Shelley competed with David Vodden, the venue’s CEO and an experienced amateur racer, securing victory by 0.4 seconds in a direct contest. Shelley employs highly accurate differential GPS, an array of motion sensors, and gyroscopes to maintain course and stability. This advanced system allows Shelley to calculate and follow the fastest racing line, adapting moment by moment—skills that enabled her to compete head-to-head with seasoned human drivers. Shelley's name honors rally pioneer Michele Mouton and reflects a collaboration between Stanford’s Dynamic Design Lab, under Chris Gerdes, and Volkswagen’s Electronics Research Lab. Their findings, presented at a major science meeting in San Jose, illustrate that while Shelley had wins in some sessions, race outcomes can change depending on circumstances. Beyond lap times, the research team tracked Vodden’s physiological signals and brain activity to understand critical aspects of human concentration and instinct in racing—a concept dubbed the 'butt sense.' Chris Gerdes notes that humans rely on judgment and subtle cues, while Shelley’s performance is all about algorithmic accuracy. Nonetheless, Shelley isn’t immune to racing’s physical demands—testing at the limit led to brake pad failures from heat stress, revealing the intense conditions race cars endure. Such challenges help researchers understand both machine limitations and the skillset of professional drivers. Ultimately, the team believes that lessons from the racetrack can transfer to public roads. Combining human intuition with high-tech automotive sensors could result in next-generation safety systems, acting as co-pilots in emergencies. As Gerdes highlights: mastering the racetrack could pave the way for safer responses to hazards like icy or unpredictable conditions.

No Thunderhill Raceway Park, no norte da Califórnia, Shelley competiu contra David Vodden, CEO do local e piloto amador experiente, vencendo por 0,4 segundo em um duelo direto. Shelley usa GPS diferencial extremamente preciso, uma série de sensores de movimento e giroscópios para manter o curso e a estabilidade. Esse sistema avançado permite calcular e seguir a linha mais rápida da pista, adaptando-se em tempo real—habilidades que a colocam no mesmo nível de pilotos profissionais. O nome Shelley homenageia a pioneira do rali Michele Mouton e reflete a parceria entre o Dynamic Design Lab de Stanford, liderado por Chris Gerdes, e o Electronics Research Lab da Volkswagen. article_content: A video showing a British man and his Saudi wife being assaulted by members of Saudi Arabia's religious police has gone viral across the Arab world. The footage, which captured a man in a headscarf jumping from a car to confront another man in a parking lot, was reportedly filmed after the couple used a women-only cashier line at a supermarket in Riyadh. According to a statement published on the blog of a well-known Saudi writer, the British man said that three men who appeared 'religious' followed him and his wife while shopping. As they checked out at the women and family cashier line, these men started to push, shove, and verbally abuse them, he claimed. The men allegedly followed the couple out to the parking lot, where a crowd gathered as the confrontation continued. The British national said the three men attacked him after he took a photo of them with his phone. He stated that while he was on the ground, the men repeatedly kicked him in the head and back. His wife reportedly left their car to defend him and was kicked in the stomach after she hit one of the men. In the short mobile phone video, the British man can be heard shouting, 'Get off of my wife! That's my wife, how dare you!' The couple called the British Embassy and locked themselves in their car until embassy security arrived and escorted them home. Saudi newspapers identified the man, but the British Embassy would not confirm his identity. He did not sign the online statement, but Ahmed Al Omran, owner of the blog where the statement appeared, wrote, 'I know the man and have met him before. He is British, married to a Saudi woman, and they have lived in Riyadh for years.' The head of Saudi Arabia's religious police (CPVPV) confirmed the video's authenticity and condemned the attack as 'unacceptable.' Their investigation found the men acted beyond their remit within the private shopping center and lied about the events. As a result, four members of the religious police were reassigned to administrative jobs outside Riyadh. A British Embassy spokesperson said consular assistance was being provided to the British national and welcomed the promise by the CPVPV's head, Sheikh Abdullatif Al ash-Sheikh, to fully investigate the incident. The event has been widely covered in Saudi and Arab media and has sparked extensive discussion online. The YouTube video has been viewed more than 400,000 times. A member of Saudi Arabia's Consultative Assembly (Shura Council) cited the case while criticizing a 'lack of discipline' and 'flawed judgment' among some religious police field staff in a council session, according to the assembly's website.

article_content: Happy Feet, a one-year-old emperor penguin, became a global sensation after being found on a New Zealand beach, 3,000 miles from his Antarctic home. The young penguin was seriously ill after eating sand, which he mistook for snow. Rescued on June 20 at Peka Peka Beach, Happy Feet underwent life-saving surgery at Wellington Zoo, where veterinarians removed 7lb of sand, sticks, and stones from his stomach. Over the next two months, he received careful care, gaining 18lb and thriving on a diet of fish milkshakes in an air-conditioned enclosure. More than 250,000 people followed his recovery online through a zoo webcam, with over 1,700 fans gathering in person to wish him farewell. On August 29, 2011, he began his four-day journey back to Antarctic waters on the research vessel Tangaroa. He travels in a custom crate, kept cool with 60 buckets of ice and will be fed fish throughout the voyage. A GPS tracker sponsored by Gareth Morgan was attached to Happy Feet, allowing people worldwide to follow his journey after release. Wellington Zoo’s chief executive, Karen Fifield, said, 'He's brought a lot of hope and joy to people. His story speaks to what makes us human.' Veterinarian Lisa Argilla noted the penguin has a 'stronger and more feisty attitude' now. Upon reaching 51 degrees south, Happy Feet will be released into the sea using a canvas slide from the deck of the Tangaroa, captained by Richard O'Driscoll. Dr. Argilla added that by next year Happy Feet should be old enough to find a mate and possibly join another colony of emperor penguins. The story has reached and inspired people globally, including visitors such as comedian Stephen Fry.

O jovem pinguim estava gravemente doente depois de comer areia, pensando que era neve. Resgatado em 20 de junho na Praia Peka Peka, Happy Feet passou por uma cirurgia que salvou sua vida no Zoológico de Wellington, onde veterinários removeram 3,2 kg de areia, gravetos e pedras de seu estômago. Nos dois meses seguintes, ele recebeu cuidados intensivos, ganhou 8 kg e se recuperou com uma dieta de vitaminas de peixe em um recinto com ar-condicionado. Mais de 250 mil pessoas acompanharam sua recuperação online por uma webcam do zoológico e mais de 1.700 fãs foram pessoalmente se despedir. Em 29 de agosto de 2011, ele começou sua viagem de quatro dias de volta às águas da Antártida a bordo do navio de pesquisa Tangaroa. Ele viaja em uma caixa feita sob medida, mantida fria com 60 baldes de gelo, e será alimentado com peixe durante toda a jornada. Um rastreador GPS patrocinado por Gareth Morgan foi colocado em Happy Feet, permitindo que pessoas de todo o mundo acompanhem sua jornada após a soltura. A CEO do Zoológico de Wellington, Karen Fifield, afirmou: 'Ele trouxe muita esperança e alegria para as pessoas. Sua história mostra o que nos torna humanos.' A veterinária Lisa Argilla comentou que o pinguim está agora 'mais forte e cheio de atitude'. Ao chegar na latitude 51 sul, Happy Feet será solto no mar por um escorregador de lona a partir do convés do Tangaroa, capitaneado por Richard O'Driscoll. A Dra. Argilla acrescentou que, no próximo ano, Happy Feet deverá estar pronto para encontrar um parceiro e talvez se juntar a outra colônia de pinguins-imperadores. A história alcançou e inspirou pessoas no mundo todo, incluindo visitantes como o comediante Stephen Fry.

article_content: Kelly Bradford, a 41-year-old single mother from Ashford, Middlesex, has chosen to cancel Christmas celebrations for her 11-year-old son, William, so she can save the £20,000 required for his private school fees. Rather than spending on holiday meals and gifts, Kelly is focused on investing in her son’s education, believing it offers long-term benefits that outweigh the joys of a single day. This year, William will receive just one present—a £9.99 Miranda DVD—and the pair will have a simple meal from whatever is available in their fridge. Although William feels sad about missing out on presents, he appreciates his mother’s dedication to providing him with better opportunities. Despite having the option of attending a nearby state school with a 'good' Ofsted rating, Kelly decided early on that private education was the best path for William. Having left school herself at 16 without qualifications, she’s determined to ensure her son doesn’t miss out on advantages she never had, even if it means giving up festive treats, pantomime outings, and stockings full of gifts. Kelly and William’s father separated six years ago, and while he supports the decision for private schooling, Kelly is solely responsible for the education costs, which include lessons in Sanskrit and Latin. Previously, Christmas had been filled with gifts and special meals, but Kelly ultimately found much of the expense was wasted. Now, after a year of saving by working long hours as a self-employed writer and broadcaster, she’s putting their resources toward William’s education instead. Kelly says she is motivated by a desire to do what’s best for her child, reminding William of how fortunate he is to have this opportunity. William admits he’s disappointed not to receive more gifts, and if money were no object, he would have chosen a virtual reality headset. Still, he acknowledges and appreciates his mother’s hard work to give him a quality education.

Marcelo, captain of Fluminense, celebrated with his teammates after their historic victory in the Copa CONMEBOL Libertadores 2023 final against Boca Juniors at Maracanã Stadium on November 4, 2023, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Fluminense were recently crowned Copa Libertadores Champions, defeating Argentine giants Boca Juniors 2-1 in a tense match that stretched to 120 minutes and saw red cards for both teams during extra time. The club received the prestigious trophy along with a $21 million prize, marking their first-ever triumph in South America’s premier football competition.

This achievement secures Fluminense a place in football history and brings significant financial benefits to the club. Despite being one of the wealthiest teams in South America, Fluminense has faced recent financial challenges. The Copa Libertadores prize money provides essential funding, helping the club remain competitive against domestic rivals like Flamengo and Palmeiras. Moreover, the overall financial impact from their victory is expected to exceed $21 million, due to increased global recognition, potential new sponsorships, and merchandising opportunities generated by their successful campaign.

Victory in the Copa Libertadores also means Fluminense will represent South America in the 2023 FIFA Club World Cup in Saudi Arabia this December, where they will compete against clubs such as Manchester City and Al Ahly. Participation in the tournament guarantees the club between $2 to $3 million, with a potential $5 million for winning the title. In addition, as champions, Fluminense will face Ecuadorian side LDU Quito in the 2024 Recopa Sudamericana; winners will receive $2 million, while runners-up get $1 million.

Looking ahead, Fluminense have also qualified for the 2025 Club World Cup, set to feature 32 of the world's top teams in a new expanded format. While prize money for this tournament has not yet been determined, it promises further financial rewards. There is also a chance for increased collaboration between CONMEBOL and CONCACAF. This could include an expanded Copa Libertadores featuring North American teams or, at minimum, participation in a new ‘Copa Interamericana,’ bringing together champions from both continents in 2024. Fluminense and Inter Miami, led by Lionel Messi, are expected to be key participants, though prize money details remain unannounced.

Besides tournament earnings, Fluminense stand to gain additional revenue from greater sponsorship bargaining power and possible transfers of key players such as André, Nino, and John Kennedy, who have attracted attention for their performances during the Copa Libertadores. All these factors, both on and off the pitch, indicate that Fluminense’s earnings from their historic title could surpass $30 million, solidifying their legacy and creating opportunities for sustained success in the coming years.

article_content: Fighting between Israeli forces and Palestinian militants outside Gaza's largest hospital, Al-Shifa, has forced thousands of people to flee, while hundreds of patients and displaced people remain inside, according to health officials. President Joe Biden has called for Shifa hospital to be protected and requested less intrusive action by Israeli forces. The hospital has lacked electricity and water for three days and is reported as no longer functioning, according to WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Patients include dozens of babies at high risk due to the power outage. More than two-thirds of Gaza’s 2.3 million population have been displaced since the war began, following Hamas’ October 7 attack on southern Israel. According to the Gaza Health Ministry, over 11,000 Palestinians have been killed, most of them women and minors, though figures do not distinguish between civilian and militant deaths. About 1,200 people in Israel died, mainly in the initial Hamas attack, and around 240 have been taken as hostages to Gaza. Humanitarian aid deliveries are hampered by fuel shortages; medical, food, and water supplies cannot be distributed as trucks are unable to operate. Officials state that fighting has damaged critical hospital infrastructure, including power and oxygen systems. International organizations and governments are calling for humanitarian pauses or ceasefires, but there is no consensus on strategy. Israel’s military released footage they say shows weapons and facilities for holding hostages in a children’s hospital, alleging Hamas uses medical centers for military purposes. Hostage families are urging the UN to help secure the release of their relatives. Evacuation efforts continue, including Jordan helping citizens leave Gaza. Sewage systems in Gaza have collapsed due to power shortages, creating environmental and health hazards. Ten hospitals in Gaza remain operational, but all are at risk of closure without new fuel and supplies. Clashes continue along the Israel-Lebanon border, with reports of casualties on both sides. The UN reports its staff and facilities in Gaza have been hit despite providing coordinates to both parties. There is internal debate in Israel regarding the length of the offensive and international pressure for a ceasefire; government officials maintain the priorities are returning hostages and eliminating Hamas. Israel has imposed bans on some foreign news channels, further restricting media access.

article_content: KHAN YOUNIS, Gaza Strip — On Friday, Hamas released an American woman, Judith Raanan, and her 17-year-old daughter, Natalie. They had been held hostage in Gaza following their abduction during Hamas’s attack on Israel on October 7, which saw about 200 people kidnapped. The pair were handed over to Israeli authorities, with Hamas stating that the release was for humanitarian reasons, facilitated in cooperation with the Qatari government. The release occurred as Israel prepares for a potential ground offensive in Gaza, aiming to target Hamas militants who control the territory. Israeli officials have stated they do not plan to take long-term control of Gaza, which is home to approximately 2.3 million people. Since October 7, Israel has launched extensive airstrikes on Gaza, bringing the region’s hospitals and families to a critical state. International protests have grown in solidarity with Palestinians, and efforts are increasing to send aid into Gaza. Judith and Natalie Raanan had traveled from suburban Chicago to Israel to celebrate Jewish holidays and were visiting Kibbutz Nahal Oz, near Gaza, during the attack. Family members had no contact with them after the abduction and were later informed by U.S. and Israeli officials that they were being held in Gaza. Families of other hostages welcomed the release and appealed for additional captives to be freed, urging the international community to press for their release. The conflict has led to significant casualties: Over 1,400 people in Israel have been killed, mainly civilians, during the initial Hamas incursion. Gaza’s Health Ministry reports over 4,100 deaths in the territory since the hostilities began, including victims from a recent hospital explosion, the cause of which is disputed. Israeli airstrikes have targeted areas in southern Gaza, where many Palestinians took refuge after evacuation orders. Clashes have also erupted between Israeli forces and militants in southern Lebanon, prompting evacuations on both sides as concerns rise over the possibility of the conflict expanding. Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant outlined a three-stage plan involving airstrikes and ground operations to dismantle Hamas, followed by operations against remaining militants, and eventually establishing a new security regime in Gaza with Israel withdrawing responsibility for the territory. The humanitarian crisis persists as Gaza’s population faces shortages of essentials such as fuel, food, water, and medicine. Efforts are ongoing to bring aid through the Rafah crossing with Egypt, though delays due to airstrike-damaged roads and security concerns have slowed progress. More than 200 trucks loaded with aid are positioned at the border. The Palestine Red Crescent Society reported receiving a warning from Israeli forces concerning a potential strike on Al-Quds Hospital, prompting urgent evacuation calls. Meanwhile, an Israeli airstrike hit near a Greek Orthodox church in Gaza City that was sheltering displaced people, resulting in fatalities, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry. Across the region, violence has sparked protests—including in countries allied with the U.S.—as Hezbollah in Lebanon and Israel exchange fire daily, raising concerns about broader regional escalation. Iran supports both Hamas and Hezbollah. Palestinian militants have launched persistent rocket attacks into Israel, and Israeli raids continue in the occupied West Bank. On Friday, two Palestinian teenagers were killed in clashes, adding to the more than 80 Palestinian fatalities reported in the past two weeks. A U.S. intelligence assessment estimated that 100 to 300 people died in the recent Gaza hospital explosion, with officials still reviewing the evidence. The U.S. and Israel suggest the explosion was caused by a misfired Palestinian rocket, but these claims have not been independently verified by the Associated Press.

article_content: Most drinkers stop when they run out of cigarettes. However, wine enthusiasts tend to continue drinking, regardless of their cigarette supply. A recent study found that making cigarettes more expensive and banning indoor smoking led to a reduction in beer and spirits consumption—but had no noticeable effect on wine consumption. Researchers analyzed tobacco prices and smoke-free policies from 1980 to 2009 across U.S. states, along with data on per capita consumption of beer, wine, and spirits. They discovered that a 20% increase in cigarette prices and stricter bans on indoor smoking coincided with a 4% drop in beer consumption and an 11% drop in spirits consumption. Wine consumption did not change significantly. Melissa Krauss, a co-author from Washington University School of Medicine, stated, 'When smokers drink alcohol, it often triggers cravings for cigarettes. Some people even smoke only when they drink.' She added that these changes were observed across the whole population, and that an even greater reduction in beer and spirits consumption might be seen among smokers alone. In the short term, reducing smoking could help some people cut down on their drinking. Researchers suggested that wine drinkers might be less affected by tobacco policies due to higher education levels, healthier lifestyles, and a lower likelihood of smoking. Richard A. Grucza, associate professor of psychiatry at Washington University, noted that increasing cigarette taxes could potentially reduce alcohol consumption, adding, 'Excluding tobacco, alcohol is by far the deadliest drug in the U.S.' He also mentioned that raising alcohol taxes could reduce excessive drinking, but faces resistance. According to him, stronger tobacco-control laws could also help limit excessive alcohol use. The researchers believe their findings could encourage further studies into whether tobacco restrictions might help reduce alcohol-related problems such as violence, drunk driving, health issues, and deaths. The study appeared in Alcoholism: Clinical & Experimental Research and aligns with previous findings that stricter smoking regulations are linked to lower smoking rates.
translated_content: A maioria dos bebedores para quando acaba o cigarro. No entanto, os apreciadores de vinho tendem a continuar bebendo, independentemente de terem cigarros. Um estudo recente descobriu que tornar os cigarros mais caros e proibir o fumo em ambientes fechados levou a uma redução no consumo de cerveja e destilados — mas não teve efeito perceptível sobre o consumo de vinho. Pesquisadores analisaram os preços do tabaco e as políticas de ambientes livres de fumaça de 1980 a 2009 em todos os estados dos EUA, junto com dados sobre o consumo per capita de cerveja, vinho e destilados. Eles descobriram que um aumento de 20% no preço dos cigarros e restrições mais rígidas ao fumo em ambientes internos coincidiram com uma queda de 4% no consumo de cerveja e de 11% no consumo de destilados. O consumo de vinho não mudou de forma significativa. Melissa Krauss, coautora da Washington University School of Medicine, afirmou: 'Quando fumantes bebem álcool, isso frequentemente desperta vontade de fumar. Algumas pessoas só fumam quando bebem.' Ela acrescentou que essas mudanças foram observadas em toda a população e que uma redução ainda maior no consumo de cerveja e destilados poderia ser vista apenas entre os fumantes. No curto prazo, fumar menos poderia ajudar algumas pessoas a diminuir o consumo de álcool. Os pesquisadores sugeriram que os apreciadores de vinho podem ser menos afetados por políticas de tabaco devido a níveis mais altos de escolaridade, estilos de vida mais saudáveis e menor probabilidade de fumar. Richard A. Grucza, professor associado de psiquiatria da Washington University, observou que aumentar os impostos sobre cigarros pode potencialmente reduzir o consumo de álcool, acrescentando: 'Excluindo o tabaco, o álcool é de longe a droga mais mortal nos EUA.' Ele também mencionou que aumentar os impostos sobre o álcool poderia reduzir o consumo excessivo, mas enfrenta resistência. article_content: Grapevine (Vitis vinifera L.) holds substantial economic and cultural significance, driving the need for rapid genetic improvements to address climate and market demands. Traditional breeding is slow, and genetically modified (GM) grapevines face regulatory hurdles due to safety concerns. CRISPR/Cas9 has become a promising tool for precise genome editing. However, most CRISPR/Cas9 applications in grapevines have so far resulted in GM plants, which are strictly regulated in many countries. The current challenge is refining CRISPR/Cas9 delivery methods to produce transgene-free, edited grapevines, avoiding unintended genetic changes. In October 2022, Horticulture Research published a perspective entitled 'DNA-free genome editing in grapevine using CRISPR/Cas9 ribonucleoprotein complexes followed by protoplast regeneration.' In this study, a Thompson Seedless grapevine cell line was engineered to overexpress GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein), making genome editing easier to track. Using tissue culture, about 10% of somatic embryos formed embryogenic callus that expressed GFP after around 10 weeks. These calluses were used to extract protoplasts, and about 30% of these could regenerate into whole plants, with all isolated protoplasts showing GFP expression. Researchers then applied CRISPR/Cas9 ribonucleoproteins (RNP1, RNP2, RNP3, RNP4) to knock out the GFP gene in these transgenic protoplasts. Two embryos, treated with RNP2 and RNP4, lost GFP fluorescence—indicating successful gene editing—with efficiencies of 23% and 34% respectively, from mature embryos to whole plants. After CRISPR editing, two GFP-negative embryos were identified, confirming successful gene knockout. Additional analysis verified targeted mutations in the GFP gene, which caused the loss of GFP expression. In summary, this study successfully demonstrates the combination of somatic embryogenesis and CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing in grapevines, opening the door for gene-edited modifications that may be more widely accepted in agriculture.

Ian Poulter narrowly missed ending a two-year title drought at the Turkish Airlines Open, after pulling a 6-foot putt left on the final hole that would have forced a play-off with American Brooks Koepka. Poulter, 38, was left to reflect on a disappointing third round score of 75 that derailed an otherwise strong tournament performance. Meanwhile, Rory McIlroy only needs to appear at the season finale in Dubai to seal the Race to Dubai title, following the outcome in Antalya.

Koepka secured victory with a seven-under-par final round of 65, holding his nerve despite challenges on the final two holes. Poulter, who opened the week with impressive rounds of 64 and 66, was self-critical about his poor third round and narrowly missed keeping pace with Koepka, despite shooting a 67 in the final round.

Marcel Siem was McIlroy's only remaining challenger in the Race to Dubai entering the final round, but finished 12-under after revealing he dislocated a rib while stretching before play. McIlroy, who has already clinched his second Race to Dubai title in three years thanks to the results in Turkey, described 2014 as the best season of his career, highlighted by major wins at The Open, the US PGA Championship, and the Ryder Cup.

Looking ahead, Poulter expressed disappointment with the outcome but aims to finish the season strong at the final event in Dubai, where he has previously found success.

article_content: Nigella Lawson returned to Twitter two months after photographs were published showing her husband, Charles Saatchi, with his hand on her neck. The television chef posted a picture of a homemade cake to celebrate The Great British Bake Off’s return but did not mention the public argument or her impending divorce from Saatchi. This was Lawson’s first tweet since the incident. She baked a Victoria sponge cake to mark the BBC2 show's new season. Since the photos appeared in June, Lawson had made no public statements. In contrast, Saatchi has addressed the situation publicly, including announcing their divorce after ten years of marriage. Returning to Twitter, Lawson wrote: 'Yum: settling down to The Great British Bake Off with a slice of this blackcurrant Victoria sponge #GBBO.' When a follower asked if she had baked the cake, she replied: 'I MADE IT - though it wouldn't get me far in the #GBBO!' Lawson also retweeted a message from the official QI account about Elizabethan customs. She had only tweeted once previously since the incident, sharing a photo of her son Bruno’s birthday cake. The Great British Bake Off’s fourth season began on BBC2, and presenter Paul Hollywood also made headlines for separating from his wife. Lawson has been seen moving her belongings out of her home with Saatchi but has not commented on the divorce. Saatchi has often been seen at Scott’s restaurant in Mayfair, where the incident took place, and initially described the event as a 'playful tiff.' He faced criticism from campaigners who accused him of trivializing domestic violence. In July, Saatchi said in the Mail on Sunday he was divorcing Lawson, though court documents indicate she filed the claim. The couple was granted a decree nisi three weeks ago, nearly a decade after marrying in September 2003 following the death of Lawson’s first husband, John Diamond. Since the separation, Saatchi’s teenage daughter has reportedly claimed Lawson left her, and friends indicate Saatchi has struggled emotionally.

article_content: Researchers have discovered that a virus found in healthy Australian honey bees, known as Israeli Acute Paralysis Virus (IAPV), could be linked to colony collapses happening across the United States. IAPV has been detected in the majority of American bee colonies hit by colony collapse disorder (CCD), which has caused some beekeepers to lose up to 90% of their hives. Honey bees play a crucial role in pollinating crops valued at over $15 billion each year in the U.S., supporting more than 90 types of fruits and vegetables worldwide. CCD first appeared in the U.S. in 2004, coinciding with the import of Australian bees. The disorder leaves behind hives containing the queen, a few newly emerged bees, and plenty of food—but the essential worker bees disappear. While Australian bees carry IAPV, they do not show signs of illness, hinting at a possible innate resistance. Genetic tests on bee samples collected over three years revealed that IAPV was present in 96% of affected U.S. colonies. However, scientists stress that multiple factors likely contribute to CCD, such as genetic vulnerabilities, parasitic pathogens, exposure to pesticides, and environmental stresses. Significantly, varroa mites, which attack every hive in the U.S. but are not found in Australia, could be influencing the prevalence of CCD. Experts are hopeful because some bees demonstrate genetic resistance to viruses like IAPV. Since there is currently no way to treat bee viruses directly, breeding bees with natural disease resistance offers promise for protecting bee populations. The next step for researchers is to determine whether IAPV by itself—or combined with other factors—causes CCD. This study brought together experts from multiple organizations, including the U.S. Department of Agriculture and Columbia University.

O IAPV foi detectado na maioria das colônias americanas afetadas pela desordem do colapso das colônias (CCD), o que fez alguns apicultores perderem até 90% de suas colmeias. As abelhas desempenham papel essencial na polinização de culturas avaliadas em mais de US$15 bilhões por ano nos EUA, apoiando mais de 90 tipos de frutas e verduras no mundo inteiro. Embora as abelhas australianas carreguem o IAPV, elas não apresentam sintomas, indicando uma possível resistência natural. Testes genéticos em amostras de abelhas coletadas ao longo de três anos mostraram que o IAPV estava presente em 96% das colônias afetadas nos EUA. Os cientistas, entretanto, ressaltam que provavelmente vários fatores contribuem para a CCD: vulnerabilidades genéticas, agentes patogênicos parasitários, exposição a pesticidas e estresses ambientais. De forma marcante, os ácaros varroa — presentes em todas as colmeias americanas, mas ausentes na Austrália — podem ter influência na predominância da CCD. Especialistas estão otimistas porque algumas abelhas demonstram resistência genética a vírus como o IAPV. Como ainda não há tratamento direto para vírus em abelhas, criar abelhas naturalmente resistentes pode ser uma solução promissora para proteger as populações. David Hammond, a 27-year-old businessman from Palmers Green, North London, tried to defraud his insurance company by claiming his fiancée's £20,000 diamond ring had been stolen while they were on holiday in Brazil. He filed a police report in Rio de Janeiro and, upon returning to the UK, submitted a claim to Aqueduct underwriters. However, when a Facebook photo showed his fiancée wearing the supposedly missing ring, the deception came to light. Despite this, Hammond continued with the false claim, even providing more fabricated details before finally retracting his claim seven months later.

At the Old Bailey, Hammond pleaded guilty to fraud. Judge Charles Wide QC sentenced him to six months in prison, suspended for a year, ordered 200 hours of community service, imposed a three-month curfew at his home each night, and required him to pay £300 in costs. The judge emphasized the seriousness of insurance fraud, saying it's not a victimless crime as it affects everyone’s premiums. He noted that Hammond had not been truthful with the police or the insurance company before eventually admitting his wrongdoing. Detective Constable Patrick Einsmann, leading the investigation, commented that Hammond’s attempt at fraud resulted in a criminal conviction just before his upcoming wedding.

article_content: An international team of astronomers has used NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to observe the eruption of Nova Vulpeculae 2021. The results of this observational campaign, published on November 8 on the pre-print server arXiv, provide important insights into the unique characteristics of this classical nova, revealing its complex variability. A classical nova is a star that experiences a sudden increase in brightness and then gradually returns to its original state, a process that can last for many months. This outburst is caused by the accretion process in a close binary system containing a white dwarf (WD) and its companion. Typically, classical novae exhibit a rapid rise in optical brightness until reaching a peak, followed by a slow decline. However, some novae display more complex behavior than the standard 'fast rise—smooth decline' pattern. Nova Vulpeculae 2021 (V606 Vul) is one of the eruptions that deviates from the traditional model. V606 Vul was detected on July 16, 2021, nine days before TESS observations began. A group of astronomers led by Kirill Sokolovsky of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign investigated V606 Vul using TESS, aiming to learn more about this nova. The researchers wrote, 'We use TESS photometry of the V606 Vul eruption to characterize variability of a nova in exquisite detail.' TESS observations covered the first of two primary peaks following the eruption of V606 Vul. The light curve indicated that the nova reached its brightest visual magnitude during the second peak, which occurred 64 days after the eruption. By analyzing the light curve, the team found periodic variations with a period of approximately 3.06 hours and an average peak-to-peak amplitude of 0.01 magnitude, present except when the nova was within 1 magnitude of peak optical brightness. They also identified mini-flares with peak-to-peak amplitudes up to 0.5 magnitude, appearing at seemingly random times in series of one or more, separated by quiet intervals. The observations show that the periodic variations disappeared when V606 Vul reached peak optical brightness. The astronomers suggest that these variations may result from azimuthal asymmetry of the photosphere surrounding the underlying binary system, but do not rule out other explanations, such as temperature asymmetry. Summing up, the authors noted this is the first use of TESS photometry to investigate nova eruptions and emphasized TESS's usefulness in studying Galactic novae. They concluded, 'First, thanks to its high photometric precision, we can characterize brightness variations in a nova with amplitudes so low that they cannot be detected from the ground. Second, the space platform's ability to conduct virtually uninterrupted observations over a month allows the study of variability on a 12–24 hour timescale, which is difficult to achieve with ground-based observations due to the diurnal cycle.'

Uma nova clássica é uma estrela que passa por um aumento súbito de brilho e, em seguida, retorna gradualmente ao seu estado original, um processo que pode durar muitos meses. Porém, algumas novas apresentam comportamentos mais complexos do que o padrão 'subida rápida—declínio suave'. A Nova Vulpeculae 2021 (V606 Vul) é uma dessas erupções que foge do modelo tradicional. A V606 Vul foi detectada em 16 de julho de 2021, nove dias antes do início das observações pelo TESS. Um grupo de astrônomos liderado por Kirill Sokolovsky, da Universidade de Illinois em Urbana-Champaign, investigou a V606 Vul usando o TESS, com o objetivo de aprender mais sobre essa nova. Os pesquisadores escreveram: 'Usamos a fotometria do TESS da erupção da V606 Vul para caracterizar a variabilidade de uma nova em detalhes minuciosos.' As observações do TESS abrangeram o primeiro de dois picos principais após a erupção da V606 Vul. A curva de luz indicou que a nova atingiu seu brilho visual máximo durante o segundo pico, ocorrido 64 dias após a erupção. Ao analisar a curva de luz, a equipe encontrou variações periódicas com período de aproximadamente 3,06 horas e amplitude média pico a pico de 0,01 magnitude, presentes exceto quando a nova estava a 1 magnitude do pico do brilho óptico. Também identificaram mini-erupções com amplitudes pico a pico de até 0,5 magnitude, surgindo em momentos aparentemente aleatórios, em séries de uma ou mais, separadas por intervalos tranquilos. As observações mostram que as variações periódicas desapareceram quando a V606 Vul atingiu o pico do brilho óptico. Os astrônomos sugerem que essas variações podem resultar de uma assimetria azimutal da fotosfera que envolve o sistema binário subjacente, mas não descartam outras explicações, como assimetria de temperatura. Resumindo, os autores observaram que este é o primeiro uso da fotometria do TESS para investigar erupções de novas e destacaram a utilidade do TESS no estudo de novas galácticas. Eles concluíram: 'Primeiro, graças à alta precisão fotométrica, podemos caracterizar variações de brilho em uma nova com amplitudes tão baixas que não podem ser detectadas da Terra. Segundo, a capacidade da plataforma espacial de realizar observações praticamente ininterruptas por um mês permite o estudo de variabilidades em escalas de 12–24 horas, difícil de ser alcançado com observações terrestres devido ao ciclo diurno.'

article_content: Hyundai and Kia announced plans to adopt the North American Charging Standard (NACS), also known as the “Tesla plug,” for their future electric vehicles. Hyundai and Kia models equipped with NACS will begin arriving in the fourth quarter of 2024. Starting in the first quarter of 2025, the companies will provide adapters for existing customers, enabling them to use Tesla Supercharger stations. Currently, Hyundai’s Ioniq 5 and Ioniq 6, as well as Kia’s EV6 and EV9, utilize the Combined Charging Standard (CCS) for DC fast charging. Other automakers that have announced adoption of NACS include Ford, GM, Rivian, Volvo, Polestar, Nissan, Mercedes-Benz, Jaguar Land Rover, and Fisker. Volkswagen and Toyota remain among the few major automakers yet to announce support for NACS. Hyundai and Kia are participating in a joint venture with BMW, GM, Stellantis, and Mercedes-Benz to develop a nationwide network of fast EV charging stations in the United States. The goal is to install at least 30,000 high-speed chargers by 2030, with the initial stations set to open in the summer of 2024. Tesla's Supercharger network is considered more reliable than many competing EV charging networks, many of which use the CCS or the less common CHAdeMO standard. Tesla reports having 45,000 Superchargers globally, including 12,000 in the US, with an average uptime of 99.95% in 2022, a slight decrease from 99.96% in 2021. Access to Tesla Superchargers was previously limited to Tesla vehicles, but this has changed as the company started allowing non-Tesla EVs to charge at its stations. In early 2023, the Biden administration announced that Tesla would further expand access as a condition to receive a portion of the $7.5 billion set aside for EV charging infrastructure in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Unlike in Europe, Tesla Superchargers in the US use a proprietary connector. To accommodate other vehicles, Tesla has installed a device called the Magic Dock, which adds a CCS adapter to the connector. article_content: During a recent ICC Cricket World Cup match at Ahmedabad’s Narendra Modi Stadium, Pakistan's cricket team faced an unfriendly reception, with crowd chants and jeers widely described as Islamophobic. Tensions escalated when Pakistan captain Babar Azam was booed after the toss, and after star batsman Muhammad Rizwan was dismissed, the crowd chanted 'Jai Shri Ram'—a slogan with religious and political significance in India, often used by Hindu nationalist groups. The stadium, named after India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi and situated in his hometown, was filled with Indian fans, while Pakistani supporters were effectively barred by authorities. Every Pakistani boundary was met with silence, reflecting the crowd's bias. India comfortably chased down Pakistan's score of 191, and the crowd continued with mocking and offensive chants. Prominent sports writers like Karthik Krishnaswamy and Kuldip Lal criticized the behavior, Krishnaswamy calling it 'unapologetic Islamophobia' and urging the Pakistan Cricket Board to take action. Lal attributed the hostility to the stadium's political environment, contrasting it with more welcoming crowds in cities such as Hyderabad and Bengaluru. Numerous Indians on social media condemned the crowd's conduct, stressing that such actions do not reflect Indian values. Gaurav Nandan Tripathi commented that the stadium itself has become a political symbol that encourages this type of behavior. Pakistan's coach Mickey Arthur remarked on the lack of support, saying the match felt more like a bilateral series than an international competition. He did not cite this as the reason for defeat but acknowledged its impact. An Indian travel website drew backlash for a pre-match ad campaign that mocked Pakistani fans, with many Indians denouncing it. For their next World Cup matches, Pakistan will compete in southern India, beginning in Bengaluru, where both critics and supporters anticipate a more respectful and sporting atmosphere. There is hope that the hostility witnessed in Ahmedabad will not be repeated and that the focus will return to the game.

article_content: A recent report from the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) raises concerns about toddler formulas—formally known as Older Infant and Young Child Formulas (OIYCFs)—saying most kids don't need them and that marketing for these products can give parents the wrong idea. Research featured in Public Health Nutrition shows sales of these formulas climbed 158% from 2006 to 2015. Experts argue this is largely because many parents, influenced by marketing, believe toddler formulas are more beneficial than they really are. Dr. George Fuchs, who led the AAP report and teaches at the University of Kentucky, points out that parents often think toddler formulas do things that regular cow’s milk and a healthy diet with fortified foods can't, but this perception is mostly fueled by advertising. The AAP says babies should get breast milk or standard infant formula until they're one year old. After their first birthday, they can switch to cow’s milk and a range of solid foods, which should start around 6 months. Toddler formulas are sometimes promoted as 'transition' or 'weaning' drinks for infants under a year, but the report stresses that, unlike infant formula, there are no strict FDA rules about what goes into toddler formulas. Dr. Keyana Washington, a pediatrician not involved in the report, adds that most toddlers don't need these formulas since they often contain more sugar and fewer nutrients compared to whole cow’s milk. She says that in the majority of cases, a combination of milk and a balanced diet covers children's nutritional needs. Dr. Nagela Sainté-Thomas, also not part of the AAP report, observes that some parents use toddler formulas as an easy go-to if their child is struggling with solid foods. However, organizations like the World Health Assembly, CDC, UNICEF, and the WHO maintain that most toddlers do just fine with breast milk, cow’s milk, water, and suitable solid foods. According to the AAP, toddler formulas aren’t necessarily dangerous for older babies, and they can fit into a balanced diet for toddlers over 12 months, but they do not offer a nutritional advantage over cow’s milk. Some companies market these formulas as if they're an essential part of a child's diet, which is misleading. The report also notes that packaging and branding similarities between toddler and infant formulas can confuse caregivers. Pediatricians interviewed by ABC News recommend a varied diet for toddlers—covering fruits, veggies, grains, proteins, dairy, and appropriate milk. If you're considering toddler formula, they suggest talking with your pediatrician. Dr. Washington emphasizes that any decision to use alternatives to cow's milk after one year should be backed by medical advice. Additional insights were provided by Dr. Daniel A. Carnegie, a preventive medicine resident at UNC Chapel Hill and member of the ABC News Medical Unit.

article_content: John Ibrahim, a well-known figure in Kings Cross, has criticized police for their handling of investigations into violence against his family. The latest incident occurred when his youngest brother, Michael Ibrahim, was shot in the shoulder on Macquarie Street in Sydney's CBD last Sunday. This marks the third attempt on the life of an Ibrahim brother in the past five years, following Sam Ibrahim being shot twice in 2011 and Fadi Ibrahim, who was shot five times in 2009. No arrests have resulted from any of these attacks. John Ibrahim urged police to be 'smarter' and spend more time investigating this latest case, expressing frustration over the lack of progress in previous incidents. In response, a NSW Police spokesperson noted that Michael was no longer cooperating with officers, emphasizing that investigations are more effective when victims participate. In the days before the shooting, there were reports that the family of another Sydney crime figure allegedly tried to broker peace. Michael Ibrahim was hit in the shoulder by one of several bullets fired as he returned home. Since his release after serving over six years in prison for manslaughter, Michael was reportedly involved in a new relationship and a party lifestyle. Hospital spokesperson David Faktor stated on Monday that Michael Ibrahim, 36, was in stable condition and had not required surgery, correcting earlier reports. Police have confirmed the shooting took place outside Michael's Macquarie Street residence, just 200 meters from NSW Parliament House. They are searching for at least two suspects and a late-model white Audi. No other injuries were reported. Macquarie Street was temporarily closed as police searched for evidence, including bullet casings. The attack occurred near several notable locations, including less than 300 meters from the site of the Lindt café siege. Michael Ibrahim had previously vowed to abide by strict parole conditions after his 2014 release from prison, motivated by his mother’s illness. His parole included electronic monitoring and restrictions from certain areas of Sydney.
