Britain spends nearly four times more on health and welfare per person than Romania, according to European Union officials. In 2012, the UK allocated approximately £7,000 in welfare for every resident, amounting to over a quarter of its national income. In comparison, Romania's provisions for healthcare, family support, and pensions were much lower. The UK ranks fifteenth among European welfare spenders, spending about £1,000 more per person than the EU average.

These figures were detailed in a recent EU paper published by the Office for National Statistics. The timing coincides with both Prime Minister David Cameron and Labour leader Ed Miliband promising to tighten access to benefits for EU immigrants. Cameron has proposed barring EU citizens from claiming welfare for four years, while Miliband supports lengthening the waiting period for new arrivals and limiting benefit payments for children living abroad.

Data shows that since autumn 2013, over 100,000 Romanians have applied for national insurance numbers to work in Britain. Chancellor George Osborne, speaking at Manchester City’s new Football Academy, has also emphasized the need to reduce welfare spending.

The EU’s statistics office Eurostat uses the 'purchasing power standard' (PPS) to compare social spending across countries by adjusting for local price differences. In 2012, Romania spent PPS 2,080.1 per person on welfare, while Britain spent PPS 7,356.8, equivalent to roughly £6,959 each. The UK’s total welfare bill was £443.3 billion, representing more than 28% of GDP.

According to ONS analysis, 44.7% of UK welfare spending went to older people—covering pensions, winter fuel, and TV licenses—while 32.8% supported healthcare services such as NHS hospitals, GPs, and subsidized prescriptions. Together, pensions, sickness benefits, and healthcare accounted for over three-quarters of British welfare outlays. Notably, 5.5% of the UK's welfare budget was spent on housing, far above the EU average.

There are ongoing debates about the use of council and social housing by recent immigrants, particularly in East London. The UK's social spending is also twice as high as Poland's (PPS 3,278.2). Romania spends the least of any EU country, while Britain's rate is 17.5% above the average. According to MigrationWatch, Romanian families can dramatically improve their living standards by relocating to Britain, where a family may claim several types of benefits.

Across Europe, the UK is the fifteenth largest spender on social protection—behind France, Germany, and Italy, but ahead of Spain, Greece, and Portugal. Luxembourg spends more per capita on welfare than any other EU country.

Chancellor Osborne has pledged to cut billions from the welfare budget if the Conservatives win the next election, with plans to reduce tax credits and freeze working-age benefits for two years, affecting families on low incomes. Last year, tax credits alone cost £29.7 billion, far more than jobseeker’s allowance or housing benefit. Osborne announced that total welfare spending is declining as a share of GDP and that a freeze on working-age benefits could reduce a low-income family’s income by up to £350 a year.

Pensions minister Steve Webb has stated he does not wish to force people to work 'until they drop,' but believes employers should recognize the untapped potential in older staff. With a predicted shortage of workers—13.5 million job vacancies expected in the next decade and only 7 million young people leaving school or college—ministers say people may have to stay in jobs until at least 70.

Employers are being urged to change their attitudes toward older workers, whose numbers are growing. According to the government, Britain faces a significant workforce gap, which could be filled by older people remaining employed longer. Currently, around 22% of the population is over 60; this is expected to increase to 28% by 2035.

Steve Webb commented to the Daily Telegraph: 'People have often asked how we will tackle ageist attitudes among employers. Demographics are going to resolve that for us. Over time, there will be roles where experienced older workers are essential, and employers who do not adapt will be left behind.'

A new government guide, 'Employing Older Workers,' has been released to help employers retain experienced staff. The guide states, 'Older people are the main untapped source of labour: unlike migrants, they already live here, and their numbers are rising. People are living and staying fit for longer; most 65-year-olds today will live beyond 80, and some could reach 110. The number of over-60s is expected to rise sharply over the next two decades, reaching 17.5 million by 2035.'

McDonald's reports that output is 20% higher in restaurants with staff aged over 60. David Fairhurst, from McDonald's UK & Northern Europe, said: 'Changing demographics in the workplace means older workers are the fastest growing age group in the labour market. Despite these numbers, their contributions often go unrecognized. At McDonald's, we employ over 1,000 people aged 60 and above, who make a significant impact on our business and customer satisfaction.'

Webb insists he does not want to force people to work into their seventies and beyond. 'This isn’t “work ‘til you drop”. It’s about enabling people to continue working where it benefits them, which is often good for their wellbeing,' Webb said. 'Hiring older workers doesn't shut out young people; it helps keep experienced, productive workers in the workforce, which is beneficial for everyone.'

article_content: In 2003, following the release of her fourth album 'In the Zone' and a highly publicized breakup with Justin Timberlake, Britney Spears participated in an interview with journalist Diane Sawyer. In her upcoming memoir, ‘The Woman in Me’, obtained ahead of release by TIME, Spears reveals she was pressured by her father to do the interview and describes feeling exploited, embarrassed, and exposed. 'It was completely humiliating,' Spears writes. 'I wasn’t told what the questions would be, and it turned out they were all embarrassing. I was too vulnerable then, too sensitive, to do this kind of interview.' Over the past two decades, there has been growing reflection on the intense scrutiny faced by young female celebrities in the 2000s, and the Sawyer interview has recently resurfaced on TikTok, where many viewers are criticizing its tone. Spears recounts that her breakup with Timberlake—who ended the relationship abruptly via text—left her devastated, but contractual obligations pushed her back to work before she was emotionally ready. Spears writes, 'I didn’t want to share anything private with the world. I didn’t owe the media details of my breakup. I shouldn’t have been forced to speak on national TV or cry in front of a stranger who kept asking harsh questions. I felt exploited, set up in front of the whole world.' During the interview, Sawyer was incisive and critical. At one point, she described Spears as 'the most valuable square inch of real estate in the entertainment universe,' while footage zoomed in on Spears' navel. Spears reflects that the interview marked a breaking point, describing feeling something dark come over her. At the time, lyrics from Timberlake's album 'Justified' seemed to blame Spears, and rumors suggested she had cheated on him. Spears alleges in her memoir that Timberlake had cheated on her multiple times and that she only kissed a choreographer in retaliation. These topics became the core of Sawyer’s questioning. Sawyer accused Spears of causing Timberlake pain and questioned her about her behavior, suggesting she was 'feeding the publicity monster.' Spears concludes that she should have been allowed to heal privately. 'It would have been better for me, but I had no choice. It seemed like nobody really cared how I felt.'

article_content: A knitting group has constructed an 8-foot (2.4m) high replica of the London Cenotaph for Remembrance Sunday. The structure is made of woollen 'bricks' sewn together and carefully assembled. About 20 residents of ExtraCare's Stoke Gifford Retirement Village started the project in July this year. "When I saw it come together, I thought it was really good," said knitting group member Jenny Rogers. The flags and decorations on the cenotaph are also knitted, and the words 'The Glorious Dead' have been embroidered. Last year, the group created a 6-foot (1.8m) knitted soldier for Remembrance Sunday, which now stands next to the cenotaph. They also crafted a knitted Queen to celebrate Queen Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee, which received a written acknowledgement from the late monarch. Ms. Rogers said the knitted cenotaph and soldier are available for anyone to view in the reception area of the retirement village. Follow BBC West on Facebook, X, and Instagram. Prince Harry was seen making a late-night visit to Nando’s chicken restaurant in Fulham after England’s World Cup qualifying match against Poland. Wearing a baseball cap, jeans, and a T-shirt, Harry ordered a chicken breast fillet with lemon and herb sauce, cheese, mashed potatoes, a double chicken breast wrap with medium spice, and chips, as reported by the Daily Mirror. The bill came to around £24. He placed his order shortly before midnight and was accompanied by a friend and his personal security team, waiting for the food while using his mobile phone before they left through the car park. This is not his first time at Nando’s — he was previously seen at the Stevenage branch in 2009 with army colleagues.

The next day, Harry, a qualified rugby coach and patron of the Rugby Football Union (RFU) All Schools Programme, participated in a coaching session at Twickenham Stadium. He joined RFU coaching staff and England World Cup winner Jason Robinson, leading drills with school children. Robinson gifted Harry a pair of boots like those he wore as an international and encouraged him to showcase his skills. Harry joked about being 'a bit past it already' but put in an energetic and committed performance. The All Schools Programme seeks to bring rugby to 750 state schools as part of England’s preparation for the 2015 World Cup. The session included a kit design workshop and training for both boys and girls, with Harry actively involved and showing strong support for youth sport.

Kale, the leafy green often featured in green juices popular among celebrities and health-conscious individuals, has seen such a surge in popularity that farmers around the world are struggling to meet demand, resulting in a global shortage. Bejo Seeds, one of the world's primary suppliers of kale seeds based in the Netherlands, recently reported it has run out of all varieties of kale seeds. This shortage is particularly impacting Australian farmers.

Tony Hubbard, head of Bejo Seeds' Australian office, told ABC's Landline, "It's a global issue, and we've been caught off guard by the extent of the demand." Traditionally used in smaller quantities, kale’s popularity has soared over the past three years, becoming a staple in green juices and a favorite among both celebrities and health enthusiasts. 

Steve Bruynen, from Bruynen Farms in Pearcedale, southeast of Melbourne, said that to keep up with kale demand, his business had to stop growing red cabbages and leeks. "We used to plant around 3,000 to 4,000 kale plants each season. Now, we're up to about 25,000, and it's still not enough," Bruynen explained.

Deborah and Darren Corrigan, among Australia’s largest kale suppliers, started with a trial of 1,500 seedlings a few years ago and now plant 150,000 seedlings weekly at their farm in Clyde, southeast of Melbourne. "It was overwhelming—I had to call around the country just to source more plants to bring into Victoria," Deborah Corrigan said.

Kale has become the fastest selling product at Coles supermarkets, according to Brad Gorman, head of Coles' fresh produce division. "Kale's growth over the past three years is almost unprecedented for a product that’s been available for this long," he remarked.

A Bejo Seeds, uma das maiores fornecedoras mundiais de sementes de couve, com sede na Holanda, informou recentemente que esgotou todas as variedades de sementes. Essa falta está afetando especialmente os agricultores australianos.

Tony Hubbard, chefe do escritório australiano da Bejo Seeds, disse ao programa Landline da ABC: "É um problema global e fomos pegos de surpresa pela dimensão da demanda." Tradicionalmente usada em pequenas quantidades, a couve teve sua popularidade disparada nos últimos três anos, virando ingrediente comum em sucos verdes e se tornando queridinha de celebridades e aficionados por saúde.

Steve Bruynen, da Bruynen Farms em Pearcedale, sudeste de Melbourne, contou que, para acompanhar a demanda por couve, sua empresa precisou parar de plantar repolho-roxo e alho-poró. "Antes, plantávamos de 3.000 a 4.000 pés de couve por temporada. Agora, chegamos a cerca de 25 mil e ainda não é suficiente", explicou Bruynen.

Deborah e Darren Corrigan, que estão entre os maiores fornecedores de couve da Austrália, começaram com um teste de 1.500 mudas há alguns anos e hoje plantam 150.000 mudas por semana na fazenda em Clyde, sudeste de Melbourne. "Foi puxado – tive que ligar o país todo para conseguir mais mudas e trazer pra Victoria," relembrou Deborah Corrigan.

A couve virou o produto que mais vende rápido no supermercado Coles, de acordo com Brad Gorman, chefe do setor de hortifruti da rede. "O crescimento da couve nesses últimos três anos é praticamente sem precedentes para um produto que já está disponível há tanto tempo", comentou.

Labour’s plan to freeze energy prices until 2017, introduced by Ed Miliband in 2013 as a flagship policy, is under fire as energy prices decline. Labour has now rebranded the measure as a ‘price cap’ so that customers’ bills will be able to fall alongside market prices. This change comes after party representatives admitted that the policy’s original rollout didn’t specify it as a cap and that the economic context has evolved. Caroline Flint, Labour’s energy spokesperson, clarified the original intent was to allow prices to drop, while Rachel Reeves acknowledged the new market conditions.

Prime Minister David Cameron and Conservative chairman Grant Shapps have seized on Labour’s shift, criticizing what they describe as confusion and inconsistency. Critics also argue that the initial freeze may have stopped energy companies from lowering prices sooner, due to political uncertainty. The debate intensified after E.On, a major energy firm, announced a 3.5% price reduction for its customers, and more companies are expected to do the same. Neil Woodford, a prominent fund manager, described Labour’s policy as ‘good politics, but bad economics,’ asserting that it has caused customers to pay more than they might have otherwise.

Representantes admitiram que, inicialmente, a proposta não utilizou o termo “teto” e reconhecem que o cenário econômico mudou. article_content: Juventus and Chile midfielder Arturo Vidal has dismissed rumors linking him to Manchester United, according to Italian reports. Although speculation has surrounded Vidal’s future, with both Manchester United and Real Madrid expressing interest in signing the 27-year-old, Vidal clarified his position when asked about a possible move: ‘I am not going to Manchester.’ Vidal recently returned to Italy and addressed journalists about his plans with Juventus, stating, ‘I am not going to Manchester. Will I stay at Juve? I’m not sure. I’ll speak with (manager) Allegri on Monday and then decide. I haven’t yet spoken to Allegri or my teammates, but a move to Manchester isn’t happening.’ Italian newspaper Gazzetta Dello Sport adds that Juventus is determined to retain Vidal, who still has three years remaining on his contract. However, the club might reconsider if a significant offer, around €45 million (£36 million), is received. Liverpool and Arsenal are also reportedly interested in acquiring the Chilean international. The possibility of Vidal not joining Manchester United is a setback for new manager Louis van Gaal, who had listed the midfielder as a key target after signing Ander Herrera from Athletic Bilbao. Since transferring from Bayer Leverkusen in 2011, Vidal has helped Juventus claim three consecutive Serie A titles, scoring 11 goals in 32 league appearances last season.

Spanish authorities have confiscated Scythian jewelry valued at €60 million (£52 million), which they state was stolen from Ukraine. Police report that the 11 ancient gold pieces were smuggled out of Ukraine in 2016 and intended for resale in Spain. The collection—featuring bracelets, necklaces, and earrings dating from the 8th to 4th centuries BC—was accompanied by forged documents claiming ownership by the Ukrainian Orthodox Church.

Previously, five people were arrested as part of an investigation into the 2021 sale of a gold belt decorated with rams' heads.

The Scythians were a nomadic people who held sway over parts of eastern Europe and Asia, including today’s southern Ukraine, from around 800 BC to 400 AD. They were renowned for their rich culture and exceptional gold craftsmanship.

In a separate incident, Ukrainian authorities stated last week that they have recovered 14 archaeological objects allegedly stolen from Russian-occupied regions, arresting a Russian man who attempted to smuggle them into the United States. These items include a Neolithic axe estimated to date from around 5,000 to 3,000 BC.

"It's safe to say that Ukraine has received a new shipment of weaponry. The only catch is that this weaponry is incredibly ancient," Ukraine’s acting Minister of Culture Rostyslav Karandieiev remarked humorously during a news conference.

Scythian artifacts are among Ukraine's most celebrated historical treasures. Ukrainian archaeologists claim that gold held in museums located in Russian-occupied territories has been looted since the large-scale invasion last year. Overall losses from the reported plundering of Ukraine’s cultural heritage are believed to reach hundreds of millions of euros.

Anteriormente, cinco pessoas foram presas como parte de uma investigação sobre a venda, em 2021, de um cinto de ouro decorado com cabeças de carneiros.

Os citas foram um povo nômade que dominou partes do leste da Europa e da Ásia, incluindo o atual sul da Ucrânia, de cerca de 800 a.C. até 400 d.C. Eram conhecidos por sua rica cultura e extraordinária habilidade com o ouro.

Em outro caso, as autoridades ucranianas informaram na semana passada que recuperaram 14 objetos arqueológicos supostamente roubados de regiões ocupadas pela Rússia, prendendo um cidadão russo que tentou contrabandeá-los para os Estados Unidos. Entre esses itens está um machado neolítico de aproximadamente 5.000 a 3.000 a.C.

"É seguro dizer que a Ucrânia recebeu um novo carregamento de armamento. O detalhe é que esse armamento é muito antigo", brincou o ministro interino da Cultura da Ucrânia, Rostyslav Karandieiev, em coletiva de imprensa.

Artefatos citas estão entre os mais célebres tesouros históricos da Ucrânia. Arqueólogos ucranianos alegam que ouro mantido em museus em áreas sob ocupação russa tem sido saqueado desde a invasão em larga escala no ano passado. As perdas com o suposto saque do patrimônio histórico e artístico ucraniano são estimadas em centenas de milhões de euros.

article_content: Alia Bhatt recently shared memorable moments from the National Awards ceremony, where she was honored with the Best Actor award for her performance in 'Gangubai Kathiawadi'. She described the experience as surreal and was deeply impressed by how well-organized the event was. During a conversation at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, Alia recounted a touching moment with co-winner Kriti Sanon. As they waited in line to take the stage, Kriti turned and asked to hug her. Alia recalled, 'We both got emotional—it was two young women living a dream and feeling grateful. We even had to stop hugging or we would have burst into tears.' Alia also spoke about her decision to re-wear her wedding saree, designed by Sabyasachi Mukherjee, for the awards. She mentioned that upon hearing her name as the winner, her first thought was to wear the saree because it felt authentic to her. She emphasized that special outfits can and should be worn more than once, both for personal meaning and to encourage sustainability. She added that women often plan to reuse their wedding outfits for other significant occasions, and she hoped to encourage more people to consider this. 'I wanted to promote mindfulness around fashion—you don’t always need something new for each event. Even re-wearing a special outfit occasionally is a meaningful step for both you and the planet,' Alia explained. Alia was accompanied by her husband, Ranbir Kapoor, who proudly took photos as she took the stage.

article_content: Paul Karason, who became known for his blue skin after self-medicating for a skin condition, died at the age of 62. Karason passed away on Monday at a hospital in Washington, as reported by NBC Today. He was admitted after suffering a heart attack, then developed pneumonia and experienced a severe stroke. Karason gained widespread attention online for his distinctive blue skin, which resulted from using a silver compound for over a decade to treat facial dermatitis. In 2008, Karason appeared on NBC's Today Show to talk about his experience. He explained that taking colloidal silver—a suspension of silver in liquid—caused him to develop argyria, a condition from the accumulation of silver in the body. Prior to his television appearance, he lived a reclusive life. His blue skin earned him the nickname 'Papa Smurf.' According to his estranged widow, he enjoyed the nickname when children used it, but was less comfortable when adults did. Silver has long been known for its antibacterial properties and has been used for centuries to fight infections. Its use declined after more effective antibiotics like penicillin were developed. In 1999, the FDA banned the use of colloidal silver in over-the-counter medicines due to the risk of argyria—a permanent discoloration caused when silver accumulates in the skin and reacts to light, similar to its behavior in photography.

article_content: Great TV series can often span multiple seasons, requiring long-term commitments from viewers. On the other hand, miniseries offer well-crafted stories within just a few episodes. Despite their shorter run times, some miniseries achieve masterpiece status, proving that powerful narratives don’t have to be lengthy. From horror favorites like The Haunting of Hill House to intense thrillers like Sharp Objects, miniseries reveal the format’s diversity, creativity, and entertainment value. The best miniseries make every minute count, highlighting the impact of focused storytelling. A bonus: many of these shows are perfect for a weekend binge. Maniac stars Emma Stone as Annie Landsberg and Jonah Hill as Owen Milgrim, who struggles with his schizophrenia diagnosis. After joining a pharmaceutical trial together, the two form an unexpected bond. Although participants are assured the experiment is safe, the three-day drug trial takes a surreal and dangerous turn. Set in a retro-futuristic New York, Maniac features striking visuals and ambitious storytelling, brought to life by the dynamic chemistry between Stone and Hill. WandaVision follows Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) and Vision (Paul Bettany) in their seemingly ideal suburban life in Westview, New Jersey. Their reality unravels as each episode shifts through sitcom styles from different decades, ultimately revealing a hidden truth about the town. Still regarded as the best MCU (Marvel Cinematic Universe) series on Disney+, WandaVision showcases the talents of Olsen and Bettany and demonstrates the miniseries format’s potential for superhero stories. Beef centers on a road rage incident between contractor Danny Cho (Steven Yeun) and business owner Amy Lau (Ali Wong), spiraling into an escalating feud. This acclaimed 10-episode Netflix series combines dark comedy and social satire, exposing themes of anger, frustration, and personal struggle. Amy’s relationship challenges and Danny’s financial troubles make their conflict relatable, and the series is both cathartic and thought-provoking. When They See Us, directed by Ava DuVernay, is based on the 1989 Central Park jogger case involving five Black teenagers wrongfully accused and convicted. The series details their arrest, trial, and the eventual exoneration and settlement in 2014. Acclaimed for its unflinching approach, When They See Us is regarded as one of Netflix’s best original shows and a powerful depiction of systemic injustice and racism in America. Maid adapts Stephanie Land’s memoir, portraying Alex Russell (Margaret Qualley), a young mother who escapes an abusive relationship and struggles to support her daughter by working as a housecleaner. The series doesn’t shy away from depicting homelessness and hardship, but it also offers moments of hope and recovery as Alex strives to secure a better life for her child. Qualley’s portrayal earned her the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Miniseries. The Haunting of Hill House, the first entry in Mike Flanagan’s anthology, adapts Shirley Jackson’s classic novel into a haunting family drama. Spanning two timelines, it follows siblings whose experiences in Hill House continue to affect them as adults. Known as one of Netflix’s scariest series, it innovates within the horror genre with emotionally layered storytelling and striking visuals. Band of Brothers, produced by Steven Spielberg and Tom Hanks, is an acclaimed miniseries based on Stephen E. Ambrose’s book, chronicling Easy Company’s journey in WWII. The 10-episode series captures the soldiers’ camaraderie, hardships, and heroism, blending dramatic realism with human stories. While dramatized in certain aspects, it is rooted in interviews, letters, and Ambrose’s nonfiction account, reflecting the real experiences of Easy Company. Sharp Objects stars Amy Adams as reporter Camille Preaker, who returns to her hometown to investigate two crimes while confronting her troubled family past. Based on Gillian Flynn’s novel, the miniseries shifts focus from the surface-level mystery to Camille’s psychological struggles. Adams delivers a compelling performance, anchoring the series’ depiction of trauma and recovery. The Queen’s Gambit features Anya Taylor-Joy as chess prodigy Beth Harmon, charting her rise through the competitive world of chess while battling addiction. The miniseries, based on Walter Tevis’s novel, became a cultural phenomenon for its period style, engaging chess portrayals, and Taylor-Joy’s award-winning performance. Chernobyl is a five-episode HBO drama recounting the 1986 nuclear disaster in the Soviet Union. The series is praised for its attention to historical and scientific detail, dramatizing the catastrophic event and its aftermath. Creator Craig Mazin further explained artistic choices in accompanying podcasts. Chernobyl stands out for its depiction of individual stories and its critique of the authorities responsible for the tragedy.

Apesar de durarem menos, algumas minisséries tornam-se verdadeiras obras-primas, provando que narrativas poderosas não precisam ser extensas. De sucessos do terror como The Haunting of Hill House a thrillers intensos como Sharp Objects, as minisséries mostram a diversidade, criatividade e valor do entretenimento desse formato. As melhores utilizam ao máximo cada minuto, destacando o impacto de uma narrativa focada. Bônus: muitas dessas produções são perfeitas para maratonar no fim de semana. Maniac traz Emma Stone como Annie Landsberg e Jonah Hill como Owen Milgrim, que lida com o diagnóstico de esquizofrenia. Depois de ingressarem em um teste farmacêutico juntos, os dois criam um vínculo inesperado. Apesar de garantirem a segurança do experimento, o teste de três dias toma um rumo surreal e perigoso. Ambientada numa Nova York retrofuturista, Maniac se destaca pelos visuais marcantes e narrativa ambiciosa, com uma química notável entre Stone e Hill. WandaVision acompanha Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) e Visão (Paul Bettany) em uma vida suburbana aparentemente perfeita em Westview, Nova Jersey. A realidade deles se desfaz à medida que cada episódio viaja por estilos de sitcom de décadas diferentes, até revelar a verdade oculta sobre a cidade. Considerada até hoje a melhor série do MCU (Universo Cinematográfico Marvel) no Disney+, WandaVision evidencia o talento de Olsen e Bettany, além de mostrar o potencial do formato minissérie para histórias de super-heróis. Beef gira em torno de um incidente de fúria no trânsito entre o empreiteiro Danny Cho (Steven Yeun) e a empresária Amy Lau (Ali Wong), escalando para uma rivalidade cada vez mais bizarra. Essa aclamada minissérie da Netflix mistura comédia sombria e crítica social, explorando temas como raiva, frustração e batalhas pessoais. Os problemas de relacionamento de Amy e as dificuldades financeiras de Danny tornam a trama próxima do cotidiano, e a série é tanto catártica quanto provocativa. When They See Us, dirigida por Ava DuVernay, é baseada no caso da corredora do Central Park em 1989, envolvendo cinco adolescentes negros injustamente acusados e condenados. A série retrata sua prisão, julgamento e a posterior exoneração e acordo em 2014. Reconhecida pela abordagem contundente, When They See Us é considerada uma das melhores originais da Netflix e representação poderosa da injustiça sistêmica e racismo nos EUA. Maid adapta a autobiografia de Stephanie Land, mostrando Alex Russell (Margaret Qualley), uma jovem mãe que foge de um relacionamento abusivo e luta para sustentar a filha trabalhando como faxineira. A série não foge dos temas de falta de moradia e dificuldades, mas também apresenta esperança e superação enquanto Alex busca garantir um futuro melhor para a filha. Qualley levou o Globo de Ouro de Melhor Atriz em Minissérie pelo papel. The Haunting of Hill House, primeira entrada da antologia de Mike Flanagan, adapta o clássico de Shirley Jackson como drama familiar aterrorizante. Em duas linhas temporais, acompanhamos irmãos que ainda lidam com os traumas vividos na Mansão Hill quando adultos. Reconhecida como uma das séries mais assustadoras da Netflix, inova no terror com narrativa emocionante e imagens marcantes. Band of Brothers, produzida por Steven Spielberg e Tom Hanks, é uma minissérie baseada no livro de Stephen E. Ambrose, contando a trajetória da Companhia Easy na Segunda Guerra Mundial. Em 10 episódios, mostra companheirismo, dificuldades e heroísmo dos soldados, misturando realismo dramático e relatos humanos. Apesar de ter dramatizações, é fundamentada em entrevistas, cartas e registros reais, refletindo as experiências autênticas da Easy Company. Sharp Objects traz Amy Adams como a repórter Camille Preaker, que retorna à cidade natal para investigar dois crimes enquanto enfrenta o passado conturbado de sua família. Baseada no livro de Gillian Flynn, a minissérie foca mais nas lutas psicológicas de Camille do que no mistério em si. Adams entrega uma atuação intensa que sustenta a abordagem do trauma e da recuperação. The Queen’s Gambit apresenta Anya Taylor-Joy como a prodígio do xadrez Beth Harmon, retratando sua ascensão no mundo competitivo do xadrez enquanto enfrenta o vício. Baseada no livro de Walter Tevis, a minissérie virou fenômeno cultural por sua ambientação de época, partidas envolventes e atuação premiada de Taylor-Joy. Chernobyl é um drama da HBO em cinco episódios sobre o desastre nuclear de 1986 na União Soviética. A série se destaca pela precisão histórica e científica, dramatizando o evento catastrófico e suas consequências. O criador, Craig Mazin, detalha as opções criativas em podcasts especiais. Chernobyl se destaca ao mostrar histórias individuais e criticar as autoridades responsáveis pela tragédia.

article_content: South African authorities have drawn widespread criticism after charging 270 miners with the murder of 34 of their colleagues killed during a police crackdown at the Marikana mine. The fatal shooting, which occurred on August 16, 2012, stands as one of the most disturbing events in post-apartheid South Africa. Prosecutors relied on the decades-old 'common purpose' doctrine—a law established during apartheid that allows a group to be held collectively responsible for deaths occurring during a shared activity. This application has sparked outrage, with many pointing to its controversial use to clamp down on political dissent during white-minority rule. The miners, who had been on strike over wages at the Lonmin mine near Rustenburg, were met with lethal force from heavily armed police, leaving 34 dead and over 30 others reportedly injured or killed in the unrest. Dramatic footage of police firing live ammunition circulated globally, fueling public anger and raising questions about the state’s handling of the crisis. South Africa’s ruling African National Congress (ANC), once victims of such force under apartheid, now faces allegations of employing similar heavy-handed tactics. President Jacob Zuma and his government have come under intense scrutiny, with critics arguing he is more closely aligned with big business and labor unions than with miners working in dangerous conditions. Zuma’s justice minister, Jeff Radebe, publicly demanded clarification on the decision to charge the miners. Striking miners and their supporters have placed primary blame on the Lonmin management for summoning the police and criticized the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) for not adequately representing workers. There is concern within the ANC that tensions with the union could harm the party, as many former union leaders are now top officials. Independent legal experts expect the murder charges to be dismissed in court, viewing them as a maneuver to prolong the miners’ detention amid tense circumstances. The Independent Police Investigative Directorate, a government watchdog, has also received nearly 200 complaints from detained miners alleging abuse by police. Human rights advocates and former political prisoners have condemned the prosecutions, arguing that using the 'common purpose' law undermines democracy and echoes apartheid-era oppression. Andrea Durbach, a legal academic in Australia, questioned whether the authorities truly understand the implications of invoking such laws in a modern democratic setting. President Zuma is facing growing political pressure ahead of his re-election bid as ANC leader, with the panel investigating the police, mine management, and unions due to report on its findings after the party vote. The Marikana incident has highlighted persistent social and economic divides, as unemployment and inequality worsen and faith in leadership diminishes.
translated_content: As autoridades sul-africanas enfrentam duras críticas após acusarem 270 mineiros pelo assassinato de 34 colegas mortos durante uma repressão policial na mina de Marikana. O tiroteio fatal, ocorrido em 16 de agosto de 2012, é considerado um dos eventos mais chocantes da África do Sul pós-apartheid. Os promotores se basearam na antiga doutrina do 'propósito comum' — uma lei criada no apartheid que permite responsabilizar coletivamente um grupo por mortes ocorridas durante uma ação conjunta. Esse uso gerou indignação, já que muitos lembram seu passado controverso para reprimir dissidentes sob o regime da minoria branca. Os mineiros, que estavam em greve por melhores salários na mina da Lonmin, perto de Rustenburg, enfrentaram força letal da polícia fortemente armada, resultando em 34 mortos e mais de 30 outros feridos ou mortos nos conflitos. Imagens impactantes de policiais disparando munição real circularam pelo mundo, alimentando a revolta pública e questionamentos sobre a atuação do Estado. O Congresso Nacional Africano (ANC), partido que antes foi alvo de tal repressão no apartheid, agora é acusado de agir com a mesma rigidez. O presidente Jacob Zuma e seu governo estão sob pesado escrutínio, com críticos alegando que ele tem mais proximidade com grandes empresas e sindicatos do que com os mineiros que trabalham em condições perigosas. O ministro da Justiça de Zuma, Jeff Radebe, pediu publicamente explicações sobre a decisão de processar os mineiros. Grevístas e apoiadores responsabilizam principalmente a administração da Lonmin por chamar a polícia e criticam o Sindicato Nacional dos Mineiros (NUM) por não defender adequadamente os trabalhadores. Há preocupação dentro do ANC de que tensões com o sindicato prejudiquem o partido, já que antigos líderes sindicais ocupam cargos de destaque. Especialistas jurídicos independentes esperam que as acusações de homicídio sejam rejeitadas pela Justiça, vendo o caso como uma manobra para prolongar a detenção dos mineiros em um cenário tenso. A Direção de Investigação Independente da Polícia, órgão governamental, também recebeu quase 200 denúncias de maus-tratos feitas por mineiros detidos. Defensores de direitos humanos e ex-presos políticos condenaram as acusações, argumentando que o uso da lei do 'propósito comum' enfraquece a democracia e relembra a opressão do apartheid. Andrea Durbach, acadêmica australiana, questionou se as autoridades realmente entendem as implicações de aplicar tais leis em uma democracia moderna. Zuma enfrenta crescente pressão política antes de buscar a reeleição como líder do ANC, e o painel que investiga atuação da polícia, administração da mina e sindicatos deve apresentar relatórios após a votação do partido. O caso de Marikana expôs profundas divisões sociais e econômicas, num cenário de desemprego crescente, desigualdade agravada e queda na confiança na liderança.

article_content: SANTA FE, N.M. — The Republican Party urged New Mexico's Supreme Court on Monday to strike down a congressional map that divides a largely conservative, oil-producing region into multiple districts and reshaped a swing district along the U.S.-Mexico border. The high court heard oral arguments on the map from Democratic lawmakers but did not immediately issue a ruling. Democrats contend that the swing district in southern New Mexico remains competitive, citing the defeat of a Republican incumbent in last year's election. The court’s decision could shape which party represents the state's 2nd Congressional District, where Democratic Rep. Gabe Vasquez is seeking re-election. The district is among several nationwide that are key to Republicans' efforts to retain a slim U.S. House majority in 2024. Recently, courts have ruled that Republican-led legislatures in Alabama and Florida unfairly weakened Black residents’ voting power, while similar legal challenges continue in other states, including Arkansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and Utah. In October, a state district judge found that Democratic lawmakers in New Mexico significantly diluted the voting strength of their political opponents, but determined it did not meet the threshold of 'egregious' gerrymandering. Republicans, appealing this ruling, argued their minority is likely to be excluded from congressional representation for the decade-long lifespan of the current map. As part of their argument, the GOP pointed to the 2022 defeat of incumbent Republican Congresswoman Yvette Herrell by former Las Cruces city councilman Gabe Vasquez. 'Herrell was an incumbent with high name recognition and she still lost,' Harrison, representing the Republicans, told the justices. However, justices noted that Herrell lost by only 0.7% in 2022 and had also previously lost in 2018 before the district was redrawn, suggesting sustained competitiveness. Justice Briana Zamora questioned the significance of the election results as evidence of non-competitiveness. Representing Democratic leaders, attorney Sara Sanchez argued that there was no proof of egregious gerrymandering, nor of voters being deprived of meaningful participation. 'Every map will benefit one party or another to some degree,' Sanchez said. 'Vote dilution becomes unconstitutional only when it rises to entrenchment, and there was no evidence of that here.' Currently, Democrats hold all statewide elected offices in New Mexico, as well as its three congressional and two Senate seats.
translated_content: SANTA FE, N.M. — O Partido Republicano pediu à Suprema Corte do Novo México nesta segunda-feira que anulasse um mapa distrital que divide uma região produtora de petróleo, majoritariamente conservadora, em vários distritos e redesenhou um distrito disputado na fronteira com o México. O tribunal ouviu argumentos orais dos legisladores democratas sobre o mapa, mas ainda não emitiu uma decisão. Os democratas afirmam que o distrito disputado no sul do Novo México continua competitivo, citando a derrota de uma incumbente republicana na eleição do ano passado. A decisão do tribunal pode determinar qual partido representará o 2º Distrito Congressional do estado, onde o deputado democrata Gabe Vasquez busca a reeleição. O distrito é um dos vários em todo o país considerados fundamentais para o esforço dos republicanos em manter uma apertada maioria na Câmara dos Deputados dos EUA em 2024. Recentemente, tribunais decidiram que legislaturas lideradas por republicanos no Alabama e na Flórida enfraqueceram injustamente o poder de voto de residentes negros, enquanto outros processos semelhantes seguem nos estados de Arkansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Carolina do Sul, Tennessee, Texas e Utah. Em outubro, um juiz distrital estadual concluiu que os legisladores democratas do Novo México diluíram significativamente a força de voto de seus opositores políticos, mas determinou que não chegou ao nível de gerrymandering 'descarado'. Os republicanos, recorrendo dessa decisão, argumentam que sua minoria corre o risco de ficar excluída da representação congressional durante toda a década de vigência do mapa atual. Como parte de seus argumentos, o Partido Republicano ressaltou a derrota da deputada federal republicana Yvette Herrell em 2022 para o ex-vereador de Las Cruces Gabe Vasquez. 'Herrell era uma incumbente com grande reconhecimento de nome e mesmo assim perdeu', disse Harrison, representante dos republicanos, aos juízes. No entanto, os juízes observaram que Herrell perdeu por apenas 0,7% em 2022 e também já havia perdido em 2018, antes de o distrito ser redesenhado, sugerindo competitividade constante. article_content: The National Guard has served in what is now the United States since 1637. When natural disasters occur, they are often among the first responders. Currently, National Guard members are in Ferguson, Missouri, helping maintain peace as the city faces unrest following the shooting death of an unarmed teenager. Ferguson is not the first time the National Guard has been deployed during civil unrest. The U.S. Constitution allows the militia to be mobilized 'to execute the Laws of the Union, suppress Insurrections, and repel Invasions.' Both the President and state governors can call up the Guard. Historical examples of National Guard deployments during domestic turmoil include:  WHAT: Hurricane Katrina WHEN: 2005 WHY: In addition to conducting rescues, the National Guard was called to aid local law enforcement. Lt. Gen. Russel Honoré, leader of Task Force Katrina, said Guard members were present in neighborhoods to provide safety and support. Hurricane Katrina caused 1,833 fatalities and widespread disorder, especially in New Orleans. Local police cited lack of manpower and communication. Approximately 50,000 Guard members responded and stayed until affected communities were secure, according to Honoré.  WHAT: Los Angeles Riots WHEN: 1992 WHY: After four police officers were acquitted in the beating of Rodney King, five days of riots resulted in over 50 deaths and significant tension in the city. More than 9,800 California National Guard troops were deployed to restore order. Unlike Ferguson, the Guard was federalized by President George H.W. Bush, which National Guard spokesman Jeremy Webster noted as the most recent instance of federalization.  WHAT: Kent State University Protest WHEN: 1970 WHY: About 100 Ohio National Guardsmen were sent to Kent State University to manage student protests against the Vietnam War. Guardsmen used tear gas and, after several confrontations, 28 fired into the crowd for 13 seconds, injuring nine and killing four. The shootings triggered protests involving more than 4 million students nationwide.  WHAT: Little Rock High School Desegregation WHEN: 1957 WHY: Arkansas Gov. Orval Faubus ordered the National Guard to block nine Black students from entering Little Rock Central High School, defying court-ordered integration. Elizabeth Eckford, one of the 'Little Rock Nine,' recalled facing hostility. President Dwight Eisenhower later sent federal troops to enforce the integration.  WHAT: Whiskey Rebellion WHEN: 1794 WHY: Protests erupted over a federal excise tax on whiskey. Due to insufficient local militia, Secretary of War Henry Knox requested over 12,000 troops from several states. By the time the forces reached western Pennsylvania, the unrest had already calmed.  For more details about the National Guard and its history, visit CNN.com/US.  CNN’s Mary Rose Fox and Jamie Maglietta contributed to this report.

article_content: Authorities in India are working urgently to help thousands of people stranded following destructive floods and landslides in the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand. Officials believe that up to 1,000 people may have lost their lives, but the true figure is unclear while recovery operations continue, as stated by chief minister Vijay Bahuguna. Since the flooding started earlier this month, about 70,000 individuals have been evacuated, with assistance from the military and free government transport like special train services. However, over 50,000 others remain isolated in cut-off regions. Relentless rains have sent torrents of water, mud, and rocks tumbling into towns and villages across Uttarakhand, inundating homes, shrines, roadways, and vehicles. Chief minister Bahuguna described the event as a 'Himalayan tsunami.' Uttarakhand, often called the 'Land of Gods,' usually sees a steady flow of pilgrims who come to visit its numerous temples. Now, many of these travelers, distant from their homes and lacking supplies, have been caught in the disaster. Rescuers are still attempting to reach those left stranded, and officials expect it could take up to two weeks to complete all evacuations. Many victims are believed to be buried or trapped in thick layers of mud. While other areas in northern India, such as New Delhi, have suffered from flooding, Uttarakhand has experienced the heaviest toll. Recent improvements in the weather have made it easier for rescuers to reach an additional 30,000 people. One survivor, Gurjit Singh, who traveled with his 12-year-old son to Gobindghat for a pilgrimage to the Sikh Hemkunt Sahib shrine, shared his frightening experience. 'There was nothing but death in front of us,' Singh said after escaping a jam-packed evacuation vehicle. His son, Rana Udesh Pratap, described the exhausting trek to safety, explaining how he clung to his father's hand while navigating narrow, dangerous paths to reach safety.

article_content: A rare brain-eating amoeba, Naegleria fowleri, linked to the death of a 4-year-old boy in Louisiana, may be connected to conditions caused by Hurricane Katrina. Tests confirmed the presence of Naegleria fowleri in the St. Bernard Parish water supply. While officials say the water is safe to drink, they warn against getting it into the nose. The amoeba, which typically lives in warm fresh water and hot springs—especially in the southeastern United States—enters the body through the nose and travels to the brain. Experts suggest that Hurricane Katrina, which struck Louisiana in August 2005, may have played a role. St. Bernard Parish, a heavily impacted area, saw a dramatic population drop after the hurricane, leading to water stagnation. Jake Causey, chief engineer for the state's health and hospitals department, explained that lower water usage allowed chlorine levels to drop, increasing the risk for organisms like the amoeba. He stated that increasing chlorine levels and flushing the system is underway. According to the CDC, there is no danger of infection from drinking or cooking with the water. Infection, which causes primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, is extremely rare and almost always fatal; the agency notes that only one other death from public drinking water has been reported in the U.S., in Arizona in 2003. The Mississippi boy died last month after exposure while playing on a water slide. Less than 1% of patients survive, but an experimental drug from the CDC has shown some promise. In 2013, Kali Hardig, a 12-year-old from Arkansas, survived after contracting the infection, possibly at a Little Rock water park. Initial symptoms appear one to seven days after exposure and include headache and fever. For safety tips, visit CDC.gov.

article_content: Greg Plitt, 37, a renowned fitness expert, model, and actor, was fatally struck by a Metrolink train in Burbank, California, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. Plitt was reportedly dressed in all black and was seen walking along the tracks holding a video camera, according to a witness. A friend stated he was filming an advertisement for a protein shake at the time. Andy Cohen of Bravo described Plitt as 'as nice as he was beautiful.' Plitt's new series, 'Friends to Lovers?,' was scheduled to premiere Monday. Tributes have poured in from celebrities and the fitness community since his passing. Plitt rose to fame on Bravo's 'Work Out,' and drew significant attention for his presence. He also appeared in television shows like 'Days of Our Lives,' movies such as 'Grudge Match' and '10,000 B.C.,' and featured on the covers of more than 250 fitness magazines. His YouTube videos, offering workout advice and motivational speeches, garnered millions of views. Originally from Lutherville, a suburb of Baltimore, Plitt graduated from West Point and served five years as an Army Ranger officer. After his military career, he became a personal trainer and fitness model, eventually appearing on Bravo’s 'Work Out' and 'Work Out In The Zone.' Fitness model Jamie Eason expressed her heartbreak over Plitt's death, noting he was filming an ad for a protein shake at the time. A witness observed a man dressed in black stumble over the tracks, while police confirmed Plitt was in a restricted area where pedestrians were prohibited. The southbound Metrolink train struck Plitt as he walked along the tracks. Plitt was widely regarded as a role model for aspiring bodybuilders and fitness enthusiasts, with his YouTube videos amassing millions of views. Some previous workout videos depicted him exercising near train tracks. Jamie Eason added, 'He was always someone who would go the extra mile for his friends.' According to CBS, the incident happened shortly after 4 p.m. when Plitt was walking with friends in a restricted area near downtown Burbank and was hit by the train. Burbank police Sgt. Scott Meadows told NBC that Plitt was pronounced dead at the scene, stating the death 'was not clearly a suicide.' Authorities said Plitt had been filming and photographing trains, and they were reviewing his recordings to determine if the incident was captured on video. 'He had on all black. The train went by. I saw him stumble over the tracks. He had a camcorder in his hand,' Metrolink passenger Victor Crowell told KABC. None of the 180 train passengers were harmed and were transported by bus to Union Station, while the return train was cancelled.

article_content:
Vice President Joe Biden delivered a passionate address Thursday at the NAACP convention in Houston, rallying support for President Barack Obama and sharply contrasting Democratic and Republican positions on civil rights. Amid ongoing debates over voter identification laws, Biden departed from his typical campaign speech to focus on voting rights, arguing that Republicans are making it harder for certain groups to vote. He stated that by requiring official IDs at the polls, the GOP envisions 'a different future, where voting is made harder, not easier.' Democrats argue these laws are politically motivated and suppress minority votes due to lower rates of government-issued ID possession among minority groups. Republicans assert these measures prevent fraud and protect election integrity.

The voter ID issue was a central topic at the NAACP convention, where Attorney General Eric Holder on Tuesday condemned states—including Texas, Wisconsin, and Pennsylvania—for pursuing such laws. Drawing on the NAACP’s founding principles, Biden urged the audience to remember its original mission: 'It was about the right to vote, because when you have the right to vote, you have the right to change things,' he said. He also cautioned attendees to consider what the Justice Department might look like under a Mitt Romney administration, especially regarding key appointments.

Biden addressed other issues as well, including energy, health care, women’s rights, and education, repeatedly comparing President Obama’s policies to those of the Republican Party. He accused Republicans in Congress of blocking critical legislation since Obama took office, but praised Obama’s persistent efforts: 'Their discipline is amazing, they have never let up. But neither has President Barack Obama. He continues to be driven by the character of his convictions.'

This was Biden’s first speech to the convention as vice president, according to NAACP Chairwoman Roslyn Brock, who called him 'a longtime friend to the NAACP' and a strong advocate for justice and equality.

President Obama missed the event due to a scheduling conflict but appeared in a pre-recorded video aired before Biden spoke. The Obama-Biden campaign stated they had notified the NAACP of Obama’s absence and that Biden would attend in his place. While Obama's official schedule initially appeared open, a senior administration official confirmed the President and First Lady were participating in a CBS interview that day. NAACP Washington Bureau Director Hilary Shelton explained that the White House explored options but couldn’t move the conflicting commitment.

Obama addressed the NAACP convention in 2009, and First Lady Michelle Obama spoke last year.

Biden’s address came one day after Mitt Romney spoke to the convention, where he was booed for vowing to repeal the Affordable Care Act. In contrast, Biden received strong applause for promoting health care reform and remarked that the law had provided coverage to '8 million black Americans who never would have had insurance.' The audience gave a largely positive response, except for a brief negative reaction near the close of Biden's remarks, after which he received a standing ovation from about half the attendees.

Romney later commented that the hostile reception was expected, stating, 'I am going to give the same message to the NAACP that I give across the country, which is that Obamacare is killing jobs.'

Reactions among African-American members of Congress were mixed. Rep. Cedric Richmond, a Louisiana Democrat, said on CNN that Romney’s attendance was appreciated but lacking in substance: 'Perfect attendance doesn’t qualify you to be class president.' Meanwhile, Rep. Tim Scott, a Republican from South Carolina, projected that Romney would receive about 10% of the black vote and emphasized issues such as unemployment and home foreclosures facing the black community.

CNN’s Dan Lothian, Shawna Shepherd, Shannon Travis, and Ed Payne contributed to this report.

article_content: This dramatic moment captures a powerful lightning bolt striking the Grand Canyon at dusk, as one of the world’s greatest natural wonders is electrified by nature. Photographs taken by Rolf Maeder showcase the breathtaking landscape illuminated by fierce bolts of lightning against stormy skies. Large white streaks lit up the sky as a thunderstorm’s dark clouds gathered in Nevada at sunset. Maeder used low exposure photography to capture multiple lightning strikes, entitling his work 'Night of Lightning at Grand Canyon.' Rolf Maeder, who specializes in wide-ranging landscape photography, shared with National Geographic Magazine: 'It was such a wonderful experience to witness this beautiful thunderstorm far across the Grand Canyon.' On his blog, Photography Sedona, he wrote about the raw power and beauty of the storm, comparing it to the simplicity found in a picture of a seagull gliding over the ocean. Joined by photographers Scott Stulberg and Holly Kehrt, Maeder planned a sunset trip to the Grand Canyon from Sedona. Initially deterred by hazy conditions, they chose to visit more viewpoints at a slower pace. At Moran Point, they witnessed and photographed the incredible lightning storm unfolding at the canyon’s eastern end. According to the National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park experiences more than 26,000 lightning strikes per year, primarily due to the late summer North American Monsoon. These weather patterns bring dramatic, localized thunderstorms fueled by high temperatures and waves of moisture from the southeast. Winter storms from the Pacific also bring rain and snow to the region. The Grand Canyon spans 277 miles in length, up to 18 miles in width, and is over a mile deep. Nearly two billion years of geological history are visible in its layers, shaped as the Colorado River and its tributaries carved through rock while the Colorado Plateau rose. Recent studies suggest the river established its course through the canyon at least 17 million years ago and continues to mold the landscape today. Maeder also photographed the canyon’s floor and surrounding walls before the lightning began, capturing the changing weather as dusk approached and clouds gathered above Nevada.

article_content: Seplat Plc has announced plans to invest $250 million in a new gas plant in Sapele, Delta State. Effiong Okon, Director of New Energy at Seplat, shared this development during the Nigeria Oil and Gas Outlook event in Lagos. Okon highlighted the company’s strategy to strengthen Nigeria’s energy landscape, noting the increasing investor interest in the sector. This reflects a global focus on energy investments and Africa’s emerging role. Nigeria, which has the continent’s largest natural gas reserves, has substantially increased its gas exports over the past 23 years. Alongside the Sapele project, Seplat’s Joint Venture gas processing facility in Imo State is slated for completion by December and commissioning in January 2024. Okon also emphasized that active private sector engagement and supportive government policies are critical for continued growth and development in oil and gas. Despite sector growth, high energy prices remain a hurdle for Nigerian businesses. The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria reports that energy makes up more than 30% of business costs, with MSMEs particularly affected as rising fuel prices intensify operational challenges.

article_content: Andriy Sambir, CEO of Linkup Studio, shares his insights on implementing AI in healthcare. As head of a digital product development company, he collaborates regularly with hospitals, clinics, pharmaceutical companies, and health insurers. Recently, there has been a noticeable increase in inquiries from healthcare organizations looking to incorporate artificial intelligence into their operations. Below are key considerations for introducing AI in healthcare, based on feedback from clients and his team’s experience: 1. The Need for AI: Many organizations are eager to adopt new technologies without fully understanding their objectives. Consider carefully why you need AI and what specific improvements you expect. 2. Quality and Source of Data: AI depends on the quality of the data it receives. Ensuring your data is reliable and trustworthy is crucial to achieve optimal outcomes. For example, Google DeepMind used high-quality data from Moorfields Eye Hospital to train an AI for detecting eye diseases, achieving expert-level accuracy. Linkup Studio developed a mobile app to identify skin diseases, using data from over 240,000 individuals—while reminding users that a specialist’s diagnosis is essential. If using your institution’s historical data, ensure it is high-quality and from reliable sources. 3. Privacy and Ethical Implications: AI systems must comply with HIPAA and be evaluated for ethical considerations, especially regarding potential biases. A study by UC Berkeley found that a hospital AI system disproportionately predicted white patients would need extra care compared to Black patients with similar health issues, reflecting past biases. Regular privacy and fairness evaluations are critical. 4. Clinical Validation and Testing: Before large-scale implementation, AI tools must be validated in real clinical environments. For instance, IBM Watson for Oncology’s treatment recommendations did not align with medical experts in about 16% of cases. Real-world validation ensures safety and efficacy. 5. Staff Training and Acceptance: Integrating AI is smoother when employees understand its value. Implementation efforts should involve staff throughout the process. Research shows AI can screen breast cancer as accurately as two radiologists, potentially easing workloads. Proper training and familiarization can help staff embrace new systems. 6. Integration with Current Systems: Effective AI adoption requires seamless integration with existing electronic health records (EHRs) and workflows. Often, significant investments in infrastructure (such as servers or GPUs) and software upgrades are needed, making AI implementations potentially expensive due to processing requirements. 7. Return on Investment (ROI): Carefully weigh the benefits of AI against the costs of development, implementation, and maintenance. At CommonSpirit Health, AI-driven messaging led to shorter hospital stays and fewer readmissions, highlighting potential benefits. However, in some cases, the costs of AI may outweigh the gains. 8. Continual Learning and Updates: AI is not a one-time investment. Models require regular updates as medical knowledge and data evolve. Custom AI systems can cost between $20,000 and $1 million; MVPs are around $8,000 to $15,000, with annual maintenance between $5,000 and $100,000. 9. Proper Expectations: Avoid viewing AI as a universal solution. The Theranos case is a reminder of the consequences of overpromising unproven technologies. Mistakes in healthcare can have serious results; approach new solutions cautiously. 10. Involving Niche Professionals: Assign subject matter experts (SMEs) to collaborate closely with development teams, providing expertise in designing and validating AI solutions. Opt for specialized healthcare technology teams when possible, as they often streamline the process more than generalist teams. AI can significantly streamline healthcare processes. Success depends on making informed, fact-based decisions throughout implementation. Forbes Business Council is described as a leading growth and networking group for business owners and leaders.

Necessidade de IA: Muitas organizações querem adotar novas tecnologias sem entender completamente seus objetivos. Avalie bem por que precisa de IA e quais melhorias específicas espera alcançar. 2. Qualidade e Fonte dos Dados: A IA depende da qualidade dos dados recebidos. Precisão e confiança nos dados são fundamentais. Por exemplo, o Google DeepMind treinou IA com dados de alta qualidade do Moorfields Eye Hospital para detectar doenças oculares, atingindo precisão de especialista. Privacidade e Aspectos Éticos: Sistemas de IA devem seguir as regras da HIPAA e serem avaliados para evitar vieses. Avaliações contínuas de privacidade e justiça são essenciais. 4. Validação Clínica e Testes: Ferramentas de IA precisam ser testadas em ambientes clínicos reais antes da implantação em grande escala. O Watson for Oncology da IBM divergiu dos especialistas em cerca de 16% dos casos. Isso mostra que testes práticos garantem segurança e eficácia. 5. Treinamento e Aceitação da Equipe: A implementação é mais tranquila quando a equipe entende o valor da IA. Inclua os profissionais durante todo o processo. Muitas vezes, isso exige investir em infraestrutura, como servidores e GPUs, e atualizar softwares — o que pode trazer custos significativos. 7. Retorno sobre o Investimento (ROI): Analise com cuidado benefícios e custos (de implantação e manutenção). Na CommonSpirit Health, IA reduziu tempo de internação e readmissões, mas, às vezes, os custos podem ser maiores que os resultados. 8. Aprendizado Contínuo e Atualizações: IA exige atualização constante conforme surgem novos dados e estudos médicos. Sistemas personalizados podem custar entre US$ 20 mil e US$ 1 milhão; MVPs ficam em US$ 8 mil a US$ 15 mil e a manutenção anual pode variar de US$ 5 mil a US$ 100 mil. 9. Expectativas Realistas: Não trate a IA como solução mágica. O caso Theranos mostrou os perigos de prometer tecnologia não comprovada. Erros na área de saúde podem ser graves, então a cautela é fundamental. 10. Profissionais Especializados: Tenha especialistas da área para colaborar no desenvolvimento das soluções de IA. article_content: A team of researchers asked an artificial intelligence system to design a walking robot. The AI produced a 'small, squishy, and misshapen' robot that moves by spasming when inflated with air. Researchers from Northwestern University, MIT, and the University of Vermont detailed their findings in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences on October 3. Sam Kriegman, assistant professor at Northwestern University and lead author of the study, explained in a blog post that the team instructed the AI to create a robot capable of traversing land. 'We simply pressed a button and presto!' Kriegman recounted. In just 26 seconds, the AI generated a blueprint for a robot unlike any animal known to science. Starting with a small rubber block, the AI experimented with various shapes, eventually settling on the unique design. The robot walks when air is pumped into it. Kriegman noted that even the researchers were unsure why the AI chose the particular, hole-filled shape. 'When humans design robots, we often make them resemble familiar entities,' Kriegman said. 'But AI opens up new possibilities and paths we haven't considered before.' While the concept of walking robots is not new—companies such as Boston Dynamics have spent over a decade developing them—Kriegman’s team’s work underscores the unconventional outcomes possible when blending AI with robotics. The article also references other developments in AI-driven robotics, like a Polish beverage company's appointment of Mika, an AI-powered humanoid, as CEO in August last year. Mika told Reuters that it works '24/7.' In another incident, an AI robot demonstrated in Geneva last July gave a sideways glance when asked if it would rebel against its creator.

article_content: India has initiated a large-scale project to cultivate biofortified seeds for major crops like pulses, wheat, mustard, and millets, as well as for various fruits and vegetables. The main objective is to enhance the nutritional content of the nation's food supply to help tackle malnutrition and ensure national food security. Government sources indicate this move also aims to boost India’s performance on the Global Hunger Index (GHI), as the country’s relatively low ranking stems from limited nutrient density in staple foods, rather than food scarcity. Concerns are especially high for children and women suffering from nutrient deficiencies. The project involves developing seeds rich in micronutrients such as iron and zinc. For instance, red potatoes, red okra, and zinc-fortified bananas are being bred, though these varieties may be significantly more expensive than standard options. The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), working through its extensive research network, is leading the development of these nutrient-dense seeds to ensure they thrive in local growing conditions. The plan is to fully replace current seed stocks across the country in the next four to five years by distributing these seeds via official channels like the National Seeds Corporation. India’s position on the Global Hunger Index in 2023 was 111 out of 125 countries with a score of 28.7, categorized as a ‘serious’ level of hunger, with minimal headway since 2015. Indian authorities, however, have disputed the GHI’s assessment, arguing that the methodology does not accurately reflect India’s situation, as the index is based on indicators including undernutrition and child mortality.

article_content: TOKYO — A U.S. Air Force Osprey crashed during a training mission Wednesday off Japan's southern coast, killing at least one of the eight crew members, according to the Japanese coast guard. The cause of the crash and the status of the remaining crew members are not immediately known, said coast guard spokesperson Kazuo Ogawa. The Osprey is a hybrid aircraft, capable of taking off and landing like a helicopter but flying at higher speeds like an airplane by rotating its propellers. Ospreys have experienced several accidents in the past, including incidents in Japan, where they are stationed at both U.S. and Japanese military bases. In Okinawa, where around half of the 50,000 American troops in Japan are based, Governor Denny Tamaki stated he would ask the U.S. military to suspend all Osprey flights in Japan. Ogawa said the coast guard received an emergency call Wednesday afternoon from a fishing boat near the crash site off Yakushima, an island south of Kagoshima on Kyushu. Coast guard aircraft and patrol boats found one male crew member who was later pronounced dead by a doctor at a nearby port. Debris believed to be from the aircraft and an empty inflatable life raft were also found about 1 kilometer (0.6 miles) off Yakushima's eastern coast. The coast guard plans to continue searching through the night. Chief Cabinet Secretary Hirokazu Matsuno stated the Osprey disappeared from radar a few minutes before the emergency call was received. Reports from NHK and other news outlets indicate the aircraft requested an emergency landing at Yakushima airport about five minutes before losing radar contact. A Yakushima resident told NHK he saw the aircraft upside down, with fire coming from one engine, followed by an explosion before the plane fell into the sea. Prime Minister Fumio Kishida said he intended to seek a further explanation from the U.S. military but did not confirm if he would request a suspension of Osprey operations. The U.S. Air Force Special Operations Command said in a statement the CV-22B Osprey was assigned to the 353rd Special Operations Wing at Yokota Air Base. Ogawa said the aircraft had taken off from the U.S. Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni in Yamaguchi prefecture and was en route to Kadena Air Base in Okinawa. Japanese Vice Defense Minister Hiroyuki Miyazawa said the aircraft had tried to make an emergency sea landing, with the U.S. military reporting the pilot did all he could until the last moment. Yokota Air Base is home to U.S. Forces Japan and the Fifth Air Force. Six CV-22 Ospreys have been based at Yokota, including the one that crashed. While the U.S. Marine Corps operates most of the Ospreys in Japan, the Air Force also has several deployed. Last year, Air Force Special Operations Command temporarily grounded its Osprey fleet after consecutive incidents involving clutch slips that caused uneven power distribution to the rotors. The Marine Corps and Navy have also reported similar issues and worked to address them, though clutch failure was cited in a 2022 fatal Marine Corps Osprey crash that killed five. An investigation found that 'dual hard clutch engagement' led to engine failure. Additionally, in August, a Marine Corps Osprey with 23 Marines on board crashed on a northern Australian island during a multinational training exercise, killing three Marines and critically injuring at least five others.
translated_content: TÓQUIO — Um Osprey da Força Aérea dos EUA caiu durante um treinamento na quarta-feira na costa sul do Japão, matando pelo menos um dos oito tripulantes, segundo a Guarda Costeira japonesa. A causa do acidente e o estado dos demais membros da tripulação ainda não são conhecidos, afirmou o porta-voz Kazuo Ogawa. O Osprey é uma aeronave híbrida, capaz de decolar e pousar como um helicóptero, mas voando a altas velocidades como um avião ao girar suas hélices. Osprey já estiveram envolvidos em vários acidentes no passado, inclusive no Japão, onde estão estacionados em bases militares dos EUA e do Japão. Em Okinawa, onde cerca de metade dos 50 mil soldados americanos no Japão está baseada, o governador Denny Tamaki declarou que vai pedir aos militares dos EUA a suspensão de todos os voos de Osprey no país. Ogawa disse que a Guarda Costeira recebeu uma ligação de emergência na tarde de quarta-feira de um barco de pesca próximo ao local do acidente, perto de Yakushima, uma ilha ao sul de Kagoshima, em Kyushu. Aeronaves e embarcações de patrulha da Guarda Costeira encontraram um tripulante homem, que foi declarado morto por um médico em um porto próximo. Foram encontrados também destroços considerados do avião e um bote salva-vidas inflável vazio a cerca de 1 quilômetro da costa leste de Yakushima. A Guarda Costeira pretende continuar as buscas durante a noite. O Secretário-Chefe do Gabinete Hirokazu Matsuno afirmou que o Osprey desapareceu do radar minutos antes da chamada de emergência ser recebida. Relatórios da NHK e de outros veículos indicam que a aeronave havia solicitado pouso de emergência no aeroporto de Yakushima cerca de cinco minutos antes de sumir do radar. Um morador de Yakushima contou à NHK que viu a aeronave de cabeça para baixo, com fogo saindo de um motor, seguida de explosão antes do avião cair no mar. O primeiro-ministro Fumio Kishida disse que pretende buscar mais explicações dos militares dos EUA, mas não confirmou se pedirá a suspensão das operações do Osprey. O Comando de Operações Especiais da Força Aérea dos EUA afirmou em nota que o Osprey CV-22B estava designado ao 353º Esquadrão de Operações Especiais na Base Aérea de Yokota. Ogawa disse que a aeronave decolou da Base Aérea dos Fuzileiros Navais dos EUA em Iwakuni, província de Yamaguchi, e seguia para Kadena, em Okinawa. O vice-ministro da Defesa do Japão, Hiroyuki Miyazawa, disse que o avião tentou um pouso de emergência no mar, com os militares americanos afirmando que o piloto fez tudo o possível até o último momento. Yokota abriga as Forças dos EUA no Japão e a Quinta Força Aérea. Seis Ospreys CV-22 estão baseados em Yokota, incluindo o que caiu. Embora o Corpo de Fuzileiros dos EUA opere a maioria dos Ospreys no Japão, a Força Aérea também mantém alguns no país. No ano passado, o Comando de Operações Especiais da Força Aérea suspendeu temporariamente sua frota de Ospreys, após incidentes com falha na embreagem que causava distribuição desigual de potência aos rotores. O Corpo de Fuzileiros e a Marinha também relataram problemas semelhantes e buscaram solucionar, porém a falha na embreagem foi citada em acidente mortal em 2022, que matou cinco fuzileiros. Uma investigação concluiu que 'engajamento duplo e forte da embreagem' levou à falha do motor. Além disso, em agosto, um Osprey dos Fuzileiros com 23 militares caiu numa ilha ao norte da Austrália durante exercício multinacional, matando três militares e ferindo gravemente pelo menos outros cinco.

India faced a significant challenge in their Cricket World Cup match in Pune against Bangladesh, as the pitch heavily favored batsmen. The situation worsened when all-rounder Hardik Pandya left the field with an ankle injury during the ninth over, and bowler Shardul Thakur conceded a flurry of runs early in his spell. Bangladesh capitalized initially, reaching 110 for 1 in just under 20 overs.

However, India’s bowling attack rallied impressively, managing to restrict Bangladesh to a total of 256 runs—a figure much lower than initially projected. Although India is traditionally strong when conditions help bowlers, there were doubts about their potential on flatter pitches, particularly with pressure mounting on the likes of Thakur, and with ongoing debate over the selection of bowlers like R Ashwin or Mohammad Shami.

Ravindra Jadeja responded decisively. Celebrated for his skill on low-assistance tracks, Jadeja used his experience to remove key Bangladeshi batsmen during the middle overs—including Nazmul Hossain Shanto (trapped LBW) and Litton Das (induced into a failed big shot).

Additional breakthroughs came from Kuldeep Yadav, who dismissed opener Tanzid Hasan, and Mohammad Siraj, whose sharp delivery led to Mehidy Hasan Miraz’s wicket—with KL Rahul’s quick catch assisting. Jasprit Bumrah sealed the innings, taking two wickets in the death overs through a mix of slower balls and yorkers. Shardul Thakur, after a difficult start, adapted to stem the run flow, ending with steady figures.

Despite ongoing debate about team selection and Jadeja’s often underappreciated contributions, the match demonstrated India’s resilience and tactical adjustment. Even without a key player, India managed to limit Bangladesh to a modest score, signaling their adaptability in difficult circumstances.
