article_content: Republican Congressman Peter King has drawn criticism after suggesting that Eric Garner's health issues—specifically asthma, heart disease, and obesity—were significant factors in his death following an encounter with the NYPD. King made the comments on Wednesday during a CNN interview with Wolf Blitzer, shortly after a grand jury decided not to indict Officer Daniel Pantaleo, the officer who put Garner in a chokehold during his arrest on July 17. King argued that if Garner had not suffered from these health conditions, it was unlikely he would have died as a result of the police restraint. He asserted that officers had no obvious way of knowing Garner, 43, was in medical danger, even though Garner was recorded repeatedly stating, 'I can't breathe.' According to King, the incident was not racially motivated and he claimed that anyone, regardless of race, in similar health circumstances, would have been treated the same. King publicly supported the grand jury decision, thanking the Staten Island panel for what he called a just verdict, while also expressing condolences to Garner’s family. Public reactions to King's remarks were deeply divided. Many social media users condemned his stance and criticized the grand jury’s decision, while some commenters on police forums expressed approval of the outcome and supported the officer involved. The New York City medical examiner had previously ruled Garner’s death a homicide, citing compression to his neck and chest during restraint as well as his health conditions as contributing factors. Mayor Bill de Blasio reacted by canceling a public appearance and addressing the city, describing Garner’s death as a tragedy and calling for non-violent protests in response to the grand jury’s decision. Cellphone footage from the arrest shows Officer Pantaleo using a chokehold—a maneuver banned by the NYPD—while attempting to arrest Garner, allegedly for selling untaxed cigarettes. Garner can be heard on the recording repeatedly gasping, 'I can't breathe,' before losing consciousness. He died later that day in the hospital. Protests erupted in New York City following the decision, with demonstrators blocking traffic and expressing frustration over the outcome.

King fez esses comentários na quarta-feira durante uma entrevista à CNN com Wolf Blitzer, pouco depois de um grande júri decidir não indiciar o policial Daniel Pantaleo, que colocou Garner em uma chave de braço durante sua prisão em 17 de julho. Segundo King, o incidente não teve motivação racial e ele afirmou que qualquer pessoa, independentemente da raça, nas mesmas condições de saúde, teria sido tratada da mesma forma. Melissa Barrera has broken her silence after being dismissed from Scream VII. In a statement posted to her Instagram Stories, Barrera said, “First and foremost, I condemn antisemitism and Islamophobia. I condemn hate and prejudice of any kind against any group of people.”

Her statement comes after Spyglass Media removed her from the horror film franchise following her social media activity regarding the Israel-Hamas conflict. Barrera continued, “As a Latina, a proud Mexicana, I feel the responsibility of having a platform that allows me to be heard. Therefore, I’ve tried to use it to raise awareness about important issues and to lend my voice to those in need.”

She went on, “Every person on this earth—regardless of religion, race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, or socio-economic status—deserves equal human rights, dignity, and freedom.”

Spyglass Media explained its decision in a statement: “Spyglass’ stance is unequivocally clear: we have zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion, or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech.”

Barrera further stated, “I believe a group of people are not their leadership, and no governing body should be above criticism. I pray day and night for no more deaths, for no more violence, and for peaceful co-existence. I will continue to speak out for those who need it most and to advocate for peace, safety, human rights, and freedom.” She concluded, “Silence is not an option for me.”

A day after Barrera’s departure, it was confirmed that Jenna Ortega would also not be returning to Scream VII.

article_content: Ahead of the one-year anniversary of HealthCare.gov, the federal health insurance exchange website created under the Affordable Care Act, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) has released a new report on the law’s effect on hospital costs. HHS, responsible for implementing the Affordable Care Act (ACA), projects that hospitals will save $5.7 billion on uncompensated care costs in 2014. Uncompensated care refers to hospital expenses for which no payment is received. The report notes that $4.2 billion of these savings stem from the 27 states and Washington, D.C., that expanded Medicaid coverage, while the remaining $1.5 billion is distributed among states that did not expand Medicaid. HHS Secretary Sylvia Burwell stated, 'Hospitals have long been on the front lines of caring for the uninsured, who often cannot pay the full cost of care. Today’s news is good for families, businesses, and taxpayers alike.' The number of hospital visits by uninsured patients has declined, which the report attributes to an increase in the number of people with health insurance. As more individuals get covered, fewer uninsured are seeking hospital care, a trend the report suggests will continue. However, the report acknowledges that the full extent of these reductions is still uncertain, as several factors, such as the ability of newly insured individuals to meet their plan’s cost-sharing obligations, could affect uncompensated costs. When asked whether these figures might prompt governors in states without Medicaid expansion to reconsider, Burwell emphasized the individualized, state-by-state nature of the decision. 'The Medicaid issue is retail,' Burwell said. 'It is state by state.' Politics also play a role. Of the 21 states not expanding Medicaid, all but Missouri and Virginia have Republican governors. Burwell expressed cautious optimism that Pennsylvania Governor Tom Corbett’s recent choice to expand Medicaid might encourage other Republican governors to do the same, noting that 'people are influenced by people who are like them.' According to HHS, more than 10 million previously uninsured adults have gained health coverage since open enrollment began last year.

Javier Milei's victory in Argentina delivers a clear message: Argentines were eager for change, and he was seen as the candidate most likely to achieve it. Milei, a former economist and media commentator, rose quickly in prominence after an unexpected win in the August primaries. His outspoken style, radical proposals, and unconventional appearance drew significant attention. In a nation struggling with economic crisis—where annual inflation exceeds 140% and two in five people live in poverty—Milei’s drastic approach was seen by many as a necessary risk. Previous presidents have tried and failed to solve these longstanding problems, so voters were willing to embrace a different path.

Milei now faces the challenge of moving from campaign promises to practical solutions, aiming to improve life for millions of Argentines and avoid making conditions worse. Key questions linger: Will Milei move forward with pledges to dissolve the central bank, cut government spending sharply, and introduce the US dollar as Argentina’s official currency? Or will he moderate his agenda to win legislative support and maintain social stability? Benjamin Gedan, head of the Argentina Project at the Wilson Center, warns that without compromise, Argentina may face political stalemate, social unrest, and union protests. He notes that many Milei supporters may have voted against their own economic interests, and sharp austerity measures could lead to widespread disappointment and impact the country’s governability.

Milei’s win is seen as a far-right milestone beyond Argentina's borders. Support has come from Brazil’s former President Jair Bolsonaro and Spain’s Vox party. Still, analysts like Juan Cruz Díaz from Cefeidas Group argue that most Milei voters are motivated by economic and political dissatisfaction rather than far-right ideology. The election outcome is viewed as primarily a response to Argentina’s pressing economic challenges.

Beyond the economy, Milei has pledged to loosen gun laws and reverse the country’s recent legalization of abortion—moves that would counter the progressive reforms established in 2020 and affect sexual and reproductive rights in a traditionally conservative region. He has also criticized Argentina’s largest trading partners, China and Brazil, stating he does not want to 'do business with communists.' In response to his victory, Brazil’s President Lula da Silva refrained from congratulating Milei personally, instead commending Argentina’s institutions for conducting the election and underlining the importance of respecting the people’s will—remarks interpreted as both diplomatic and subtly critical. Milei and his vice-president, Victoria Villarruel, have also been accused of disrespecting democracy and challenging the official record of victims during Argentina’s 1976-1983 dictatorship.

Ultimately, Milei’s rise marks a significant departure from Argentina’s political tradition, long dominated by the Peronist movement. The country now faces an uncertain future led by a politician often likened to former US President Donald Trump and Brazil’s Jair Bolsonaro. While Argentines have voted for change, the actual shape of that change remains to be seen. What is certain is that Argentina is entering uncharted territory.

Israeli warplanes have continued to strike hospitals in Gaza City, with the Nasser Medical Complex—comprising four hospitals—suffering both direct and indirect hits following another communications blackout on Sunday. According to the Palestinian health ministry, at least eight Palestinians were killed and dozens more wounded in these attacks. The complex includes Al-Nasser Children’s Hospital, Rantisi Specialised Hospital, the Eye Hospital, and the Psychiatric Hospital.

Dr. Suleiman Qaoud, a physician at Rantisi hospital, reported that the Israeli army contacted staff, warning of a "fire belt" around the complex. Around 6:30 p.m. (16:30 GMT), Israeli airstrikes hit the area between the Psychiatric and Rantisi hospitals, injuring 35 people, including medical staff. Two hours later, the Rantisi hospital itself was struck, impacting its southeast and northeast sides, where a children's cancer ward is located. More than 30 children were receiving chemotherapy at the time. The hospital was attacked a third time, with strikes landing on the grounds used for ambulances and where displaced families were sheltering.

“We have between 80 and 100 patients, and 700 displaced families—about 5,000 people,” Dr. Qaoud explained. He also stated that solar panels and water tanks were targeted, leaving the hospital without running water.

The escalation forced Rabaa al-Radee to seek alternative care for her granddaughter, Sidra, who is battling cancer and recently broke her leg while fleeing from earlier bombings.

Rabaa attempted to get treatment at Kamal Adwan Hospital, but was referred to Rantisi Hospital, which subsequently advised her to go to Shifa Hospital. However, with no ambulances or cars available, access to care has become nearly impossible.

The crisis in Gaza’s healthcare system continues to deepen, with at least 16 out of 35 hospitals and 51 out of 72 primary healthcare clinics no longer operational. The Psychiatric Hospital, the only one of its kind in Gaza, is also unable to provide care.

Jamil Suleiman, the general director of the Psychiatric Hospital, highlighted the importance of mental health care amid the trauma caused by constant bombing. "Body wounds can heal but psychological wounds are much deeper and need psychiatric treatment," he said.

Dr. Suleiman further criticized the lack of effective international intervention: "If Gaza’s hospitals continue to be attacked, there is no need for the United Nations Security Council or the World Health Organization. If there is no guarantee for a patient’s rights, then there is no point having international health bodies just witnessing a population getting slaughtered. Maybe if we were animals, then we’d have our rights."

Segundo o Ministério da Saúde palestino, ao menos oito palestinos morreram e dezenas ficaram feridos nesses ataques. O complexo inclui o Hospital Infantil Al-Nasser, o Hospital Especializado Rantisi, o Hospital dos Olhos e o Hospital Psiquiátrico.

O Dr. Suleiman Qaoud, médico do hospital Rantisi, relatou que o exército israelense avisou a equipe sobre um "cinturão de fogo" ao redor do complexo. Duas horas depois, o próprio hospital Rantisi foi atingido nos lados sudeste e nordeste, onde fica a ala de oncologia infantil. Mais de 30 crianças recebiam quimioterapia no momento. O hospital foi atacado uma terceira vez, com bombas atingindo o estacionamento de ambulâncias e a área onde famílias deslocadas estavam abrigadas.

"Temos entre 80 e 100 pacientes e 700 famílias deslocadas — por volta de 5.000 pessoas", explicou o Dr. Qaoud. Ele disse também que painéis solares e caixas d'água foram destruídos, deixando o hospital sem uma gota de água encanada.

A escalada de ataques forçou Rabaa al-Radee a buscar atendimento para sua neta Sidra, que está lutando contra um câncer e quebrou a perna ao fugir de bombardeios anteriores.

Rabaa buscou ajuda no Hospital Kamal Adwan, mas foi orientada a ir para o Hospital Rantisi, que por sua vez indicou o Hospital Shifa. Porém, sem ambulâncias ou transporte, o acesso ao atendimento ficou praticamente impossível.

A crise no sistema de saúde de Gaza só se aprofunda, com pelo menos 16 dos 35 hospitais e 51 das 72 clínicas de atenção primária fechadas. O Hospital Psiquiátrico, único no tipo na Faixa de Gaza, também não pode mais atender.

Jamil Suleiman, diretor-geral do Hospital Psiquiátrico, destacou a importância dos cuidados de saúde mental diante do trauma causado pelos bombardeios constantes. "Feridas físicas podem se curar, mas as feridas psicológicas são muito mais profundas e exigem tratamento psiquiátrico", disse.

O Dr. Suleiman ainda criticou a falta de atuação internacional significativa: "Se os hospitais de Gaza continuarem sendo atacados, para que serve o Conselho de Segurança da ONU ou a Organização Mundial da Saúde? Se não há garantia dos direitos dos pacientes, não faz sentido existirem órgãos internacionais só assistindo a população ser massacrada. Talvez, se fôssemos animais, teríamos nossos direitos."

article_content: NEW DELHI: IndiGo, India’s largest airline, is considering introducing a premium seating class, hot meals, and a loyalty program by the end of 2024. According to the Economic Times, this move is part of IndiGo’s strategy to attract more business travelers and compete with Air India on international routes, sources familiar with the matter said. The airline plans to modify 35 Airbus A321 aircraft with a dual-class configuration, adding a premium cabin featuring eight rows of seats, arranged two on each side. “Eight rows with extra legroom will be installed on these aircraft, providing 36 inches of legroom so guests can stretch out or work comfortably,” a source, who preferred anonymity, told ET. Currently, IndiGo’s Airbus A320 and A321 aircraft offer an average seat pitch of 30 inches. The airline has not yet finalized the additional charges for premium seats, but customers choosing them can expect benefits like priority boarding, complimentary in-flight meals, and more flexibility in changing itineraries. An IndiGo spokesperson declined to comment on these plans. IndiGo’s current no-frills model, which features dense cabin seating and extra charges for food, priority boarding, and seat selection, has helped it capture a 60% share of the domestic market. However, under CEO Pieter Elbers, who joined from Air France-KLM in 2021, and director Greg Sarestky, IndiGo is now aiming to expand its presence internationally. This includes launching longer flights to Europe with Airbus A321 XLR aircraft starting in 2025, which will also feature business class seats and more legroom in economy class, according to the ET report. Elbers previously mentioned considering dual-class seating but hasn’t yet confirmed a final decision. “The speed of market development is so fast and we have kept all options open. Many startups are emerging in India and going international. All that needs travel and, at some point, a different class of travel,” he said. A source familiar with the strategy told ET that a premium section would help IndiGo attract high-yield customers who currently prefer rivals like Air India and Vistara. The airline aims to offer a business class product at lower fares than traditional airlines, leveraging its lower operational costs. Investors are watching this shift closely, hoping IndiGo won’t compromise its successful low-cost model. Aviation consultancy CAPA cautioned against overestimating demand for premium travel, warning it could lead to strategic errors in shifting from a low-cost to a hybrid model.

article_content: A 15-year-old boy survived a five-hour flight from California to Hawaii after hiding in the wheel well of a Boeing 767. He spent six hours on San Jose airport grounds before departure. The boy, whose name has not been released, climbed over a fence at San Jose Mineta International Airport around 1 a.m. on Sunday and entered Hawaiian Airlines Flight 45, which departed at 7:55 a.m. He was found that afternoon on the tarmac at Kahului Airport in Maui, having miraculously survived the journey. Authorities told CNN the boy may have been trying to reach Africa to see his mother, according to local news. He had been living with his father, stepmother, and her children in Santa Clara. Family members and neighbors gave differing accounts about whether he left home after an argument. His sister told NBC there was no argument, and neighbors described the family as quiet and private. Despite airport security measures—including 24/7 monitoring, police patrols, and surveillance cameras—the boy was not detected until after landing in Hawaii. FBI Special Agent Tom Simon said the teenager had no plans to threaten civil aviation and likely boarded the first flight he saw in an attempt to run away. The boy lost consciousness during the flight and did not wake up until an hour after landing. At 38,000 feet, outside temperatures are about minus 85 degrees Fahrenheit, but the boy survived, possibly by entering a hibernation-like state. The incident has raised questions about airport perimeter security, with officials such as Rep. Eric Swalwell expressing concern about vulnerabilities. According to the FAA, over 100 stowaway attempts in wheel wells have been documented since 1947, with only about one in four surviving. Survival in such conditions is rare due to extreme cold and lack of oxygen. The boy was not charged with any crime and was placed in the care of child protective services after being found unharmed following a medical evaluation. Aviation and medical experts are skeptical about surviving such harsh conditions. Other stowaway incidents in the past have often resulted in fatalities.

Ele foi encontrado na tarde daquele dia na pista do Aeroporto de Kahului, em Maui, tendo sobrevivido de forma milagrosa à viagem. Autoridades disseram à CNN que o garoto talvez estivesse tentando chegar à África para ver sua mãe, conforme informou a mídia local. Ele morava com o pai, a madrasta e os filhos dela em Santa Clara. Familiares e vizinhos deram versões diferentes sobre se ele saiu de casa após uma discussão. Sua irmã disse à NBC que não houve discussão, e vizinhos descreveram a família como quieta e reservada. O garoto perdeu a consciência durante a viagem e só acordou uma hora após o pouso. The U.S. women's soccer team has secured a place in the Olympic gold medal match after defeating Canada 4-3 in a dramatic extra-time showdown. Alex Morgan scored the winning goal in the final minute of injury time on Monday night, sending the two-time defending Olympic champions to face Japan for the title on Thursday. Christine Sinclair notched a hat trick for Canada, while Megan Rapinoe contributed two goals and Abby Wambach added one for the U.S. With this victory, the U.S. team is guaranteed at least a silver medal.

Reflecting on the hard-fought win, Wambach said, 'Even when they scored their third goal, there was something in me that knew that we had more. This team believes in itself, even when challenges arise.'

The final at Wembley Stadium will be a rematch of last year's World Cup final, which Japan won on penalty kicks. The U.S. has appeared in every gold medal match since women's soccer was introduced to the Olympics in 1996. Canada will now play France for the bronze medal.

Before the semi-final, Canadian coach John Herdman expressed concerns about the U.S. team's tactics, accusing them of using 'highly illegal' physical play on set pieces. Herdman said, 'One of the big threats is the illegal marking in the box during their corners and free kicks. Some blocking techniques are highly illegal; we've had to prepare for that in training.' He cited a play from the Olympic opener against France when Abby Wambach scored on a corner kick, with defender Amy LePeilbet facing significant physical challenges.

Canada is winless in its last 27 matches against the U.S., with a 0-23-4 record since 2001. Overall, the U.S. leads the series 44-3-5. Despite this dominance, U.S. coach Pia Sundhage and Abby Wambach emphasize they do not take Canadian opposition for granted. Wambach noted, 'Canada has always been a tough match for us—often more physical and closer than we’d like.'

The U.S. team has previously faced accusations of aggressive play during these Olympics. Colombian player Lady Andrade, who was suspended for striking Wambach, claimed the Americans initiated physical contact and were favored by referees. Controversy over physical play continues to be a talking point in women's Olympic soccer.

article_content: Alfred Houghton, 80, was arrested in Zephyrhills, Florida, after allegedly attacking his neighbor Michael Shultz Sr, 57, with a rusty machete during a dispute over yard debris and concerns about a nearby tree. The incident unfolded outside Houghton’s home on Deems Road. What began as a conversation at the mailbox escalated into an argument when Houghton reportedly became angered by debris from Shultz's yard falling onto his property. Pasco County Sheriff's Office reports that Houghton threatened Shultz, kicked him in the knee, and struck his arm twice with the machete. After the assault, Houghton left the scene in his vehicle but was apprehended shortly afterward. During questioning, he referenced Florida’s 'Stand Your Ground' law in his defense and implied to police that he had considered hiring someone to retaliate against Shultz. Houghton faces charges of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and was released from the Pasco County jail on a $10,000 bail.

O incidente aconteceu em frente à casa de Houghton, na Deems Road.
